The coalition formed, in their account, because of legitimacy, past experience at state level, converging programmes, voter expectations and party interest.

On China, the authors report that the Greens label it a "competitor, partner and systemic rival", favour values-based diplomacy, link trade to human rights and environmental standards, and criticise Chinese human rights practices. They warn that this could hinder the EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment and increase pressure on China. They nonetheless conclude that Green toughness is not pro-American, since the party also warns against dependence on the United States. They also argue that campaign rhetoric is not binding, because governing requires cooperation with China on climate and other global issues and China is Germany's largest trading partner. They see room for improvement in relations through shared views on sustainability and peace. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic view of the German Greens' trajectory and of how Chinese scholars assess their foreign policy in the early months of the new government.
quoteEn: The German Greens' toughness towards China does not mean they are pro-American.
quoteZh: 德国绿党对华强硬并不意味着亲美。

t: Recent developments in Latin American socialism: current situation and trends
zh: 近年来拉美社会主义的发展：现状与趋势
paras: Writing in 2022, Li Han and Yuan Dongzhen ask where socialism in Latin America stands after the retreat of the region's "pink tide". They argue that its development has always been cyclical and that recent years brought new setbacks, yet that left parties and socialists have not abandoned their principles or their search for alternatives. In the authors' view, favourable conditions and constraints together point to a path that is winding, moderate and diverse.

The article has three parts. The first describes the new difficulties: a worsening political and economic environment, renewed attacks from the right, and concrete setbacks in Ecuador, Venezuela and Bolivia, the main testing grounds of "21st-century socialism". The second surveys the present situation under three headings: holding to socialist principles and practice, criticism of and resistance to neoliberalism, capitalism and imperialism, and theoretical exploration and self-reflection. The third assesses favourable conditions, constraints and likely trends.

On the setbacks, the authors link the post-2015 decline of the left to the end of the commodity-driven "golden decade", the return of neoliberal right-wing governments and hostility from the United States and Europe. They cite the end of Ecuador's 14-year experiment, Venezuela's uncertain prospects and the setbacks in Bolivia. On the other side, they report communist parties, ruling left parties and forums such as the São Paulo Forum, ALBA and the Puebla Group reaffirming socialism, and calling for original theory, as in the document "Our America Consensus". They also report self-criticism of bureaucracy, corruption and the lack of a left popular culture.

The authors name three favourable conditions: a left that is roughly balanced with the right, regional solidarity among left organisations, and persistent poverty and inequality that, they say, make socialist ideas appealing. They name three constraints: multiparty electoral systems with regular turnover of governing parties, weaknesses of left parties such as charismatic leadership and thin organisation, and external pressure, notably the US strategy of "backing the right and striking the left". They conclude that Latin American socialism will advance in a winding, cyclical way, will tend towards moderation because elites and middle strata fear radical change, and will stay diverse, with communist, nationalist and democratic socialist currents competing and influencing one another. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic overview of Latin American socialism after 2015, with details of party congresses, regional forums and statements by left leaders.
quoteEn: Under the interaction of favourable conditions and constraining factors, the development of Latin American socialism will show a trend towards twists and turns, moderation and diversity.
quoteZh: 在有利条件和制约因素交互作用下，拉美社会主义发展将呈现曲折性、温和化和多样性的趋势。

glossary.explanation: A label for the socialist projects of left governments in Venezuela, Bolivia and Ecuador from the early 2000s, associated with Hugo Chávez. It presents itself as a new, participatory alternative to neoliberalism and to earlier socialist models.
A common term for the wave of left and centre-left election victories across Latin America from the late 1990s. The article treats it as having receded after 2015.

A document proposed by Cuba and adopted at the São Paulo Forum in 2017 as the left's answer to the neoliberal Washington Consensus. The article says it sets out shared values and aims without prescribing action plans for individual countries.

t: On the unity of theory facing reality and reality tending towards theory
st: With a note on an important proposition in Marx's "Contribution to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Law: Introduction"
zh: 论理论面向现实与现实趋向理论的统一
zhSub: 兼论《﹤黑格尔法哲学批判﹥导言》中的一个重要命题
paras: Chinese scholars broadly agree that theory should face reality, but Guo Dajun notes that whether reality should also tend towards theory remains disputed. Guo takes Marx's line in the 1844 Introduction to the critique of Hegel's philosophy of law, that it is not enough for thought to strive towards realisation and reality itself must strive towards thought, as the starting point. The article's thesis is that the two directions are inseparable aspects of the theory–reality relation and that only their mutual interaction and conversion can resolve it.

The article has three parts. The first rereads Marx's discussion of 'abolishing philosophy' and 'realising philosophy' through his critique of the German 'theoretical political party' (the Young Hegelians) and the 'practical political party'. The second asks how theory should face reality, and the third why reality should tend towards theory. Guo draws on Marx, Engels and Lenin, and on examples including skyscraper construction, the 2008 Sanlu milk-powder scandal, non-Euclidean geometry, semiconductors and the post-1978 reform experience.

In Guo's reading, Marx's phrase means neither rejecting all philosophy nor rejecting theory. It means clearing out the idealism of Hegelian philosophy and turning theory into practical transformation. Guo then argues that theory serves reality through four functions: explanation, criticism, regulation and guidance. Theory must do so as theory, which Guo says means avoiding both withdrawal from reality and pragmatic trend-chasing, and recognising the intermediate link of practical concepts between theory and action. For the converse thesis, Guo holds that practice is limited by historical conditions and by the non-rational factors of its agents. Theory's relative independence and forward-looking character lets it predict trends, set goals and correct these limits.

Guo concludes that theory alone facing reality is insufficient and that reality must also tend towards theory. Guo warns against 'practice-ism' (a term attributed to Zhao Jiaxiang), which downplays theory, and against short-term, countermeasure-style research. Guo urges long-term theoretical study and cites the Party's experience of theoretical leadership, Deng Xiaoping's theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's close reading of Marx's 1844 Introduction applied to current debates on theory, practice and research culture in China.
quoteEn: The question of how theory should face reality should be understood from the essential functions of theory.
quoteZh: 应当从理论的本质功能上去理解理论如何面向现实的问题。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of socialist development since the reform era. Deng Xiaoping's formulation is cited as its origin in the article.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Chinese official discourse presents it as Marxism adapted to the twenty-first century.
A critical label, attributed by Guo to the philosopher Zhao Jiaxiang, for the tendency to treat practice as the sole or supreme standpoint of Marxism and downplay theory.

keywords: Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Law

t: The causes of the Soviet collapse, analysed thirty years on
zh: 30年后深析苏联解体原因
paras: This text is a Chinese translation of an article by the Russian philosopher Vladimir Nikolaevich Shevchenko, written on the thirtieth anniversary of the Soviet Union's dissolution in December 1991. Shevchenko asks why the USSR collapsed so quickly and argues that the main cause was the degeneration of part of the Party and state elite. External pressure, in the author's account, was an important secondary factor, and the collapse was not historically inevitable.

The article opens with Putin's December 2021 remark that the collapse was a tragedy for most Russians, and with his claim that the country lost about 40 per cent of its territory, productive capacity and population. It is organised in three sections: the elite's degeneration as the principal cause; external factors, above all Cold War psychological and informational pressure; and the need to build socialism in line with a country's own conditions and civilisational character. It closes with remarks on nationality policy and on Russia–China relations.

Shevchenko holds that the elite judged socialism inefficient, chose Western-style capitalism and used Gorbachev's reforms as cover for a plan to dismantle the system and privatise state property. As evidence, the author cites Aleksandr Yakovlev's own later writings, in which he describes a tactic of using Lenin against Stalin, then social democracy against Lenin, then liberalism against revolutionary spirit. Shevchenko adds that Western Cold War strategy worked on Soviet values and historical memory, and that Soviet ideology had no answer to spiritual needs once consumerism spread from the late 1960s. The author also says reformers ignored the particularities of Soviet socialism and of Russian civilisation, which in this account prizes social justice and spiritual over material needs.

Shevchenko contrasts this with the path of reform and opening up and socialism with Chinese characteristics, which the author says Russian Marxists admire as a way of keeping socialist ideals while adapting to national conditions. The article claims that a renewed socialism could have emerged in the USSR had civilisational specifics been respected. It says the Soviet nationalities policy had been a real achievement and that reformers deliberately stirred nationalism. The author notes growing nostalgia, the role of the Eurasian Economic Union in restoring ties, and Russia's close relationship with China. Read the original if you want a Russian Marxist philosopher's view of the Soviet collapse as published in a Chinese journal, or an example of how Russian–Chinese ideological affinity is framed.
quoteEn: The main responsibility for the demise of the Soviet Union and Soviet socialism lies with the ruling elite.
quoteZh: 苏联和苏联社会主义灭亡的主要责任在于统治精英。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched by the Chinese Communist Party in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
The official name for China's current path and system, combining Party leadership, public ownership and market mechanisms. It is presented as socialism adapted to Chinese conditions.

t: What determines the rise and fall of a political party: historical warnings from the Soviet Communist Party's failure to reach its centenary
zh: 什么决定了一个政党的兴衰——苏联共产党没能走过百年的历史警示
paras: Why did a Marxist party that was once among the most powerful in history collapse after only 88 years? Writing in the year the Communist Party of China marked its centenary (2021), Li Ruiqin asks what governs the rise and decline of a ruling party. The article argues that the Soviet party fell because it drifted away from the people, lost its capacity for theoretical innovation, and was finally led by a general secretary who had abandoned Marxism.

The article opens with the Bolshevik and Soviet party's achievements: the October Revolution, the Red Army, industrialisation under the five-year plans, the war against fascism, and support for socialist states in Eastern Europe. It then works through three lessons in turn: institutional safeguards against bureaucratism, theoretical innovation and the party's vanguard character, and the quality of party leadership. Li draws on Lenin, Marx, Plekhanov, the Russian communist leader Gennady Zyuganov and the former East German official Schirmer. The piece ends with Xi Jinping's remarks and the Chinese party's institutional arrangements since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Li first contends that Lenin foresaw the revival of bureaucracy and set up supervisory bodies, but that relying on officials' personal consciousness without secure institutions left a latent risk of separation from the masses. Second, Li argues that from the Khrushchev era and especially from the 1970s, ideological rigidity, lifelong tenure and patronage allowed entrenched interest groups to form. In the article's account, these groups shelved critical social-science research, bred a crisis of belief, and eroded the party's legitimacy. Third, the author holds that Gorbachev exploited these problems under the banner of "humane and democratic socialism", used his office to turn personal will into state will, and ended by dissolving both the party (August 1991) and the Soviet Union (December 1991). Who becomes leader may be accidental, Li says, but a Marxist party's leader must stand on the right side of world history.

Li concludes that the Soviet party's decline had no hidden cause: it moved away from the people and from Marxism, and its leadership betrayed the trust placed in it. In the author's view, the Communist Party of China has answered the questions the Soviet party left unsolved by combining the right path, scientific theory and effective institutions, and by strengthening supervision and people's status as masters of the country. Li expresses confidence that the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core will lead the cause forward in the new era. Read the original if you want to see how a CASS scholar draws lessons from the Soviet collapse for Chinese Party-building at the centenary.
quoteEn: The Soviet Communist Party's passage from strength to decline was a process of moving ever further from the people, until it degenerated into a party that had turned its back on Marxism and on the will of the people.
quoteZh: 苏共由盛到衰，是与人民渐行渐远，直至蜕变为一个背离马克思主义、背离人民意志的过程

glossary.explanation: In the article, officials who held key posts and used them for private gain. The author argues they resisted reform until it let them legalise their wealth.

t: Political degeneration, institutional collapse and national disintegration: the 30th anniversary of the CPSU's demise
zh: 政治蜕变、制度崩溃与国家分裂——苏共败亡30周年
paras: Writing in 2021, the year of the Chinese Communist Party's centenary and the 30th anniversary of the Soviet collapse, Zhang asks why the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU) lost power and the USSR broke apart. The article's answer is that the decisive cause lay inside the CPSU: its leadership abandoned scientific socialism, weakened and finally gave up the Party's leading role, and so brought down the state. Zhang presents the comparison as a warning for the Chinese Party in a period of great global change.

The article is a historical-political analysis of the Gorbachev years (1985–1991). It first discusses Western ideological pressure and the leadership's loss of belief. It then takes in turn the absolutisation of democracy and glasnost, the takeover of media, the rise of ethnic conflict, informal organisations and radical forces. Further sections deal with constitutional changes (Article 6, multiparty politics, the presidency) and the CPSU's organisational split. A final section draws lessons for China.

Zhang argues that Western 'peaceful evolution' and psychological warfare found a receptive audience among Soviet leaders such as Gorbachev and Yakovlev, who turned to social democracy. Their absolute treatment of democracy and openness, in Zhang's account, destroyed ideological consensus, dismantled the Party's authority and encouraged separatism. Zhang holds that the Party's own steps (removing its constitutional leading role, creating a presidency that bypassed the Politburo, letting republican parties act independently, and abandoning democratic centralism) turned it from a leading party into a parliamentary party and then dissolved it. Citing figures on economic decline and over 170 ethnic conflicts, Zhang concludes that without correct Party leadership there would have been no Soviet Union. Among the many explanations of the collapse, Zhang follows Mao Zedong in seeking the principal contradiction, which the article locates in the Party itself.

Zhang concludes that the Party's leadership is the key to the success of socialist construction and reform. Zhang calls on the Chinese Communist Party to hold firmly to the Four Cardinal Principles, strengthen the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds, keep the leading position of Marxism in ideology, and resist Western value diplomacy. The article also stresses reliance on the people and the expansion of whole-process people's democracy. Read the original if you want a representative Chinese official-academic account of the Soviet collapse and the lessons the Chinese Party draws from it, with extensive citation of Soviet and Russian sources.
quoteEn: In a word, without the Party's correct leadership there would be no Soviet Union, and hence no Soviet socialist cause.
quoteZh: 一句话，没有党的正确领导，就没有苏联，也就没有苏联社会主义事业。

glossary.explanation: A term used in Chinese Party discourse for alleged Western strategies of changing socialist systems from within through ideological, cultural and political means rather than war.
A formula promoted under Xi Jinping calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

A concept popularised under Xi Jinping describing China's political system as democratic at every stage, from elections to consultation and decision-making. It is presented as an alternative to Western electoral democracy.
Principles set out by Deng Xiaoping in 1979: keeping to the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship, the leadership of the Communist Party, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought.

t: An analysis of the new historiography of American communism
zh: 美国共产主义新史学探析
paras: Yang Ningcong examines the "new historiography" of American communism, which the author says has gradually displaced the "traditional" school since the 1980s. The article argues that, unlike in Britain, the two American schools stand in opposition on political stance and discourse. The new school therefore corrects and replaces the old one rather than developing it. Yang contends that it has become the mainstream of the field and matters for the US communist movement.

The article has four parts. It first defines the new historiography through four features: its historical stage, its stance, its handling of sources and its view of causal factors. It then explains why the school arose and how that rise shows itself. Next it describes the school's two main tasks. It closes with the school's significance and prospects. Yang draws on Russian historian Maxim Kirchanov, on Theodore Draper and on former traditionalists such as Harvey Klehr and John Earl Haynes.

Yang presents the old school as shaped by McCarthyism, using unreliable sources and treating American communism as a Soviet import. The new school is credited with a historical-materialist stance, closer archival work and attention to domestic roots. The causes of its rise include generational turnover among historians, New Left scholars entering universities and neoliberal pressure on students. Others are the post-2008 widening of inequality, internet circulation and digitised Russian archives. Its institutions are the society Historians of American Communism (founded 1982) and the journal American Communist History (2002). Its two main tasks are criticising anti-communism and reassessing the Communist Party USA. The reassessment stresses the party's role as a Americanised, domestic party in the Depression and anti-fascist struggles and in labour, farmer, Black and women's movements. It also stresses the \"irreplaceable\" role of Stalin.

Yang concludes that the new school helps Americans, especially the young, judge communism more objectively. In the author's view it also supports the communist movement and gives US communist history a scientific footing. The author warns that the school's work is still fragmented and that traditional historiography may revive under Trump. Yang remains optimistic because archive collections covering 1892–2019 have been assembled at New York University. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic account of how US historians have revised the history of American communism, including the author's own assessment of it.
quoteEn: The political stances and discourse systems of the new and old historiographies of American communism are opposed, so the relation between them is not one of revival or of inheritance and development, but of replacement and correction, breaking the old to establish the new.
quoteZh: 美国共产主义新旧史学的政治立场和话语体系是对立的，因此新旧之间的关系并非复兴或者继承与发展的关系，而是替代和纠正的破旧立新关系。

glossary.explanation: The anti-communist political campaign of the early 1950s in the United States, named after Senator Joseph McCarthy. The article treats it as the ideological basis of the traditional school.

t: The role of the Comintern in the founding of the Communist Party of China
zh: 共产国际在中国共产党成立过程中的角色作用
paras: Marking the centenary of the Communist Party of China (CPC), Gong Yutao asks what part the Communist International (Comintern) played in the Party's founding in July 1921. The article argues that the Comintern played a special and important role that should not be forgotten and should be assessed objectively. In Gong's account, its contribution to the founding itself was positive, though it should not be exaggerated.

The article has four parts. It first sets out the background: the Comintern's founding in 1919, its drive to create communist parties worldwide, and its Eastern strategy, including the 1920 Baku congress of the peoples of the East. It then follows the Comintern's direct involvement through its envoys Voitinsky, Maring (Henk Sneevliet) and Nikolsky, up to the First National Congress. A third part examines how Comintern requirements shaped the Party's name, programme and resolutions, and a short conclusion weighs the Comintern's overall record.

Gong's core argument is twofold. First, the Comintern helped materially: Voitinsky reached agreement with Li Dazhao and Chen Duxiu, helped set up early Party organisations in Shanghai, Beijing, Wuhan, Changsha, Guangzhou, Jinan and among Chinese abroad, and gave funding. Maring and Nikolsky helped prepare the First Congress and, according to Gong, Maring's warning after an intruder appeared saved the delegates from arrest. Second, the Comintern shaped the Party's form. Gong argues that the CPC was built on Lenin's theory of the Party and the Russian model, and that the name, the recognition of the dictatorship of the proletariat, the organisational principles later called democratic centralism, and the break with reformist parties all reflect Comintern requirements, especially the Conditions of Admission of the Second Comintern Congress.

Gong concludes that over its 24 years the Comintern's role in the CPC's development was two-sided, and that its negative effects later caused heavy losses and drew wide criticism. Gong says that at the founding stage its work was, in the words of an earlier verdict the article quotes, 'more beneficial than not'. He adds that the First Congress documents often paid too little attention to Chinese conditions, a gap the Second Congress partly addressed with Comintern help. Citing a line the article quotes, he adds that the Party would have emerged without the Comintern, because its founding answered China's own historical needs. Read the original if you want a Chinese official-history account of Comintern envoys, the First Congress and the Party's Leninist and Russian organisational model.
quoteEn: There is no doubt that in the founding and early development of the Communist Party of China, the Comintern played a special role and exerted influence in many respects.
quoteZh: 毫无疑问，在中国共产党成立和早期发展过程中，共产国际曾扮演着特殊角色，发挥着多方面的作用。

glossary.explanation: The Third International, founded in Moscow in 1919 under Lenin to coordinate communist parties worldwide; it was dissolved in 1943. The CPC joined it as a section in 1922.

The Comintern's policy of supporting anti-imperialist national movements in Asia and creating communist parties there, as part of world revolution. The 1920 Baku congress was one of its main expressions.

The Leninist organisational principle that combines discussion within the Party with binding, centralised discipline once a decision is made. The CPC treats it as its fundamental organisational principle.

glossary.zh: 中国共产党第一次全国代表大会
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó Gòngchǎndǎng Dì-yī Cì Quánguó Dàibiǎo Dàhuì
glossary.literal: First National Congress of the CPC
glossary.explanation: The founding meeting of the CPC, which began in Shanghai on 23 July 1921 and ended on a boat on South Lake, Jiaxing. It adopted the Party's first programme and first resolution.

t: Theoretical basis, historical experience and practical drivers for building a China–Vietnam community with a shared future
zh: 构建中越命运共同体的理论基础、历史经验与实践动力
paras: Since 2015, Xi Jinping has repeatedly described China and Vietnam as a "community with a shared future of strategic significance". Writing in 2021, Pan Jin'e asks what lies behind this positioning and argues that it rests on three foundations: a shared ideological basis, a store of historical experience, and the practical results and potential of bilateral cooperation. The author presents it as significant for both countries and for world socialism.

The article has four parts. It first examines the common Marxist-Leninist grounding of the two parties and the foreign-policy thought of each side. It then reviews the revolutionary friendship from the early twentieth century and the course of relations since diplomatic ties in 1950. Next it surveys political, economic, cultural and pandemic-era cooperation, including trade and investment figures from Chinese customs and Vietnamese sources. A conclusion looks ahead, drawing a comparison with the China–Laos community.

Pan's central move is theoretical. Marx's three social forms, ending in the "true community", and Lenin's views on long coexistence of socialism and capitalism are said to justify cooperation in a transitional period. Pan reads the community with a shared future for mankind as a development of this, and the China–Vietnam version as its application to two Party-led socialist states. Pan traces Chinese diplomatic thought from Mao Zedong to Xi, and Ho Chi Minh's thought on joining national independence with socialism. Pan holds that relations returned to course after setbacks because the two parties set clear guidance at each stage, such as "comrades plus brothers" and the "sixteen-character" guideline. Practical drivers include trade rising from US$32 million in 1991 to US$192.28 billion in 2020, border economic zones, and mutual pandemic help. The author also acknowledges that unresolved maritime disputes and negative perceptions among Vietnamese citizens are obstacles.

Pan concludes that the community has solid theoretical, historical and practical foundations and is the right approach for the new period. Both countries' development goals are described as aligned, and the author calls for stronger strategic trust, careful handling of maritime issues and an upgrade of the comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership. Read the original if you study Party-to-Party relations in China and Vietnam, or want to see how Chinese scholars link the community with a shared future for mankind to Marxist theory and bilateral history.
quoteEn: Building a community with a shared future of strategic significance between China and Vietnam has a solid theoretical basis, valuable historical experience and strong practical drivers, and is the correct approach to preserving and developing bilateral relations in the new historical period.
quoteZh: 构建中越具有战略意义的命运共同体具有坚实的理论基础、宝贵的历史经验和强大的实践动力，是新的历史时期维护和发展两国关系的正确方案。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping's foreign policy, applied both globally (a community with a shared future for mankind) and to bilateral relations, including with Vietnam and Laos.
A formula agreed by Chinese and Vietnamese Party leaders in 1999: long-term stability, future orientation, good-neighbourliness and comprehensive cooperation.
A phrase attributed to Ho Chi Minh describing the revolutionary bond between China and Vietnam, widely used in official narratives of bilateral ties.

glossary.zh: 全面战略合作伙伴关系
glossary.explanation: The formal level of China–Vietnam relations, declared in 2008.

t: The people's democracy of the Paris Commune and its lessons for today
zh: 巴黎公社的人民民主及当今镜鉴
paras: Marking the 150th anniversary of the Paris Commune, Chai Shangjin asks what its short life (72 days) reveals about the essential features of a socialist state system. The article argues that the Commune was the first great attempt at proletarian dictatorship and a "new, truly democratic state power", and that its principles point the way for building socialist institutions and improving governance today.

The article has three main sections. The first reconstructs the Commune's character from Marx, Engels and Lenin: its fusion of legislative and executive functions, universal election and recall of officials, and a "cheap government" with low salaries. The second traces the line from the Commune through Lenin's soviets to Mao Zedong's people's democratic dictatorship and today's Chinese institutions, covering popular sovereignty, proletarian dictatorship and Party leadership. The third uses the Commune as a mirror for criticising Western representative democracy.

Chai's central claim is that "the people as masters of the country" is the essence of socialism, and that it rests on proletarian dictatorship and on leadership by a communist party, whose absence the author names as a main reason for the Commune's defeat. On this basis the author describes China's system as one of fused legislative and executive power, in which multi-party cooperation and consultation replace Western party competition. Western representative democracy is characterised as electoral democracy, elite rule on behalf of monopoly capital, and a separation of powers degraded into partisan conflict; the article cites US election disputes and the Capitol events as evidence. Following Engels, Chai holds that the form of government (zhengti) is determined by the class nature of the state (guoti).

Chai concludes that the superiority of a system is not a matter of design but is shown through comparison with capitalism and through concrete history. The article endorses Xi Jinping's "eight criteria" for judging whether a political system is democratic and effective, and calls for continuing to improve the system of people's mastery of the country. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party-affiliated scholar draws on the Paris Commune to defend socialist democracy and criticise Western democratic models.
quoteEn: The people being masters of the country is the essence and core of socialist democratic politics.
quoteZh: 人民当家作主是社会主义民主政治的本质和核心。

glossary.en: the people as masters of the country
glossary.literal: the people act as masters of the household
glossary.explanation: A standard Chinese Party formula for popular sovereignty under socialism, presented as the core of China's democratic system.

Mao Zedong's formulation of China's state system: democracy within the people and dictatorship over their enemies, led by the working class and based on the worker-peasant alliance. It is presented as the Chinese form of proletarian dictatorship.

glossary.en: the class nature of the state (guoti)
glossary.explanation: Guoti refers to which class holds state power; zhengti refers to the form in which power is organised. Chinese Marxist theory holds that the former determines the latter.

glossary.zh: 中国共产党领导的多党合作和政治协商制度
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó Gòngchǎndǎng lǐngdǎo de duōdǎng hézuò hé zhèngzhì xiéshāng zhìdù
glossary.explanation: China's party system, in which the Communist Party rules and eight other parties take part in consultation and advisory roles. Official accounts present it as distinct from both multi-party competition and one-party rule.
Xi Jinping's eight tests for judging whether a country's political system is democratic and effective, including orderly leadership succession and effective checks on power.

t: The pandemic and the crisis of the capitalist system in the view of the foreign Left
zh: 国外左翼视域下的疫情与资本主义制度危机
source: Report on the Development of the International Communist Movement (2020–2021), Social Sciences Academic Press, June 2021, pp. 98–113
paras: Writing in 2021, Xing surveys how left-wing scholars, commentators and communist parties outside China interpreted the COVID-19 pandemic. The article's starting point is that the contrasting records of capitalist and socialist countries exposed the defects of the capitalist system, which Xing describes as a consensus among the foreign Left. Its thesis is that the pandemic revealed the nature of capitalism and that socialism is the fundamental solution.

The article is organised in four sections: the profit-driven capitalist mode of production as the root of the virus's spread; the sharpening of inequality by class and race; the deepening of institutional crisis under neoliberal policy; and the hegemonic features of Western blame-shifting towards China. It draws on figures such as David Harvey, Noam Chomsky, John Bellamy Foster, Christian Fuchs and Michael Roberts. It also draws on statements by the Communist Parties of Britain, the USA, Canada, Australia and Israel, and on pandemic and economic statistics.

In Xing's account, citing these sources, capitalism puts profit before life. This is shown in 'herd immunity' strategies, premature reopening and a pharmaceutical and health system that treats care as a commodity. Inequality is then traced to class: the article cites higher death rates among Black and poor populations, mass job losses concentrated among women and minorities, rising billionaire wealth, and state relief aimed at large firms. Decades of neoliberal austerity, privatisation and financialisation are said to have left Western states unable to prepare for the crisis or to cooperate, as in the reported lack of EU aid to Italy. Western accusations against China are read by the quoted leftists as deflecting blame and containing a possible alternative to capitalism.

Xing concludes that capitalism is a system that enriches a few rather than protecting the many. In contrast, the article presents China, Vietnam, Cuba and other socialist countries as having controlled the epidemic and restored growth, citing China's 2020 GDP growth of 2.3% and Cuba's low death rate. It argues that this demonstrates the superiority of the socialist system and that longing for socialism will resonate more widely in capitalist countries. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholarship at the Academy of Marxism collects and presents foreign leftist criticism of capitalism during the pandemic.
quoteEn: The pandemic has exposed the nature of the capitalist system, and socialism is the fundamental way to solve the problem.
quoteZh: 疫情暴露了资本主义制度的本质，社会主义才是解决问题的根本方式。

t: Socialist countries' successful control of COVID-19 shows the superiority of the socialist system
zh: 社会主义国家成功管控新冠肺炎疫情彰显社会主义制度优越性
source: Report on the Development of the International Communist Movement (2020–2021), Social Sciences Academic Press, June 2021, pp. 83–97
paras: Writing in 2021, Pan Xihua asks why China, Vietnam, Cuba, Laos and North Korea contained COVID-19 far better, in the author's account, than the developed capitalist countries. The article's answer is that the outcome reflects the superiority of the socialist system. Pan sets the pandemic as a contrast between "disorder in the West" and "order in China".

The article reviews the anti-epidemic measures of the five ruling communist or workers' parties under five headings: centralised and unified Party leadership, the ability to concentrate resources on major tasks, a people-centred value orientation, respect for science, and internationalism. Each section describes the five countries in turn, then links the practice to passages from Marx, Engels and Lenin. A closing section discusses lessons for the international response.

Pan's central move is to treat each practice as an expression of classical Marxist requirements. Party leadership is presented as the greatest socialist advantage and as the "one source of orders" behind efficient decisions. Public ownership of the means of production is said to give a basis of common interest that lets the state direct scarce resources, as in the Wuhan hospital construction, nationwide medical support and Cuba's free three-tier health system. Pan reads the people-centred principle, the stress on science and the aid China and Cuba sent abroad as practical confirmation of Marxist teaching on the masses, on science as a historical force, and on proletarian internationalism.

Pan concludes that the pandemic tested systems of national governance and that, in the article's view, socialism passed while the capitalist states, with delayed responses, "herd immunity" policies and politicised blame, failed. The author does not claim that socialist countries handled every problem perfectly. Pan calls for international solidarity, opposition to politicising public health, and scientific rather than superstitious responses. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party-affiliated scholar ties comparative pandemic experience to the doctrine of socialist superiority and to classical Marxist texts.
quoteEn: The virus knows no borders, but social systems have borders.
quoteZh: 病毒无国界，但是社会制度有国界

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Party discourse stressing that governance should serve the people's interests. In the pandemic it was expressed as "the people first, life first".
In the Marxist tradition, the solidarity of workers and socialist states across borders, from the slogan "Workers of all countries, unite!". Lenin's term was "proletarian internationalism".

t: The international communist movement presses forward in a period of turbulence and change
st: Report on the development of the international communist movement, 2020–2021
zh: 动荡变革期的国际共产主义运动砥砺前行
zhSub: 2020~2021年国际共产主义运动发展报告
paras: This annual report, published in World Socialism Studies in August 2021, surveys the international communist movement in 2020 and the first half of 2021. Pan argues that the Covid-19 pandemic and 'changes unseen in a century' have made the trend of the East rising and the West declining more evident. In Pan's account, socialist countries showed institutional strengths while capitalist ones showed weaknesses, yet the world remains one of 'strong capitalism, weak socialism', so the movement must keep pressing forward.

The report has four parts. It first covers commemorations of Engels's 200th birthday and Lenin's 150th, and the centenary reviews and tactical adjustments of communist parties. It then compares pandemic responses in socialist and capitalist states, followed by the development plans and party congresses of Vietnam, Laos, North Korea and Cuba. It closes with the external pressures and events of mid-2021, including the Communist Party of China's centenary.

Pan's central comparison treats the pandemic as an 'X-ray' of social systems. Using figures for infections and growth, the author credits China, Vietnam, Laos, North Korea and Cuba with unified Party leadership, a people-first outlook and the capacity to concentrate resources. Pan reports that China, Vietnam and Laos had positive growth in 2020. By contrast, Pan reports that in the West the pandemic spread through profit-driven production and neoliberal cuts to public health, with inequality, unemployment and unrest including the Black Lives Matter protests. Pan also reports that some Western communist parties, such as those in the United States and France, built left alliances and gained influence.

Pan concludes that socialist parties are reinforcing ideological work against Western 'peaceful evolution' and seeking closer solidarity. Pan reads the Biden administration's 'alliance of democracies' as an attempt to launch a 'new Cold War'. The report describes the July 2021 protests in Cuba as a US-engineered 'colour revolution' and notes the proposed ban on the German Communist Party's election participation. Read the original if you want a Chinese official-academic overview of how the world's communist parties and socialist states were assessed in 2020–2021, with data on the party congresses in Vietnam, Laos, North Korea and Cuba.
quoteEn: The Covid-19 pandemic is like an X-ray machine: through it one can observe the strengths and weaknesses of different social systems and the problems in their models of governance.
quoteZh: 新冠肺炎疫情就像X光透视机，透过它可以观察到不同社会制度的优劣及其治理模式的问题所在。

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎinián wèiyǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.explanation: A phrase in Chinese Party discourse, associated with Xi Jinping from around 2017–18, for a perceived shift in the global balance of power away from the West.
A Chinese and socialist-state term for alleged Western strategies of undermining socialist systems through ideological, cultural and economic means rather than force.
A term used in Chinese official discourse for popular uprisings that it regards as externally orchestrated to overthrow governments.

t: The Communist Party of China's continuing contribution to the international communist movement
zh: 中国共产党为国际共产主义运动持续贡献力量
paras: Marking the centenary of the Communist Party of China in 2021, Ji Zhengju asks how the Party's hundred years of revolution, construction and reform have contributed to the international communist movement and the cause of world socialism. The article argues that the Party has made a continuous contribution in four areas: the practical path, theory, institutions and culture.

The piece is a commemorative commentary organised in four numbered sections, each opening with a statement of the contribution made "from" one dimension: practice, theory, institutions and culture. It moves from the revolutionary path and the socialist transformation to the reform era, from the sinicisation of Marxism to the institutional system set out at the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019), and then to cultural resources.

On practice, Ji lists the rural-encirclement revolutionary road, the rapid socialist transformation of the world's most populous country, and the survival and success of socialism with Chinese characteristics after the Soviet collapse. Ji also lists Chinese modernization as an experience for developing countries. On theory, Ji argues that adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times produced a line of theoretical achievements from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, which is said to make an original contribution to the movement. On institutions, Ji describes a tiered system of fundamental, basic and important institutions, with Party leadership as the most essential feature. Ji cites the Soviet Union's fate, thirty years after its dissolution, as a warning against weakening that leadership, and presents China's handling of Covid-19 as proof of institutional advantage. On culture, Ji credits the combination of traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture, including the spirits of Jinggangshan, Yan'an and the Long March.

Ji concludes that a Party that grew from some fifty members to over 95 million is now the world's largest governing party. Standing at the junction of the "Two Centenary Goals", Ji expects socialism with Chinese characteristics to widen and to contribute more to human progress and the international communist movement. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's 2021 centenary discourse frames China's role in the international communist movement.
quoteEn: Leadership by the Communist Party of China is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the greatest strength of its institutional system.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的领导是中国特色社会主义最本质的特征，是中国特色社会主义制度的最大优势。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's model of socialism combined with market reforms, in use since the 1980s. It is presented as Marxism applied to Chinese conditions.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, stressing a huge population, common prosperity, balanced material and cultural-ecological progress, and peaceful development.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The Party's formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete conditions and with each era, yielding successive theoretical systems.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is described as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021 and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.

t: The young Engels's critique of classical liberalism
zh: 青年恩格斯对古典自由主义的批判
paras: Kou Dongliang asks how the young Engels came to criticise and move beyond classical liberalism, and why this matters for the formation of Marxism's new worldview. The article argues that Engels's critique of economic, political and cultural liberalism was an important link in that process. It holds that Engels moved from a vague longing for liberation to a working-class standpoint and a communist vision of freedom.

The article follows Engels's development in three stages. It begins with his break with Pietism, his attachment to Young Germany and then to the Young Hegelians, and his assessment of "German liberalism" through to the 1848 revolution. It then turns to his Manchester years (1842–44) and his critique of free competition and "legal freedom" in works such as Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy. It ends with his working-class standpoint, his idea of free labour and his account of communist freedom.

Kou's central argument is that Engels saw liberal freedom as formal and bound to private property. On economic liberalism, Engels is said to identify three flaws in competition: the inversion of the human–thing relation, since people become slaves to things; the hostility among individuals pursuing the same interests; and the blindness of production, which produces commercial crises. On political liberalism, Engels acknowledges the historical gains of rights such as the 1824 freedom of association in Britain. Even so, he treats constitutional monarchy and bourgeois democracy as the rule of property and as "illusory" freedom. Kou also notes Engels's judgment that political liberalism could never be realised in Germany, because of a national preference for abstract principle and a weak bourgeoisie that compromised with feudal absolutism.

Kou concludes that, from the standpoint of the working class, Engels grounded socialism in the facts of industrial Britain, especially in The Condition of the Working Class in England. He then helped found scientific socialism with Marx. Engels's Principles of Communism defines communism as the doctrine of the conditions of proletarian emancipation and pictures a planned, associated society in which all members develop fully. Kou argues that the Marxist view of freedom thereby surpasses classical liberalism both in its class narrowness and in its illusory content. Read the original if you want a detailed, text-based account of Engels's early intellectual path from German liberalism to communism, drawing on his 1839–45 writings.
quoteEn: The Marxist view of freedom surpasses both the class narrowness and the illusory content of classical liberalism.
quoteZh: 马克思主义自由观既超越了古典自由主义的阶级狭隘性，也超越了古典自由主义的内容虚幻性。

glossary.explanation: A 17th–18th-century revivalist movement within German Lutheranism that stressed inner devotion and Bible reading. Engels grew up in a strongly Pietist milieu and criticised it in his early writings.
A radical literary group of the 1830s that advocated freedom of the press and belief, constitutional government and women's emancipation. Engels was briefly associated with it.
A circle of philosophers who drew radical, critical conclusions from Hegel's philosophy in the 1830s–40s. Both Marx and Engels belonged to it before developing their own views.

glossary.en: Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy
glossary.explanation: Engels's 1843–44 essay critiquing classical political economy and private property. Marx drew on it in his own early economic studies.
Engels's term for the outlook he and Marx developed in the 1840s, namely historical materialism and scientific socialism.

t: Reflections on the world's entry into a period of turbulence and change amid changes unseen in a century
zh: 百年大变局下世界进入动荡变革期的思考与启示
paras: Writing in 2021, Zhou Miao takes up Xi Jinping's judgement that the world has entered a "period of turbulence and change" (2020), which deepens the earlier assessment of "changes unseen in a century". The article asks how this judgement relates to the established view that peace and development are the themes of the era, and how China should pursue development in a more unstable world. Zhou argues that the turbulence results from capitalist crisis, a shift in the balance between the two systems, and US-led efforts to preserve the old international order. Zhou concludes that China remains in a period of important strategic opportunity.

The article has four parts. It first sets out the Marxist concept of an era and the "theme of the era", tracing it from Engels and Lenin through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and later Party congress reports. It then explains the background to the new judgement under three headings. A third part assesses China's prospects and responses, and a short conclusion ties these to the 14th Five-Year Plan period beginning in 2021.

Zhou first distinguishes the world's themes from the nature of the era. Peace and development are the two major strategic questions facing the world, Zhou says, but the era itself is still shaped by capitalism's basic contradictions, hegemonism and an unjust old international order. On the causes of turbulence, Zhou draws on Kondratiev's long-wave theory to place the world economy in a downswing since the 2008 financial crisis. Zhou also describes an "East rising, West declining" trend in the relation between the two systems, driven by the success of socialism with Chinese characteristics. A third cause is the US response to its relative economic decline: Zhou calls neoliberal financialisation a parasitic and unsustainable accumulation model, and argues that US strategy aims to suppress China and shift the costs of crisis onto others.

Zhou contends that turbulence does not cancel China's strategic opportunity, which is "great potential" and depends on both objective conditions and subjective effort. The article proposes applying the new development philosophy to achieve high-quality development, coordinating development with security (including financial security), and building a new development pattern centred on domestic circulation. It also calls for reform of global governance and for building a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want to see how a CASS Marxist scholar links Leninist theories of the era and long-wave crisis theory to official judgements about the international environment in 2021.
quoteEn: The neoliberal financialised accumulation system has seriously deepened polarisation worldwide and created an unequal world system, leading to the international financial crisis, prolonged world economic stagnation and global political and economic turbulence; this is the fundamental cause of the world's entry into a period of turbulence and change.
quoteZh: 新自由主义金融化积累体系使世界范围内的两极分化极为严重，造成了不平等的世界体系，从而导致了国际金融危机、世界经济发展的持续低迷和全球性的政治经济动荡，这是世界进入动荡变革期的根本原因。

glossary.literal: great changes not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping has used since about 2017–2018 to describe a shift in the global balance of power and the international order. It is widely used in Chinese official discourse.

glossary.literal: the world has entered a period of turbulence and transformation
glossary.explanation: A judgement Xi Jinping put forward in 2020, presented as a further stage of the "changes unseen in a century" assessment, stressing growing instability and uncertainty.
A framework introduced in 2015 comprising innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. It is presented as guiding China's economic and social policy.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, of moving the economy from fast growth to growth focused on quality, innovation and meeting people's needs.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, promoted since 2012–2013, advocating shared development, common security and reform of global governance.
A strategy announced in 2020 that centres on domestic circulation, with domestic and international circulation reinforcing each other.

t: Cuba's model update under the test of COVID-19 and the Eighth Congress of the Cuban Communist Party
zh: 新冠肺炎疫情考验下的古巴模式更新与古共八大
source: Report on the Development of the International Communist Movement (2020–2021), Social Sciences Academic Press, June 2021, pp. 166–182
paras: He Qin examines how Cuba, hit in 2020 by COVID-19 and a tightened US blockade, handled the pandemic while pushing ahead with the "updating" of its socialist model, and what the Eighth Party Congress (April 2021) meant for that process. The article, a chapter in a 2021 yearbook on the international communist movement, argues that Party leadership and people-centred institutions produced notable pandemic results, while the update remains behind schedule and now faces a generational handover.

The text has three parts. The first covers Cuba's anti-epidemic experience and its overseas medical aid. The second reviews the update process since the Seventh Party Congress (2016), its achievements and problems, and the pandemic-era adjustments, above all the reform of the dual-currency system. The third describes preparations for the Eighth Congress, the leadership succession, Party-building and the congress's economic agenda.

On the pandemic, He credits unified Party and government direction, mass organisations and family-doctor clinics, and a long-standing welfare system. The author cites figures such as a cure rate above 93% against a 69% global average, four candidate vaccines in clinical trials, and 53 medical brigades sent to over 40 countries. He presents this internationalism as a contrast with US hostility. On the economy, He lists persistent problems: egalitarian pay with weak incentives, low agricultural output, narrow exports, ageing and pension pressure, and the blockade. The 2020 strategy and the currency reform, which will end the convertible peso, unify exchange rates and shift subsidies from goods to persons, are described as the key step, with official forecasts of an economic fall of 11% in 2020 and inflationary risk of 3,200%.

He reports that the Eighth Congress made Miguel Díaz-Canel First Secretary after Raúl Castro stepped down, completing the transfer from the revolutionary generation. It focused on Party functions, ideological work and cadre policy, and committed to deepening the update while keeping the state sector dominant. He concludes that the new leaders face the dual test of holding to the socialist road and renewing the model, and that Cuban socialism can move forward only by balancing reform, development and stability. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly account of Cuba's pandemic response, currency reform and 2021 Party congress, including the official data and documents it draws on.
quoteEn: Only by handling properly the relationship between reform, development and stability can Cuban socialism break through its difficulties and carry on the cause into the future.
quoteZh: 唯有处理好改革、发展和稳定的关系，古巴社会主义才能破局前行，继往开来。

glossary.explanation: The arrangement since 1994 in which the Cuban peso and the convertible peso both circulated, with different exchange rates. The 2020–21 reform aims to abolish the convertible peso.

glossary.literal: Eighth Congress of the Cuban Communist Party
glossary.explanation: The congress of the Communist Party of Cuba held in April 2021, which elected Díaz-Canel First Secretary in place of Raúl Castro.

t: The New Economic Policy in Lenin's political perspective
st: A close reading of "Notes of a Publicist" and related works
zh: 列宁政治视野下的新经济政策
zhSub: 研读《政治家札记》等著作
source: Contemporary World and Socialism (Dangdai shijie yu shehuizhuyi), 2021 no. 4
paras: After the shift from War Communism to the New Economic Policy (NEP) in March 1921, capitalist economic elements revived in Soviet Russia and drew doubt and hostility inside and outside the Russian Communist Party (Bolsheviks). Yu Liangzao asks how Lenin answered these voices in two works, "Notes of a Publicist" and "The New Era and the New Forms of the Old Mistakes". The article argues that Lenin placed the NEP in a political perspective, set within international and domestic politics, and that this method guided correct understanding of the policy and still offers lessons today.

Yu works through the two texts in four sections. The first covers Lenin's periodisation of the revolution into four stages and his claim that the Party had reached the "highest and most difficult stage". The second sets out what Lenin said relying on the proletariat's revolutionary spirit required. The third examines his critique of erroneous currents. The fourth is Yu's own assessment, which links Lenin's ideas to present-day Party tasks.

Yu's central claim is that Lenin read the NEP against the whole course since October 1917 and against the French Revolution and the Paris Commune, rather than as an isolated set of economic measures. In this reading, the revolution had completed the bourgeois-democratic tasks, left the imperialist war and built Soviet power, so a limited growth of capitalist elements under proletarian state power was no cause for alarm. Lenin called it a "concession" and a "strategic retreat" with limits, and Yu reports that he also named dangers: isolation and the risk of restoration. Lenin's tasks were mainly political: set cautious aims, lay the foundations of a socialist economy, regroup a weakened working class and consolidate the worker–peasant alliance. Yu says Lenin classed the Mensheviks, Socialist-Revolutionaries and Second International right as petty-bourgeois reformism making "old mistakes in new forms". He placed the "Workers' Opposition" on the "left", charging it with semi-anarchism and with denying Party leadership. Yu credits Lenin with political discernment and judgement.

Yu concludes that Lenin's approach is instructive for the Communist Party of China in a period of "great changes unseen in a century". The author links it to Xi Jinping's calls to strengthen political judgement, political understanding and political execution, and calls Xi's statements a continuation and enrichment of Lenin's thought. Lenin's critique of erroneous currents is also said to bear on resisting historical nihilism, "wholesale Westernisation" and democratic socialism, as the author names them. Read the original if you want a Chinese Party-theory reading of Lenin's NEP texts and of how they are tied to current ideological work.)
quoteEn: Lenin examined the New Economic Policy and the course of Soviet Russia since the October Revolution in a political perspective. He saw that the proletariat held state power and the leadership and control of social and political life, so a certain degree of growth of capitalist economic elements was nothing to fear.
quoteZh: 列宁将新经济政策和十月革命以来的苏俄历史进程置于政治的视野下审视和研究，他看到无产阶级掌握着国家政权，掌握着社会政治活动的领导权和控制权，因而资本主义经济因素一定程度的发展不可怕

glossary.explanation: The policy Soviet Russia adopted in 1921 in place of War Communism. It replaced grain requisition with a tax in kind and allowed private trade, leasing and concessions.
The emergency economic system of the Civil War period (1918–1921), marked by grain requisitioning and wide nationalisation of industry.
A faction in the Russian Communist Party (Bolsheviks) that arose around 1920–21 in the trade-union debate. It wanted trade unions to manage the economy.

glossary.zh: 政治判断力、政治领悟力、政治执行力
glossary.pinyin: zhèngzhì pànduànlì, zhèngzhì lǐngwùlì, zhèngzhì zhíxínglì
glossary.en: political judgement, political understanding and political execution
glossary.literal: political judgement, political comprehension, political executive ability
glossary.explanation: A trio of capacities that Xi Jinping has asked Party members, especially leading cadres, to strengthen as part of the Party's political building.

t: New circumstances and features of world socialism today
zh: 当今世界社会主义发展的新形势新特点
source: Journal of China Executive Leadership Academy Pudong, 2021 no. 2
paras: Writing in 2021, Chai Shangjin asks how world socialism is developing amid what Chinese official discourse calls changes unseen in a century and the global COVID-19 pandemic. The article argues that socialism faces a major test but also an exceptional opportunity: the trend is favourable, with several bright spots, while the Western capitalist model is in decline.

The article is organised in four parts. It first surveys the ruling communist parties of Vietnam, Laos, North Korea and Cuba, covering party-building, economic reform and pandemic response. It then turns to non-ruling communist parties in developed and developing countries, followed by anti-capitalist movements and currents of thought. The final part examines the changing relationship between the socialist and capitalist systems.

Chai's central claims run along three lines. The existing socialist states, in the author's account, have kept Party leadership, pursued renewal and opening, and shown institutional strengths in the pandemic, while seeking a strategic community among themselves and backing China's idea of a community with a shared future for mankind. Non-ruling communist parties, the author says, are strengthening organisation, forming left-wing alliances to seek an alternative to capitalism, and benefiting from protest movements such as Occupy Wall Street and Black Lives Matter and from rising interest in a "new socialism". Finally, Chai contends that the pandemic exposed Western governance failures, intensified ideological competition, especially between the United States and China, and accelerated an "East rising, West declining" trend.

Chai concludes, citing Deng Xiaoping, that socialism's eventual replacement of capitalism is an irreversible but winding historical course, and that its fate depends on proving its superiority in developing the productive forces. In the author's view, reform and opening up has borne out Deng's judgement, and the success of socialism with Chinese characteristics will increasingly influence the future of world socialism. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned Chinese account of the state of ruling and non-ruling communist parties around 2020–21, with country-by-country data and examples.
quoteEn: Ultimately, the replacement of one system by another depends on who gains the advantage in competition.
quoteZh: 制度更替最终取决于谁在竞争中占据优势。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13 as the basis of China's vision for international relations, stressing common interests and cooperation.
The policy begun in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping of economic reform at home and opening to the outside world.
The official name for China's path and system since the reform era, combining Party leadership, public ownership as the mainstay and a socialist market economy.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi nián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.literal: great changes not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping to describe the current shifts in the global balance of power and international order.

t: A centenary retrospective and its lessons: the Communist International and its relationship with the Chinese revolution
zh: 百年回眸与启示：共产国际及其与中国革命的关系
source: Contemporary World and Socialism (当代世界与社会主义), 2021 no. 3
paras: Marking the centenary of the Communist Party of China in 2021, Wang Zifeng and Pan Jin'e revisit the Communist International (Comintern, 1919–1943) and its ties to the Chinese revolution. They draw on how communist parties around the world reassessed the Comintern in 2019, its hundredth anniversary. The authors argue that the Comintern was a historical necessity that made major contributions but also committed serious errors, and that this record offers lessons for today's international communist movement.

The article has three parts. The first places the Comintern in the world proletarian movement: whether its founding was necessary, what it contributed, and what its faults were. The second follows Zhou Enlai's 1960 remark, attributed to Mao Zedong, that the Comintern was "good at both ends, poor in the middle", and divides its relations with China into three eight-year phases (1919–1927, 1927–1935, 1935–1943). The third draws four lessons for the present.

On the first part, the authors reject views that the Comintern was a "premature birth" or the product of subjective will. They cite the Second International's wartime betrayal, Lenin's theory of imperialism, and the growth of left-wing parties after the October Revolution. They list faults that communist parties acknowledged in 2019: over-centralised organisation that subordinated parties to Soviet interests, shifting and mistaken policy towards social democracy, and dogmatic export of the Soviet experience. On China, they credit the Comintern in the first phase with spreading Marxism, helping found the Party, shaping the first Kuomintang–Communist cooperation, training cadres and providing funds, while faulting its concessions to the Kuomintang right. In the second phase, they hold that its "Third Period" theory and its representatives' directives produced three "Left" errors and heavy losses until the Zunyi Meeting of 1935. In the third phase they credit its united-front line, but criticise Soviet pressure and Wang Ming's "everything through the united front" line.

The four lessons are: to recognise internationalism as a condition of proletarian liberation, and rebuild international unity among socialist forces; to unite around Marxism and the communist ideal, treating ideological agreement as more important than organisational form; to observe the principles of independence, equality, mutual respect and non-interference in inter-party relations, and to accept diverse paths to socialism; and to use the building of a community with a shared future for mankind as a banner for cooperation among communist parties. The authors present socialism with Chinese characteristics as a mainstay of world socialism. Read the original if you want a Chinese Academy of Social Sciences account of the Comintern's record in China, or the official Chinese reading of how foreign communist parties reassessed it in 2019.
quoteEn: The revival of the world socialist movement must rebuild the international union of socialist forces under the banner of internationalism.
quoteZh: 世界社会主义运动的复兴必须在坚持国际主义的旗帜下，重建社会主义力量的国际联合。

glossary.explanation: The Third International, founded in Moscow in 1919 under Lenin and dissolved in 1943. It organised communist parties worldwide and played a major role in founding and directing the early Communist Party of China.

An enlarged Politburo meeting held in January 1935 during the Long March. Chinese Party history treats it as the turning point at which Mao Zedong's leadership was established and Comintern-backed dogmatism was ended.
A Comintern doctrine adopted around its Sixth Congress (1928). It held that capitalism was entering a final crisis, and it called for a sharp turn to the left.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping's foreign policy thinking, stressing shared interests and cooperation among states. Official sources present it as a guiding vision for international relations.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since the reform era. It is presented as Marxism adapted to China's conditions.

t: European communists on the successful experience of the Communist Party of China
zh: 欧洲共产党人对中国共产党成功经验的探讨
paras: Published in July 2021, around the centenary of the Communist Party of China (CPC), this short commentary asks how communists from European parties explain the CPC's achievements. Zhang argues that these figures widely praise the Party's record and consider its experience worth learning from elsewhere.

The piece collects statements from leaders and members of communist and left parties in Russia, Belarus, Britain, the Czech lands, Germany, Italy, Spain, Switzerland and Portugal. It also cites the European Left. Their remarks are grouped under five headings: theory, history, the people, practice and the world.

Zhang reports that these figures credit the CPC's adherence to Marxism and its adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They also credit its founding mission, its commitment to putting the people first, and its principle of seeking truth from facts. Speakers such as Aleksei Sokol, Robert Griffiths and Maria Teresa Mora are quoted on the Party's ties to the people, the fight against Covid-19 and the elimination of absolute poverty. Alberto Lombardo is quoted comparing China's epidemic response with that of some Western countries. Hans Modrow is quoted saying that human rights and democracy should not be reduced to periodic voting. On the global dimension, the Spanish and Italian party leaders are quoted endorsing the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind.

Zhang concludes that many European communists admire the CPC's achievements, regard its experience as a model for others, and expect further successes. The text is mainly a thematic compilation of foreign views, which the author presents as support for the Party's approach. Read the original if you want a quick sample of how Chinese commentary presents European communist views of the CPC at its centenary.
quoteEn: The core secret of why the CPC has been able to lead China to brilliant achievements is that it has always kept close ties with the people and won their deep trust and broad support.
quoteZh: 中国共产党之所以能成功带领中国取得辉煌成就，核心秘诀是始终保持与人民的紧密联系，得到了人民的高度信任和广泛支持。

glossary.explanation: A principle of Chinese Marxism, associated with Mao Zedong and later Deng Xiaoping, that policy should proceed from actual conditions rather than doctrine. The CPC treats it as its basic ideological line.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism's basic principles to China's conditions and developing it further. The article uses the earlier form, Marxism's sinicization.
A Chinese international infrastructure and cooperation programme announced in 2013, linking China with Asia, Africa and Europe.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping that calls for cooperative global governance and shared development.

t: The Party's external exchanges: an inseparable part of China's revolution and construction
zh: 党的对外交往：中国革命与建设事业不可分割的一部分
paras: Writing in the centenary year of the Communist Party of China (2021), Yu Hongjun, a former deputy minister of the Party's International Department, argues that the Party's external exchanges have been an integral part of China's revolution and construction since 1921. The article contends that these exchanges have evolved with each period, coordinating with state diplomacy, and that they are now an indispensable component of major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics.

The article is a historical survey in four periods: the revolutionary war years, the early People's Republic, the era of reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012) under Xi Jinping. It draws on episodes such as ties with the Comintern and the Soviet Union, with Ho Chi Minh, and with foreign sympathisers like Edgar Snow, Agnes Smedley and Rewi Alley. It then moves to the founding of the International Liaison Department, the restoration of relations with communist, socialist and centre-right parties, and institutionalised dialogues with US, European, Russian, Japanese and Indian parties.

Yu's central claim is that the Party gradually moved from dependence on, and struggle against, Soviet guidance towards independence. From 1955 it abandoned judging other parties by Soviet standards and drafting their programmes. After 1978, the author says, Deng Xiaoping's principle that no party may act as a 'father party' became the four principles of independence, complete equality, mutual respect and non-interference, written into the Party constitution in 1982. Yu argues that this framework let the Party rebuild ties after the 1989–91 upheavals, and that under Xi, exchanges serve the Belt and Road Initiative and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind. The author reports that the Party will neither import nor export models.

Yu concludes that Party diplomacy, extended even through the 2020 pandemic by video meetings, has not stagnated but is expanding. In the article's account, understanding China requires understanding the Party, and the Party will keep strengthening exchanges for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want an insider's periodised account of the Party's inter-party relations, with details on institutions, dialogue mechanisms and policy turning points.
quoteEn: From the very beginning, the Party's external exchanges were an important component of China's revolutionary cause.
quoteZh: 党的对外交往，一开始就是中国革命事业的重要组成部分。

glossary.explanation: The Party's own relations with foreign political parties and organisations, distinct from but coordinated with state diplomacy. It is also called 'external work' (对外工作) and is handled mainly by the International Department.
The Party body, founded in 1950, that manages relations with foreign parties. It is now usually called the International Department of the CPC Central Committee.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978.
A Chinese international cooperation and infrastructure initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of foreign policy and world order, stressing shared interests and cooperation among states.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's official long-term national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream and Xi Jinping's leadership.

t: Lenin's theory of strategy and tactics in the socialist movement and its lessons
zh: 列宁关于社会主义运动战略与策略的理论与启示
paras: Writing in 2021, Zhou Miao asks what Lenin's theory of strategy and tactics in the socialist movement can offer at a time of what Chinese official discourse calls great changes unseen in a century, a period the author says the Covid-19 pandemic has accelerated. The article argues that Lenin greatly developed the Marxist theory of strategy and tactics, and that studying it helps China and the world socialist movement keep strategic focus, think strategically and plan accordingly.

The article begins with the background: sharpening contradictions in monopoly capitalism, the growth of bourgeois strategic theory, and the earlier work of Marx and Engels, who Zhou says treated strategy as the overall line of the proletarian party and tactics as the concrete means of carrying it out. It then sets out five areas of Lenin's thought: his distinction between strategy and tactics, the analysis of the epoch as the premise of policy, firmness of principle combined with tactical flexibility, internationalism, and the consolidation of Soviet power. A final section draws lessons for present-day China.

Zhou's central claims are that Lenin made accurate judgement of the era and of the balance of class forces the basis of strategy, rather than revolutionary sentiment alone. On this basis Lenin proposed that socialism could win first in one country, and later that the fate of world revolution depended on Russia, India, China and other eastern countries. After 1917, the author says, Lenin urged shifting the focus to construction, learning from advanced capitalist civilisation, using divisions among enemies, and winning even temporary and unreliable allies, while rejecting opportunist compromise.

Zhou draws three lessons for the present. First, Marxism should guide a clear reading of the era, and Xi Jinping's judgement on great changes unseen in a century is presented as continuing this tradition. Second, the Party should keep the whole picture in view, through the two overall situations, strategic thinking and the bottom-line approach. Third, it should unite all forces that can be united, including through the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind, with communist and left parties supporting China's modernization.
