The conduct of international affairs through multiple states acting under shared rules and institutions such as the UN, as opposed to unilateral action.

t: The lies and disorder of American-style democracy under money politics
zh: 金钱政治下美式民主的谎言与乱象
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 16 October 2020, argues that elections are not the same as democracy. Jin contends that American presidential elections, presented by the United States as a democratic model, are in essence a money game manipulated by capital and parties, and that they fail to protect citizens' political rights.

The piece proceeds through five headed sections: capital-controlled "money rule"; "rule by selected masters", where voters can only choose agents of capital; the gap between the electoral system and "rule by the majority"; social division rather than integration; and loss of governing capacity through struggles over interests. Its evidence includes the Electoral College, the 2000 Bush–Gore result and a remark by former president Jimmy Carter.

Jin starts from the Marxist claim that an election is a political form whose character depends on its economic basis. Under private ownership of the means of production, the author argues, elections serve bourgeois rule. Campaign finance from the wealthy and corporations, media control over voters' information, and policy favours for donors are said to turn elections into oligarchy. Jin adds that the Electoral College and winner-takes-all rules distort popular will, that low turnout reflects voters' sense of being unrepresented, and that campaigning breeds partisan attacks, populism and short-termism. The author also claims that televised performance favours showmanship over governing ability, and that executive–legislative gridlock and interest-group bargaining reduce efficiency.

Jin concludes that, in a country where money dominates politics, talk of political participation is empty without money. Citizens' political rights, the author says, are hard to guarantee. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Chinese official-academic commentary in 2020 framed a Marxist critique of US elections.
quoteEn: American presidential elections are no more than a money game in which parties manipulate public opinion.
quoteZh: 美国总统选举不过是一场政党操纵民意的金钱游戏。

t: Drawing strength for the road ahead from the great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression
zh: 从伟大抗战精神中汲取前行力量
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 14 October 2020, takes up the question of what the "great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression" means today. Cui Wenlong argues that this spirit, formed during the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japan, remains a precious spiritual resource. In the author's view, it can drive the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and also advance world peace and development.

The piece opens by summarising the war as the longest, largest and costliest national liberation struggle in modern Chinese history and the first to end in complete victory. It then cites Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium marking the 75th anniversary of victory, which listed the spirit's components: patriotism, national integrity, heroism and conviction of victory. The body is organised in three parts: the spirit as a source of unity, as a source of drive to overcome difficulties, and as a contribution to world peace.

On unity, Cui argues that the Party's leadership and the anti-Japanese national united front show how all forces can be mobilised, and that the same approach is needed for national rejuvenation. On drive, the author cites casualty and economic-loss figures from the war and the heroism of martyrs. Cui links this to the present, claiming that as China grows stronger, hostile forces abroad try to distort the Party's history and the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The author calls for strategic composure, confidence in that path, and a "spirit of struggle" guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, with Mao Zedong's On Protracted War as a model of scientific analysis. On peace, Cui presents China's resistance as the first major anti-fascist theatre, and draws from it lessons for peaceful development, win-win cooperation and remembering history without perpetuating hatred.

Cui concludes that carrying forward the spirit of resistance helps China meet obstacles on the road to rejuvenation and supports a community with a shared future for mankind, in which no country can face global challenges alone. The author states that China will not develop at other countries' expense. Read the original if you want an example of how official commentary in 2020 tied the memory of the anti-Japanese war to Party leadership, the united front and China's present foreign-policy language.
quoteEn: Realising a great dream requires waging a great struggle, promoting the spirit of struggle and strengthening the ability to struggle.
quoteZh: 实现伟大梦想必须进行伟大斗争，发扬斗争精神，增强斗争本领。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of the Chinese Communist Party, presented as restoring China's national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation". It has been strongly emphasised since Xi Jinping's leadership began in 2012.

The wartime alliance of classes, parties and groups against Japan, led in the Party's account by the Communist Party and cooperating with the Nationalists. It is cited in Party writing as a model for broad coalition-building.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's slogan for a vision of international relations based on interdependence, cooperation and shared interests. It is now a standard phrase in Chinese foreign-policy discourse.
The official name for China's political and economic system since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership with a socialist market economy.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

t: Mao Zedong's reflections and explorations on solving the problem of poverty
zh: 毛泽东关于解决贫困问题的思考与探索
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in September 2020, as China announced the elimination of absolute poverty, Wu Xiaoni revisits how Mao Zedong, as core of the Party's first generation of central leadership, thought about why China was poor and how poverty could be removed. The article argues that Mao identified the roots of poverty, set out basic paths for tackling it, and left experience that still offers lessons, despite mistakes made along the way.

This short commentary is divided into three parts. The first deals with the social-system roots of poverty and the move to socialism. The second turns to food supply and the rural poor. The third treats poverty as a question of developing the productive forces, covering mechanisation, education and science, and industrialisation. It draws on Mao's speeches and writings from 1919 to the late 1950s, together with economic figures for the early People's Republic.

Wu begins from the Marxist view, citing Capital, that private ownership of the means of production is the source of poverty. Mao, in this account, traced China's poverty to its semi-colonial, semi-feudal condition. The article says the revolution removed the "three big mountains", and the socialist transformation completed in 1956 was the fundamental guarantee. As evidence it cites growth in gross industrial and agricultural output of 67.8 per cent between 1952 and 1957. It then shows Mao treating grain as the first priority ("eating is the first great matter"), and rural cooperative medical care as a form of basic security. Finally, Wu presents Mao's view that poverty means low living standards caused by low productive forces. Mao therefore called for agricultural mechanisation, a "technological revolution" and a "cultural revolution".

Wu concludes that, under Mao's leadership, the poverty and backwardness of old China changed greatly, and that an independent and relatively complete industrial system laid the material basis for ending poverty. The article acknowledges failures, naming the Great Leap Forward and especially the Cultural Revolution, which it says caused heavy losses. It maintains that Mao nonetheless clarified the roots of poverty, established the standing of rural anti-poverty work, and deepened understanding of the grain question. Read the original if you want a concise, officially oriented account of how Mao's thinking on poverty is presented in the context of the 2020 poverty-alleviation campaign.
quoteEn: Being poor means a low standard of living. Why is the standard of living low? Because the level of productive forces is low.
quoteZh: 所谓穷就是生活水平低。为什么生活水平低呢？因为生产力水平低

t: The great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression will forever inspire the Chinese people to forge ahead
zh: 伟大抗战精神永远激励中国人民砥砺奋进
paras: Marking the 75th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, this commentary (first published in Guangming Daily on 2 September 2020) takes up the meaning of the "great spirit of resistance". Liu and Xu argue that the war was a contest of will and spirit as well as of military and economic strength. They hold that this spirit remains a lasting source of strength for the Chinese people as they pursue the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece follows the framing of Xi Jinping, who since the 18th Party Congress (2012) has repeatedly stressed promoting this spirit. It is organised in three parts: the significance of the spirit, its content, and how to carry it forward in what the authors call the great struggle of the new era. Mao Zedong's wartime texts, including On Protracted War, and Xi's 2014 speech marking the 69th anniversary supply the main authorities.

On significance, the authors make three claims. The spirit made up for China's material and technological weakness against a stronger imperialist Japan. It also raised national awakening to a new stage, because it covered all citizens and the whole country and put national interest first. Finally, it gives present-day struggles a source of patriotic energy. On content, they follow Xi's four-part formulation: patriotic feeling that every person bears responsibility for the nation's fate, national integrity that prefers death to surrender, heroic courage to fight to the end, and unshakeable confidence in victory. Each is illustrated with wartime episodes, such as the Mukden Incident pledge, the December Ninth Movement, Mei Lanfang's refusal to perform, Yang Jingyu, Ma Benzhai's mother and the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain. The authors trace confidence in victory to a belief that justice prevails and to China's long history of surviving ordeals.

The authors call for applying the spirit to the "great struggle" of the new era through three attitudes: daring to struggle, being good at struggling, and struggling tenaciously. They ask Communists to show courage in the face of major issues, to draw on the wartime strategy of protracted people's war, to identify principal contradictions and unite all possible forces, and to persist step by step. They present the war's experience as a model for meeting present risks and obstacles. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary in 2020 linked memory of the anti-Japanese war to the Party's call for struggle in the new era.
quoteEn: The War of Resistance against Japan was a contest of military and economic strength, but even more a contest of will and spirit.
quoteZh: 抗日战争，既是一场军事实力和经济实力的较量，更是一场意志和精神的较量。

glossary.literal: great spirit of the War of Resistance
glossary.explanation: A formula elaborated by Xi Jinping, notably in his 2014 speech, for the values attributed to the Chinese people in the war against Japan. It is summed up in four qualities: patriotism, national integrity, heroism and confidence in victory.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely associated with the Chinese Dream and Xi Jinping's leadership.
A phrase used by Xi Jinping for the demanding challenges and risks the Party and people must face in the new era. It is invoked to call for courage and tenacity in pursuing national goals.
Mao Zedong's 1938 strategy for defeating a stronger Japan through a long war in three stages, relying on mobilised people and guerrilla warfare.

t: Research on the anti-Japanese base areas: a new attempt from theory to documentary breakthroughs
zh: 抗日根据地研究：从理论到文献突破的新尝试
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 1 September 2020, Jin Yilin argues that the history of the anti-Japanese base areas deserves deeper study and that progress depends on collecting and sharing source materials. The short commentary combines a claim about the base areas' historical significance with a proposal for digital documentary work.

The first part compares the Chinese War of Resistance with resistance movements in Europe and Southeast Asia, which Jin describes as tactical aids to the Allies. The second part turns to the state of research, the value of privately held documents, and a call for wider cooperation.

Jin contends that the Communist-led armed forces opened a battlefield behind enemy lines and raised guerrilla warfare to a strategic level. In this account, the base areas' governing institutions were the prototype of the central government of 1949, and Marxism was adapted to Chinese conditions from Yan'an. On research, Jin holds that existing work is conceptual at the macro level and fragmentary at the micro level, and that a persuasive overall narrative can only rest on detailed study. Many documents are hard to find in libraries, so Jin points to private collections, such as the handwritten work notes of Zhang Linchi and Chen Shunyu, now online on a digital platform, and the holdings of the Eighth Route Army Memorial Hall in Wuxiang.

Jin calls on more institutions, scholars and private collectors to put scattered documents onto the anti-war documents data platform, so as to "share sources and write history together". Jin cites Xi Jinping's 2015 call for national coordination and for research that is deep overall and detailed on specific topics. The aim, Jin says, is to present China's voice to the world with ample sources. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how Chinese historians frame the base areas and plan digital source-sharing for War of Resistance history.
quoteEn: Only by studying endless details thoroughly can one hope to summarise them into a persuasive macro-level narrative.
quoteZh: 只有把无穷的细节研究透，才有可能高度概括出一个有说服力的宏观叙事。

glossary.explanation: Territories behind Japanese lines where the Communist-led forces built armed forces, administration and mass support during the War of Resistance (1937–45).
The name given in 1937 to the Red Army units reorganised under the Nationalist–Communist united front against Japan.

t: The Communist Party of China as the mainstay of the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression
zh: 中国共产党是抗日战争的中流砥柱
paras: Written after Xi Jinping's speech of 3 September 2020 marking the 75th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance, this article by Qu Qingshan elaborates the speech's judgement that victory was a great victory in which the Communist Party of China played the role of mainstay (zhongliu dizhu). Qu presents this as the correct conclusion from the fourteen years of the war and argues that the Party was the decisive force behind the national struggle.

The article is organised in five sections, each tied to a statement by Xi. It treats the Party as the earliest advocate and fighter against Japan after the 1931 Mukden Incident; as founder and defender of the anti-Japanese national united front; as author of the line of all-out war, the protracted-war strategy and guerrilla warfare; as leader of the enemy-rear battlefield and of the people's armed forces; and as the forger of the great spirit of resistance. It draws on Party declarations, Mao Zedong's wartime texts and military statistics.

Qu's central claim is that the Party's political and strategic leadership, rather than any single battle, shaped the outcome. He contrasts the Party's mass-mobilising line with what the article calls the Kuomintang's one-sided, government- and army-centred line, and explains Kuomintang retreats and Communist growth in these terms. Qu cites Mao's On Protracted War and its three predicted stages, and holds that the enemy-rear battlefield became the main battlefield. As evidence he gives the share of Japanese forces in China fought by Party-led troops (59 per cent in 1938, 75 per cent in 1941, 69 per cent in 1945) and the Hundred Regiments Offensive of 1940. By spring 1945, he says, the base areas covered about 950,000 square kilometres and nearly 100 million people, with 910,000 regular troops.

Qu concludes that remembering the war means remembering that the Party's mainstay role was the key to victory, and that this requires upholding Party leadership. He also calls for upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and for strengthening Party building. He ends by repeating Xi's warning that attempts to distort the Party's history will not be tolerated. Read the original if you want a representative example of the official Party account of the anti-Japanese war and its use in current arguments for Party leadership.
quoteEn: The fundamental reason why Kuomintang forces kept retreating during the war while the Communist-led forces kept growing is that the Communist Party upheld the line of all-out resistance, whereas the Kuomintang upheld a one-sided line controlled by the government and centred on the army.
quoteZh: 在抗战中，之所以出现国民党军队节节败退、共产党军队不断发展壮大的现象，其根本原因就在于中国共产党坚持全面抗战路线，而国民党坚持政府操控、军队主体的片面抗战路线。

glossary.explanation: A classical idiom for a steadfast force that holds firm amid turmoil. Xi Jinping used it in 2020 to describe the Party's role in the anti-Japanese war.
The wartime alliance of the Communists, the Kuomintang and other groups against Japan. It was formalised with the second Kuomintang–Communist cooperation in 1937.
Official term for the guerrilla war and base areas run by Communist-led forces behind Japanese lines, set against the Kuomintang-led frontal battlefield.
Mao Zedong's strategy, set out in 1938, of winning through a long war in three stages: strategic defence, stalemate and counter-offensive.
The Communist Party's wartime line of mobilising the whole population to fight, as opposed to the Kuomintang's reliance on government and regular armies.

t: A great victory against aggression, a historical turning point for national rejuvenation
zh: 反抗侵略的伟大胜利 民族复兴的历史转折
paras: Marking the 75th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War in 2020, Yang argues that the war was the first complete victory in modern China's resistance to foreign invasion. The article contends that it set the historical turning point from deep national crisis towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. It presents remembering the war as a way to cherish peace and to carry the 'great spirit of resistance' into the pursuit of the Chinese Dream.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first sets out the war's significance, running from the 1931 Mukden Incident to Japan's surrender in 1945. The second draws out the basic experience of the victory. The third sets out lessons for the present, on Party leadership, the resistance spirit, world peace and the building of a world-class military. Yang supports the account with casualty and aid figures and with remarks by foreign observers such as J. F. C. Fuller and Theodore White.

Yang's core reasoning is that victory over a stronger imperialist power came from five factors. These were the anti-Japanese national united front, the strategy of protracted war, a two-battlefield pattern, an international anti-fascist alliance, and the Communist Party's leadership. On protracted war, Yang says the Nationalists' strategy relied on government, army and foreign help and grew passive. In Yang's account, the Communist Party's version rested on mobilising the people through guerrilla warfare, base areas and people's armed forces. The frontal battlefield is said to have been the main one in the first stage, while the enemy-rear battlefield became the main one from the stalemate stage. The article puts China's war dead and injured at over 35 million and credits China with tying down over two-thirds of Japan's army.

Drawing on this history, Yang calls for unwavering adherence to Party leadership centred on Xi Jinping, citing the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds. Yang also urges patriotic education and a defence of the postwar international order against hegemonism, unilateralism and bullying, and urges building 'a community with a shared future for mankind'. The article states that weakness invites attack and calls for a modernised army ready to fight. Read the original if you want an example of how the Party's official journal narrates the war and links it to present-day political and military tasks.
quoteEn: Victory in the War of Resistance rewrote the humiliating history of a century of repeated defeats and forced cessions of territory and indemnities; from then on the Chinese nation escaped the fate of colonial enslavement, the people were greatly encouraged in spirit, and national self-confidence rose greatly.
quoteZh: 抗日战争的胜利，改写了近代百年中国抗击外来侵略屡战屡败、被迫割地赔款的耻辱历史，中华民族从此摆脱了被殖民奴役的厄运，中国人民在精神上受到极大鼓舞，民族自信心得到极大提高。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, taken to mean restoring China to national strength and prosperity after the 'century of humiliation'. It is closely tied to the Chinese Dream.
A slogan Xi Jinping popularised from 2012. It stands for national rejuvenation, prosperity and collective well-being.
The broad alliance of the Communist Party, the Nationalists and other parties and classes against Japan, formed in the late 1930s. Official histories treat it as a basis of victory.
The strategy, associated with Mao Zedong's 1938 writings, of trading space for time and wearing down a stronger enemy through three stages: defence, stalemate and counter-offensive.
Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's position as core of the Central Committee and the Party's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing cooperation and shared interests. It is promoted as an alternative to hegemonism and bloc politics.

t: Drawing powerful momentum for moving forward from the "Four Histories"
zh: 从“四史”中汲取奋发前行的磅礴力量
paras: Writing in Hongqi Wengao in 2020, Xie Xiaojuan asks what lessons the "Four Histories" should give Chinese readers as the country enters a new era. Opening with Xi Jinping's remark that history is "the best textbook" and "the best sobering agent", the commentary argues that studying the Party's history, the history of New China, the history of reform and opening up, and the history of socialism's development yields conviction, courage, loyalty to the Party and reliance on the people.

The piece is organised under four headings. The first places China in the long course of socialism, from Marx and Engels through Lenin to socialism with Chinese characteristics. The second reviews turning points in Party history and the experience they contain. The third presents the Communist Party as the axis of all Four Histories. The fourth treats the people as the force that makes history.

Xie's central claim is that the record shows the Party repeatedly facing critical choices and turning danger into opportunity. As examples the commentary lists the founding of the Party, the Zunyi Conference, the peaceful resolution of the Xi'an Incident, the rejection of a Kuomintang plan to divide China along the Yangtze, and the truth-criterion debate that opened reform and opening up. It also cites the Party's response to Western sanctions and to claims that Marxism is outdated. The author draws four lessons: combining Marxist principles with China's actual conditions, holding to the people's standpoint, thinking strategically, and correcting errors through the Party's self-reform. The Party's leadership is called the most essential feature and the greatest strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Citing the historical-materialist view that the people drive history, Xie says their creativity is released once they find the right direction and become masters of society.

Xie concludes that learning the Four Histories means reaffirming steadfast loyalty to the Party, so that the claims of historical nihilism collapse of themselves and attempts to sever the Party from the people fail. Perseverance and reliance on the people are said to ensure that the goal of a modern socialist great power is reached. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated commentary in 2020 presented the Four Histories as a source of political confidence and legitimacy.
quoteEn: The axis of the "Four Histories" is the Communist Party of China and its leadership.
quoteZh: “四史”的轴心是中国共产党和中国共产党的领导。

glossary.explanation: A collective term for the history of the Communist Party of China, the history of New China, the history of reform and opening up, and the history of socialist development. Party study campaigns have promoted it, notably from 2020.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978.
An official formulation for the Party's capacity to correct its own errors and renew itself without external pressure.
In official usage, a label for interpretations that negate the Party's historical record or the revolutionary and socialist past.
The official name for the Party's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.

t: How the Party promoted the popularisation of Marxism in the Yan'an period
zh: 延安时期我们党是如何推进马克思主义大众化的
paras: Liu Zhiming opens with Xi Jinping's call, made during an inspection tour in Yunnan, for talent like Ai Siqi who can explain the localisation of Marxism well and make it popular and accessible. Liu asks how the Party handled the popularisation of Marxism (马克思主义大众化) in the Yan'an period. The article argues that the Party answered two questions: which Marxism to use to educate the masses, and how to do it. Liu holds that the answers left experience that can guide the current effort in the new era.

The article is a short commentary in two parts. The first examines Yan'an practice under two headings: insisting on a 'living Marxism', and insisting on 'integration with the people'. It draws mainly on Mao Zedong's writings, supplemented by Xi Jinping's remarks on Mao's prose style. The second part draws three lessons for today.

On the first question, Liu says the 'living Marxism' is Marxism sinified, combining universal truth with Chinese realities. Mao called it 'creative Marxism', and Liu stresses that this does not mean abandoning study of the classics. On the second, Liu lists the Party's measures: social investigation of each class before propaganda; policies serving peasants' material interests, such as rent and interest reduction and the production campaign; and plain language learned from ordinary people. Liu cites Mao's essays, Ai Siqi's Popular Philosophy, a reading list of five theoretical works for workers, peasants and soldiers, folk forms and slogans, and model figures such as Zhao Zhankui, Zhang Side and Norman Bethune. Different audiences, according to educational level, were taught in different ways.

Liu draws three lessons. First, cadres and the public should be armed with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, studied in depth, systematically and in unity of knowing and doing. Second, the Party must stay close to the masses; Liu quotes Mao that one can teach the masses only by being their pupil, and argues that those who set themselves up as the masses' masters will find no use for their talents. Third, work should start from China's realities, respond to people's needs, apply the mass line to all governance and treat popular satisfaction as the basic standard. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of Yan'an-era propaganda methods and how they are linked to present-day theoretical education.
quoteEn: Insisting on using 'living Marxism' to educate the masses means, in essence, arming the whole people with sinified Marxism.
quoteZh: 坚持用“活的马克思主义”化大众，其实质就是用中国化的马克思主义来武装全国人民。

glossary.explanation: The effort to make Marxist theory understandable and persuasive to ordinary people through plain language and familiar forms. It is a recurring theme in Chinese Party theory, going back to the Yan'an period.
Mao Zedong's term for Marxism combined with Chinese realities and expressed in a Chinese style, as opposed to dogmatic repetition of texts.
The Party's method of work, 'from the masses, to the masses', in which leaders gather popular views, turn them into policy and return to the people to implement it. Developed in the Yan'an period.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since the 19th Party Congress (2017), written into the Party and state constitutions.
A policy in the anti-Japanese base areas that lowered peasants' land rents and loan interest, instead of confiscating land outright.

t: International opinion criticises political provocations against China by some US politicians
zh: 国际舆论批评美国一些政客涉华政治挑衅
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2020, Di Yingna and Gao Tianding present a compilation of foreign comment on a run of US measures against China. These include the closure of the Chinese consulate general in Houston, the rejection of four decades of China–US relations, attacks on the Communist Party of China and calls for comprehensive containment. The authors describe these actions as political provocation and conspiracy theory that violate international law and basic norms of international relations. They argue that they have drawn sustained criticism from the international community.

The piece is a collage of quotations from politicians, scholars, diplomats, media outlets and organisations in the United States, Russia, Egypt, Iran, Turkey, Britain, France, Belgium, Brazil and elsewhere. It is organised in three sections: the damage to bilateral ties from the consulate closure; reactions to Secretary of State Mike Pompeo's speech at the Nixon Library; and the claim that US conduct is pushing the world into instability. Cited voices include Jimmy Carter, Richard Haass, Ezra Vogel, Jeffrey Sachs, Ray Dalio, Kishore Mahbubani and Gennady Zyuganov.

In the authors' selection, commentators say that closing the consulate harms people-to-people exchange and commerce, and that it contradicts values the US professes. Critics of Pompeo's speech are quoted as saying that it misreads history and Nixon's policy of engagement, and that it is an ideological tirade resembling an election speech. The authors cite foreign commentators who say that the attempt to separate the Chinese people from the Communist Party is flawed, and they report survey figures on Chinese public trust in government (93% in a Harvard Kennedy School study, 95% in an Edelman survey). A third group of quotations warns that trade, technology, geopolitical and ideological confrontation could harm the US itself, deflect domestic failures over Covid-19, and deepen a global recession.

The authors conclude, through the voices they cite, that provocation against China is dangerous, damaging and destined to fail, and that cooperation rather than confrontation serves the world. They do not offer analysis of their own beyond the selection and framing of sources. Read the original if you want a catalogue of the international criticism that Chinese Party media chose to present in mid-2020, with named sources, as a way to see how official discourse portrayed the deterioration in China–US relations.
quoteEn: The provocations of some US politicians have dragged the world situation into unknown territory.
quoteZh: 美国一些政客的挑衅行为已经将世界形势拖向未知领域

t: Assessing the significance of victory in the War of Resistance from the historical perspective of national rejuvenation
zh: 从民族复兴的历史视野审视抗战胜利的重大意义
paras: Writing in Hongqi Wengao in 2020, Jin Minqing takes up Xi Jinping's remark of 3 September 2020, made at the symposium marking the 75th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan. Xi called that victory a historical turning point from deep national crisis towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Jin argues that the war's significance should be read within the long process of national rejuvenation, and that its victory marked a key step in escaping foreign aggression and winning independence and liberation.

The article opens by sketching the century of humiliation after 1840 and the repeated failures of earlier struggles. It then sets out five ways in which the victory bears on rejuvenation: it established the leading force, showed the guiding ideology, clarified the path, stirred national self-confidence, and gathered the people's strength. Each section looks back at the war years and forward to later stages of the Party's history.

Jin's central claim is that the war settled what earlier movements lacked: an advanced party, a scientific theory, a correct road and a mobilised people. On leadership, Jin credits the Chinese Communist Party with a decisive, "mainstay" role. The article cites figures for Party membership, troops and base areas, and describes the Party's independence from the Comintern and from the Nationalists. On ideology, Jin holds that works such as On Protracted War and On New Democracy produced Mao Zedong Thought, the first major leap in adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. On the road, Jin points to the new-democratic revolution, the base areas' land and political practice, and the call for a coalition government. Jin also describes the war as a people's war, resting on the united front and the masses.

Jin concludes that the 1945 turning point was only a beginning, and that it had to be extended into the practice of rejuvenation through further struggle. The article presents the later achievements of revolution, construction and reform, and the opening of the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, as the continuation of that turning point. It also credits the war with producing a great spirit of resistance and a stronger patriotic national consciousness. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-aligned scholarship in 2020 linked the anti-Japanese war to the narrative of national rejuvenation.
quoteEn: The War of Resistance was in the final analysis a people's war; it was by relying closely on the broad masses that the fundamental strength to defeat the enemy was obtained.
quoteZh: 抗日战争归根到底是人民战争，正是紧紧依靠广大人民群众，才获得了战胜敌人的根本力量。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China to strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation" that began in 1840. It has been central to Party discourse, especially since Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream.
A proposal the Party put forward in 1945 for a government of all parties and groups to replace Nationalist one-party rule.

t: Engels's contribution to the popularisation of Marx's philosophy in his later years
zh: 恩格斯晚年对马克思哲学大众化的贡献
paras: Marking the 200th anniversary of Engels's birth, Wang Haifeng asks what the late Engels did to turn Marx's philosophy into something the broad public, and above all the working class, could absorb. The article, a short commentary first published in Guangming Daily in August 2020, argues that Engels made a major contribution to this popularisation (dazhonghua) and that it still matters for popularising Marxist philosophy in contemporary China.

The piece is organised in four parts. Three cover Engels's later work: systematising Marx's philosophy and setting out its principles, defending its truth and scientific character, and bringing out its realism and its popular character. A final part draws three lessons for Chinese Marxist philosophy today.

On systematisation, Wang says Engels gathered ideas scattered through Marx's texts and debates, presented the two great discoveries (the materialist conception of history and the theory of surplus value) together with scientific socialism as one philosophical system, and recast scholarly writing in plainer language. Anti-Dühring and Ludwig Feuerbach and the End of Classical German Philosophy are the chief examples, and Engels also traced Marx's relation to Feuerbach and Hegel. On defence, Wang describes Engels rebutting Paul Barth's reduction of historical materialism to "economic determinism" and the claim that Marx plagiarised Rodbertus. Wang adds that Engels refined the theory itself, stressing the reaction of the superstructure on the economic base and treating motives, necessity and chance, great individuals and the "resultant of forces" in history. On realism and popular character, Wang argues that Engels exposed capitalist exploitation to the masses and stressed Marx's concern with human independence, individuality and liberation.

Wang concludes that Engels's efforts reversed the influence of vulgar materialism among ordinary Social Democrats and spread the communist worldview more widely. For China today, Wang draws three lessons. Building an academic system of Marxist philosophy should serve major theoretical and practical problems and the people's aspiration for a better life, not become an "a priori structure". Marxist philosophy must hold its basic standpoint and confront rival currents of thought, since any retreat would forfeit its scientific character and truth. And having made progress in academic rigour, the field should now give more weight to popularisation. Read the original if you want a brief, officially oriented account of how Engels's late writings are presented as a model for popularising Marxist philosophy in China.
quoteEn: To make the broad masses, including the working class, truly accept Marx's philosophy, the key is to bring out the theoretical purpose and value pursuit of realising human freedom and liberation that this philosophy contains.
quoteZh: 要使包括工人阶级在内的广大民众真实接受马克思哲学，最为关键的是，彰显这一哲学所蕴含的实现人类的自由和解放的理论旨趣和价值追求

glossary.explanation: The effort to make Marxist theory understandable and usable by ordinary people, a long-standing theme in Chinese Marxist discourse.
The theory of history, also called historical materialism, that Marx and Engels developed; the article treats it as the core of Marxist philosophy.
A quality attributed to theory that serves the people and their liberation. It is frequently used in Chinese Marxist writing.
The organised body of concepts, disciplines and discourse that Chinese official policy calls for building in the humanities and social sciences.

t: The broadest international cooperation as the solid foundation for defeating world fascism
zh: 最广泛的国际合作是战胜世界法西斯的坚实基础
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 1 September 2020, Wang Jianlang asks why the anti-aggression camp prevailed in the Second World War. The author's answer is that the allied states built the broadest international cooperation, uniting countries with different cultures, levels of development and ideologies. Wang argues that once this alliance formed, it largely decided the course and outcome of the war.

The commentary has three parts. The first traces how the idea of "indivisible peace" emerged from the League of Nations and the early years of Japanese and German aggression. The second examines how ideological divides were set aside, in China, between China and the Soviet Union, and between the Western powers and Moscow. The third turns to the post-war United Nations and to the present, which Wang describes as another moment of crisis.

Wang contends that the old, nation-bound view of security had to give way before cooperation became possible. In the author's account, the League's failure to punish Japan after the 1931 Mukden Incident set a precedent for German aggression in Europe. China's appeals, Roosevelt's 1937 "quarantine" speech and Japan's 1938 "new order in East Asia" slogan gradually moved Britain and the United States from neutrality towards aiding China. Pearl Harbor, in Wang's view, proved the theory of indivisible peace. The second pillar was ideological flexibility: Wang cites the Nationalist–Communist united front, Soviet aid to China, and Churchill's 1941 pledge to help the Soviet Union despite his long anti-communism. The Communist Party of China is portrayed as a supporter of both the national and the international anti-fascist united front.

Wang concludes that firm commitment to international cooperation is the only correct choice for overcoming crises. The author sees today's world, with sharpened economic and ideological tensions and the COVID-19 pandemic, as facing a choice between cooperation and selfish national-first policies. Wang criticises the United States for unilateralism that, in the author's words, breaks basic rules and has brought the greatest instability since 1945. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese historians use the anti-fascist alliance to frame a 2020 argument for multilateralism.
quoteEn: Historical experience tells us that unwaveringly taking the road of international cooperation is the only correct choice for humanity to overcome crises and keep society developing in a healthy way.
quoteZh: 历史经验告诉我们，坚定不移地走国际合作的道路，是人类战胜危机，保持社会健康发展的唯一正确选择。

glossary.explanation: The idea that aggression in one region threatens security everywhere. In the article it is tied to collective security and to China's wartime appeals to the international community.
The wartime cooperation between the Nationalist Party and the Communist Party of China against Japan, formed in the late 1930s after a decade of civil war.

t: Research on the anti-Japanese base areas: new attempts from theory to documentary breakthroughs
zh: 抗日根据地研究：从理论到文献突破的新尝试
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 1 September 2020, asks how research on the anti-Japanese base areas can move forward. Jin Yilin argues that the base areas deserve deeper study because of their strategic and political importance, and that progress now depends mainly on collecting and sharing historical documents, including those held privately.

The piece has two parts. The first recalls the Chinese Communist Party's role in the War of Resistance against Japan. The second turns to the state of the sources and to a concrete example of digitised archives.

In the first part, Jin contends that, unlike resistance groups in occupied Europe and Southeast Asia, which assisted Allied forces tactically, the Party-led forces opened a rear-area battlefield and raised guerrilla warfare to a strategic level. Jin cites Mao Zedong's 1938 writings to show that guerrilla war needs base areas as its rear. Jin adds that the base-area governments were prototypes of the central government of 1949. In the second part, Jin says existing studies tend towards conceptual generalisation at the macro level and fragmentation at the micro level, and holds that a convincing macro narrative can only rest on thorough detailed research. As a model, Jin describes how the Zhang Linchi and Chen Shunyu wartime manuscripts, over 1,600 pages from the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei border region, went online on a documents platform with family authorisation.

Jin calls for more institutions, scholars and private collectors to deposit scattered materials on a shared wartime-documents platform, in line with Xi Jinping's 2015 guidance on research priorities. The aim is "shared sources, jointly written history" and telling China's story to the world. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how Chinese historians frame the base areas and the case for digitising private archives.
quoteEn: Only by studying endless details thoroughly can one hope to generalise a convincing macro-level narrative.
quoteZh: 只有把无穷的细节研究透，才有可能高度概括出一个有说服力的宏观叙事。

t: Lessons of the fall of the Berlin Wall and the hope of world socialism: reading "The 30th Anniversary of the Fall of the Berlin Wall"
zh: 柏林墙倒塌的教训与世界社会主义的希望——读《柏林墙倒塌30周年记》
paras: Writing in 2020, on the 30th anniversary of German unification, Li Ruiqin reviews a collection edited by Egon Krenz, the last General Secretary of the East German ruling party (SED). Its Chinese title is rendered here as The 30th Anniversary of the Fall of the Berlin Wall: Reflections from the Former East German Side. More than ten former East German party, state and military leaders and a defence lawyer contributed to it. Li argues that the book draws lessons from the failure of East German socialism and regards China as the bearer of hope for world socialism.

The review presents the contributors' views under five headings: weak party leadership as the main cause of failure; the Western strategy of "peaceful evolution" aimed at East Germany; the double pressure of Gorbachev's reforms and Western strategy; the post-1990 treatment of East German leaders; and the contributors' view of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Li quotes figures such as Hans Modrow, Heinz Keßler, Heinz Hoffmann, Wolfgang Herger, Manfred Gerlach's contemporaries and Harry Tisch's colleagues only through the book's own wording, and also cites Mao Zedong.

Li reports that the contributors blame a leadership that grew silent and passive in 1989, neglected Party building, lost the trust of the people through bureaucracy, formalism and concealed errors, and ignored Marxist social science. Li presents their claim that the West ran a planned campaign, using media, "citizens' organisations" and Gene Sharp's handbooks. The contributors also say Gorbachev's reversal on German unification removed the Soviet support on which East Germany depended. Li adds that the former leaders describe unification as an annexation, with deindustrialisation, mass unemployment, prosecutions of generals and officials, and what Li calls a class reckoning.

In Li's account, the contributors, including Herger, Peck and the lawyer Friedrich Wolff, hold that the failure could have been avoided and was a setback, not the end of socialism. They see China's people-centred development, its public land ownership and its Party programme as a new strategy for socialism today. Li concludes that these reflections carry historical significance and a practical warning for upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics and for the revival of world socialism. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist reading of East German memoirs on 1989 and of how they portray China.
quoteEn: Separation from the masses is a fatal threat to a ruling party.
quoteZh: 脱离群众是执政党的致命威胁。

glossary.explanation: A term in Chinese Party discourse for the claim that Western powers seek to transform socialist states into capitalist ones by non-military means such as ideology, culture and media.
The official name for China's path of socialist construction since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, a socialist market economy and a Marxist ideological framework.

t: The international significance of China's War of Resistance against Japan and of research on it
zh: 中国抗日战争与抗战史研究的国际意义
paras: Marking the 75th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War (this commentary appeared in Guangming Daily in August 2020), Wang Chaoguang asks what the Chinese war effort meant beyond China. Wang argues that China fired the first shots of the anti-fascist war, set an example for weak countries resisting strong enemies, and was the main Eastern theatre of the global war.
The piece moves through three claims about China's wartime role and then turns to the state of scholarship. It ends with a call for broader, more international research on the war in the East.

Wang points to the Japanese invasion from 1931 and the full-scale war from 1937, and says that for over ten years China alone resisted Japan in the East. The article cites 1937 figures: industrial output under a quarter of Japan's, steel under one per cent, and aircraft one fifth. Wang credits protracted war and guerrilla warfare with wearing Japan down. China's resistance, in this account, tied down Japan's main forces. It kept Japan from attacking the Soviet Union in 1941 and limited its southward advance. China also fought in Burma and supplied air bases and logistics. Wang takes China's founding membership of the United Nations and its permanent Security Council seat as allied recognition of this contribution.

Wang says the Chinese theatre receives little attention internationally, sometimes with belittlement or misunderstanding, and that this should change. Wang proposes new topics, such as the war's influence on Asian independence movements against colonial rule, and says Chinese support for Korean, Vietnamese and Indian movements and the role of overseas Chinese show its Asian and global significance. Wang concludes that war-history research should serve national rejuvenation and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese scholars present the war's international meaning and the research agenda they propose.
quoteEn: The Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japan pitted the weak against the strong, and set a benchmark for invaded weak countries in the Second World War that rose up to resist and in the end triumphed.
quoteZh: 中国人民的抗日战争是以弱敌强，为二战中被侵略弱国奋起抵抗并最终以弱胜强树立了标杆。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2012–13. It stresses shared interests and joint development among countries.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'. Official English usually renders it as 'the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation'.

t: Studying the classics to advance Marxist theoretical education
zh: 研读经典著作 推进马克思主义理论教育
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in August 2020, Li Xiaoguang asks how Marxist theoretical education in China can be strengthened, and answers that the close study of the Marxist classics is the necessary route. Opening with Xi Jinping's call, in the third volume of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China, for Communists to make reading the classics a habit and a spiritual pursuit, Li argues that educators must first educate themselves before teaching others.

This is a short commentary organised around four benefits of studying the classics. It treats in turn the firming up of the people's stand in theoretical education, the complete and accurate grasp of Marxism's basic tenets, an understanding of the methods of Marxist education, and the raising of educators' overall competence. Li supports each point mainly with passages from Xi Jinping, Engels, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and the Communist Manifesto.

Li's central claim is that Marxism's basic principles are the systematised result of reading and distilling the classic texts, so they cannot be grasped fully without returning to the sources. As examples, Li traces historical materialism from The German Ideology through Marx's 1859 preface to Engels's Socialism: Utopian and Scientific, and places the theory of surplus value in Capital, the theory of the state in Engels and Lenin, and the view of practice in the Theses on Feuerbach. The classics also show how Lenin and Mao combined basic principles with national conditions, which Li treats as the core of the method of Marxist education, namely seeking truth from facts. Li adds that educators with higher theoretical competence can explain Marxism as an organic whole, resolve confusion about real problems and help people resist erroneous currents of thought.

Li concludes that only through deep, sustained, problem-oriented study of the classics can educators hold the right stand, grasp the tenets, absorb the methods and raise their competence, and so advance Marxist theoretical education. The piece is a statement of the official line on classics study rather than a scholarly analysis of the texts. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated academics in 2020 justified classics reading as the basis of ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The basic views and principles of Marxism are all further generalisations built on the interpretation of the classic works.
quoteZh: 马克思主义的基本观点和原理都是源自经典著作解读基础上的进一步概括。

glossary.explanation: The teaching of Marxist theory to Party members, officials and students, including ideological and political courses in schools and universities. It is treated in China as a means of upholding Marxism's leading position in ideology.

The principle, stressed in Party discourse, that the Party and its theory must start from and serve the interests of the people. Li presents it as the basic orientation of Marxism and of theoretical education.
A long-standing Party principle of starting from actual conditions rather than from doctrine, closely associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping.

t: Carrying forward the Yan'an Spirit to advance the great cause of the new era
zh: 弘扬延安精神 推进新时代伟大事业
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 5 August 2020, asks how the Yan'an Spirit can serve the advancement of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. Fan argues that the spirit, which nourished generations of Communists through revolution, construction and reform, will supply strong momentum for this cause.

The piece is organised around four elements of the Yan'an Spirit, each tied to a present-day task: firm political direction, emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts, serving the people, and self-reliance with hard struggle. Each section links the Yan'an experience to Xi Jinping's statements and to current conditions.

On political direction, Fan holds that the first requirement is guidance by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, together with the Two Upholds, and that political firmness depends on theoretical firmness. On seeking truth from facts, Fan calls for innovation in theory, practice, institutions and culture, while avoiding both impatient overreach and conservative complacency. On serving the people, Fan calls for development centred on the people, tackling unbalanced and inadequate development, and improving livelihoods.

Fan concludes that, because China remains in the primary stage of socialism and the world faces great changes, with unilateralism and protectionism aimed at China, self-reliance and hard struggle must continue. Fan stresses that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is closer than ever and that direction and effort must not slacken. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2020 tied the Yan'an Spirit to Party theory and current policy.
quoteEn: Without hard struggle grounded in reality, even the best goals and the best blueprints are only flowers in a mirror and the moon in the water.
quoteZh: 不立足实际艰苦奋斗，再好的目标，再好的蓝图，也只是镜中花、水中月。

glossary.explanation: The set of values attributed to the Communist Party's base at Yan'an (1935–1948), such as serving the people, self-reliance and seeking truth from facts. It is regularly invoked in Party education.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
The official assessment of China's present historical stage, used since the 1980s to explain why market mechanisms and mixed ownership coexist with socialism.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.

t: The rich connotations of the Yan'an Spirit
zh: 延安精神的丰富内涵
paras: Published in Guangming Daily in August 2020, this short commentary asks what the Yan'an Spirit consists of and why it still matters to the Communist Party of China. Dai opens with Xi Jinping's remark during his April 2020 Shaanxi inspection that the Yan'an Spirit has nurtured generations of Communists. The author argues that its core is a firm and correct political direction, an ideological line of emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts, the fundamental purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly, and a pioneering spirit of self-reliance and hard struggle.

The article is organised in three sections, each giving the Yan'an Spirit a different identity: a spiritual result of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, a distillation of the Chinese revolution's struggles, and an expression of the Party's essential character. Dai moves from the Yan'an period of the late 1930s to mid-1940s back to earlier setbacks, then forward to the present.

Dai's central argument is that the Yan'an Spirit grew out of the Party's integration of Marxism with Chinese revolutionary practice, which the author says was achieved only after the Party leadership reached Yan'an. In this account, the line of seeking truth from facts, the mass line, serving the people and self-reliance emerged together as Mao Zedong and others used Marxism as a microscope and telescope. The author is also drawn to the costs of earlier failures, citing Party membership falling from nearly 60,000 to 10,000 after the first revolution, and reports that during the Yan'an years the Central Committee made no further major errors. Its self-reliance, Dai says, was shown in the large-scale production campaign against the Nationalist blockade, and its service ideal in Mao's speech at Zhang Side's memorial. Dai concludes that the spirit follows from the Party's nature and original aspiration: seeking happiness for the people and rejuvenation for the nation.

Dai concludes that carrying forward the Yan'an Spirit means above all preserving this essential character. In the new era, the Party should keep a people-centred approach to governance, hold to the value of acting for the people's fundamental interests, and continue drawing strength from the spirit to win new victories for socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how the Yan'an Spirit is interpreted in Party historiography and ideological education.
quoteEn: The Yan'an Spirit is a product of the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context, and also an embodiment of it.
quoteZh: 延安精神是马克思主义中国化的产物，也是马克思主义中国化的体现。

glossary.explanation: The set of values and working style attributed to the Party leadership based in Yan'an (1935–1948), now treated as part of the Party's official spiritual lineage. It is usually summarised as political direction, seeking truth from facts, serving the people and self-reliance.
An ideological principle associated with Mao Zedong's Yan'an writings and later with Deng Xiaoping. It calls for starting from actual conditions rather than dogma.
The Party's declared fundamental purpose, drawn from Mao Zedong's 1944 speech 'Serve the People'.
The Party's method of leadership, in which it gathers the views of the people, concentrates them and then returns them as policy. It was formulated during the Yan'an period.

glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The official term for fitting Marxist theory to China's concrete conditions and history. Mao Zedong promoted it in the late 1930s.

t: Continuing the great struggle with many new historical features
zh: 继续进行具有许多新的历史特点的伟大斗争
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in August 2020, studies the discussion of the "great struggle" in the newly published third volume of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. Liu and Zhao take up the Party leadership's judgement that China is engaged in a great struggle with many new historical features. They argue that Party members must understand these features, grasp the basic requirements of the struggle and become cadres who both dare and know how to struggle.

The piece has three sections. The first identifies four new historical features of the struggle in the new era. The second sets out four basic requirements: the direction, the objects, the laws and the capabilities of struggle. The third turns to practical demands on individual Party members and cadres. Throughout, the authors rely on passages from Xi Jinping's volume.

On the new features, Liu and Zhao link each to a context and a quality the struggle must have. Accelerating global change, the Covid-19 pandemic and what they describe as provocations by individual Western countries call for foresight. The critical stage of national rejuvenation calls for initiative, and reform entering its "deep waters" calls for tenacity. Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, in their account, calls for a revolutionary character. On requirements, they state that the main direction is upholding Party leadership and the socialist system without wavering. They add that risks to these, to sovereignty and core interests, or to the goal of national rejuvenation must be met with resolute struggle. They also call for applying dialectical principles of contradiction, firm on principle but flexible in tactics, and for building capability through ideological training, political testing and practice.

For cadres, the authors call for a firm Party and people's standpoint, with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as guidance, and for the Two Upholds. They also urge deeper study, a sustained fighting spirit in the final months of the campaign to build a moderately prosperous society and poverty alleviation in 2020, and a stronger sense of responsibility. Leaders are asked to support those who take responsibility. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party press presented the "great struggle" doctrine in 2020 and the conduct it expects of cadres.
quoteEn: The struggle of Communists is not blind struggle, but the full exercise of human subjective initiative under the guidance of objective laws.
quoteZh: 共产党人的斗争不是盲目的斗争，而是在客观规律指导下人的主观能动性的高度发挥。

glossary.explanation: A phrase in Xi Jinping's discourse for the Party's confrontation with major risks and challenges on the way to national rejuvenation. It is used to call for vigilance and fighting spirit among Party members and cadres.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The requirement to resolutely uphold Xi Jinping's position as core of the Party Central Committee and the Party's whole leadership, and the authority of the Central Committee.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's drive for stricter discipline, anti-corruption work and internal management since 2012.
An official goal of broad, basic prosperity, whose full completion the Party set for 2020, the first of the "two centenary goals".

t: The generative logic of Lenin's theory of agricultural development
zh: 列宁农业发展理论的生成逻辑
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in July 2020, asks how Lenin's theory of agricultural development was built up as a system. Wu and Liu argue that it follows an internal logic running from the peasant movement through land distribution, the worker-peasant alliance and cooperative labour to modern agriculture. They present it as an innovation on the revolutionary theory of Marx and Engels.

The article treats the theory as five linked components, each tied to Lenin's writings and to Russian and Soviet practice from the early twentieth century. These include the 1905–1907 revolution, the land decrees after October, War Communism's surplus-grain requisition and the tax in kind that followed it, and electrification.

In the authors' account, the peasant movement is the starting point because it identifies which class forces can carry agricultural change, with confiscation of landlords' land as its core measure. Land distribution is the thread through the whole theory, resting on land nationalization. The worker-peasant alliance, which includes middle peasants who must be both helped and educated, supplies the organisational form. Cooperative labour and agricultural associations are said to carry institutional and communist values. Mechanization and electrification complete the sequence by turning small-peasant production into large-scale modern farming.

The authors conclude that Lenin offered a model of uniting theory and practice, applying the principle of seeking truth from facts and the mass line, and showing pioneering courage on hard agricultural problems. They hold that these methods remain relevant to China's socialist modernization and to agricultural development in the new era. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language outline of how Lenin's agrarian thought is presented in contemporary Chinese Party scholarship.
quoteEn: The system of Lenin's theory of agricultural development follows its own generative logic.
quoteZh: 列宁农业发展理论体系遵循着自身的生成逻辑。

glossary.explanation: A principle of basing policy on actual conditions rather than doctrine. It is associated with Mao Zedong and later Deng Xiaoping, and is a standard Party formulation.
A Party method of work, associated with Mao Zedong, that stresses drawing on the masses' views and returning policies to them.
A Marxist-Leninist concept of political alliance between the working class and the peasantry. It is treated as the basis of Soviet and Chinese socialist state power.

t: Lenin's great insights into revolutionary dialectics and their practical application
zh: 列宁关于革命辩证法的伟大创见及实践运用
paras: Marking the 150th anniversary of Lenin's birth, Sun Laibin asks how economically and culturally backward Russia came to take the socialist revolutionary road, a long-debated theoretical question. Sun argues that, before and after the October Revolution, Lenin used materialist dialectics to answer it and so creatively developed the 'revolutionary dialectics' of Marxism. The article presents this as Lenin's reply to Kautsky, Plekhanov and Sukhanov, who charged that the revolution was 'premature' or 'botched'.

This short commentary in the Guangming Daily is organised around three dialectical pairs that Sun draws from Lenin's writings: necessity and choice, the general and the particular, and advance and setbacks. Each section pairs Lenin's responses to his critics with quotations from Marx, Engels and Lenin. Sun also draws on later Chinese leaders, including Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

On necessity and choice, Sun reports that Kautsky likened the revolution to a premature birth. Lenin, in Sun's account, replied that critics recited formulas instead of studying living reality. Sun holds that the objective economic, class and international conditions, together with subjective readiness, were largely in place. Because people act consciously in history, the revolution was not artificially manufactured, yet it depended on the masses' initiative. On the general and the particular, Sun stresses Lenin's view that all nations will reach socialism but not in the same way, and that uniform schemas amount to a 'crude painting of Suzdal'. Lenin foresaw that revolutions in the East would show even more particularity, which Sun says Chinese revolutionary practice later confirmed. On advance and setbacks, Sun notes Lenin's view that starting the revolution was easier in Russia than completing it. Lenin held that history is no 'pavement of Nevsky Prospekt', and Sun cites his candid handling of the failure of war communism and the turn to indirect transition.

Sun concludes that socialism is a wholly new system built in a relatively backward country, so it must meet difficulties and zigzags. In Sun's reading, Lenin's greatness lay in persistent exploration and firm confidence. Sun cites Deng Xiaoping's comments after the collapse in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe, and Xi Jinping's statement that the road is winding but the future bright. Sun presents these as evidence that world socialism advances through setbacks, and that socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era is flourishing. Read the original if you want a concise, officially oriented Chinese account of how Lenin's dialectics is used to defend the October Revolution and to guide contemporary socialist practice.
quoteEn: This also vividly shows that historical development is an organic unity of necessity and choice, of objective laws and conscious initiative.
quoteZh: 这也生动表明，历史的发展是必然性与选择性、客观规律性与自觉能动性的有机统一。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path and system of socialism since the reform era. Party texts present it as Marxism adapted to China's conditions.
The term the article uses for the dialectical method applied to revolutionary strategy. It is attributed to Lenin's analysis of the conditions, paths and setbacks of socialist revolution.

The article's term for the path Lenin adopted after the failure of war communism. It leads to socialism through intermediate steps (associated with the New Economic Policy) rather than by direct measures.

t: The latest development of the Marxist view of ecology
zh: 马克思主义生态观的最新发展
paras: This short newspaper commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in June 2020, argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization is the latest development of the Marxist view of ecology. Xu holds that the thought has major theoretical and practical significance for developing Marxism, for socialism with Chinese characteristics, and for the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind.

The piece first states the significance of the thought, then lists seven ways in which it advances the Marxist view of ecology. It ends with a short assessment of results since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and a set of practical demands.

Xu's core claim is that the thought joins strict protection of the ecological environment with sound development, and does so in seven respects. It integrates the relevant ideas into a systematic body of thought within Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and it condenses them into a new concept of green development. It places them in the overall layout of Party and state work and grounds them in the principle of putting the people and their lives first. It presents the dialectical unity of protection and development more fully, moves the work onto institutional and legal tracks, and places it within the vision of a community with a shared future for mankind.

Xu concludes that the thought guides ecological civilization building in the new era and that the Party has achieved historic, turning-point and overall changes in this field since 2012. Xu calls for study and implementation of the thought, for turning it into concrete decisions, plans and measures, and for the spirit of the Foolish Old Man who removed the mountains, so that China contributes to building a beautiful world. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party commentary frames Xi's ecological thought as a stage in Marxist theory.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization is the latest development of the Marxist view of ecology.
quoteZh: 习近平生态文明思想是马克思主义生态观的最新发展。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization is presented as one component of it.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. Official texts use it to frame cooperation on issues such as the environment.
An official concept for a model of development that gives weight to environmental protection. It has been part of Party strategy since the 2000s and is prominent in Xi-era policy.
One of the five concepts of the new development philosophy announced in 2015. It stresses harmony between economic growth and the environment.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization
community with a shared future for mankind

t: Engels's philosophy of law and its contemporary value
zh: 恩格斯的法哲学思想及其当代价值
paras: Marking the 200th anniversary of Engels's birth, this piece from Guangming Daily (13 July 2020) asks what Engels contributed to the Marxist philosophy of law and why it matters now. Gong argues that Engels's legal thought is an organic part of Marxist legal philosophy and offers useful guidance for advancing law-based governance and the modernization of China's rule of law.

The article is organised in two parts. The first reconstructs Engels's legal philosophy under three headings: ontology, theory of value and theory of development, drawing on Ludwig Feuerbach and the End of Classical German Philosophy, Anti-Dühring, The Housing Question, The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State, and his late letters. The second part draws three lessons for contemporary China.

On ontology, Gong reports that Engels treats law as determined by material economic conditions, even though legal form hides its economic content. Engels also rejects mechanical determinism: state power and law react back on the economic base and interact with other elements of the superstructure. On value, Gong stresses Engels's view of freedom as insight into necessity and his critique of the Proudhonist idea of "eternal justice", which Engels saw as an idealised reflection of existing economic relations. On development, Gong summarises Engels's account of the origins of law and state in the growth of production and exchange. Gong adds his comparative reading of English and continental private law, and his claim that economic necessity ultimately asserts itself through contingency.

Gong draws three conclusions for the present. First, law-based governance must fit national conditions, so China should follow the path of the rule of law of socialism with Chinese characteristics and not copy foreign models. Second, the rule of law should be given a strategic role in modernizing the system and capacity of national governance. Third, it should embody a people-centred value orientation that meets growing popular demands for democracy, fairness and justice. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese Party-academic account of how Engels's texts are mobilised to support the official line on the rule of law in the 2020 "new era".
quoteEn: Different social and historical environments inevitably give rise to different state systems and paths of legal development.
quoteZh: 不同的社会历史环境必然形成不同的国家体制与法律发展道路。

glossary.literal: comprehensively governing the country according to law
glossary.explanation: A Party policy line, prominent since the Fourth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2014), that makes the rule of law a core part of national governance under Party leadership.

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义法治道路
glossary.en: the path of the rule of law of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The official name for China's model of legal development, which is presented as distinct from Western models and as rooted in national conditions and Party leadership.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernizing the system and capacity of national governance
glossary.explanation: A goal set out at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). It refers to improving state institutions and their effectiveness.

t: Engels and Marx's "turn to political economy"
zh: 恩格斯与马克思的“政治经济学转向”
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in the year of the 200th anniversary of Engels's birth, Liu Xiuping asks how Marx came to turn from law, literature and philosophy to political economy. The author argues that Engels played a key role in prompting this turn, which Liu treats as decisive for Marx's later critique of capital.

The commentary has three parts. It first traces Engels's early observations of capitalist society in Barmen, Bremen and Manchester, and the works he wrote between 1843 and 1845. It then turns to the "troubling doubts" Marx developed at the Rheinische Zeitung. Finally it compares Marx's Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 with Engels's writings.

Liu argues that Engels moved from humanitarian indignation at workers' conditions to seeing economic facts as the basis of class antagonism and political history. Marx's Rheinische Zeitung experiences, such as the debates on the wood-theft law, had left him asking how universal freedom is possible when private interests dominate the state. Reading Engels's Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy for the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher gave him the key to the economic relations of civil society. Liu then identifies three links with the Manuscripts: the aim of criticising political economy for taking private property as given, the use of Engels's material on English workers in the analysis of alienated labour, and a shared view of private property's historical role, which Marx treats as a path of negation of the negation toward communism.

Liu concludes that Engels's close attention to concrete social problems and empirical material helped Marx answer his early doubts. In Liu's view, it also prepared Marx to pursue the question of capital philosophically and theoretically. Read the original if you want a short account of Engels's influence on Marx's early economic studies, as presented in a Chinese Party-press commemoration.
