A term for literary and documentary works about the Chinese revolution that are treated as canonical and used in political education.

t: What the 70th anniversary of the founding of New China tells us
zh: 新中国成立70周年告诉我们什么
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2019, Yang Zhizhao asks what seven decades of New China teach. The short commentary answers that only under the leadership of the Communist Party of China, on the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, can the country grow strong, the nation be rejuvenated and the people become prosperous. Yang calls this an indisputable fact and an unshakeable truth.

The piece moves from a comparison of past and present living standards to four ways in which, in Yang's account, Party leadership has given people dignity as well as material comfort. It closes with a call for responsibility directed at all citizens and at Party members and cadres in particular.

Yang contrasts earlier worries about food and clothing with today's poverty reduction, 5G networks, widespread consumer goods and online services. The four gains are a rising international standing, linked to reform and opening up and the Belt and Road Initiative; stronger national capacity, shown in disaster relief such as the 1998 Yangtze floods and the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake; strong national defence; and sustained attention to cultural life, including promotion of core socialist values. Yang attributes the move from "standing up" to "becoming prosperous" to "becoming strong" to reform and opening up, the socialist path and the Party's original aspiration and mission.

Yang concludes that building socialism with Chinese characteristics is everyone's responsibility, and that Party members and cadres should follow the Party closely, carry on revolutionary traditions and work towards the Two Centenary Goals and the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Qiushi presented the 70th-anniversary narrative of Party leadership and popular gratitude.
quoteEn: Only under the leadership of the Communist Party of China, by taking the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, can the country grow strong, the nation be rejuvenated and the people become prosperous.
quoteZh: 只有在中国共产党的领导下，走中国特色社会主义道路，国家才能强盛，民族才能振兴，人民才能富裕。

glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's official name for its path of socialist development since reform and opening up, combining Marxism with China's conditions.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2013.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic (2049).
A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, meaning the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
A 24-character set of official values at national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since 2012.

t: The contemporary value of the May Fourth spirit
zh: 五四精神的当代价值
paras: Writing for Red Flag Manuscripts in 2019, the centenary year of the May Fourth Movement, Wang Jianmin asks what the May Fourth spirit means for China today and how it should be defended against reinterpretation. The article argues that the spirit's contemporary value lies in young people in the new era internalising and putting it into practice. It also holds that attempts to deny the Movement's significance amount to historical nihilism and must be corrected.

The piece is framed by Xi Jinping's April 2019 statements: his call at a Politburo study session for more research on the Movement, and his speech at the centenary meeting on 30 April. It has two parts. The first sets out the content of the May Fourth spirit and its present-day value. The second criticises historical nihilism on the question of the Movement and closes with practical remarks on how to pass the spirit on.

Wang defines the spirit as patriotism at its core, with opposition to feudal culture and acceptance of progressive ideas as its value pursuit, democracy, science and progress as its essence, and emancipating the mind and pursuing innovation as its soul. On this basis the article presents it as strengthening young people's patriotism, serving as a vehicle for cultivating and practising the Core Socialist Values, and driving the Chinese Dream. It is also described as a source for the Four-sphere Confidence and as nourishment for young Marxists. In the second part, Wang describes historical nihilism as presenting itself as academic reassessment while pursuing a political aim of discrediting revolution and the Communist Party. The article rejects claims that the Movement was a bourgeois revolution led by the national bourgeoisie or instigated by the Beiyang government. It cites Xi's characterisation of the Movement as a patriotic, anti-imperialist and anti-feudal revolutionary movement and calls for a historical-materialist method.

Wang concludes that the state, society and individuals should treat history scientifically, resist historical nihilism and keep developing the May Fourth spirit. Young people, in Wang's view, show patriotism by doing their own work well and becoming useful talents. Wang also names current shortcomings in transmitting the spirit: formalism, failure to keep pace with the times, weak clarification of misunderstandings and inadequate guidance. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the 2019 official narrative of May Fourth was presented and defended in Party-theory writing.
quoteEn: The contemporary value of the May Fourth spirit lies in the internalisation and practice of that spirit by the broad mass of young people in the new era.
quoteZh: 五四精神的当代价值在于新时代广大青年对五四精神的内化和践行。

glossary.explanation: The values associated with the 1919 May Fourth Movement, which official discourse summarises as patriotism, progress, democracy and science.

A label used in official Chinese discourse for interpretations seen as denigrating the Party's revolutionary history and its leaders. Authors using the term treat such interpretations as politically motivated.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values at the national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A slogan introduced by Xi Jinping in 2012, centred on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: The political drivers behind the "Chinese miracle"
zh: “中国奇迹”背后的政治动因
paras: Published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2019, this short commentary asks which theory can explain China's development achievements over seven decades. The author (the byline "Hong Wen" may be a pen name) argues that Western neoliberals, who expected economic liberalisation to bring political liberalisation and democratisation, have repeatedly misread China. In the article's account, the decisive explanation lies in politics: the leadership of the Communist Party and the political path of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The piece has three sections. The first, on political leadership rooted in national conditions, surveys the Party's revolutionary role and the policy turns since reform and opening up. The second discusses China's democratic practice, comparing it with Western electoral and multiparty systems. The third places the "Chinese miracle" in the context of what it calls great changes unseen in a century, and presents a "win-win" philosophy in foreign relations.

The author's central move is to treat Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee of achievement, citing the shift to economic construction, the restoration of the line of "emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts", the Party's basic line, the "three-step" strategy and the Five-Year Plans. The author then contends that no "universal" democracy exists, and that China's consultative democracy, the multiparty cooperation system under the Party, regional ethnic autonomy and "one country, two systems" suit Chinese conditions. Western universal suffrage, multiparty competition and the separation of powers are described as producing social division, polarisation and inefficiency. Finally, the article borrows the label "civilisational state" and says its essence is a "people-centred" orientation, which it links to peaceful development rather than zero-sum games.

The author concludes that the fundamental political driver of China's miracle is the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the political advantage expressed in the claim that Party leadership is its most essential feature. The author also holds that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is consistent with world peace and common development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a 2019 Party journal presented the political explanation for China's economic record and its contrast with Western democracy.
quoteEn: Party leadership is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the greatest strength of its system; the Party is the supreme political leadership force.
quoteZh: 党的领导是中国特色社会主义最本质的特征，也是中国特色社会主义制度最大的优势，党是最高政治领导力量。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, in use since the 1980s. It combines Party leadership and public ownership with a socialist market economy.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

An official term for the practice of consultation among the Party, other parties and social groups, for example through the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. Official sources present it as a distinctive form of Chinese democracy.
Deng Xiaoping's formula under which Hong Kong and Macao keep their own economic and legal systems within China. Official sources present it as a model for governing them.
An official principle that policy should serve the people's interests. It is prominent in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse.

glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in official discourse since around 2017 to describe a shifting global order, including the relative rise of emerging economies.

t: Why the Communist Party of China is able to create miracles
zh: 中国共产党为什么能够创造奇迹
paras: Why has the Communist Party of China repeatedly recovered from near-destruction? Wang Chuanli opens with a view he attributes to many foreign observers: that the Party grows stronger under setbacks and keeps producing seemingly incredible achievements. Wang's answer is that these outcomes follow from the Party's own distinctive strengths, which the article sets out as six advantages.

The article first lists episodes that Wang presents as miracles. They include survival after the Kuomintang massacre of 1927, the Long March after the five encirclement campaigns, and the Party's resilience after the collapse of the Soviet Union and Eastern European socialism. Wang adds that reform and opening up continued, and that the Party handled the 1997 Asian financial crisis, the 1998 floods, the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake and the global financial crisis. Wang then devotes a section to each advantage: its members, its theory, its relations with the masses, its organisational structure, and its traditions, style and discipline.

Wang argues that the Party's members are exceptionally able and selfless. Examples include figures of privileged origin who gave up wealth, and models such as Jiang Zhuying, Wang Jinxi, Jiao Yulu and Kong Fansen. Wang describes the Party as a learning party that treats Marxism as a guide to action rather than dogma, and credits its Party school system and repeated study campaigns, from Yan'an rectification to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The Party's ties to the people are likened to the giant Antaeus drawing strength from the earth. Wang cites Mao Zedong's line on the masses as the true bastion of iron and Deng Xiaoping's account of the early 1960s hardship years. Its organisation is said to reach every sector, to rest on the principles that the Party manages cadres and commands the gun, and to have mobilised 87 million members for special Party dues after the Wenchuan earthquake.

Wang concludes that the Party's capacity for criticism and self-criticism, its united front, its internal democratic centralism and its refusal to tolerate corruption explain its vitality. Wang cites the execution of Liu Qingshan and Zhang Zishan, and the present full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, as evidence that fighting corruption makes the Party stronger and more trusted. The article presents continuous self-reform as the way the Party stays vital. Read the original if you want an example of how a 2019 Party-journal piece explains the Party's record through its own qualities, in a popular and celebratory register.
quoteEn: The Party has not been weakened by the appearance of corruption; on the contrary, overcoming corruption has strengthened its immunity, making it purer, stronger and more trusted by the people.
quoteZh: 党没有因为出现腐败现象而变得软弱，反而因为克服腐败增强了免疫力，变得更加纯洁，更加坚强有力，更加赢得人民群众的信赖。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Xi Jinping era, since 2012, covering anti-corruption work, discipline enforcement and Party-building.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Party, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A Party practice of mutual and self-examination of faults, emphasised in the Yan'an rectification campaign and in Party life since.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, combining discussion with binding unity in implementation.
The Party's strategy of uniting the broadest range of social forces behind its central tasks; Mao called it one of the Party's "three magic weapons".

t: The adoption of the unitary form of state structure in new China and its great significance
zh: 新中国单一制国家结构形式的确定及其重大意义
paras: Why did the People's Republic choose a unitary rather than a federal state structure, and what does that choice mean? Sha Jiansun, in a piece first published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2019, argues that the choice came from a process of exploration and accumulated practical experience. In Sha's account, a unitary state combined with regional ethnic autonomy fits China's basic national conditions and the fundamental interests of all its peoples.

The article opens by defining state structure as one of the two main aspects of state form, alongside the form of government, and distinguishes unitary from federal systems. It then sets out the four basic institutions of new China: the state system, the people's congress system, the unitary multi-ethnic state with regional ethnic autonomy, and the multi-party cooperation system under Communist Party leadership. The historical narrative runs from the Party's Second National Congress (1922) to the 1949 Common Programme, the 1952 Outline for implementing regional ethnic autonomy, the 1954 Constitution and the current Constitution.

Sha notes that the Second Congress, lacking its own experience, followed the Soviet model and called for a Chinese federal republic. Experience then changed the Party's view: a 1947 directive on Inner Mongolia stated that the autonomous government was not independent. Sha reports Li Weihan's reasons to Mao Zedong in 1949: ethnic minorities were about 6 per cent of the population against 47 per cent in the Soviet Union, they lived in scattered and interspersed settlements, and China's peoples had united equally in revolution without ever separating. Zhou Enlai added that imperialist designs on Tibet, Xinjiang and Taiwan made it necessary to name the state a republic, not a federation, while still granting autonomy. Sha stresses that regional ethnic autonomy can exist in either system, and that China's operates within a unitary state.

Sha concludes that this structure secures national unity and ethnic solidarity and territorial integrity, and mobilises all peoples while allocating resources on a nationwide basis. It also guarantees ethnic equality and lets minorities manage their own affairs, which Sha calls one of the basic paths to developing people's democracy. Sha argues that upholding and developing it is part of maintaining confidence in the system. Read the original if you want a short, document-based official account of how the unitary state and ethnic regional autonomy were settled in 1949.
quoteEn: The reality shows that the Han cannot do without the minority peoples, the minority peoples cannot do without the Han, and the minority peoples cannot do without one another.
quoteZh: 现实的情况表明，汉族离不开少数民族，少数民族离不开汉族，各少数民族也相互离不开。

glossary.explanation: China's basic system for minority areas: autonomous organs are set up in areas where minorities live in concentration and exercise autonomy rights granted by the Constitution and law, under central leadership.
A state structure in which a single sovereign state is made up of ordinary administrative or autonomous regions, as opposed to a federation of political entities.
The class nature of state power, in Chinese constitutional theory; for China, the people's democratic dictatorship led by the working class and based on the worker-peasant alliance.
Part of the official 'confidence' formula (the Four-sphere Confidence), referring to confidence in China's socialist institutions.

glossary.zh: 中国人民政治协商会议共同纲领
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó Rénmín Zhèngzhì Xiéshāng Huìyì Gòngtóng Gānglǐng
glossary.literal: Common Programme of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference
glossary.explanation: The provisional constitutional document adopted in September 1949, which served as the basic law until the 1954 Constitution.

t: Marxism and the fate of the Communist Party of China are closely bound together
zh: 马克思主义与中国共产党命运紧紧相连
paras: Writing in Hongqi Wengao in 2019, as the Communist Party of China (CPC) approached its 98th year, Han Xiping asks why the Party rose from a few dozen members to the world's largest party and led the Chinese people from standing up, to growing prosperous, to growing strong. Han's answer is that the Party has consistently held Marxism as its guiding ideology, kept developing it, advanced the adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions, and pursued theoretical innovation on the basis of practice.

The piece is a historical survey in four steps. It covers the introduction of Marxism to China around the 1920s and the founding of the Party in 1921. It then treats the Party's wartime and revolutionary experience, including the proposal of the "Sinicization of Marxism" in 1938. Next it turns to the reform-era theoretical system, from Deng Xiaoping Theory to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It ends with practical tasks for studying that thought.

Han argues that Marxism, as a scientific theory, answered the needs of a China in which peasant, landlord and national-bourgeois efforts had failed, and that the October Revolution made its arrival possible. Han presents the Party's early setbacks, which the article attributes to dogmatism and mechanical copying of Soviet and Comintern experience, as proof that Marxist principles must be combined with Chinese reality. In Han's account, Mao Zedong's rural-based revolutionary path and the 1938 proposal produced Mao Zedong Thought. Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought are each presented as answers to a major question of their era, and as successive outcomes of the same method.

Han concludes that the Party's history is in essence a history of Marxism spreading in China and being combined with Chinese practice. Han describes Xi Jinping Thought as the latest result of this process and as "Marxism of contemporary China, Marxism of the twenty-first century". Han calls for arming the whole Party with it through study of the Outline for Study, reading it alongside earlier theoretical achievements, and wider outreach through lecture groups and media. Read the original if you want an example of the official Party narrative linking Marxism, the Party's history and the study of Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: Unity in thought is the basis for unity in action; once theory grips the masses, it becomes a powerful material force.
quoteZh: 思想上的统一是行动上一致的基础，理论一经掌握群众，就会变成强大的物质力量。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete conditions and culture. Mao Zedong put forward the formulation in 1938.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sixiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology written into the Party constitution in 2017. The Party presents it as the latest theoretical achievement in adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for China's path and system since reform and opening up, associated with Deng Xiaoping's formulation from around 1982.
The guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, adopted in the early 2000s. It stresses people-centred, coordinated and sustainable development.
Jiang Zemin's theory, put forward around 2000. It holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.

t: Trump, the Republican Party and Westmoreland County
zh: 特朗普、共和党和威斯特摩兰县
paras: This is a Chinese translation of an article by the US author Margaret Power (the name is given in Chinese as 玛格丽特·鲍尔). It asks why Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania, moved from a Democratic stronghold to a Republican one. Trump took 63.5% of its vote in 2016. The author, who grew up in the county, argues that the shift reflects economic restructuring, the decline of unions and generational change. Above all, in the author's view, it reflects white supremacist ideas and conservative social values.

The article opens with a visit to a Trump merchandise shop and an account of the county's 2016 result. It then reviews the county's history from the coal-and-coke boom of the 1880s–1920s, through the Ku Klux Klan and the New Deal, to the factory closures of the 1980s. It turns to the rise of local Republicans, the Mellon-funded media and the Tea Party, then to the 2016 campaign and the March 2018 special election in Pennsylvania's 18th district. Power draws on interviews with local Republican officials and activists.

Power describes a county that is 95.3% white (2010 census) and was held by the Democrats from 1932 until 2000 largely through union loyalty. When mills closed, she argues, workers lost the shared identity and 'emotional community' that unions gave them. Non-union jobs and large Protestant churches filled the gap. Her interviews show children of union Democrats accepting Reagan-era stories about welfare recipients and presenting themselves as the 'deserving poor'. They also show a fear of 'others' (Black people, non-white immigrants, Muslims) that she says joins economic anxiety with status anxiety. She reports that Trump's women supporters set aside his treatment of women in favour of border security, a strong military and 'making America great again'.

Power concludes that Trump's election and policies rest on real economic, social and political foundations at home. She holds that white supremacy and conservative values were decisive, though economic change contributed. She admits she does not know whether such voters can change. She says she changed after being pushed to learn about other people's lives, and she calls for building awareness of other racial, gender and national groups, so that they are seen as a 'resource' and not a threat. Read the original if you want a detailed local case study, based on interviews, of how deindustrialisation and racial attitudes fed Republican support in a white working-class area of the US.
quoteEn: But in the end, I think the most important factor is white supremacist thinking and conservative social values, which many people here regard as inherently American values and are willing to fight to preserve or restore.
quoteZh: 但是说到底，我认为，最重要的因素是白人至上思想和保守的社会价值观，这里的很多人把这种价值观视为美国人与生俱来的价值观，他们愿意为维护或恢复这种价值观而斗争。

t: The fundamental guide to a new era of socialist ecological civilization: studying Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization
zh: 走向社会主义生态文明新时代的根本指针——深入学习习近平生态文明思想
paras: Yang Huang presents Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization, systematically summarised at the National Conference on Ecological and Environmental Protection in May 2018, as the fundamental guiding principle for China's green development and the building of a "Beautiful China". The article argues that the thought is rooted in China's realities, draws on traditional Chinese ecological wisdom and the experience of other countries, and uncovers general laws governing the development of ecological civilization. It also treats the thought as an integral part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article has four parts. The first places the thought in intellectual and practical context: Chinese tradition, Marxist ecological views, the rise and fall of past civilizations, and China's current environmental problems. The second sets out its core content in six principles. The third identifies its distinguishing features. The fourth describes its strategic framework and practical levers, including the five systems of ecological civilization, green development and the campaign against pollution.

Yang's central claim is that the thought develops Marxism's view of nature. It continues Engels's warning about nature's retaliation and extends Marx's theory of productive forces through the formulas "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets" and "protecting the ecology is protecting productive forces". Yang adds that only socialism, with its capacity to concentrate resources, can truly resolve the contradiction between humanity and nature. The article ties the thought to the changed principal contradiction of the new era, in which demand for a beautiful environment has become part of people's aspirations for a better life. It says the six principles, from harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature to jointly building global ecological civilization, show a historical outlook, a people-centred stance and scientific methods such as bottom-line and systems thinking.

Yang concludes that building ecological civilization requires a cultural system, an ecological economy, accountability for officials judged by more than GDP growth, strict institutions and rule of law, and an ecological security system. The article adds that development remains essential, but must take a green form and be unified with environmental protection. It calls for winning the battles for clean air, water and soil, and for improving rural living environments. Read the original if you want a clear exposition of the official 2018–19 framing of Xi's ecological thought and of how it is tied to Marxist theory and Chinese tradition.
quoteEn: Only socialism can truly resolve the contradiction between humanity and nature and achieve harmony between them.
quoteZh: 只有社会主义才能真正解决人与自然的矛盾，实现人与自然的和谐。

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of ideas on environment and development summarised at the National Conference on Ecological and Environmental Protection in May 2018. It is presented officially as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: green waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2005. It holds that a good environment is itself economic wealth, so that protecting it and developing the economy are not opposed.

A Chinese Party-state concept for a model of development that harmonises human society with the natural environment. It has been part of official strategy since the early 2000s and was added to the Party's overall plan at the 18th Party Congress (2012).

The Party's formula for the main problem facing society. The 19th Party Congress (2017) redefined it as the contradiction between people's growing needs for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization

t: Cuba's 60 years of building a cultural power: experience and lessons
zh: 古巴60年来创建文化强国的经验及启示
paras: Marking the 60th anniversary of the Cuban Revolution in January 2019, Mao Xianglin asks why a small, economically underdeveloped socialist country of 11.22 million people has survived decades of US pressure. The article argues that one important reason is Cuba's effort to build itself into a cultural power (wenhua qiangguo). It holds that Cuba, before 1959 marked by a colonial culture, has since become what the author calls a recognised power in education, medicine, sport and culture, and describes this as a miracle.

The article draws four lessons from Cuban experience. They are a balanced policy towards intellectuals that combines leniency and strictness; making the quality of people's cultural life a goal of the revolution, so that the people move from practising culture to creating it; the need for struggle in building socialist culture; and faithful inheritance of Cuba's revolutionary cultural tradition in order to foster cultural confidence. Mao draws on Fidel Castro's 1961 speech to intellectuals, the 1975 Party programme, the 1976 constitution, and Cuban statistics on literacy, libraries, publishing and broadcasting.

On intellectuals, Mao presents Castro's formula "within the revolution, everything; against the revolution, nothing" as a guiding principle written into Party and state policy, and says Cuba has kept a relaxed social atmosphere despite strict politics. The author concedes a leftist deviation in the late 1960s and early 1970s, the "grey five years". Mao defends the handling of the Heberto Padilla case and the 2003 arrest of 75 dissidents, arguing that both rested on espionage or national-security charges, not on dissent, and disputes Western media figures on political prisoners. On struggle, the article describes four ideological campaigns: the 1980s rectification process, the mid-1990s campaign, the return of the boy Elián González in 2000, and the 2002 constitutional amendment declaring socialism irrevocable after dissidents' petition.

On tradition, Mao points to Cuba's retention of its national name, flag and anthem, and to the inclusion of José Martí's and, in the 2019 constitution, Fidel's thought among guiding ideas. The article also notes the spread of Cuban literacy campaigns to left-led Latin American governments and its teachers and doctors abroad. It concludes that these achievements stem from the Party and state's high priority on socialist culture. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's favourable account of Cuban cultural policy, including its treatment of intellectuals and dissidents, and the lessons drawn for socialist cultural construction.
quoteEn: Cuba is nevertheless a country universally recognised as a power in education, medicine, sport and culture.
quoteZh: 古巴却是一个被世人所公认的教育强国、医疗强国、体育强国和文化强国。

glossary.explanation: A term in Chinese political discourse for a country with strong cultural production, education and influence. Here the author applies it to Cuba.

glossary.literal: leniency and strictness complementing each other
glossary.explanation: A policy approach that pairs tolerance with firm limits. The author uses it to characterise Cuba's policy towards intellectuals.
Confidence in a nation's own cultural tradition and socialist culture, a theme prominent in Chinese official discourse. The author applies it to Cuba.

t: The US trade war in the eyes of foreign scholars: "Make America Great Again" or deeper crisis?
zh: 外国学者眼中的美国贸易战——“让美国再次伟大”还是深陷危机？
paras: Writing in World Socialism Studies (2019, no. 4), Gan Haixia reviews how foreign scholars, mostly critical or Marxist, have interpreted the trade wars Donald Trump launched against US allies and China under the slogan "Make America Great Again". The article asks what kind of war this is, why the United States started it, what it is likely to produce, and where capitalism is heading. It reports the scholars' view that the war will leave the US deeper in crisis rather than "great again", and that neoliberalism is nearing its end. Gan then judges the scholarship scientific and critical but lacking totality, thoroughness and constructiveness.

The article has four parts. It first discusses the nature of the trade war, then what lies behind it, then the predicted outcome and the future of capitalism, and ends with Gan's own assessment. It draws on figures such as Chad Bown and Douglas Irwin, Leo Panitch and Sam Gindin, Michael Roberts, Martin Wolf, Nicole Aschoff, Joseph Choonara, Nancy Fraser, John Bellamy Foster, Richard Baldwin, Edward Luce, Alex Callinicos and David Kotz.

In the account Gan reports, the trade war is first a replay of old protectionist thinking, comparable to the Smoot-Hawley tariffs and to the Reagan-era response to Japan's rise. Roberts ties free trade or protectionism to the profitability of capital. It is also a "circus performance" that distracts from the real causes. Behind it, the scholars see a "Long Depression" (Roberts's term) that has never really ended, a political crisis of which Trump is a symptom rather than a cure, and an effort to restore imperial hegemony. Foster, for one, describes this effort as neo-fascist. The scholars predict that tariffs will not revive industry or jobs, will endanger the dollar's dominance, and will isolate the US. They conclude that Trump's election and similar revolts signal the collapse of neoliberal hegemony, though they cannot say when it will end.

Gan credits the scholars with scientific method: they compare historical cases, look beyond appearances and dare to forecast. Gan faults them on three counts. Their analysis does not grasp the whole organism of US capitalism. It stops short of tracing the trade war to the contradiction between private appropriation and socialised production, and to the competition between capitalist and socialist systems and between neoliberalism and Marxism. And it offers no constructive solution, only abstract calls for progressive forces to act. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist academic's survey of Western left interpretations of the Trump trade war, together with the official-leaning critique of their limits.
quoteEn: They failed to hold consistently to Marx's method of critiquing capitalism, and so failed to grasp the inevitability of the US launching a trade war.
quoteZh: 他们没能始终坚持马克思的资本主义批判方法，从而未能抓住美国挑起贸易战的必然性

glossary.explanation: Michael Roberts's term for the prolonged period of weak growth after the 2008 financial crisis, which the article's scholars say has not ended.
The market-oriented policy and ideological regime of deregulation, financialisation and globalisation that the article's scholars see as losing its political legitimacy.
A Marxist criterion of analysis that treats an event as part of an organic whole, not as a sum of separate aspects. Gan uses it to judge the foreign scholars' work.

t: Upholding the dialectical materialist worldview and remoulding one's worldview
zh: 坚持辩证唯物主义世界观与改造世界观
paras: Writing in World Socialism Studies (2019), Hou Huiqin argues that the worldview with which the Party arms itself is the touchstone separating genuine from false Marxism, and that dialectical materialism must be upheld unwaveringly. The article contends that a current of anti-materialist thought, which stigmatises materialist philosophy, now threatens this position, including inside the world socialist movement.

The article has four parts. It first places today's struggle over worldview in the context of Lenin's fight against empirio-criticism and the 'return to Kant' in early twentieth-century Russia. It then turns to Chinese intellectuals and the task of building a philosophy and social science with Chinese characteristics. The third part analyses the 'practice turn' in Marxist philosophy, and the last draws on Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping for ways to transform intellectuals' worldviews.

Hou's central claim is that the Western 'existential turn', which claims to transcend epistemology, separates practice from the theory of knowledge, denies material ontology and dissolves the basic question of philosophy, thereby restoring idealism's dominance. Hou says that the Chinese call for a 'practice turn' or 'practice ontology' in Marxism repeats this move. In Hou's account, practice is not itself the ground of the world. It has a materialist meaning only when it is explained through materialism, as Lenin held against Mach. Marx, on this reading, reached his theory of practice after a materialist turn and shared Feuerbach's view that nature sets the limits of human reason. Hou therefore treats the dialectics of nature as the foundation, and says that attacks on it since the 1980s prepared the ground for practice ontology. Hou also holds that liberal individualism among intellectuals, including some Party members, obstructs political identification with socialism with Chinese characteristics.

Hou calls for deeper criticism of idealism, renewed study of Marxist materialism and of the dialectics of nature, and conscious remoulding of worldviews. Following Mao, Hou says that no ideological vacuum exists, that a climate for studying Marxism must be created against 'de-ideologisation', and that intellectuals must stay close to the people and to production. Read the original if you want a detailed example of the argument within Chinese Marxist philosophy that defends materialist ontology against the 'practice turn' and ties it to Party ideological work.
quoteEn: One cannot use practice to explain materialism; one must use materialism to explain practice.
quoteZh: 不能用实践说明唯物论，而必须用唯物论去说明实践。

glossary.explanation: The view, associated with the 'practical materialism' current in Chinese Marxist philosophy, that practice rather than matter is the basic ground of Marxist philosophy. Hou rejects it as a route to idealism.
The term Hou uses for a shift in modern Western philosophy away from epistemology towards existence and lived practice. Hou reads it as a turn to subjective idealism.
A concept from Mao Zedong's writings on intellectuals, meaning their conscious change of outlook through study of Marxism and contact with the masses.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path, theory and system since the reform era.

t: The thought of a community with a shared future for mankind as inheritance and development of the theory of the "Three Worlds"
zh: 人类命运共同体思想是对“三个世界划分”理论的继承和发展
paras: Liu Runwei asks how the thought of a community with a shared future for mankind, which the article treats as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, relates to Mao Zedong's earlier theory dividing the world into three. Liu's thesis is that the community idea is the theory's logical inheritance and development, and its "theoretical form" in the new era.

The short piece has three parts. It first sets out four layers of meaning in the community idea. It then compares the idea with the three-worlds theory and sketches the historical eras behind each. Finally it urges that the idea be put into practice.

Liu reads the community's goal as the same ideal as communism, put in different words. Liu also names hegemonism as the most fundamental real threat to it. The article summarises the three-worlds theory as a judgement of the world pattern, a statement of China's place as a socialist developing country that will never seek hegemony, and a set of foreign-policy principles including the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence. Liu argues that the community idea shares each element. On Liu's account, the earlier theory suited an era of US–Soviet rivalry and capitalist temporary ascendancy. After the Soviet and East European upheavals, Liu sees an era of declining imperialism and reviving world socialism. In it, US power is isolated and world power is dispersing, which Liu calls changes unseen in a century. Liu says this makes the community idea timely and helps build a wider anti-hegemonist united front, especially with the "second world" of developed countries.

Liu concludes that the idea must be carried out unwaveringly. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Liu says, the leadership has put diplomatic emphasis on the third world, citing the Belt and Road Initiative and the China–Africa and China–Arab forums. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese scholar ties current diplomatic doctrine to Maoist-era theory.
quoteEn: The thought of a community with a shared future for mankind is a logical development of the "three worlds" theory under the conditions of the new era.
quoteZh: 人类命运共同体思想是在新时代条件下对“三个世界划分”理论合乎逻辑的发展。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping has promoted since about 2013 as a vision for international relations based on shared development, security and opposition to hegemony.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name of the Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
A China-led programme launched in 2013 for infrastructure and economic cooperation across Asia, Africa and Europe.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Building a community with a shared future for mankind: a banner leading the world in meeting present challenges and moving towards the future
zh: 构建人类命运共同体：引领世界应对当前、走向未来的旗帜
paras: Writing five years after Xi Jinping first put forward the initiative, Zheng Keyang asks why the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind has won such wide support, and what answer it gives to what the author calls the global question of the age. Zheng presents the concept as a union of theoretical and practical innovation. In Zheng's account, it ties the development of socialism with Chinese characteristics to China's work with other peoples on global challenges.

The piece begins with the international setting: a new round of technological and industrial change, shifts in the balance of power, and what Zheng describes as hegemonism, power politics, protectionism and unilateralism led by the United States. It then traces the concept from Xi's 2013 speech in Moscow into a system of goals, principles and pathways, and cites the Belt and Road Initiative, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, BRICS and UN resolutions as evidence of growing recognition. Zheng also answers critics, rejecting charges that the Belt and Road amounts to a 'Chinese invasion' or a 'debt trap'.

Zheng's core argument gives four reasons for the concept's appeal, drawn from Xi's diplomatic thought. First, China is a socialist country led by the Communist Party, and the reform-era achievements are described as the work of adapting socialism to Chinese conditions, so the concept extends domestic policy outward. Second, Chinese culture values harmony, and China's modern experience of aggression is said to make it oppose bullying, so that a strong China will not repeat the Western pattern of the powerful seeking hegemony. Third, the Party's people-centred stance is held to apply to foreign policy, making the Chinese Dream compatible with other nations' dreams. Fourth, Zheng argues, China keeps its word in international agreements, a trust that Belt and Road cooperation is said to deepen.

Zheng concludes that the project is an unprecedented, long-term undertaking that will meet uncertainties and risks and will need generations of common effort. Developed countries are urged to take on more responsibility, and developing countries to do what they can. Zheng states that China will contribute to reforming global governance and remain a builder of world peace, a contributor to global development and a defender of the international order. Read the original if you want an example of how the community with a shared future for mankind was explained in Chinese Party-theoretical writing in 2019, including its rebuttals of Western criticism.
quoteEn: China's advocacy and vigorous promotion of building a community with a shared future for mankind is precisely a concentrated expression of the national essence of socialist China.
quoteZh: 中国倡导并力推构建人类命运共同体，正是社会主义中国国家本质的集中体现

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept that Xi Jinping first used in 2013. It calls for cooperation, shared security and common development among states, and it has since been written into Party documents and UN texts.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up. It combines Party leadership and public ownership with market mechanisms.
A slogan promoted by Xi Jinping from 2012, meaning national rejuvenation and the well-being of the people.

t: The valuable experience of the Comintern
zh: 共产国际的宝贵经验
paras: This text is a Chinese translation of an article by the Russian communist leader Gennady Zyuganov, written for the centenary of the Communist International (Comintern) in 2019. It asks what the Comintern's 24 years left to the communist movement today. Zyuganov argues that it joined Marxism-Leninism to the workers' movement worldwide, helped found proletarian parties, strengthened international working-class solidarity and mobilised people against imperialism and fascism. He also credits it with raising colonial national liberation movements to a new level.

The article is a chronological survey. It begins with the Communist League (1847), the First International (1864–1876) and the Second International (1889), which Zyuganov says collapsed into opportunism and social chauvinism in 1914. It then follows the Bolsheviks' road to a new International through the Zimmerwald and Kienthal conferences, and walks through the Comintern's congresses from 1919 to the Seventh in 1935. It ends with the dissolution in 1943 and later forms of party cooperation.

Zyuganov's central claim is that Lenin's line steered the Comintern through changing conditions. He reports the Second Congress's twenty-one conditions of admission and its resolution linking proletarian and colonial struggles. He cites the shift after 1921 from offensive slogans to winning a majority of workers and building a united workers' front. He also describes the Seventh Congress's definition of fascism and its People's Front policy, which in his account shaped anti-fascist movements in France, Spain and China. He presents the Comintern's dissolution as justified by the parties' maturity and the wartime need for independent tactics, and treats Trotskyism as a counter-revolutionary current the Comintern exposed.

Zyuganov says the Comintern laid the groundwork for later communist victories and the world socialist system. He blames later damage on bureaucratisation, dogmatism, the Sino-Soviet split, Eurocommunism and the Soviet collapse. He points to China, Vietnam, Laos, Cuba, North Korea and Latin America's left governments as evidence that socialism endures. Because global capital has dropped the masks of "democracy" and "human rights", he calls for closer ties among communist parties, a task he says only parties firmly committed to socialism can carry out. Read the original if you want a Russian communist leader's own account of the Comintern and of how it bears on today's international communist coordination.
quoteEn: Today we urgently need stronger ties among communist forces.
quoteZh: 我们今天迫切需要共产主义力量之间加强联系。

t: Carrying forward the "May Fourth spirit" and the direction of the youth movement: striving to realise the "original aspiration" and fulfil the "mission"
zh: 发扬“五·四精神”，坚持青年运动方向，为实现“初心”、完成“使命”而奋斗
paras: Writing for the centenary of the May Fourth Movement in 2019, Ge Yuanren asks whether the path of integrating young intellectuals with workers and peasants, which Mao Zedong set out in 1939 as the "direction of the youth movement", still matters today. The article answers that it does. In the author's view, the path was needed in wartime and remains needed in peacetime, and it must continue until the Party's "original aspiration" and "mission" are finally achieved. Ge adds that the question bears on the ideological security of the socialist state and the political security of the Communist Party's governing position.

The article has three parts. The first presents the May Fourth Movement as an anti-imperialist, anti-feudal patriotic movement led by young intellectuals with workers and peasants as its main force, and treats the founding of the Communist Party as one of its main results. The second part defends the rural "sent-down youth" (zhiqing) movement of the first three decades of the People's Republic, citing the 1955 cooperative-movement episodes and Mao's remark that the countryside is a "vast world". The third part argues for the path's present relevance and cites Xi Jinping's speeches and the careers of several academicians who were once sent-down youth.

Ge's central claim is that the dispute over this path is a struggle between proletarian ideas of hardship and service to the people and feudal and bourgeois ideas such as "those who excel in study become officials" and contempt for manual labour. Ge says that these older ideas survive among students and that many young people have been taught to put themselves first and money above all. Ge holds that reform-era achievements have not abolished the "three major differences" (between town and country, worker and peasant, mental and manual labour), so intellectuals still need to work among workers and peasants to find problems and develop a proletarian worldview. As evidence, the article presents sent-down youth who became academicians, including Jiang Yi, Cui Xiangqun, Ding Jian, Fu Xianzhi and Zhai Mingguo. Ge says their experience gave them a sense of duty and the endurance to resist money and fame.

Ge concludes that the path "cannot be abandoned or changed" and must be kept up from generation to generation. The author reads Xi Jinping's remarks on hardship, on rural revitalization and on urban-rural integrated development as supporting this view. The article also objects to treating the sent-down youth experience as something to demonise. Read the original if you want to see how a Marxist writer in 2019 defended the sent-down youth movement and tied it to the Party's founding aims and to current youth and rural policy.
quoteEn: The path of young intellectuals integrating with workers and peasants cannot be abandoned or changed; it must be upheld until our "original aspiration" is realised and our "mission" is fulfilled.
quoteZh: 知识青年走和工农相结合的道路不能丢、不能改，必须坚持，直到我们的“初心”实现、“使命”完成。

glossary.explanation: A Party slogan referring to the founding ideals of the Communist Party, usually paired with "mission". It was widely promoted from 2017 in the campaign "Remain true to our original aspiration and keep our mission firmly in mind".
The historical task the Party sets itself, here defined by the author as reaching socialism and then communism.

glossary.literal: educated youth going up to the mountains and down to the villages
glossary.explanation: The movement, strongest from the 1950s to the 1970s, in which urban educated young people were sent to the countryside and border regions. Its assessment is still disputed in China.
The differences between town and country, workers and peasants, and mental and manual labour. Marxist tradition expects socialism to abolish them.
A national strategy announced at the 19th Party Congress (2017) to develop the countryside and narrow the gap between town and country.

t: Why the competitiveness of the CPI(M) in Kerala has kept growing since the turn of the century
zh: 新世纪以来印共（马）在喀拉拉邦竞争力持续增强的原因
paras: Zhang Shuhuan and Xie Jiabao ask why the Communist Party of India (Marxist), CPI(M), has grown steadily stronger in electoral competition in the Indian state of Kerala in the twenty-first century. They note that the party lost power in West Bengal and Tripura but remains in office in Kerala. They argue that this is the result of several factors acting together. Broad representation of the people's interests is the fundamental cause, a correct election strategy the direct cause, and sound party building the main cause.

The article, published in 2019, first documents the party's rising strength. It covers three state assembly elections won as largest party (2006, 2011, 2016), three panchayat (rural self-government) rounds and three urban local-body rounds, and it notes that the Bharatiya Janata Party remains marginal. It then devotes one section to each of the three causes. The authors present the party as the strongest communist party in a capitalist country and treat Kerala as a lesson for such parties.

On the fundamental cause, the authors describe land reform, the People's Planning Campaign, food distribution, pensions, employment schemes and benefits for scheduled castes and tribes as measures for the vulnerable, who they say make up over 80 per cent of the population. They add an economic-growth-first strategy, citing GDP rising from 31 to 125 billion US dollars between 2005/2006 and 2018/2019. They also describe the party's handling of land seizures, privatisation and Tuluva ethnic militancy. On strategy, they stress alliances with ideologically close parties in the Left Democratic Front, which they contrast with the loose United Democratic Front. They add tailored manifestos and candidates, courting independents, support for several religious communities, small-donor fundraising and the use of constituency delimitation. On party building, they cite membership growth from 293,141 to 463,472 (2000–2018) and training and expulsions for indiscipline. They also cite the resolution of the Achuthanandan–Vijayan factional split, the four-tier organisation, and mass organisations and the daily Deshabhimani.

The authors conclude that Kerala offers lessons for the international communist movement. Communist parties must genuinely represent the people, keep strengthening themselves, and adapt their electoral tactics to changing conditions. In this way, they say, Marxism can show new vitality in the twenty-first century. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly account of a communist party that governs at state level in a capitalist country, with detailed election and membership data.
quoteEn: The CPI(M)'s steadily growing competitiveness in Kerala is the result of several factors acting together: broad representation of the people's interests is the fundamental cause, masterful election strategy the direct cause, and good party building the main cause.
quoteZh: 印共（马）在喀拉拉邦竞争力持续增强是多种因素综合作用的结果，其中广泛代表民众利益是根本原因，高超的竞选策略是直接原因，良好的自身建设是主要原因。

t: China is undergoing rapid and profound change
st: A Chinese compilation of John Bachtell's series on socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era
zh: 中国正在经历快速而深远的变革
orig: Series of articles on the CPUSA website, 2018
paras: This text is a Chinese-language compilation (编译) of a series of articles by John Bachtell, then chairman of the Communist Party USA, written after a visit to China at the invitation of the Communist Party of China (CPC) from 26 May to 3 June 2018. Visiting Beijing, Hefei and Shenzhen, Bachtell concludes that China is going through rapid and profound change. In his view this will have a major effect on China's 1.4 billion people, the global economy, international relations and the future of socialism. The editors present his assessment as evidence that socialism with Chinese characteristics is recognised by communists in the most developed capitalist country.

The compilation is organised under five headings drawn from six articles: the achievements of reform and opening up; ecological civilization as a national strategy; China's global diplomacy; the role of trade unions in governance; and the CPC as a strong, united and open party. Each section combines figures, interviews and impressions from the trip with Bachtell's own commentary and comparisons to the United States.

On the economy, Bachtell describes the shift from egalitarian collective farming to a socialist market economy. He cites poverty reduction, rising wages, the "Made in China 2025" plan, and a public sector that he says accounts for about 60 per cent of fixed investment. He also lists costs: unequal development, a growing capitalist stratum and billionaires, sharper class contradictions and environmental damage. He portrays the turn to ecological civilization, the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind as responses to climate crisis and globalization, set against Trump-era protectionism, which he calls doomed to fail. He presents the All-China Federation of Trade Unions, with 308 million members, as a partner in planning and an institutional pillar of the political system, and he defends its CPC ties against foreign criticism.

Bachtell sees the CPC as a pragmatic party that adapts Marxism to Chinese conditions, practises self-criticism and self-reform, fights corruption and refuses to impose its model on others. He notes that it faces many problems and errors. The text ends with his view that the scale of China's development will shape the world whatever the Party intends. Read the original if you want to see how a leading US communist, in a text republished in China, assessed Chinese development and how Chinese editors framed that endorsement.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China is blazing a path across unknown territory.
quoteZh: 中国共产党正在开辟一条穿越未知土地的道路。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Chinese official discourse that places environmental protection alongside economic, political, cultural and social development. The 18th Party Congress (2012) wrote it into the Party constitution as part of the overall plan.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept put forward by Xi Jinping from 2013. It calls for multilateralism, mutual respect among states and shared development.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to finance and build infrastructure and trade links across Asia, Africa and Europe.
The official name for China's post-1978 economic system, which combines market mechanisms with a leading public sector and Party leadership.
The policy launched under Deng Xiaoping in 1978 that introduced market reforms and opened China to the global economy.

t: Lessons of the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics for developing countries' roads to modernization
zh: 中国特色社会主义道路对发展中国家现代化道路的启示
paras: Writing in 2019, Xu Shicheng asks what the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics can offer developing countries seeking modernization. The article argues that China's development since reform and opening up shows the vitality of socialism, supplies successful experience for developing countries and is a major contribution by the Chinese nation to human civilisation. Xu presents China's road as able to surpass the Western road to modernization.

The piece opens with definitions of modernization drawn from two Peking University scholars, Luo Rongqu and Qian Chengdan, and traces China's own goals from the Four Modernizations of the 1960s and 1970s through the three-step strategy to the Two Centenary Goals and the two-stage plan set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017). It then lists the typical problems of developing countries, such as single-commodity economies, weak innovation, corruption, inequality and poverty, financial crises and flawed policy. It cites figures on China's growth, poverty reduction and trade, then sets out ten lessons.

In Xu's account, the lessons are: treat development as the first task of governing; adopt a strategy and model suited to national conditions and keep growth fast; build a fairly complete market economy; reduce poverty step by step and precisely; keep reforming political and economic institutions; link the national economy to the world economy and join globalization; raise living standards under a people-centred approach; build an innovative country; form a strong leadership core; and manage domestic and international situations while building a community with a shared future for mankind. Xu illustrates these with the evolution of the socialist market economy, China's three stages of opening up, the Belt and Road Initiative, and comparative poverty data for Africa and Latin America.

Xu contends that the Communist Party's leadership is the fundamental reason China found the right road, and that latecomer states especially need an advanced party at the centre. The article also stresses diversity of development models: China's success, Xu argues, undermines the Western 'end of history' thesis, and other countries should draw on Chinese experience without copying it. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of how Chinese scholarship in 2019 framed China's experience as a reference for the Global South, with supporting statistics.
quoteEn: It is impossible for two entirely identical countries in the world to adopt entirely identical development models.
quoteZh: 世界上不可能有两个完全一样的国家能够采取完全一样的发展模式。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's theory, path and system of socialism since reform and opening up, associated with Deng Xiaoping's formulation in 1982.
The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978, introducing market-oriented reforms and opening China to foreign trade and investment.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic (2049).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept calling for countries to cooperate on shared challenges and mutual benefit.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme launched in 2013, linking Asia, Africa and Europe.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The economic system adopted at the 14th Party Congress (1992), combining market allocation of resources with public ownership as the main body of the economy.

t: Studying the history of contemporary China requires studying the history of world socialism
zh: 研究当代中国史离不开对世界社会主义史的研究
paras: Zhu Jiamu argues that the history of contemporary China cannot be separated from the history of the world socialist movement. Writing in 2019, Zhu holds that contemporary China's past, present and future are all part of world socialism, and that the study of each field depends on the other.

The short article opens with Xi Jinping's speech marking forty years of reform and opening up, then traces the roughly seventy years of the People's Republic. It takes in the 1949 transition to socialism and the First Five-Year Plan, the war-preparation and Third Front construction of the 1960s and early 1970s, the opening to the United States, and the turn to reform and opening up around 1978.

Zhu's central move is to explain each turning point by the interaction of domestic conditions and the international socialist movement. The early Soviet alliance and aid are presented as enabling rapid industrialisation while strengthening the socialist camp. The Sino-Soviet split and the Vietnam War are said to have driven the Third Front and the opening to the United States. Reform and opening up is attributed mainly to rigidities in the old economic system, but also to the Soviet decline and the era's turn to peace and development. Zhu concludes that reform and opening up both advanced Chinese socialism and "rescued, defended and developed" world socialism.

Zhu holds that socialism with Chinese characteristics is socialism, and, given China's size, an important part of the world movement. The movement is still at a low ebb but shows signs of recovery, and the era remains one of transition from capitalism to socialism. Zhu calls for firm belief in the victory of socialism and communism, together with practical policies suited to the primary stage of socialism and patience in long-term cooperation and struggle with capitalism. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how Party-affiliated historians link Chinese Communist Party history to the international communist movement.
quoteEn: Contemporary China's past, present and future are all part of world socialism: studying the history of contemporary China cannot do without studying the history of the world socialist movement, and studying the latter cannot do without studying the history of contemporary China.
quoteZh: 当代中国的过去、现在和将来，都是世界社会主义的一部分，研究当代中国史离不开对世界社会主义运动史的研究，研究世界社会主义运动史也离不开对当代中国史的研究。

glossary.explanation: A Party thesis, formalised in the 1980s, holding that China is still in an underdeveloped phase of socialism lasting a long historical period. It is used to justify policies suited to China's level of productive forces.
The official name for the path, system and theory of socialism developed in China since reform and opening up began in 1978.
The policy launched around 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, combining domestic economic reform with opening to foreign trade and investment.

t: A community with a shared future for mankind as China's proposal for global governance
zh: 人类命运共同体为全球治理提供“中国方案”
paras: Published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2019, this commentary argues that building a community with a shared future for mankind is China's "Chinese proposal" for world peace, development and global governance. The author, given in the source only as Huang Ping, presents it as an idea set out by Xi Jinping against a background of what the text calls changes in the world unseen in a century. It was written into the preamble of the Constitution in 2018.

The piece has three parts. The first traces China's commitment to peaceful development over the 70 years since 1949. The second argues that China's growth offers opportunities to other countries. The third describes the concrete content of China's approach to global governance and gives the Belt and Road Initiative as a practical example.

Huang's central claim is that peaceful development is a choice of history, of present conditions and of values. In the author's account, Western powers pursued expansion by force under a "law of the jungle" and zero-sum logic, while old China suffered aggression after 1840. The author holds that China has followed the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, made pledges never to seek hegemony or expansion, and drawn on a cultural tradition of "harmony in diversity". On governance, the article sets out commitments to mutual respect and dialogue, win-win openness against protectionism and unilateralism, equality among civilisations, and cooperation on the environment. It describes these as a response to economic stagnation, widening development gaps, conflict and populism.

Huang concludes that the idea continues seven decades of Chinese diplomacy and offers a way past the old logic that a strong state must seek hegemony and past the "Thucydides trap". The author acknowledges possible traps, risks and attempts at a "new Cold War", but treats the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation as irreversible. China is portrayed as a responsible power and as a development model for countries that want to grow while keeping their independence. Read the original if you want an example of how official Chinese commentary in 2019 framed the community with a shared future for mankind historically, morally and as a basis for global governance.
quoteEn: Peace guarantees development; development promotes peace.
quoteZh: 和平，保证发展；发展，促进和平。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humanity
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13. It calls for countries to cooperate on shared challenges and was written into the Chinese Constitution's preamble in 2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal of restoring China to strength and international standing after the period of foreign domination from 1840.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence
glossary.explanation: Principles of mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. They were set out by China in the 1950s and affirmed at the 1955 Bandung Conference.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The contemporary significance of local red culture
zh: 地方红色文化的当代意义
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2019, no. 20), Zhao Yuezhi and Sha Yao ask how red culture, the cultural legacy of the Chinese revolution, should be promoted in the new era. They use the image of a tree: national narratives of the revolution are the trunk and local narratives the branches and leaves. The authors argue that promoting red culture must not stop at the trunk, and that local revolutionary stories need to be developed as well.

The short commentary is organised under three headings: locality (zai di xing), contemporaneity (shidai xing) and mass character (qunzhong xing). It starts from spirits named after places, such as the Long March spirit and the Jinggangshan, Yan'an and Xibaipo spirits. It then uses Lishui in Zhejiang and its "southwest Zhejiang revolutionary spirit" as its main case, and refers briefly to the Yimeng spirit of Linyi.

On locality, the authors say that the nationally known revolutionary spirits remain irreplaceable. They add that, amid fragmented communities, Cold War ideology, the "farewell to revolution" current and internet-era historical nihilism, the overall narrative needs vivid local stories to support it. In their view local narratives enrich the national one and do not deconstruct it. Embedded in kinship and village ties, they can connect with people's lives and emotions. On contemporaneity, the authors argue that red culture must enter people's hearts and daily practice, and not only histories and museums. They say Lishui has turned the Red Army's hardship and courage into present-day drive for development, and uses online and offline media and red tourism. On mass character, they hold that the revolution's spirit was forged in fusion with the countryside and the peasantry. They cite Xi Jinping's 2013 redefinition of the Yimeng spirit as a bond between the Party and the people, and describe the Red Army's work in southwest Zhejiang in the same terms.

The authors conclude that the effect of promoting a local revolutionary spirit should be judged by how deeply it resonates and wins popular support locally, and not by its fame. They end by posing, as a task of the times, how to keep to the mass line so that ecological civilisation, poverty alleviation and rural revitalisation advance together, with peasants as the real subject of rural revitalisation. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-affiliated scholars link local revolutionary history, ideological work and rural policy.
quoteEn: Promoting local revolutionary spirit in the new era means using local revolutionary narratives to enrich and supplement the national narrative, not to deconstruct the overall narrative.
quoteZh: 新时代弘扬地方革命精神，是以地方革命叙事来丰富和补充全国性的叙事，而不是解构总体性叙事

glossary.explanation: The cultural legacy of the Chinese Communist revolution, including its sites, stories, relics and values. It is promoted in official education and tourism.
An official term for views seen as denying or belittling the revolutionary tradition and the Party's historical record. Party writers treat it as an ideological danger.
A Party working method that stresses drawing on the masses and serving them. It was developed in the Mao era and is still invoked today.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to promote the economic, ecological and cultural development of the countryside.
The national campaign to eliminate extreme rural poverty. It was a priority of the Party leadership in the late 2010s.

t: The rule of law as an important guarantee of China's sustained development
zh: 法治建设是中国持续发展的重要保障
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2019, no. 20), Zhi Zhenfeng asks what role the rule of law has played in China's sustained development. Zhi argues that economic growth shapes people's sense of gain, while legal development shapes their sense of security, and that national success is a coordinated "collective dance" rather than a one-legged hop. The rule of law, in this reading, is one of the "four beams and eight pillars" of the Chinese miracle.

The article has three sections. The first treats certainty and predictability as the inner requirement of legal development and offers evidence on personal and property security. The second draws common lessons from countries' experience of building the rule of law. The third sets out what Zhi calls the "Chinese code": holistic coordination of legal construction with other fields under Party leadership.

Zhi cites homicide rates (0.62 per 100,000 in China in 2016, against 4.88 in the United States in 2015), a Gallup safety ranking of tenth, low police numbers per capita, rising per-capita income and growing foreign patent and trademark filings as signs of security and property protection. From a comparative survey Zhi draws five generalisations. Legal development correlates with economic growth and with stability. It does not necessarily depend on Western-style electoral democracy. It requires a stable, strong government. And it must restrain the "key minority" of officials. Zhi then describes a "state capacity paradox": strong state capacity is necessary for the rule of law but not sufficient, as strongman politics or fusion of religion and state in some Latin American and Middle Eastern countries are said to show. China, the author says, takes a realist path in which the Party steers legal construction as part of overall national development, disciplines its own power through anti-corruption work and acts within the constitution and the law.

Zhi concludes that the core of the socialist rule-of-law path with Chinese characteristics is upholding Party leadership, which the article calls the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the fundamental guarantee of socialist rule of law. Building a law-based China is presented as part of modernising the system and capacity of national governance. Read the original if you want an official-line argument, with comparative statistics, on how Chinese scholars link legal development, state capacity and Party leadership.
quoteEn: State capacity is a necessary condition for success in building the rule of law, but not a sufficient one.
quoteZh: 国家能力是法治建设成功的必要条件，而非充分条件。

glossary.explanation: A phrase in Xi Jinping's discourse for leading officials, especially senior cadres, whose conduct is seen as decisive for governance and discipline.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernising the system and capacity of national governance
glossary.explanation: A goal formally set out at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2013, covering institutional improvement and the competence of governing bodies.

t: Seventy years of advancing the great project of Party building in new China: basic practice and lessons
zh: 新中国70年推进党的建设伟大工程的基本实践及启示
paras: Marking the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic in 2019, this article asks how the Communist Party of China has carried forward the "great project" of Party building since 1949, and what lessons follow. The author argues that treating Party building as a great project is an innovation in the Party's "great self-reform" and an important instrument for leading the "great social revolution". The author holds that the experience offers guidance for the new stage of this project in the new era.

The article is a chronological survey in four parts. It begins with Mao Zedong's 1939 formulation of the project and the Party's efforts in the first decades after 1949, then moves to the reform and opening up period under Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao. Next it treats the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012) under Xi Jinping, and it closes with six lessons. Each stage is presented through the question of what kind of Party to build and how to build it.

Liu's central claim is that social revolution and self-reform must advance together, so that Party building keeps pace with the Party's wider undertakings. For the early decades the author cites rectification campaigns and growth in membership from 5.8 million to 6.369 million. For 1978–2012 the author points to the new ideological line, cadre reform, institutionalisation and anti-corruption bodies, and membership growth from 36.981 million to 85.127 million. For the Xi era the article highlights full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, the eight-point regulation, the revision or formulation of more than 140 Party regulations, and an anti-corruption campaign it calls overwhelmingly effective.

The article draws six lessons: pursue social revolution and self-reform together; strengthen Party leadership and Party building comprehensively; update the overall goals and layout of Party building; combine ideological education with rule-based governance; align a people-centred stance with reform and innovation; and treat the "key minority" of leading cadres and the Party's broad membership as inseparable. The author concludes that these practices have made the Party a long-term governing party and a strong leading force for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a compact official-style periodisation of Party-building policy from 1949 to 2019, with dates, regulations and membership figures.
quoteEn: The great social revolution must rely on the great self-reform to provide its fundamental guarantee.
quoteZh: 伟大社会革命必须靠伟大自我革命提供根本保证。
