glossary.explanation: An economic policy line announced by Xi Jinping in 2015. It seeks to improve the quality and structure of supply, for example by cutting excess capacity, rather than relying on demand stimulus alone.
The official goal, set out from 2017, of shifting from high-speed growth to growth stressing quality, efficiency and innovation.
The 19th Party Congress (2017) redefined it as the contradiction between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.

glossary.pinyin: sān qù yī jiàng yī bǔ
glossary.en: three cuts, one reduction, one improvement
glossary.literal: three removals, one lowering, one filling-up
glossary.explanation: The five tasks of supply-side structural reform: cutting overcapacity, destocking and deleveraging, reducing costs, and improving weak links.

t: Dialectical materialism is the world outlook and methodology of Chinese Communists
zh: 辩证唯物主义是中国共产党人的世界观和方法论
paras: This is a speech by Xi Jinping, delivered on 23 January 2015 at the 20th group study session of the Political Bureau of the 18th Central Committee and published in Qiushi in 2019. Xi presents dialectical materialism as the world outlook and methodology of Chinese Communists. He argues that Party members and officials must consciously apply it if the Party is to achieve the "Two Centenary Goals" and the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation.

Xi opens by tracing the Party's use of Marxist philosophy, from Mao Zedong's essays on practice and contradiction to Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao. He then sets out four areas for study and application: the material unity of the world, the laws of contradiction, the methods of materialist dialectics, and the relation between knowledge and practice. Classical Chinese sayings and idioms appear throughout alongside quotations from Engels.

On the first point, Xi holds that policy must start from objective reality rather than subjective wishes. The largest reality, in his account, is that China remains in the primary stage of socialism, though he stresses that conditions keep changing and that new contradictions require fresh analysis. He also says consciousness can act strongly on matter, which is why ideals and convictions are the "calcium" of Communists. On contradiction, he urges officials to face problems directly and to separate principal from secondary contradictions. He cites the "Four-sphere Comprehensive" agenda as an example of combining overall planning with a focus on key points. He describes metaphysics as the easy alternative to dialectics, which demands investigation and a development-minded, comprehensive, systematic view.

Xi concludes that practice is the source and purpose of knowledge, and that theory detached from practice becomes dogma. He calls for confidence in theory and strategic resolve. He also insists that theoretical innovation has no end, and that it must interact with practical innovation to develop twenty-first-century Marxism in China. Read the original if you want a primary statement of how the top Party leadership presents Marxist philosophy as a practical method of governance.
quoteEn: Once theory is divorced from practice, it becomes rigid dogma and loses its vitality and life force.
quoteZh: 理论一旦脱离了实践，就会成为僵化的教条，失去活力和生命力。

glossary.explanation: Official Party assessment that China remains at an early, underdeveloped phase of socialism that will last a long time. It underpins policy on economic development and the mixed economy.
Slogan promoted by Xi Jinping from 2012 that identifies the dream with national rejuvenation, national prosperity and the people's wellbeing.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary (2049).
Xi Jinping's strategic framework, set out from 2014: comprehensively building a moderately prosperous society, deepening reform, advancing the rule of law and strictly governing the Party.

t: Writing a newer and more beautiful chapter for the era
st: Studying and implementing the spirit of Xi Jinping's important speech at the meeting celebrating the 70th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China
zh: 书写出更新更美的时代篇章
zhSub: 深入学习贯彻习近平同志在庆祝中华人民共和国成立70周年大会上的重要讲话精神
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 16 October 2019, is a study piece on Xi Jinping's speech at the meeting marking the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic. Li Zhongjie takes up Xi's three-part formula: China's yesterday is already written in humanity's records, its today is being created by hundreds of millions of people, and its tomorrow will certainly be better. Li reads the formula as showing historical continuity and as a call to write a newer and more beautiful chapter.

The article is organised under three headings that follow Xi's three time frames. The first looks back from the founding of New China to the long history of Chinese civilisation, and to Xi's summary of what the 70 years added. The second turns to the present, using the names of the National Day parade's mass formations as a guide. The third looks ahead and stresses that the road remains long.

Li argues that the founding of New China ended a century of humiliation and opened the road to national rejuvenation. He says the 70 years are best summed up in three points taken from Xi's remarks: opening the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, ending absolute poverty, and an independent, peaceful foreign policy that contributes to a community with a shared future for mankind. On the present, Li groups the parade formations into past history, ongoing tasks and the undertakings pursued since the 18th Party Congress (2012) under Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. He treats the smooth organisation of the celebration as evidence of high governance capacity.

Li concludes that China's tomorrow will be better because of the material base and governing experience built up over 70 years, and especially since reform and opening up. He adds that the road ahead will not be smooth and that the Party is "on the road", citing Xi's warnings about complacency and corruption. He notes that the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee was about to take up improving the system and modernising state governance, and he calls on all to unite and keep the Republic strong. Read the original if you want an example of how official commentary of 2019 presented Xi's anniversary speech and its past–present–future framing.
quoteEn: Whether we can continue yesterday's splendour of China and turn tomorrow's China into reality depends above all on what we create today.
quoteZh: 我们能不能延续昨天中国的辉煌，能不能把明天的中国变成现实，关键都要看我们今天的创造。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

The official name for China's path and system since reform and opening up, introduced by Deng Xiaoping in the early 1980s. It combines Party leadership and a socialist system with market-oriented reform.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–2013. It calls for cooperation and shared development among states.
The policy launched in late 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented economic reform and opening to the outside world.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.literal: modernisation of the state governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal put forward at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). It refers to improving the institutions and capacity through which the Party and state govern.

t: Drawing striving strength from heroes
zh: 从英雄身上汲取奋发力量
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 22 October 2019, takes up Xi Jinping's remark at the state medals and honorary titles ceremony that heroes emerge only where heroism is revered and where people strive to be heroes. Qin argues that the Chinese nation has always honoured heroes, and that the new era needs more of them.

The piece is organised around four injunctions: revere heroes, defend heroes, learn from heroes and care for heroes. It places them against the 70 years since the founding of the People's Republic and the goal of the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation, and it cites classical Chinese poetry as evidence of a long tradition of hero-worship.

Qin reasons that rejuvenation will not come easily and requires a "great struggle" against risks and challenges, so more model figures are needed. Heroes are described as the nation's backbone, so Qin says that people who deliberately blacken them or distort history must be met with vigilance. The author points to the Law on the Protection of Heroes and Martyrs, in force since 1 May 2018, as legal backing. Learning from heroes means first knowing their deeds, then putting them into practice. Qin holds that greatness comes from ordinary work done well.

On caring for heroes, Qin calls for honours and rewards for them, and for attention to their families, so that heroes do not "shed both blood and tears". The conclusion is that reverence, defence, learning and care together draw the strength needed for the new era. Read the original if you want a brief example of how the People's Daily framed hero commemoration in 2019.
quoteEn: Greatness comes from the ordinary, and the ordinary makes greatness.
quoteZh: 伟大出自平凡，平凡造就伟大。

glossary.explanation: A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, centred on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

glossary.en: Law on the Protection of Heroes and Martyrs
glossary.explanation: A Chinese law in force since 1 May 2018 that penalises defaming or denigrating heroes and martyrs.

keywords: Law on the Protection of Heroes and Martyrs

t: Speeches at the symposium marking the 130th anniversary of Li Dazhao's birth
zh: 在纪念李大钊同志诞辰130周年座谈会上的发言
paras: This is a set of four speeches given at the symposium commemorating the 130th anniversary of Li Dazhao's birth, originally published in the People's Daily on 28 October 2019. The speakers are Qu Qingshan (president of the Party History and Literature Research Institute), Liang Yanshun (deputy head of the Central Publicity Department), Qiu Shuiping (Party secretary of Peking University) and Wang Dongfeng (Party secretary of Hebei). Together they present Li as a pioneer of Marxism in China and a principal founder of the Communist Party, and as a model for present-day Party work.

Qu concentrates on Li's intellectual contribution to exploring China's revolutionary road. Liang describes Li as the earliest Marxist in China, a systematic propagandist of Marxism and an explorer of its application to Chinese conditions. Qiu stresses Li's decade at Peking University, his influence on students and his role in founding the early Beijing Communist organisation. Wang reviews Li's activities in Hebei and then reports Hebei's recent economic, ecological and livelihood results under Xi Jinping.

On the substance of Li's thought, Qu and Liang point to his writings after the Russian Revolution, notably "My Marxist View" and "Further Discussion of Problems and Isms". They report that Li held Marxism to be a tool to be studied for how it applies to China's political and economic conditions, not a dogma to be imported whole. Both credit him with early formulations: that China's democratic revolution must be led by the proletariat, rely on the peasantry and build a democratic united front, and that Chinese socialism would have its own characteristics. Qu adds Li's views on Party-building: a clear political character, strong organisation, mass links and a purpose of serving the people, which he ties to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

Each speaker links the commemoration to current tasks. Liang calls for arming the whole Party with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Qiu proposes building Chinese philosophy and social science with their own disciplinary, academic and discourse systems. Wang pledges Hebei's loyalty to the Party Central Committee and its commitment to the Two Upholds and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want to see how senior Party and university officials in 2019 presented Li Dazhao's legacy and tied it to Party-building, ideology and regional development.
quoteEn: Comrade Li Dazhao was the earliest disseminator of Marxism in China and the earliest explorer of the adaptation of Marxism to China.
quoteZh: 李大钊同志是马克思主义在中国的最早传播者和马克思主义中国化最早的探索者。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official slogan, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012), for tightening discipline, anti-corruption work and organisational standards within the Communist Party.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for applying Marxism to China's concrete conditions and updating it for the present era.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and in the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely associated with the Chinese Dream.

t: Deeply understanding the adherence to a people-centred approach
zh: 深刻领会坚持以人民为中心
authors: Beijing Municipal Research Centre for Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 30 October 2019 under the name of a Beijing municipal research centre on Xi Jinping Thought, sets out what it means to "adhere to a people-centred approach". It argues that this principle, part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, makes the people's standpoint the fundamental standpoint, makes the people's yearning for a better life the goal of struggle, and requires the Party to carry out its own great self-reform.

The text is organised in three sections after a short introduction. The first treats the principle as an expression of what it calls Marxism's most distinctive trait, its character as a doctrine of the people. The second links it to the Communists' "original aspiration and mission". The third concerns the foundations of the Party's long-term governance.

In the first section the authors hold that Marxism is rooted in the people and aims at human liberation. They list the Party's commitments as evidence: serving the people wholeheartedly, the mass line, governing for the people, and the four criteria of whether the people support, approve, are happy with and agree to its work. In the second section the article ties the people-centred approach to three aims: the people's yearning for a better life, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and a larger contribution to humanity. It cites the redefined principal contradiction, the Party's livelihood goals, a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative. In the third section the authors argue that, because the Party has no interests apart from those of the country, nation and people, it can find the courage to reform itself. They say this requires winning popular support, opposing formalism and bureaucratism, and accepting public supervision, and they claim that campaigns since the 18th Party Congress (2012) have achieved results.

The article concludes that only by keeping the people at the centre can the Party stay close to the masses, resist the dangers it identifies (spiritual slackness, inadequate ability, detachment from the masses and corruption), and secure the "most reliable" class and popular base for long-term rule. It presents the principle as both a theoretical proposition and a basic strategy for the new era. Read the original if you want an authoritative example of how Party-affiliated theorists link Marxism's "people" orientation to governance, common prosperity and Party discipline in 2019.
quoteEn: The people-oriented character is the most distinctive trait of Marxism.
quoteZh: 人民性是马克思主义最鲜明的品格。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018 as the Party's guiding ideology.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A slogan of Xi-era governance stressing that development should start from and benefit the people. The 19th Party Congress (2017) listed it among the basic policies for upholding socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of gathering views from the masses and returning them as policy ("from the masses, to the masses").
An official goal of shared wealth for all people, which Chinese leaders present as an essential feature of socialism.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, presented as a vision of cooperative international relations.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in official discourse since 2012, also called the Chinese Dream.

t: Basic lessons of China's ideological work since reform and opening up
zh: 改革开放以来我国意识形态建设的基本经验
paras: Published in Guangming Daily in August 2019, this short commentary asks what experience the Communist Party of China has accumulated in building socialist ideology over the 40 years of reform and opening up. Li and Feng argue that the Party has consistently prioritised ideological work and has drawn four basic lessons, which they say have consolidated the foundations of China's socialist system.

The article opens with Xi Jinping's call to sum up the Party's publicity and ideological experience and keep applying it. It then takes the four lessons in turn, each under its own heading: Marxism's guiding position, the Party's absolute leadership, theoretical innovation, and innovation in methods.

On the first two points, the authors hold that Marxism's guiding role can only be established through concrete practice in economic, political, cultural, social and ecological construction. They add that ideological work must stay under the Party's absolute leadership, which in their view rests on the Party's nature and tasks. Citing Mao Zedong, they say leadership must be won by correct policies and exemplary work that persuade the public, and they propose strengthening theory, Party building and the training of successors. On innovation, they argue that inheritance and innovation cannot be separated without falling into dogmatism or adventurism. They present Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as successive products of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions.

On methods, the authors call for continuing political and ideological work and public opinion guidance while giving them new content. They name education, cultural and ethical-ideological progress, and core socialist values as means of increasing ideology's appeal and cohesion. They conclude that both successes and failures are a spiritual asset, and that new challenges can be met only through theoretical innovation under Marxist guidance. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style summary of how Party commentators framed ideological work in 2019.
quoteEn: Advancing with the times is Marxism's most important theoretical character; continuous theoretical innovation grounded in practice, on the premise of upholding and inheriting its basic principles, is the source of Marxism's enduring vitality.
quoteZh: 与时俱进是马克思主义最重要的理论品格，在坚持和继承马克思主义基本原理的前提下，不断进行实践基础上的理论创新是马克思主义永葆生机和活力的源泉。

glossary.explanation: The Party's work of shaping beliefs and public opinion through theory, propaganda, education and culture. It is treated in Party documents as a matter of political security and leadership.
A theory associated with Jiang Zemin, introduced around 2000. It holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the majority.
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept, adopted in the early 2000s, stressing people-centred, coordinated and sustainable development.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.zh: 社会主义核心价值体系
glossary.explanation: A set of officially promoted values and ideals, formulated in the 2000s and 2010s, meant to unify society around Party-led socialism.

t: Achievements, reflection and new prospects: the broad trends of historiography in New China over 70 years
zh: 成就、反思与新的前景——新中国史学70年发展大势
paras: Marking the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic in 1949, this piece, first published in Guangming Daily in August 2019, offers a short overview of how Chinese historiography has developed since the founding of New China. Qu Lindong's thesis is that, under the guidance of Marxist theory, Chinese historical scholarship has achieved "brilliant" results in theory, research fields, scholarly output, personnel and international influence. The author presents the history as a sequence of achievement, reflection and renewed tasks.

The article moves through three stages. It first recalls the origins of Chinese Marxist historiography in the 1920s and 1930s and its achievements in the 17 years from the 1950s to the mid-1960s. It then turns to the period after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), which Qu characterises by "reflection and advance". Finally it sets out four tasks for historiography in the new era that began with the 18th Party Congress (2012).

For the first 17 years, Qu points to a wave of study of Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought, debates on major questions (periodisation of ancient history, peasant wars, land ownership, "sprouts of capitalism", and others), and the training of a younger generation of historians. The author also admits detours caused by "Left" political currents and dogmatism. After 1978, Qu reports, scholars such as Yin Da, Hou Wailu, Liu Danian and Bai Shouyi called for a complete grasp of historical materialism, a "nationalisation" of Marxist historical science, and a contemporary commitment to historical integrity grounded in seeking truth from facts. Qu adds that publication since the 1990s has been the largest in the history of New China, but that importing foreign scholarship raises the problem of how Chinese historiography can show its own character and gain discursive power.

For the new era, Qu proposes four tasks: creatively transforming the inherited legacy of historiography while building a disciplinary, academic and discourse system with Chinese characteristics; treating foreign historiography rationally, neither rejecting nor blindly following it; establishing a people-centred view of history; and strengthening history's service to society, in line with Xi Jinping's letter to the Institute of History at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. Qu presents these as the main prospects for the field. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese historians periodise their own discipline and frame its current tasks.
quoteEn: This task can be summed up as reflection and advance.
quoteZh: 这个任务，可概括为反思与进取。

glossary.explanation: A principle associated with Mao Zedong and revived by Deng Xiaoping from 1978, meaning that policy and scholarship should rest on actual conditions rather than dogma.

glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de shíyī jiè sān zhōng quánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978)
glossary.explanation: The December 1978 meeting of the Communist Party's Central Committee, regarded as the starting point of reform and opening up and of the move away from "Left" policies.
The Marxist theory that material production and social relations drive historical development; it is the declared theoretical basis of Chinese Marxist historiography.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A phrase from Xi Jinping-era Party discourse, stressing the people's主体 position (as the main body of history and of development).

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义进入新时代
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì jìnrù xīn shídài
glossary.explanation: The Party's description, since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and especially the 19th (2017), of the present stage of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: Seeking truth from facts and pioneering innovation: historical materialism and research on the history of the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 实事求是与开拓创新——唯物史观与抗日战争史研究
paras: Writing in the Guangming Daily in August 2019, Chen Hongmin asks how research on the War of Resistance against Japan should be guided and renewed. The article argues that the progress made in the 70 years since 1949 owes much to historians' adherence to historical materialism, and that future work must pair this guidance with methodological innovation.

The short commentary opens with Xi Jinping's assessment of the war's significance and his call for deeper research. It then discusses the method of historical materialism, the scholarly debate over who won the war, and the 2015 commemorations. It closes with a case of innovation: digital archives and big data.

Chen identifies two basic methods drawn from historical materialism: seeking truth from facts and concrete analysis of concrete problems. Applying them, the author rejects the long-standing binary between crediting the Nationalist government and crediting Communist-led forces alone. In Chen's account, post-reform scholarship reached a consensus: the war was a struggle of the whole nation under the anti-Japanese national united front, with the Communist Party as its "mainstay", and was the main Eastern theatre of the world anti-fascist war. On innovation, Chen notes that Japan's Asian Historical Records Center, set up in 1999, offers one-sided official sources. In response, the national social science fund's special project on the war funded a free, permanently open platform for documents on the war and modern Sino-Japanese relations, which by the end of 2018 held over 13 million pages.

Chen concludes that, guided by historical materialism and by Xi's call to let archives, materials and testimony speak, the field can advance further. The author stresses that controlling large source databases confers a degree of discursive power. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned statement of how Chinese historians frame the war's historiography and digital source-building.
quoteEn: In the internet age, whoever builds a complete, easy-to-use large historical-source database holds, to a certain extent, the discursive power in that field of research.
quoteZh: 在互联网时代，谁建立了资料完备、使用方便的大型史料数据库，谁就在一定程度上掌握了该领域研究的话语权。

glossary.explanation: A principle long associated with Mao Zedong and revived under Deng Xiaoping, stressing that conclusions should rest on empirical reality rather than dogma. Here it is presented as a core method of historical materialism.

The wartime alliance between the Communist Party and the Nationalists and other groups against Japan, formed in the late 1930s. Official Chinese historiography credits the Communist Party with proposing it.

t: Historical materialism and Marxist research on Chinese intellectual history
zh: 唯物史观与马克思主义中国思想史研究
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in August 2019, surveys how historical materialism has shaped the study of Chinese intellectual history since the early twentieth century. Yang argues that Marxist research on the subject, guided by this method, became the mainstream of the field and offers a scientific ontology and methodology for future work.

The piece moves chronologically. It starts with early modern scholarship and Hu Shi's 1919 outline of Chinese philosophy, then covers the May Fourth period, the 1930s and 1940s, the post-1949 decades, the era of reform and opening up, and the twenty-first century. Along the way it names scholars and works, among them Hou Wailu, Feng Youlan, Ren Jiyu, Zhang Qizhi and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences project General History of Chinese Thought, launched in 2014.

Yang's central claim is that Marxist scholars used historical materialism to trace how social being and economic relations underlie ideas, and they treated Chinese thought as a test of the theory's universal truth. Hou Wailu's work established the field's paradigm and gave rise to the "Hou Wailu school". Before reform and opening up, Yang says, the struggle between materialism and idealism served as the organising thread, with Soviet influence, and this brought dogmatism, mechanical materialism and over-politicisation. After the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), the author describes a return to a richer, more historically sensitive method, including the history of scholarship, social thought and religion.

Yang concludes that Marxist research has applied the theory of social formations, the determination of social consciousness by social being, and class analysis, and has expressed a people-centred character. In the new era, the author expects it to explain the essence and laws of ideas and the inner dynamic of Chinese culture's continuity, serving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned overview of the main works and stages of Marxist intellectual history in China.
quoteEn: The principle of historical materialism that ideas originate in the process of real life provides a scientific ontology and methodology for the study of intellectual history.
quoteZh: 唯物史观的思想观念源于现实生活过程的原理，为思想史的研究提供了科学的本体论与方法论。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, prominent in official discourse especially since 2012, of restoring China's national strength and international standing.
In Marxist theory, the historical types of society defined by their economic base and relations of production, such as feudal or capitalist society.

t: The philosophical character of materialist dialectics
zh: 唯物辩证法的哲学品格
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 31 July 2019, takes its cue from the Outline for Studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Huang and Chen argue that grasping the philosophical character of materialist dialectics is part of meeting the Outline's call to master Marxist ways of thinking and working.

The article is organised in three sections. It treats materialist dialectics in turn as a scientific methodology uniting theory and practice, as a scientific theory of knowledge that guides practice, and as a doctrine whose essential traits are innovation and practicality.

As methodology, the authors say, materialist dialectics supplies correct ways of thinking and working: practice as the sole criterion of truth, the people as the force creating history, and objective, comprehensive, developmental and interconnected observation. As epistemology, it is applied to major relationships in China's development, above all reform, development and stability. Huang and Chen cite the primary stage of socialism as the basic national condition that makes development the Party's first task. They describe development as the aim, reform as the driving force and stability as the precondition. In the third section they cite Engels's remark that Marx's worldview is a method rather than a dogma. They read the shift in China's principal contradiction, traced from the Eighth Party Congress (1956) to the 19th Party Congress (2017), and the post-1978 succession of theoretical innovations as proof that the dialectic is practical and innovative.

The authors conclude that practice and innovation have no end, and that China must face the remaining difficult problems directly. They call for people-centred development, the new development philosophy and comprehensive deepening of reform and opening up, so that practical and theoretical innovation continue together. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated philosophers present dialectics as a working method for policy in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Innovation and practicality are inherent in materialist dialectics; opposing ossification and stressing practice are its essential requirements.
quoteZh: 创新性和实践性是唯物辩证法的题中应有之义，反对僵化和注重实践是唯物辩证法的本质要求。

glossary.explanation: An official thesis, developed from the 1980s, that China remains at an early stage of socialist construction. It is used to justify the priority given to developing the productive forces.
A framework put forward in 2015 stressing innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world begun in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: The dual theoretical horizon of political economy and philosophy of right in Capital
zh: 《资本论》中政治经济学和法哲学的双重理论视域
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in August 2019, Xiao Shimei asks what disciplinary character Capital has. Earlier readers placed it in the relation between philosophy and economics, and more recently between political philosophy and political economy. Xiao proposes a third reading, following the logic of problems in the development of Marx's thought. The article argues that Marx's critique of political economy inherently contains a dual horizon, that of political economy and that of the philosophy of right (法哲学, legal philosophy).

The piece has three parts. The first traces Marx's turn from critique of the philosophy of right to critique of political economy, from his legal training and his work at the Rheinische Zeitung to the Paris Notebooks and the 1844 Manuscripts. The second asks what the turn amounted to and where the legal-philosophical dimension went afterwards. The third shows how the dual horizon appears in Capital and what it means for present practice.

Xiao reads Marx's critique of private property as the marker of the turn, and distinguishes three attitudes to it. Classical political economy and the historical school of law take an uncritical positivism. Proudhon offers a metaphysical critique of right, treating property as a legal relation detached from economic relations. Marx instead grasps property relations as relations of production. Because legal and production relations justify each other in a circle, Xiao argues, law cannot condemn the existing order, so Marx used the empirical method of political economy to answer questions of the philosophy of right that legal philosophy could not solve itself. The dialectic carried those questions into political economy. Xiao cites Capital's remark that defining bourgeois property means describing bourgeois production relations. Xiao also sets out correspondences: the labour theory of value with a theory of labour ownership, surplus value with a theory of the alienation of ownership, and the historical tendency of accumulation with the self-sublation of that alienation.

Xiao concludes that the dual horizon joins the critical side of Marx's theory to its normative side. A theory with only critique and negation, Xiao says, suits tearing down the old world but causes problems in building a new one. Deng Xiaoping's questions of what socialism is and how to build it are described as normative. Xiao holds that normative questions become more pressing in socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era, and that the unity is therefore essential to adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. Read the original if you want a short account of how Marx's legal philosophy and political economy relate, and how a Chinese scholar links this to current practice.
quoteEn: After turning to the critique of political economy, Marx did not leave the problem field of the philosophy of right; rather, he was using the method of political economy to solve the problems of the philosophy of right.
quoteZh: 马克思在转向政治经济学批判以后，不但没有离开法哲学的问题领域，反而是在用政治经济学的方法解决法哲学的问题

glossary.explanation: The Chinese rendering of the German Rechtsphilosophie, as in Hegel's Elements of the Philosophy of Right. It covers questions of the legitimacy and rational basis of law, property and the state.
Marx's name for his theoretical project and the subtitle of Capital. The author reads it as combining empirical analysis with dialectical negation.
The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up. Since the 19th Party Congress (2017) it is described as having entered a "new era".

t: As long as China is here, openness will not be scarce
zh: 有中国在，开放不会稀缺
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 18 September 2019, asks why China keeps expanding its opening to the outside world while unilateralism, trade protectionism and anti-globalisation sentiment rise elsewhere. Huang Ping argues that economic globalisation is an irreversible trend of the times and that wider opening is China's correct response to it.

The piece moves from the global setting to China's own record and then to a general prescription. It first notes that no country can modernise behind closed doors or tackle global problems alone. It then reviews more than 40 years of reform and opening up, and ends with the author's view of how the world should respond to protectionism and isolationism.

Huang contends that China's shift from a closed or semi-closed economy to all-round opening produced sustained rapid growth, higher living standards and a stronger national position, showing that reform drives development and opening brings progress. In this account, "China and the world" is no longer a question of whether China should stay open, but of how an increasingly important member of the international community finds its place and plays a larger role. The author characterises protectionism, populism and cultural xenophobia in some countries as irrational and irresponsible, and warns that zero-sum thinking and the "law of the jungle" would worsen problems, possibly with catastrophic results.

Huang concludes that China, still the largest developing country and still in the primary stage of socialism, will continue on the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, deepen reform and open wider, so that its door will only open further. The author calls on all countries to pursue consultation, civilisational exchange and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how an official-press commentary in 2019 framed China's case for openness against protectionism.
quoteEn: Economic globalisation is an irreversible trend of the times, and China's expansion of opening up is the correct choice in keeping with this trend.
quoteZh: 经济全球化是不可逆转的时代潮流，中国扩大对外开放是顺应这一时代潮流的正确选择。

glossary.explanation: An official thesis that China remains at an early stage of socialist development, with relatively underdeveloped productive forces. It frames long-term policy and China's self-description as a developing country.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since the reform era, combining Party leadership with a market-oriented economy.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13, calling for shared responsibility, cooperation and mutual benefit among states.
The policy line launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented reforms and opening China's economy to foreign trade and investment.

t: Experience and lessons from the economic development of the People's Republic of China
zh: 新中国经济发展的经验和启示
paras: Writing for the People's Daily in September 2019, on the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic, Han Baojiang asks what lessons can be drawn from seven decades of Chinese economic growth. Han's answer is that sustained growth came from six sustained commitments, which together are said to offer guidance for promoting high-quality development in the new era. The article opens by contrasting the poor, war-ravaged country of 1949 with today's second-largest economy, largest manufacturer and largest goods trader.

The piece is a short commentary organised under six headings: leadership of the Communist Party of China, the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, an innovative development philosophy, the reform direction of the socialist market economy, opening up as a basic national policy, and reliance on the initiative of the people. Each section moves chronologically through the Mao, Deng, Jiang, Hu and Xi periods. Each is supported mainly by quotations from party leaders, above all Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

Han's central claim is that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of development. In this account the Party has set direction at each stage, from building an independent industrial system to promoting high-quality development, and it plays a role no other political force can replace. Han adds that the socialist system, built on public ownership as the mainstay and the ability to concentrate resources on major undertakings, underpinned rapid industrialisation. On the market, Han credits the shift from a 'basic' to a 'decisive' role for markets in allocating resources, and points to high savings and capital formation, surplus rural labour and rising total factor productivity as sources of growth. Reform and opening up are presented as complementary: foreign capital, technology and management filled domestic gaps, while grassroots inventions such as the household contract responsibility system and township enterprises show the people's creativity.

Han concludes that these experiences enabled China to cover in decades a path that developed countries took centuries to travel. Han also looks ahead, arguing that in a period of 'great changes unseen in a century' the advantages of the socialist system must still be used fully. Han further calls for developing advanced manufacturing and the real economy while balancing it with virtual economy and services. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the official narrative of 70 years of economic development was framed in the People's Daily in 2019.
quoteEn: Upholding the leadership of the Communist Party of China is the fundamental guarantee for achieving economic development.
quoteZh: 坚持中国共产党的领导，是实现经济发展的根本保证。

glossary.explanation: The official goal, set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017), of shifting the economy from high-speed growth to growth emphasising efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
The Party's official name for China's path and system since the reform era, combining Party leadership, public-ownership-based mixed economy and a socialist market economy.
The economic system adopted officially in 1992, in which markets allocate resources under Party leadership and with the public sector as the mainstay.
The policy begun in 1978 of engaging with foreign trade, capital and technology, designated a basic national policy.

t: The historical logic of the People's Republic's seventy years of striving
zh: 新中国砥砺奋进70年的历史逻辑
paras: Writing for the People's Daily on 25 September 2019, on the eve of the 70th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic, Qu Qingshan asks what inner logic runs through the country's seven decades of change. The answer, in the article's account, is that only socialism with Chinese characteristics can develop, enrich and strengthen China. Qu opens with Xi Jinping's description of the leap from "standing up" to "becoming prosperous" to "becoming strong".

The piece has three main parts. The first presents the creation, upholding and development of socialism with Chinese characteristics as the fundamental achievement of the 70 years. It traces this through successive leadership groups, from Mao Zedong to Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping. The second part treats the three-stage leap as the most striking feature of the period, and cites figures on trade, GDP, urbanisation and poverty reduction. The third part draws out the "inner logic" in four propositions.

Qu argues that each stage built on the one before. Socialist revolution and construction supplied the basic system, and the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) opened reform and opening up. Later leaderships, with the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, carried the path forward. The article cites 2018 figures: an economy of 90 trillion yuan, per capita GDP of about $9,900, and rural poverty down from 98.99 million to 16.6 million since 2012. Qu credits these results to the Party's adaptation of Marxism's basic principles to Chinese conditions, which in this reading released productive forces. The four propositions are that socialism with Chinese characteristics is the only road to national strength; that Party leadership is its most essential feature and the guarantee of success; that reform and opening up is the fundamental driving force; and that the people are the decisive force.

Qu concludes that the Party must keep raising the banner of socialism with Chinese characteristics and hold to the Four-sphere Confidence. He also calls for the "four consciousnesses" and the Two Upholds, for reform and opening up to continue, and for the mass line and a people-centred approach in governing. The text frames this as a source of spiritual strength for further advance. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed account of how the Party presented the 70-year history of the People's Republic in 2019.
quoteEn: The most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics is leadership by the Communist Party of China, and the greatest strength of its system is leadership by the Communist Party of China.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义最本质的特征是中国共产党领导，中国特色社会主义制度的最大优势是中国共产党领导。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's path, theory and system since reform and opening up. It was popularised by Deng Xiaoping from 1982.
Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A Party slogan, used from 2018, requiring members to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party's centralised, unified leadership.
Jiang Zemin's theory, introduced around 2000. It holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the vast majority of the people.
Hu Jintao-era guiding ideology that stresses people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development.

t: An important path for building the core socialist values
st: Promoting reading and building a "scholarly society"
zh: 社会主义核心价值观建设的重要路径
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 26 September 2019, argues that encouraging people to read more and building a "scholarly society" (shuxiang shehui, a society filled with the fragrance of books) is an important path for cultivating and promoting the core socialist values. Luo opens with Xi Jinping's call for more reading and presents reading as a way to raise people's intellectual level and strengthen their spiritual strength.
The piece has two parts. The first explains why a reading society matters for values-building. The second sets out three priorities for putting it into practice.

Luo contends that core values are the spiritual bond of a nation and that reading transmits culture and shapes national character. The author treats a reading society as an inherent part of cultivating the core socialist values, and links it to Chinese cultural confidence and to building a culturally strong socialist country. On priorities, Luo first calls for Party members, cadres and the public to read original works and study Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, Party history and the history of the People's Republic. The author also asks them to understand the main currents of Western social thought so as to resist erroneous ideas. Second, Luo urges the creative transformation and innovative development of fine traditional Chinese culture, with cultural workers producing works that carry contemporary values. Third, Luo calls for government guidance and support, reading activities run by cultural institutions, and the use of internet and digital platforms, noting that China has over 800 million internet users.

Luo concludes that when reading becomes a conscious habit among the people, the country's spiritual outlook and level of civilisation will rise considerably. The goal is a society where every household and place is filled with books. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2019 tied reading campaigns to ideological education and cultural policy.
quoteEn: Building a scholarly society is an inherent part of cultivating and promoting the core socialist values.
quoteZh: 建设书香社会，是培育和弘扬社会主义核心价值观的题中应有之义。

glossary.explanation: A set of twelve values promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering the national, social and individual levels. They are used as the main framework for official ideological and moral education.
A slogan for a society in which reading is widespread and valued. It is associated with national reading campaigns promoted by Party and government bodies.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name of Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Party members are expected to study it.
An official term for confidence in China's cultural tradition, revolutionary culture and socialist culture. It is part of the 'Four-sphere Confidence' formulation.

t: Continuing the struggle for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
zh: 为中华民族伟大复兴接续奋斗
paras: Marking the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic in this People's Daily commentary (September 2019), Zhu Jiamu asks how the Communist Party has pursued its historical mission of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation since 1949. Zhu's answer, drawing on Xi Jinping's phrase that each generation has its own Long March, is that the past seven decades form a "new Long March" with three strands.

The piece is organised around these three strands: upholding and developing the socialist road, pursuing socialist modernization, and safeguarding and promoting world peace and development. Each is treated as a 70-year record, running through successive Party leaderships from Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping.

On the socialist road, Zhu argues that the Party, combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete conditions, held that only socialism could achieve national rejuvenation. Zhu traces a sequence in which Mao established the basic socialist system, Deng Xiaoping opened socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao carried it forward. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Zhu says, it has entered a new era. On modernization, Zhu cites an independent and fairly complete industrial system, the "two bombs and one satellite" achievements, and over 220 industrial products ranking first in the world. On peace, Zhu cites leaders' statements and the Belt and Road Initiative to portray China as a builder of world peace.

Zhu concludes that seven decades of history show China consistently pursuing a foreign policy of peace and shared development, and presents the new era as renewed vitality for scientific socialism in twenty-first-century China. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official 2019 narrative linking the Party's successive leaderships to national rejuvenation, modernization and a community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteEn: The 70 years of New China are 70 years of upholding and continually broadening the socialist road.
quoteZh: 新中国70年是坚持和不断拓展社会主义道路的70年。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, closely associated with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream".
The Party's official name for its model of socialism, launched under Deng Xiaoping in the reform era.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative announced in 2013.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping-era slogan for China's vision of international relations based on cooperation and shared development.

t: The great significance of socialism with Chinese characteristics entering a new era in the history of human social development
zh: 中国特色社会主义进入新时代在人类社会发展史上的重大意义
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in September 2019, Jiang Hui takes up Xi Jinping's statement that the entry of socialism with Chinese characteristics into a new era matters not only for China but for world socialism and the history of human society. The article argues that this entry has significance on three levels: for the development of Marxism, for world socialism, and for how humanity approaches modernization and global problems.

The commentary is organised under four headings. It treats the contribution to twenty-first-century Marxism, the opening of a new stage in world socialism, the widening of paths to modernization, and Chinese proposals for common global problems.

On theory, Jiang holds that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is the latest form of twenty-first-century Marxism. It is said to enrich Marxist philosophy, political economy and the theory of stages of socialist development. On world socialism, Jiang argues that China is solving the problem of how economically and culturally backward countries can build socialism, and that its success has answered the "failure of socialism" and "end of history" claims made after the Soviet and Eastern European upheavals. On modernization, Jiang contends that there is no universal model. In Jiang's account the Western path shows serious drawbacks, and China's path differs because it does not rest on colonial plunder, is people-centred, seeks balanced development and pursues peace.

Jiang concludes that China offers developing countries a new option for countries wanting both faster development and independence. It also contributes ideas on globalization, governance and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official 2019 account of the new era's global and historical significance.
quoteEn: There is no universal model of development in the world.
quoteZh: 世界上没有普世的发展模式。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, in use since the 1980s. It combines Marxism with China's conditions and market-oriented reform.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13. It calls for shared responsibility and cooperation among states.

t: Grasping the historical logic of the 70 years of New China's development
zh: 把握新中国七十年发展的历史逻辑
paras: Writing in People's Daily on the eve of the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic (2019), Li Jie asks how the periods before and after reform and opening up should be understood in relation to each other. Following Xi Jinping, Li argues that they are two interconnected periods with major differences, but that in essence both are the Party leading the people in exploring socialist construction. This, Li says, is the basic guide to seeing the seventy years as one continuous historical logic.

This short commentary is organised under three headings: the course of exploring socialism with Chinese characteristics, the original aspiration and mission of Communists, and the Party's strong leadership. Each is presented as a thread running through both periods. Li supports the first two with economic, education, health and income statistics.

On the first thread, Li argues that socialism with Chinese characteristics was founded on more than twenty years of earlier construction. Li cites the near-complete industrial system, breakthroughs in nuclear and space technology, new political institutions and the "second integration" of Marxism with Chinese conditions. On the second, Li presents rising living standards, school enrolment, life expectancy and poverty reduction, before and after 1978, as proof of continuity. On the third, Li holds that the Party corrected the Cultural Revolution and the "two whatevers" errors from within its own leadership, and that the Party's self-reform now continues this work.

Li concludes that without the Communist Party there would be no New China, and that the Party's prosperity goes with that of the nation. Li calls this the most profound lesson of the seventy years. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official 2019 account of continuity between the Mao-era and reform-era periods, with the statistics Li uses.
quoteEn: Without the historical experience, positive and negative, provided by the exploration of socialist practice before reform and opening up, and without the intellectual, material and institutional achievements it accumulated, reform and opening up could hardly have proceeded smoothly.
quoteZh: 没有改革开放前的社会主义实践探索提供的正反两方面的历史经验，没有其积累的思想成果、物质成果、制度成果，改革开放就难以顺利推进。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path and system of socialism, associated with Deng Xiaoping's reform era.

A formulation for the Party's effort in the Mao period to combine Marxism-Leninism with Chinese realities, drawing on lessons from the Soviet Union; it is treated as a second stage after the first adaptation of Marxism to China.
A 1977 formula holding that whatever policy decisions Mao made and whatever instructions he gave must be upheld; it was later criticised and set aside in the late 1970s.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, used prominently since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Understanding arduous struggle through Party history
zh: 从党史中感悟艰苦卓绝
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily in September 2019, takes up the call to understand what "arduous struggle" (jianku zhuojue) is and where it comes from. It frames this as a required lesson of the campaign to "remain true to our original aspiration and keep our mission firmly in mind". Xie argues that looking back on 98 years of Party history strengthens members' and cadres' resolve to follow the "new Long March" of the new era.

The piece moves from the Party's founding circumstances to the Long March, then to the Party's growth, and finally to present tasks. It draws on the Red Army's march, a quotation from Mao Zedong, and figures on Party membership.

Xie contends that the Party's historical background, political character and mission required it to lead the people in arduous struggle. The author cites the Long March: over 600 battles, nearly 100 rivers crossed, more than 40 mountains climbed and the grasslands traversed. In Xie's account, every step from "standing up" to "growing rich" to "becoming strong" was won through such struggle. Growth from just over 50 members at the First Congress to over 90 million is attributed to the Party's constant adherence to its original aspiration and mission. Hardship, Xie says, also formed revolutionary optimism and a spirit of sacrifice.

Xie concludes that this generation's Long March is to achieve the Two Centenary Goals and the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation. Many "snowy mountains" and "grasslands" remain, and the author rejects both complacency and love of ease. Party members and cadres are urged to know Party history, promote the spirit of arduous struggle and strengthen their commitment to their mission. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party history is used in 2019 ideological education.
quoteEn: Today, the Long March of our generation is to achieve the Two Centenary Goals and realise the Chinese Dream of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 今天，我们这一代人的长征，就是要实现“两个一百年”奋斗目标、实现中华民族伟大复兴的中国梦。

glossary.en: remain true to our original aspiration and keep our mission firmly in mind
glossary.literal: do not forget the original heart, firmly remember the mission
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan associated with Xi Jinping. In 2019 it named a Party-wide education campaign for members and cadres.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary (2049).
A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, equating the dream with the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

t: Without the Communist Party, there would be no New China
zh: 没有共产党 就没有新中国
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 11 September 2019, on the eve of the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic, this commentary asks what has driven the historic changes in China since 1949. Ouyang Song answers that the decisive factor has been the leadership of the Communist Party of China. The author concludes that, in the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics, the Party must unwaveringly uphold and improve its leadership and unwaveringly make itself stronger.

The piece has three parts. It first surveys 70 years of change, then argues that Party leadership explains that change, and finally sets out why the leadership must be upheld and the Party built up. It opens with Xi Jinping's description of the founding of the Party, the founding of the People's Republic, and reform and opening up as three historic landmarks on the road to national rejuvenation.

Ouyang divides the argument into two historical claims. Without the Party there could have been no New China, as shown by the 28 years of the new-democratic revolution. Without the Party there could have been no building and development of New China either. The author cites economic figures: GDP rising from 67.9 billion yuan in 1952 to more than 90 trillion yuan in 2018, per capita gross national income of 9,732 dollars, and over 700 million rural people lifted out of poverty since reform and opening up. Ouyang also lists scientific and engineering achievements. The author credits centralised, unified Party leadership with national unity, a consolidated state power, sustained growth, and the handling of crises, and draws five lessons: Marxism as guide, communist ideals, the socialist path, a people-centred stance, and the Party's self-reform.

Looking ahead, Ouyang gives three reasons why the Party must be upheld unwaveringly: its position as the highest political leading force, the role of Party building within the 'four greats', and the Party's founding mission. The author calls for a high degree of conscious commitment to the Two Upholds, for improved institutions of Party leadership, and for political building as the lead task in Party building. Read the original if you want a representative example of how the Party press framed the 70th anniversary and the case for Party leadership in 2019.
quoteEn: Over 70 years, China has undergone great historic changes.
quoteZh: 70年来中国发生了伟大的历史性变迁

glossary.explanation: A Party requirement, set out in 2018–19, to firmly uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and the Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism, developed since reform and opening up began in the late 1970s.
The policy launched in 1978 that introduced market-oriented economic reform and opened China to foreign trade and investment.
The Party's term for its own continuous self-correction and purification, presented as a way to stay advanced and clean while in power.
Xi Jinping's formula from 2017: the great struggle, the great project of Party building, the great cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and the great dream of national rejuvenation.

t: The inner logic of the Chinese Communist Party's self-reform
zh: 中国共产党自我革命的内在逻辑
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in September 2019, Xu Baojian asks why the Chinese Communist Party regards courage in self-reform as its most distinctive trait and greatest advantage. Xu's answer is that a Marxist party can only keep its advanced nature and purity, and fulfil its mission, if it is willing to carry out the Party's self-reform. The article presents this as both the source of the Party's vitality and the distilled lesson of nearly a century of struggle.

The commentary opens with a quotation from Xi Jinping, who says the Party's greatness lies not in avoiding mistakes but in facing problems squarely and repairing itself. It then builds its case from three connected angles: a theoretical logic, a historical logic and a practical logic. Each section moves from the nature of Marxist parties, to the Party's own record from 1927 to the present, to the conditions it faces now.

On theory, Xu contrasts bourgeois parties, which in the article's account cannot turn criticism on themselves because of class and historical limits, with Marxist parties, which have no interests apart from those of the people and the proletariat as a whole. Xu cites Marx's remark that proletarian revolution criticises itself and grows through doing so. On history, the article lists turning points: the 1927 August 7 Meeting, the 1935 Zunyi Meeting, the Rectification Movement from 1942, the "two musts" of 1949 and the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978). It treats the post-2012 drive for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party as the latest case. On practice, Xu argues that the Party's external situation (a new historical position, a changed principal contradiction, new risks) and its internal situation (9,059.4 million members, a changed membership profile, a shift to long-term governing) require continued self-reform.

Xu concludes that advanced nature and purity are never permanent, so the Party must keep fighting impurity in ideas, politics, organisation and work style, along with complacency and hedonism. The article calls on the Party to carry its great self-reform through to the end, so as to support the "two centenary goals" and the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party commentary in 2019 justified self-reform in theoretical, historical and practical terms.
quoteEn: Courage in self-reform is our Party's most distinctive character and also its greatest strength.
quoteZh: 勇于自我革命，是我们党最鲜明的品格，也是我们党最大的优势。

glossary.explanation: A formula stressing that the Party must correct its own errors and purify itself through its own efforts. It became prominent in Party discourse under Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the campaign since the 18th Party Congress (2012) to tighten discipline, curb corruption and improve Party conduct.
A demand set out by Mao Zedong in March 1949, at the Second Plenum of the 7th Central Committee. It says the Party must stay modest and prudent and keep its style of hard struggle.
A Party-wide campaign of study and criticism launched in Yan'an in 1942 to unify thinking and correct styles of work.
A slogan introduced by Xi Jinping in 2012 describing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
Official targets of a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021 and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Forging the soul and strengthening the backbone through Party history and the history of New China
zh: 以党史和新中国史铸魂补钙
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily in September 2019, argues that Party members and cadres should study the history of the Party and the history of New China as a central part of the "Stay true to the founding mission" campaign. Lü presents the two histories as the most important content of history as "the best textbook". Studying them, the author says, lets cadres draw nourishment and wisdom from the Party's growth and the People's Republic's seventy years of effort.

The piece opens by citing Xi Jinping's call, made during an inspection tour in Gansu, to organise Party members and cadres to study these histories. It then gives three reasons for doing so, each tied to the campaign: cultivating the Party spirit of Communists, understanding the rules of Party building, and strengthening the drive to work for national rejuvenation.

On the first point, Lü argues that historical nihilism leads some people to distort Party history in order to deny the Party's leadership and the socialist system with Chinese characteristics, while some members neither know nor study this history. Study is meant to instil firm ideals and convictions. Second, Lü says the histories show how the Party grew from about 50 members to over 90 million, overcame risks, and practised self-reform, so cadres can grasp the experience and rules of Party building and develop strategic, historical, dialectical, innovative, rule-of-law and bottom-line thinking. Third, Lü holds that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation will demand still greater effort, and that lessons from reform and opening up since 1978 can help cadres keep their direction as reform enters a difficult stage.

Lü concludes that studying Party history and the history of New China keeps cadres theoretically clear-headed and politically steadfast and strengthens the Party's ruling foundation. Read the original if you want a brief example of how the official case for Party-history education was framed in 2019.
quoteEn: Party members and cadres should study Party history and the history of New China seriously to forge their souls and strengthen their backbone, deeply feel the power of belief, the light of ideals and the hardship of struggle, and always remain theoretically clear-headed and politically firm.
quoteZh: 党员、干部要通过认真学习党史、新中国史铸魂补钙，深切感受信仰之力、理想之光和奋斗之艰，始终保持理论上的清醒和政治上的坚定

glossary.en: Stay true to the founding mission
glossary.literal: Do not forget the original aspiration, keep the mission firmly in mind
glossary.explanation: A Party-wide education campaign launched in 2019 for Party members and cadres, centred on the Party's original aspiration and mission.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views that question or reinterpret the Party's history and revolutionary record, seen as aimed at undermining the Party's legitimacy.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of national revival, associated with Xi Jinping's idea of the Chinese Dream.
The policy of economic reform and openness to the outside world launched in 1978 at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee.

keywords: Stay true to the founding mission

t: Revisiting the Party's history, bearing in mind the original aspiration and mission
zh: 重温党的历史 牢记初心使命
authors: Beijing Research Centre for Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 14 August 2019, this commentary by the Beijing research centre for Xi Jinping Thought opens a series on Party and national history. It follows a notice from the central leading group for the "Remain true to our original aspiration and keep our mission firmly in mind" campaign, which made studying the history of the Party and of New China part of that campaign. The authors argue that the Party's original aspiration and mission, seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation, was already present at the Party's founding and runs through its whole history.

The article first cites Xi Jinping on why Party and national history is a required course, then reads the founding period through four themes: a sense of responsibility, conviction, struggle and service to the people. It draws on the 58 founding members, early biographies of Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Li Dazhao and Li Da, the documents of the First and Second Party Congresses (1921, 1922), and the stories of martyrs such as Chen Tanqiu, He Shuheng and Deng Enming.

The authors argue that the founders were mostly educated and not poor, so they joined the revolution out of national and historical responsibility rather than personal hardship. They say these founders then chose Marxism and communism after comparing options, and that the First Congress programme (public ownership, proletarian dictatorship) and the Second Congress's anti-imperialist, anti-feudal programme show Marxism being adapted to Chinese conditions. The Party's history is described as a history of struggle and sacrifice. For each revolutionary stage the article lists how the Party mobilised the masses, and it traces a line of concepts from "serve the people" and the mass line to "people-centred development", the latter presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought.

The article concludes that the Party's experience lies in governing well through correct lines and policies, making popular wishes the basis of decisions and balancing fundamental with specific interests and long-term with immediate ones. It also calls for respecting the people's principal position and drawing on their initiative, so that all sources of social wealth can flow freely. The piece is hortatory and offers an officially framed account of the Party's early history. Read the original if you want to see how Party-affiliated researchers in 2019 presented the founding generation as the source of the Party's present-day mission and mass-line language.
quoteEn: The history of the Communist Party of China is a history of struggle.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的历史就是一部奋斗史。

glossary.en: Remain true to our original aspiration and keep our mission firmly in mind
glossary.literal: Do not forget the original heart, firmly remember the mission
glossary.explanation: A Party-wide education campaign launched in 2019 under Xi Jinping. It centres on the Party's stated founding aim of seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.
The Party's working method of drawing ideas from the masses and returning them as policy. It is credited to Mao Zedong and written into the Party Constitution.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A principle of Xi Jinping Thought, set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017), that development should be for and reliant on the people.

t: The Party's exploration of discipline building in the early years of the People's Republic
zh: 新中国成立初期党对纪律建设的探索
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 21 August 2019, asks how the Chinese Communist Party strengthened its discipline after taking power in 1949. Wu Yang­song argues that, facing a changed environment and new tasks, the Party paid particular attention to discipline building in these years and made a series of effective new explorations.

The article identifies five lines of work: ideological and political education, institution building, strict demands on senior cadres, themed campaigns, and personal example set by the older generation of revolutionaries. It draws on Central Committee directives, Mao Zedong's instructions and documents from 1949 to 1954.

Wu first describes problems among some cadres, such as alienation from the masses, bureaucratism and a sense of entitlement. According to the article, the Central Committee responded with education, including Liu Shaoqi's eight standards for Party members, and with new bodies: discipline inspection commissions were set up at all levels from late 1949 under Zhu De, with detailed rules on penalties up to expulsion. The article presents the 1951 execution of Liu Qingshan and Zhang Zishan, the Three-Anti campaign and rectification drives as measures that targeted the 'key minority' of senior cadres. It adds that Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai applied discipline to themselves and their families, citing Mao's rejection of a bronze statue and Zhou's ten family rules.

Wu concludes that these measures, taken together, markedly strengthened political, integrity and work discipline and created a better disciplinary climate within the Party. The text presents this record as a model of Party building. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed account of early-PRC Party discipline, with citations to primary documents.
quoteEn: Governing the country means governing officials, and governing officials means getting a grip on the key minority.
quoteZh: 治国就是治吏，治吏就是要抓住关键少数。

glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Party discourse, notably by Xi Jinping, for senior leading cadres whose conduct is said to shape the behaviour of the whole Party.
A 1951–52 campaign against corruption, waste and bureaucratism among Party and government officials, launched early in the People's Republic.
