glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's strength and international standing.

t: An innovative theory of far-reaching significance for the development of world socialism and human progress
zh: 对世界社会主义发展和人类进步具有深远意义的创新理论
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in June 2018, Lin Jianhua asks what global significance Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era holds. The article argues that the Thought, which arose as socialism with Chinese characteristics entered a new era, makes a historic contribution to developing Marxism, to world socialism and to human progress. In Lin's account it deepens understanding of the laws governing Communist Party rule, socialist construction and human social development.

The commentary has three parts. It first places the Thought in the line of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions, from the arrival of Marxism-Leninism after the October Revolution. It then considers the Thought's meaning for the world socialist movement, drawing on Xi Jinping's historical periodisation of socialism. Finally it turns to the Thought's implications for global development, for building a community with a shared future for mankind, and for developing countries choosing a path to modernization.

Lin presents the Thought as the latest result of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and as contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism. It is said to answer systematically what kind of socialism with Chinese characteristics should be upheld and how, drawing on a people-centred outlook, harmony between humanity and nature, and the community with a shared future. The article stresses, following Xi, that the periods before and after reform and opening up must not be used to negate each other. It also argues that China's experience shows more than one road to modernization. Lin lists three Chinese contributions: Party governance through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, state governance through modernizing the governance system and capacity, and global governance through the Belt and Road Initiative. Lin also cites China's economic weight, including a contribution to global growth above 30% for several years.

Lin concludes that China has moved from having no path, to following others' paths, to its own path, and now to showing others a path, which is described as a contribution of world value. With the "two centenary goals" achieved, the Thought's historical standing in the world socialist movement is expected to become clearer. The article ends with a confident declaration that China is nearing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a representative example of how Party-aligned commentary in 2018 framed the international significance of Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: Socialism with Chinese characteristics did not fall from the sky.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义不是从天上掉下来的

glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and generating new theory from that practice.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping, calling for shared responsibility and cooperation in international relations.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy since 2012 stressing strict discipline and anti-corruption within the Communist Party.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: Lessons of twentieth-century socialist practice for the development of socialism in the twenty-first century
zh: 20世纪社会主义实践给21世纪社会主义发展提供的启示
source: World Socialism Movement (Shijie shehuizhuyi yundong), 2018 no. 1
paras: Writing in 2018, Song asks what a century of 'actually existing socialism' can teach socialism in the twenty-first century and the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The article argues that this history, running from the October Revolution through the upheavals in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe to the rise of socialism with Chinese characteristics, yields eight basic lessons.

The article takes a macro-historical view and sets out the eight lessons in turn. They concern ideals and convictions; the early stage of the new socialist civilization; the continuing dominance of contemporary capitalism; the people's wellbeing; the link between socialism and reform; the role of the Party; national security and 'soft and hard power'; and anti-imperialism and anti-hegemonism in international relations. Each is supported by references to Soviet and Eastern European experience and to statements by Xi Jinping.

Song's central claim is that twentieth-century socialism arose in economically and culturally backward countries on the periphery of the world capitalist system. In Song's reading, 'impatience' and attempts to leap over historical stages left institutional defects, so the new civilization is still at its starting point. It must therefore develop in interaction with capitalism and the world system, combining openness with self-reliance, and must draw on market mechanisms even where they carry capitalist features. Song adds that the Soviet collapse shows the decisive role of the Party: where it changes or weakens, socialism declines. The collapse also exposed gaps in ideological and overall security, and Song attributes the Soviet turn to hegemonism to the damage done to socialism's international image.

Song concludes that Chinese Communists have grasped these lessons and applied them. Song cites the primary stage of socialism, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, the anti-corruption campaign since the 18th Party Congress (2012), a comprehensive national security system, and the proposal of a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative. Reform is to continue so that it benefits the people, and the rule of law is to replace rule by individuals. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how Chinese Party theorists in 2018 drew lessons from the Soviet experience for socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteEn: Twentieth-century socialist practice has shown again and again that, in an environment where capitalist forces and their world system still hold a relative advantage and dominance, socialist states must coexist, compete and struggle with them over the long term, which requires that both hard and soft power be strong and that the overall national security system have no weak links.
quoteZh: 20世纪社会主义实践一再证明,在资本主义力量及其世界体系仍占据相对优势和主导的环境下,与之长期共处、竞争和斗争,社会主义国家的硬软实力建设“两手都要硬”、国家总体安全体系不能有短板。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since reform and opening up. It combines Party leadership and public ownership with market mechanisms.

The official thesis, developed in the 1980s, that China is still in an early and long-lasting stage of socialism. It is used to justify market reforms and the priority given to developing the productive forces.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012. It covers Party discipline, institution-building and the anti-corruption campaign.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations, stressing common security, development and openness.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013.

t: Marx and Engels's analysis and critique of "true socialism" and its contemporary implications
zh: 马克思恩格斯对“真正的社会主义”的分析批判及其当代启示
source: Studies on Marxism-Leninism (Makesi Liening zhuyi yanjiu), 2018 no. 3
paras: Many present-day currents claim to be the "true socialism". Li Xiaoguang asks how Marx and Engels analysed the original "true socialism", a German current of the 1840s, and what their method offers for judging what socialism is and how to build it. The article argues that the current rested on Germany's backward socio-economic order, wore the shell of German "philosophy", and in class terms expressed the petty bourgeoisie. In Li's reading, Marx and Engels's critique of these three features pinpoints the current's essential flaw.

The article has three parts. The first presents "true socialism" as a distinctive German phenomenon, naming Moses Hess as its main proponent alongside Karl Grün and others. The second traces the works in which Marx and Engels criticised it, from Engels's 1845 writings through The German Ideology and Engels's \"German Socialism in Verse and Prose\" to the Communist Manifesto of 1848, and then sets out three lines of critique. The third draws lessons for today, citing Xi Jinping, Deng Xiaoping and the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017).

Li argues that Marx and Engels first attacked the current's theoretical pillars: an abstract, biological view of human nature and a gospel of universal love that rejected violent overthrow. Against this they set the view that the human essence is the ensemble of social relations and that communism is the real movement abolishing the existing state of things. Second, they traced its philosophical premises to Hegelian speculation and Feuerbach's humanism, which Li says detached French socialist writings from the conditions that produced them. Third, they exposed its petty-bourgeois class basis. The current feared both capital and the rising proletariat, and in Marx and Engels's account it became a scarecrow used by absolutist governments against the bourgeoisie.

For the present, Li draws three requirements. First, Marxism must remain the sole guiding ideology, and Li opposes pluralism in guiding thought, citing the principle that dropping the basic principles of scientific socialism means abandoning socialism. Second, the people must be the class basis of socialist practice, in contrast with the petty-bourgeois base of \"true socialism\". Third, theory must be combined with practice, so that socialism is neither applied dogmatically nor arbitrarily revised; Li relates this to the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the primary stage of socialism. Read the original if you want a Chinese study of how the \"true socialism\" critique is used to set criteria for judging claims to socialism today.
quoteEn: The class basis on which "true socialism" stood, and the class nature it represented, were thus fully exposed.
quoteZh: “真正的社会主义”所立足的阶级基础、代表的阶级性质则暴露无遗。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's line since the reform era, combining Marxism with China's national conditions.
An official thesis, formalised in the 1980s, holding that China is still in an early, long-lasting stage of socialist development.

glossary.zh: 新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The 19th Party Congress (2017) declared socialism with Chinese characteristics to have entered a new era. The article uses it to mark a new stage and a changed principal contradiction.

t: Characteristics of the early spread of the Communist Manifesto in China
st: Seen through the translation and dissemination of the Manifesto
zh: 《共产党宣言》在中国早期传播的特点
zhSub: 以《共产党宣言》的翻译和传播为视角
source: Contemporary World and Socialism (当代世界与社会主义), 2018 no. 3
paras: Why did the Communist Manifesto lead China's early Marxists to a communist faith, and how did it arrive? Wang argues that before the 1930s its translation and spread were uneven and gradual rather than synchronised. The article identifies four features: incremental translation with selective dissemination, multiple routes and multiple tiers of dissemination, subjective and "Chinese-style" interpretation, and a dual movement of dissemination and the adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions.

The article covers the period from about 1899 to the late 1920s. It traces translation from isolated sentences (1899–1907), through individual chapters (1908–1919), to Chen Wangdao's first full translation in 1920. It then compares the uses made of the text by missionaries, bourgeois reformers, bourgeois revolutionaries led by Sun Yat-sen, anarchists and early Marxists. Wang also follows the Manifesto's routes into China via Japan, France, Germany, English and Soviet Russia, and its spread through newspapers, schools, societies, publishers, handwritten copies and workers' schools.

Wang's central claim is that every group read the Manifesto for its own purposes. Zhu Zhixin took up class struggle and Ye Xiasheng the ten measures of chapter two, both in support of Sun's Three Principles of the People. Among Marxists, Li Dazhao stressed historical materialism and Chen Duxiu the dictatorship of the proletariat, but all did so out of conviction. Wang says translation variation widened or narrowed meanings: citing Gao Fang, the final slogan had 57 renderings before the 1930s. Sun equated communism with his "principle of people's livelihood". Others likened it to traditional Chinese ideals of great harmony and equalisation. Wang holds that such readings eased acceptance but risked distortion and "mechanical application".

Wang concludes that early Marxists differed from other groups because they neither smuggled in their own agenda nor spread the text for its own sake. They used it to analyse and solve China's practical problems, as in Li Dazhao's call to apply historical materialism to China and Mao Zedong's rural investigations. In this account, belief was formed and strengthened through the interplay of dissemination and adaptation. Wang urges Communists, now that socialism with Chinese characteristics has entered a new era, to keep studying the classics and hold to the Party's founding mission. Read the original if you want a detailed account of translators, routes and interpretive disputes in the Manifesto's early Chinese reception, as presented in official Chinese scholarship.
quoteEn: The faith of the early Marxists was gradually established and continually reinforced in practice.
quoteZh: 早期马克思主义者的信仰逐渐确立,并在实践中不断得到强化。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's theory and path of socialist development since the reform era. The article refers to its entry into a "new era".

glossary.en: adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions
glossary.explanation: The Party's term for applying Marxist theory to China's concrete circumstances and fusing it with Chinese conditions and culture. Mao Zedong popularised it in the late 1930s.
Sun Yat-sen's revolutionary doctrine of nationalism, democracy and people's livelihood (minsheng). The article says bourgeois revolutionaries drew selectively on the Manifesto to support it.
The Marxist theory that material production and economic relations shape social and political life. The article says Li Dazhao selected it as the Manifesto's core.
The Marxist-Leninist concept of working-class political rule in the transition from capitalism to socialism. The article says Chen Duxiu emphasised it.

t: New growth areas in contemporary foreign Marxism studies
zh: 当代国外马克思主义研究的新增长点
paras: Lei Yu argues that ideology, the production of space, world-systems and biopolitics are the new growth points in contemporary Marxism outside China. Reading these four themes as accounts of capitalism, the author suggests, allows researchers to form a realistic judgement, a theoretical grasp and a critical reflection on capitalism today. The piece appeared in China Social Sciences Today in 2018.

The commentary takes each theme in turn. On ideology it follows Lukács, Althusser and Žižek; on space, Lefebvre, Harvey, Soja and Castells; on world-systems, Wallerstein and dependency theory; on biopolitics, Foucault and the Italian line of Negri, Esposito and Agamben.

Lei presents these as ways of seeing how capitalism has become more multi-dimensional and more concealed. Lefebvre's shift from producing commodities in space to producing space itself is read as a change in capitalism's reproduction. Wallerstein's world economy is linked to Luxemburg and Lenin, and to the unevenness between centre and periphery. Each theme comes with a warning. Ideology must be tied to its material base, because ideology has no history of its own. Spatial studies must not turn metaphysical or discuss cities in isolation. Left thinkers who worship contingency are said to drift into opportunism and to over-politicise everything.

Lei concludes that capitalism should be examined from several angles, with the full history of Marxist thought and capitalism's empirical history as reference points. The author names Marx's historical dialectics, which starts from material life and social being, as the key methodology for studying contemporary capitalism. Read the original if you want a short Chinese-academy overview of how these four strands of foreign Marxism are framed and cautioned against.
quoteEn: Therefore, using Marx's historical dialectics to see through and grasp the development of contemporary capitalism will be an important methodology for theoretical research.
quoteZh: 因此,以马克思历史辩证法来透视和把握当代资本主义的发展,将是理论研究的重要方法论。

t: Five bright spots in the recent development and changes of communist parties abroad
zh: 当今国外共产党发展变化的五大亮点
paras: Writing in 2018, the 170th anniversary year of the Communist Manifesto, Chai Shangjin asks how communist parties outside China are faring and what is changing in them. The article argues that these parties are, on the whole, in a clear upward phase after the low point that followed the Soviet collapse. Chai also stresses that they face serious challenges, notably populism and right-wing pressure.

The article is organised around five features: the regrouping of strength, the strengthening of organisation, "keeping to fundamentals while innovating" in theory, unity and cooperation within the left, and a growing tendency to "look east" to China. Chai surveys ruling parties (Vietnam, Cuba, Laos, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Nepal) and non-ruling parties in Western Europe, Japan, South Asia, South Africa, Latin America, Russia and Central Asia. Membership and seat figures are cited party by party.

Chai's central claim is that parties recover where they rebuild organisation and update theory without abandoning Marxism. Parties that stuck to isolated doctrinal statements, or that gave up Marxist guidance and democratic centralism for "flattened" structures, lost members and split, as in Moldova. Parties that restored democratic centralism, strengthened grassroots branches and used online tools, such as those in France, Spain and Vietnam, are presented as gaining strength. Chai says many parties now treat Marxism as a guide to action, reject a single model of socialism and pursue parliamentary or legal struggle and left alliances. In his account, the Marx bicentenary conference in Shenzhen in May 2018, with over 70 parties from 50 countries, showed foreign parties' interest in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the Belt and Road Initiative and China's poverty reduction.

Chai concludes that the central problem for these parties is how to exercise political leadership within broad left fronts while populism squeezes their base. He says China should treat foreign doubts, such as criticism of its wealth gap, rationally. He adds that China neither "imports" nor "exports" models, and that the success of socialism with Chinese characteristics will advance the world socialist movement. Read the original if you want a party-by-party overview, with membership and seat figures, of foreign communist parties as seen from a Chinese Party-affiliated perspective in 2018.
quoteEn: Only through innovation can communist parties escape their present predicament and effectively attract and lead the people in the struggle for socialism.
quoteZh: 共产党只有创新,才能摆脱目前困境,有效吸引和领导人民开展社会主义斗争。

glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng

glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.
A Chinese infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with Asia, Africa and Europe.
The official name for the Chinese Party-state's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.
A Leninist organisational principle combining discussion within the party with binding unity of action once decisions are taken.

t: On China's approach to reforming global governance
zh: 论全球治理改革的中国方案
paras: Writing in 2018, Li Dan asks how China has responded to the crisis of economic globalization and of global governance, and what its proposal for reform contains. The article argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) China's leaders, with Xi Jinping at the centre, have produced a fairly systematic 'Chinese approach' (Zhongguo fang'an) to global governance. In Li's account this approach comes at a time when Western-led governance is failing, and it leaves a distinct Chinese imprint on the new round of globalization.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why reform of the global governance system is both possible and historically necessary. It points to the shift of economic weight from West to East and to what it calls the failure of US and European governance solutions. The second traces how the Chinese approach took shape in Xi's speeches from 2013 to 2017, from BRICS and G20 addresses through Davos and Geneva to the 19th Party Congress (2017), and in the practice of the Belt and Road Initiative. The third and longest part describes the approach under five headings: governance actors, methods, platforms, paths and goals.

Li diagnoses a 'governance deficit' in the expanding range of global problems, the fragmentation of governing actors and the mismatch between demand and supply. On this reading, the present system is really hegemonic 'world governance' by the West, above all the United States, with the Group of Seven at its core. The Chinese approach, by contrast, is said to insist on equal participation and to reject both domination by one state and rule by a few. It favours rule-based consultation, with new and old institutions working side by side: the UN, the WTO, the IMF and the World Bank are kept and added to by the G20, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and the Boao Forum. New financial bodies, including the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the BRICS bank, are included as well. It also seeks greater representation and institutional power for developing countries.

Li concludes that the goal is a community with a shared future for mankind and an inclusive, win-win globalization. The article notes that the idea has been written into several UN resolutions. It expects the Chinese approach to be enriched as China moves from follower to builder and leader, with the Belt and Road Initiative treated as the practical test of Xi's view of global governance. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars present Xi Jinping's global governance thinking, with citations to his speeches from 2013 to 2017.
quoteEn: Equal joint governance is the primary difference between China's governance approach and historical British colonial governance and American hegemonic governance.
quoteZh: 平等共治是中国治理方案与历史上英国殖民治理和美国霸权治理的首要区别。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humankind
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first used internationally in 2013. It presents the interests and fates of all countries as bound together, and it is now a central slogan of Chinese foreign policy.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure, trade and investment links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond, along overland and maritime routes.
A phrase used in official discourse for China's proposals on international problems, here global governance. The article treats it as a systematic body of ideas drawn from Xi Jinping's speeches.
A phrase for the gap between the world's growing need for governance and the inadequate supply of rules, institutions and ideas.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Can North Korea replicate the "Vietnam model"?
zh: 朝鲜可否复制“越南模式”
paras: Writing in 2018, after North Korea's sudden shifts in domestic and foreign policy, Pan and Zhou ask whether Pyongyang will follow China and Vietnam into socialist reform and opening up. Media reports said Kim Jong Un told South Korea's president he was willing to learn from the "Vietnam model", and US Secretary of State Pompeo urged North Korea to copy Vietnam's path. The authors answer that North Korea can draw on some Vietnamese practices but cannot replicate the model.

The article first defines the "Vietnam model", a term that has no formal definition, through three features of Vietnam's renovation: its economy, its politics and its foreign policy. It then compares North Korea with Vietnam on the country's own intentions, its stage of socialist development, the historical formation of political power, the context of change, and external conditions, including relations with the United States, the two Koreas and China.

The authors describe the Vietnam model as a market-led, export-oriented economy with encouragement of private enterprise, "controllable democracy" under Communist Party leadership, and a balancing foreign policy that draws closer to Washington against China. They argue that North Korea differs on each count. Vietnam regards itself as still in a transition to socialism, while North Korea holds to a self-reliant planned economy and the aim of a "strong and prosperous socialist state" that remains unfinished. Vietnam's dispersed leadership contrasts with North Korea's highly centralised power, which the authors trace to colonial-era political traditions, early factional strife and a military confrontation with the US–South Korea alliance. Vietnam began renovation in 1986 amid a regional shift to markets, whereas North Korea has announced a focus on economic development but, the authors stress, no marketisation or integration with the world economy.

The authors conclude that North Korea will study selected Vietnamese methods, especially how a socialist state moves from a command economy to using market mechanisms, but will not copy the model. They argue that US–Vietnam ties rest on a shared interest in balancing China, and that North Korea, committed to independence and with no core-interest conflict with China, will not serve as a US tool against Beijing. Pompeo, they predict, is likely to be disappointed. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly view, from 2018, comparing the Vietnamese and North Korean reform paths and the geopolitics around them.
quoteEn: Therefore, in terms of the path of socialist reform, North Korea's transformation cannot possibly be a complete copy of the Vietnam model, but it can draw on certain Vietnamese practices.
quoteZh: 因此, 从社会主义改革路径来说, 朝鲜变革不可能完全复制越南模式, 但可以借鉴越南的某些做法。

glossary.explanation: An informal label for Vietnam's market-oriented renovation (Doi Moi) since 1986. It has no official definition, and Western and Chinese commentators use it with different emphases.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the world economy that China began in 1978. The article uses it as a comparison point for Vietnam and North Korea.

t: Vietnam's anti-corruption drive: no longer afraid of "breaking the vase to catch the rat"?
zh: 越南反腐, 不再担心“逮鼠碎瓶”?
paras: Writing in early 2018, Pan Jin'e asks why Nguyen Phu Trong, General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam, has moved so forcefully against corruption when he once warned against smashing the vase while catching the rat. The article's answer is that Nguyen spent two years preparing the ground through ideological, institutional and legal measures. In Pan's view he now feels confident enough to drop the caution of his 2014 remark.

The commentary opens with Nguyen's October 2014 "catching the rat without breaking the vase" statement, which Vietnamese social media read as an excuse for inaction. It then turns to the post-APEC (2017) crackdown, above all the arrest and public trial of Dinh La Thang, a former Politburo member and Ho Chi Minh City Party secretary. Pan organises the case around four new features: scale and rank, the large sums and interest chains in banking and oil, procedural legality with suspicious timing, and a complicated, murky backstory.

Pan cites 205 first-instance corruption cases involving 433 people in 2017, and a trial of Dinh and 21 co-defendants with media access and defence lawyers. The article describes Dinh's illegal investment in Oceanbank and the losses of the state oil group, which linked several state-owned enterprises. It reads the procedure as evidence of progress toward a socialist state under the rule of law. It also notes that the arrests came before the 2015 Criminal Code took effect on 1 January 2018, which dropped the charge used against Dinh. Some observers, Pan reports, see factional motives, since Dinh was promoted by former prime minister Nguyen Tan Dung, who is placed in a "southern" faction opposed to Nguyen Phu Trong's "northern" one. Disputed accounts of how fugitive Trinh Xuan Thanh returned, and the arrest of another fugitive, suggest further cases.

Pan concludes that final verdicts and the pursuit of bigger "tigers" remain uncertain, but that Nguyen now voices new slogans: "no one can be an outsider" and a well-fed fire will light even green wood. Since Vietnam has sent delegations to China to learn anti-corruption methods, Pan suggests that success would be a new version of following China in "crossing the river by feeling the stones". Read the original if you want a short Chinese scholarly reading of Vietnam's 2017–18 anti-corruption campaign and its links to China's experience.
quoteEn: Judging by developments over the past two years, Nguyen Phu Trong advanced step by step, preparing thoroughly for a comprehensive anti-corruption drive through ideological and public-opinion groundwork and by strengthening Party institutions, anti-corruption mechanisms and the legal system.
quoteZh: 从过去两年形势的发展过程来看, 越共总书记阮富仲步步为营, 先后通过思想和舆论造势、加强党内制度建设、政党和反腐机制建设、法律建设等多种途径, 为开展全面反腐做了充分准备。

glossary.en: catching the rat without breaking the vase
glossary.literal: catch the rat, smash the vase theory
glossary.explanation: A saying Nguyen Phu Trong used in 2014, attributed to Ho Chi Minh and earlier leaders. It means pursuing corrupt officials without damaging political stability and development.

glossary.en: crossing the river by feeling the stones
glossary.explanation: A phrase associated with Deng Xiaoping's reform era in China, meaning cautious experimentation without a fixed blueprint.

t: Contributing Chinese solutions to the world
zh: 向世界贡献中国方案
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in October 2018, Chen Shuguang asks how China can respond to the shared problems facing humanity: uneven world economic development, weak global governance, rising protectionism and frequent regional crises. The author's answer is that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era supplies "Chinese solutions" (Zhongguo fang'an) in three areas: development, governance and civilisation.

The commentary is organised under three headings. The first covers development, the second global governance, and the third civilisation. Each sets out a Chinese position and contrasts it with the existing order, which the author describes as built and dominated by the United States and the West. Throughout, the Belt and Road Initiative serves as the main example.

On development, Chen says China addresses the global "development deficit" through ideas (an open, inclusive and balanced vision of economic globalisation), through new multilateral financial institutions such as the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the Silk Road Fund, and through the Belt and Road Initiative. On governance, the author argues that China wants to reform rather than overthrow the present order, defending the purposes and principles of the UN Charter. Chen sets "extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits" against a model of rule by a few great powers, and presents the Belt and Road as an open platform, not a geopolitical bloc. On civilisation, Chen holds that earlier international norms were the globalisation of Western spirit and cultural hegemony. The article proposes in its place a community with a shared future for mankind, common human values, equality among civilisations and a "correct approach to justice and interests".

Chen concludes that China's success shows the Western model, Western-style institutions and the capitalist road are not the only path to modernisation, and that each nation may choose its own path and system. The author says these proposals lay a basis for rebuilding the rationality of international exchange in an era of globalisation. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese commentators in 2018 framed Beijing's contributions to global development, governance and civilisational dialogue.
quoteEn: China does not intend to start anew or overturn the existing order, but to defend the international order centred on the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and to push it in a more just and reasonable direction.
quoteZh: 中国不是要另起炉灶、推倒重来，而是要捍卫以联合国宪章宗旨和原则为核心的国际秩序，推动国际秩序朝着更加公正合理的方向发展。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A Chinese-led programme of infrastructure and economic cooperation announced in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–2013, holding that countries' fates are interdependent and calling for cooperation and a more equitable international order.
A standard phrase in official discourse for China's proposals on global problems, usually paired with "Chinese wisdom".

glossary.pinyin: gòng shāng gòng jiàn gòng xiǎng
glossary.en: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
glossary.literal: joint discussion, joint construction, joint sharing
glossary.explanation: The official formula for China's approach to global governance and the Belt and Road: decisions made jointly, projects built jointly, and benefits shared.

glossary.en: correct approach to justice and interests
glossary.literal: correct view of righteousness and interests
glossary.explanation: A principle Xi Jinping put forward in 2013 for dealing with other countries, giving priority to moral considerations (yi) alongside material interests (li), especially in relations with developing countries.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The fading "American Dream"
zh: 褪色的“美国梦”
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao, 2018, no. 19), Huang Ben takes up the "American Dream", which, the author says, many Chinese treat as a beacon while knowing little of American history or of ordinary American life. The article argues that the Dream did exist in certain periods, but only because of particular opportunities and policies, and that it is now fading under present-day social and economic policy.

The commentary first traces the Dream through four historical phases: the Homestead Act era of the late nineteenth century, the early twentieth-century industrial period, the Cold War boom of the 1950s–70s, and the post-Cold War decades. It then examines the policy basis of the Cold War period (wage policy, welfare and mass public higher education, and the incorporation of trade unions) and compares it with current figures on wages, university fees and young people's living conditions.

Huang's central claim is that the Dream's high point was a product of external pressure rather than benevolence. In the author's account, the successes of the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe in the 1950s and 60s led the American ruling class to placate wage earners, by sharing growth, expanding welfare and cheap public universities, and drawing union leaders into the Democratic Party, so that workers would not turn to socialism. After the upheavals in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe, Huang argues, this motive disappeared. The author cites a 2017 Brookings report that real wage growth averaged only 0.2 percentage points a year from 1973 to 2016, along with soaring tuition and 2015 data showing 40 per cent of young Americans living with relatives. Huang attributes stagnation to the gains going to Wall Street and Silicon Valley elites and to the decline of unions.

Huang concludes that the Cold War was won by the American ruling class, not by its wage earners, and that class stratification is hardening and class contradictions are sharpening. The author nonetheless cautions that the United States remains the largest economy and a technological leader, retaining hegemony through its trade advantages and dollar seigniorage, and that its decline will be slow. China, Huang says, should simply do its own work well so that the Chinese Dream of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation reaches every citizen. Read the original if you want an example of how a Party journal in 2018 framed the decline of the American Dream through class analysis and the Cold War.
quoteEn: The victory in the Cold War belongs to the American ruling class, not to American wage earners.
quoteZh: 冷战的胜利，属于美国统治阶级，而不属于美国工薪阶层。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-standing Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's slogan of the Chinese Dream.
A slogan promoted by Xi Jinping from 2012, which links national rejuvenation with the well-being of individual citizens.
A Party-run theoretical journal, published biweekly under the Qiushi Journal group, which carries commentary on ideology and current affairs.

t: Beware of the discourse traps deliberately set by the West
zh: 警惕西方蓄意设置的话语陷阱
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, Zhao asks how Chinese Party members and scholars should treat the "trap" theories that Western politicians and scholars have attached to China's rise. The article argues that these theories are tools in a contest over discourse power, and that they should be analysed critically rather than adopted wholesale. In Zhao's view, uncritical use of them risks pulling Chinese thinking onto a logical track set by Western discourse.

The piece has three parts. The first places the struggle for discourse power in the history of ideological conflict, from Cold War "peaceful evolution" to the "end of history" and "clash of civilizations" theses. It draws on Michel Foucault's idea that discourse is a form of power, and on speeches by Xi Jinping on ideological work. The second part examines three theories in turn: the "Thucydides Trap", the "middle-income trap" and the "Tacitus Trap". The third part sets out three tasks for the Party.

Zhao's central move is to treat each theory differently while placing all three within the discourse contest. The "Thucydides Trap", Zhao says, was not Thucydides' own idea but was coined by Graham Allison, and Zhao cites Qian Chengdan's view that it reflects Cold War thinking. The "middle-income trap" originates in a World Bank report. Zhao presents it as a real development bottleneck that China can pass through, citing per capita GDP of 8,600 US dollars in 2017 and the supply-side structural reform agenda. The "Tacitus Trap" is a modern extrapolation from a line in Tacitus. Zhao treats it as a warning about public trust, which Xi Jinping applied to Party–mass relations in 2014. For the three tasks, Zhao calls for studying influential ideas and answering them, strengthening Marxist theoretical education, and building a socialist ideology with real cohesion. This also means a Chinese discourse system that avoids using Western concepts to trim and analyse Chinese reality.

Zhao concludes that Communists need theoretical clarity in order to have political clarity, and that Western theories and concepts should not be applied mechanically to Chinese practice. The author urges the Party to ground analysis in Marxism, to take up Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and to strengthen the Four-sphere Confidence. Read the original if you want an example of how official Party commentary in 2018 framed Western concepts about China as ideological contests, and how it handled the three "traps" differently.
quoteEn: Only with theoretical clarity can there be political clarity, and only with theoretical firmness can there be political firmness.
quoteZh: 只有理论上清醒才能有政治上清醒，只有理论上坚定才能有政治上坚定

glossary.explanation: The capacity to shape the terms of debate and have one's ideas accepted. Chinese official writing links it to ideological leadership and to international influence.
A term used in Chinese Party writing for alleged Western efforts to bring about the political transformation of socialist states by non-military means, such as ideas, culture and media.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up. It combines Party leadership, a socialist system and a market-oriented economy.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, a slogan promoted by the Party leadership.

t: Characteristics and essence of China–US relations in the new era
st: With an analysis of Soviet diplomatic errors in its later period and the mistaken concept of a "new Cold War"
zh: 新时代中美关系特点及其本质
zhSub: 兼析苏联后期的外交失误及目前“新冷战”概念的错误
paras: Writing in 2018, after the 19th Party Congress (2017), Zhang Wenmu asks what the essence of China–US relations is in the new era, and what foreign policy follows from it. The article argues that the rivalry is at bottom a contest between systems: not the US as a nation-state against China, but Wall Street's financial and arms capital and its White House agents against a socialist China led by the Communist Party. On this basis Zhang rejects the notion of a "new Cold War".

The article has five sections. It sets out the system-competition thesis, argues that the US has become an enemy of world peace, and takes up the first question of Chinese diplomacy, namely who are enemies and who are friends. It then criticises the "new Cold War" concept, and ends with strategy and tactics for the "great struggle" with new historical features. Zhang draws heavily on Mao Zedong's remarks and on Lenin's theory of imperialism, and cites Eisenhower, George Kennan, Henry Kissinger and the economist John Ross.

Zhang contends that since the Second World War the US has been captured by the military-industrial complex, and that under Trump the political base of finance capital has shifted from petrodollars to arms dollars, which profit from battlefields rather than markets. Peace therefore becomes the enemy of US policy, and China, as the side defending peace, holds the moral high ground. Citing figures on Western investment banks' declining share in Asia and on slow growth in the G7, Zhang follows Lenin in holding that shifting power relations under capitalism tend towards force. Zhang reads the Soviet acceptance of the "cold war" framing, which obscured arms-capital interests, as a costly error. Mao's "three worlds" analysis is held up as the dialectical alternative. In Zhang's view, the "new Cold War" label would push Americans and Europeans to the other side and waste China's advantage of having friends everywhere.

Zhang concludes that China should separate monopoly-capital "America" from the American nation, and treat the developing countries as natural allies. Time is on China's side, as Zhang sees it, since the US now resembles the late Soviet Union and Trump resembles Khrushchev. China should avoid Brezhnev-style across-the-board offensives and follow Mao's line of "wearing down time without damaging vitality": an overall defence combined with local offensives, as in the 1962 border war with India. Read the original if you want an example of a Chinese Marxist-Leninist, Mao-inspired reading of US–China rivalry as class and system conflict.
quoteEn: The essence of the competition in China–US relations in the new era is a competition between systems.
quoteZh: 新时代中美关系的竞争本质是制度竞争。

glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's 1970s division of the world into the superpowers (US and USSR), the intermediate developed countries, and the developing countries. It guided China's foreign policy in that decade.
A label used in Chinese and foreign commentary for deepening US–China rivalry. Zhang rejects it as analytically misleading.
A phrase from Mao's 1941 telegrams on long-term struggle against Japan, meaning to endure and avoid decisive confrontation while the balance of forces is unfavourable.

t: Forty years of reform and opening up and theoretical confidence in socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 改革开放40年与中国特色社会主义理论自信
paras: Writing in 2018, the fortieth anniversary of reform and opening up, Yang Chao asks where the theoretical confidence of socialism with Chinese characteristics comes from. The article argues that a high degree of theoretical consciousness and confidence is one of the most distinctive features of this socialism. In Yang's account, the clearest sign of that confidence is the steady emergence of theoretical achievements and a mature theoretical system over four decades. It now stands higher and firmer, Yang says, as socialism with Chinese characteristics has entered a new era.

The article traces the confidence to the practice of reform and opening up since the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), and organises the discussion into four sources. These are the thought-liberation movements that laid the intellectual basis, the creative answers given to the questions of each period, the achievements that serve as practical proof, and the creations of the people as an inexhaustible source of momentum. A closing section links the argument to the guidance given to deepening reform in the new era.

Yang's first move is to present thought liberation as the precondition of every theoretical breakthrough, from the debate on the criterion of truth to the primary stage of socialism and the new era. It produced a line of theory, listed as Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Second, the author holds that practice has verified the theory. Yang cites the economy's rise to second in the world and per capita GDP growth from 155 dollars in 1978 to 8,516 dollars in 2016. Third, drawing on historical materialism, Yang describes the theory as the people's own. In this reading it grew from initiatives such as the Xiaogang household contract system and township enterprises, and it is confirmed by popular acceptance.

Yang concludes that Xi Jinping Thought gives scientific guidance for deepening reform and opening up in the new era and shows the vitality of Marxism. The article holds that upholding socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era is upholding scientific socialism, and that upholding Xi Jinping Thought is upholding Marxism. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party theorists in 2018 justified theoretical confidence by linking thought liberation, theoretical innovation, practical results and the people's role.
quoteEn: An important meaning of theoretical confidence is to use the basic standpoint, viewpoints and methods of Marxism to study and solve practical and epochal questions, distilling new theories with scholarly rigour and summarising new practices that reflect underlying regularities.
quoteZh: 理论自信的重要意蕴，就是运用马克思主义基本立场、观点、方法对实践和时代课题进行研究和解决，提炼出有学理性的新理论，概括出有规律性的新实践

glossary.explanation: One of the 'confidences' stressed in Party discourse: conviction in the scientific validity of the Party's theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It was later grouped with confidence in the path, system and culture.
The Party's official name for its path of socialism since reform and opening up, combining a socialist political system with market-oriented reforms.
The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978, introducing economic reform at home and opening to the outside world.
The official thesis that China, because of its low level of productive forces, will remain for a long historical period in an early stage of socialism.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party Constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.
A guiding concept of the Hu Jintao era, stressing people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.
A theory associated with Jiang Zemin, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.

t: The contemporary value and world significance of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era
zh: 新时代中国特色社会主义的当代价值与世界意义
paras: Writing in 2018, Li Haiping asks what socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era means beyond China itself. The article argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era belongs to the world as well as to China. In Li's account, its rise has changed China, is reshaping the world order, and offers fresh hope for peace and development.

The article is organised under four headings. They cover the opening of a new stage in the adaptation of Marxism to China and to the times, a new path to modernization, answers to the problems of world socialism, and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind. Li draws on statements by Engels, Deng Xiaoping, Lenin and Xi Jinping, and on a list of Party concepts developed since reform and opening up.

Li's central claim is that socialism with Chinese characteristics has broken the Western template of modernization. In the author's account, China moved from poverty to a moderately prosperous society in about forty years, without territorial expansion, colonial plunder or the logic of capital ruling over labour. This is presented as a second successful and just road to modernization, a model for developing countries trapped by copying the West. Li also argues that China's persistence after the Soviet collapse refuted the 'end of history' thesis. Set against financial and debt crises in the West and turmoil elsewhere, China is described as having answered, in theory, line and practice, the question of socialism's future in a backward country. Li adds that China has contributed over 30 per cent of world economic growth for several years and that its proposals on security, development and global governance respond to global problems.

Li concludes that socialism with Chinese characteristics has opened a new realm for scientific socialism, revived world socialism in the twenty-first century and moved the international communist movement into a new stage. The author expects the system's advantages to become more evident and its influence to grow, while acknowledging heavier tasks and greater risks ahead. Read the original if you want a representative example of how the official Chinese narrative framed the global significance of the new era in 2018.
quoteEn: The Chinese road has not only changed China's own historical fate and its former backwardness; it has also ended the linear view of history in which the Western model rules the world, opening up the second successful and just road to modernization in human society.
quoteZh: 中国道路不仅改变了自己的历史命运，更改变了原来落后的面貌，也终结了西方模式主宰世界的线性史观，开辟了人类社会第二条现代化的成功之路、正义之路

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name of Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017. It is presented as the current stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path since reform and opening up. It combines Marxist principles with China's conditions, including a socialist market economy.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012. It calls for shared security, development and global governance through multilateral cooperation.
The policy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented economic reform and opening to the outside world.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The US trade war cannot change the historical window of opportunity in which China finds itself
zh: 美国打贸易战改变不了我国所处的历史机遇期
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2018, as US–China trade frictions escalated, Wang Yiming takes up a question some people raise: does the US trade war alter the period of historical opportunity (lishi jiyuqi) in which China is developing? Wang answers that, although the war brings new variables, the opportunity period has not fundamentally changed. The answer depends, the author says, on distinguishing what has changed in the external environment from what has not.

The article has three parts. The first examines the external environment and argues that, despite visible changes, China still faces a relatively stable setting. The second assesses the impact on exports and growth while holding that the fundamentals of China's long-term economic prospects remain intact. The third sets out how to keep the opportunity period by turning external pressure into momentum for development, reform and opening up.

Wang's central argument is that four global trends persist: economic globalization, the era theme of peace and development, the collective rise of emerging markets, and reform of global governance. Domestically, the author lists what has "not changed": a middle-income group of over 400 million and a full industrial system; an economy with resilience, ample potential and room for manoeuvre; growth foundations in technology, human capital and infrastructure; and an improving economic structure, with consumption contributing 78.5% of growth in the first half of the year. Wang adds that China's socialist system can concentrate resources on major tasks. The author concedes that future opportunity will carry more risks and challenges than before and will depend on China's ability to shape the international economic environment.

Wang concludes that the best defence is a proactive strategy: keep development as the first priority, with emphasis on the real economy, innovation and domestic demand; press ahead with comprehensive deepening of reform, including shifting government functions, market access and property rights protection; and widen opening up, including looser foreign investment access, a better business environment and more autonomy for free trade pilot zones. Read the original if you want an official 2018 statement of how Chinese policy circles argued that the trade war would not derail China's trajectory.
quoteEn: It can be affirmed that, although the US trade war has brought new variables, the historical window of opportunity in which China finds itself will not undergo fundamental change as a result.
quoteZh: 可以肯定，虽然美国打贸易战带来了新的变数，但我国所处的历史机遇期并不会因此发生根本改变。

glossary.explanation: The policy course launched in 1978 that introduced market-oriented reforms and opened China to foreign trade and investment.

t: The achievements of 40 years of reform and opening up have won wide international praise
zh: 改革开放40年成就赢得国际社会广泛赞誉
paras: Writing in Qiushi on the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up (2018), Yu Yunquan and Sun Jingxin collect the views of foreign politicians, scholars, journalists and international officials on China's development since 1978. Their thesis is that these external voices help Chinese readers understand the historical standing and world impact of reform and opening up more fully, and approach the new era's reform with greater confidence.

The article is organised around four themes, each introduced by a quotation and supported by a series of named foreign commentators. These are the achievements of the 40 years; the reasons for their success; the effects on the world, especially developing countries; and the outlook for reform in the new era. The commentators come from Australia, the United States, Russia, Japan, Spain, France, Britain, Turkey, India, Brazil, South Korea, Ireland and elsewhere, along with the UN Secretary-General and the IMF head.

The authors argue that outside observers credit China with transforming its economy and technology and lifting more than 700 million people out of poverty, citing figures such as per capita GDP rising from about 200 dollars to over 8,000. For the causes, they report foreign views that stress the Party's capacity to correct errors, the advantages of socialism with Chinese characteristics, long-term planning, a people-centred approach and a pragmatic line of seeking truth from facts. They then present China as a driver of global growth, a pillar of multilateralism and peace, and a model for other countries, with one French commentator saying about 30 per cent of world growth came from China.

The authors conclude that the international community expects China to meet new challenges by deepening reform, citing Xi Jinping's remark that reform and opening up has no completion point. They add that if the Chinese people keep their original aspiration and work hard, reform will achieve more and have wider global influence. The piece is a curated showcase of favourable foreign opinion, with every claim carried by quotation. Read the original if you want to see how an official Party journal marshals international voices to support its account of reform and opening up in 2018.
quoteEn: Through these international perspectives, we can understand more fully the historical standing and world influence of reform and opening up, and throw ourselves with greater confidence and vigour into the great practice of reform and opening up in the new era.
quoteZh: 通过这些国际视角，我们可以更为全面地理解改革开放的历史地位和世界影响，更加自信昂扬地投入到新时代改革开放的伟大实践中。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched under Deng Xiaoping from 1978. Official discourse treats it as the defining feature of contemporary China's development.
The official name for China's current path and system, combining Party leadership, a socialist market economy and other features. It dates from the 1980s and is the central formula of Party ideology.

t: Continuously advancing the compilation, translation and study of Marxist classics in the new era
zh: 不断推进新时代马克思主义经典著作编译和研究工作
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2018, Wei Jianhua takes up the task of compiling, translating and studying the Marxist classics. Taking up Xi Jinping's call at the Marx bicentenary meeting for Communists to make reading the classics a habit and a spiritual pursuit, Wei argues that such work is the basic foundation of Marxist theoretical construction. The new era, in Wei's account, sets new and higher requirements for it.

The piece looks back on the 97 years of the Communist Party of China and the roughly century-long work of Chinese translators of the classics. It then sets out four principles that the work must always follow. These are a rigorous scientific attitude, a Marxist style of study, popularisation among the public, and a policy of producing both results and talent.

Wei argues that translators must supply more accurate texts and more reliable editions for what Xi calls the Party's compulsory course. Texts must also be read against the historical context of nineteenth-century Europe, while the work answers the questions of the present era. Wei holds that wrong views, such as the claim that Marxism is outdated, call for clear and engaging classic readers, especially for young people. Translating the classics is described as speaking on behalf of the sages, which demands accuracy, authority and firm political conviction.

Wei concludes that translator training should be as carefully tended as the texts themselves, following Xi's instruction to build a core corps of translators of the classics. This is meant to sustain theoretical work and to advance the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a concise official statement of how Party theorists framed the purposes and standards of classics translation in 2018.
quoteEn: We must cultivate translators of the classics with the same care with which we polish the classic translations themselves.
quoteZh: 要像精心锤炼经典译文那样，精心培育经典编译人才

t: Seeing the truth about the "state capitalism" charge
zh: 认清“国家资本主义”问题的真相
paras: Writing in 2018, as the United States opened a trade war with China, Qiu Shi takes up the label "state capitalism", which the article says is being attached to China's economic system. The article argues that the charge, which rests on China's state-owned enterprises, government intervention and industrial policy, misdescribes China. In the author's view, it also hides a deeper contest over development path and political system.

The piece is organised in four sections. It first asks who the real "state capitalists" are, drawing on Lenin's concept and on the history of Western capitalism and the United States. It then examines the motives of the "state capitalism" thesis, citing Hillary Clinton, Ian Bremmer, The Economist and Davos. The third section defends the socialist market economy against the charge. The last section turns to the treatment of state capitalism in Lenin's thought and in the early People's Republic.

Qiu's core argument is that pure free-market capitalism has never existed. Citing Marx on primitive accumulation, the article holds that state power has always driven capitalist development. It adds US figures on government spending and public employees, and the role of public investment in innovation. The author then separates market economy from capitalism: a market economy is a resource-allocation method that can combine with either system. State firms and government regulation exist in both, the article says, and the difference lies in whether they serve monopoly capital or the people. The charge, in this account, rests on a double standard that Qiu likens to Friedrich List's image of "kicking away the ladder". Qiu also says that Lenin and Mao Zedong treated state capitalism under socialism as a transitional form, which ended once socialist transformation was complete.

Qiu concludes that the socialist market economy under the Party's leadership, shaped by reform and opening up and by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, has nothing to do with "state capitalism". The article presents it as a successful Chinese approach that combines government and market, and says China will not take the "wrong road" of state capitalism. Read the original if you want an official Party-journal rebuttal of the "state capitalism" label, including its use of Lenin, Marx and Mao on the term.
quoteEn: Equating state-owned enterprises with "state capitalism" is also untenable.
quoteZh: 把国有企业等同于“国家资本主义”，也是站不住脚的。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining market allocation of resources with public ownership as the mainstay and Party leadership.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
A term used by Lenin for capitalism under state control or regulation. Western critics use it to describe China's economy, which the article rejects.

t: Time to end the "neo-colonialism" argument
zh: “新殖民主义论”可以休矣
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2018, after the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, Wang Yiwei takes up Western claims that China's growing role in Africa amounts to "neo-colonialism". The author argues that the charge contradicts the facts, that China's history and its development path give it no colonial disposition, and that the accusation reveals the strategic anxiety of certain Western forces rather than anything about China-Africa relations.

The commentary is built in four sections. It first discusses China's alleged lack of a colonial "gene", then presents the Belt and Road Initiative as an aid to decolonisation in Africa. The third section explains why the neo-colonial label is applied, and the last looks ahead to a closer China-Africa community with a shared future. Wang draws on the summit remarks of African leaders, Xi Jinping's speech, a McKinsey report and project statistics.

Wang's central move is a definitional one. Neo-colonialism, in the author's account, is a product of the capitalist system, in which developed capitalist states keep controlling and exploiting politically independent countries; it therefore cannot be pinned on a socialist China. Wang contrasts Zheng He's voyages with Western conquest, and describes colonial-era Africa as oriented towards European metropoles and marginalised in globalisation. In this reading, the Belt and Road Initiative, through infrastructure links, development finance and a "government plus market" model, helps Africa build internal connections and industrialise. Wang cites China's "five noes" (no interference in African countries' chosen paths, no meddling in internal affairs, no imposed will, no political conditions on aid, no political self-interest in investment) and figures such as the 60 billion US dollars pledged and the roads, ports and jobs expected from Chinese-built projects.

Wang concludes that China-Africa ties are South-South relations, fundamentally unlike the North-South relations between Africa and the West, and that aligning the Belt and Road Initiative with African and UN development agendas will create a "golden age" and a model for a community with a shared future for mankind. Wang presents African disillusion with Western models and US protectionism as pushing African states to "look east". Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese official-theory journal rebuts the neo-colonialism charge and frames China-Africa cooperation.
quoteEn: China's investment in Africa differs fundamentally from Western predatory investment; the essence of China-Africa cooperation is mutual benefit and win-win results.
quoteZh: 中国在非洲的投资和西方的掠夺式投资有根本区别，中非合作的本质是互惠共赢。

glossary.explanation: A China-led programme, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, to build infrastructure and economic links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping to describe a vision of international relations based on shared interests and cooperation. Chinese official texts also apply it to bilateral ties such as China-Africa relations.

t: Resolutely resisting the harassment and erosion of literary and artistic creation by historical nihilism
zh: 坚拒历史虚无主义对文艺创作的袭扰与侵蚀
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2018, Ai Fei argues that literature and art are a privileged entry point for historical nihilism, which uses their influence to spread, distort people's thinking and erode creative work. The article contends that resisting this is an important task for the literary and artistic field, and that the way to do so is a correct view of history and a people-centred orientation in creation.

The piece has three sections. The first traces the link between nihilism and modern Western art, from Nietzsche's "God is dead" to modernism and postmodernism after the two world wars. The second describes how historical nihilism has affected literary and artistic creation in China. The third sets out ways of consciously resisting it, drawing on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping.

Ai holds that nihilism arose in nineteenth-century Europe as capitalist values displaced Christian ones, and that modernist works such as Ulysses, Waiting for Godot and Guernica expressed the despair left by the world wars. In this account, nihilism spread globally under the banner of "modernity" through capitalist cultural production. For China, Ai says that since the "new period" some creators have treated anything historical or national as outdated and revolutionary themes as leftist, and have favoured the dark side of life for commercial appeal. As evidence, Ai cites the parodying of Yue Fei and Qin Hui, of The Yellow River Cantata ("the river roars" turned into "the year-end bonus roars"), and of the martyr Qiu Shaoyun. Ai says these cannot be read as mere entertainment: they negate history, revolution and Chinese culture, and in Xi Jinping's words aim at denying the guiding role of Marxism and the leadership of the Communist Party. Ai also links the resulting lack of artistic "peaks" to this tendency.

Ai concludes that writers must hold firmly to a correct view of history, nation, state and culture, and to cultural confidence. The author calls for art to go among the people and to place them at the centre of creation, citing Marx, Engels, Lenin on Gorky's Mother, Mao's Yan'an Talks and Xi's call to take root among the people and in life. Socialist realism, Ai argues, has produced works that nourished the people, which shows historical nihilism to be contrary to the laws of history. Read the original if you want an example of how a 2018 Party-journal article connects the critique of historical nihilism to literary policy and to the doctrine of art serving the people.
quoteEn: Only by moving towards the people, devoting oneself to the people, going deep among the people and writing about the people can literature and art effectively and fundamentally separate themselves from historical nihilism.
quoteZh: 只有走向人民、皈依人民、深入人民、书写人民，才是文艺同历史虚无主义彻底分离的有效途径和根本方略。

glossary.explanation: A term used in Party discourse for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's and revolution's history and the historical choice of socialism. It is frequently invoked in ideological campaigns.
A concept promoted under Xi Jinping, calling for confidence in China's traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture. It later became part of the Four-sphere Confidence.

glossary.literal: Yan'an Forum on Literature and Art
glossary.explanation: Meetings held by Mao Zedong in 1942 that set the Party's line that literature and art should serve the people and workers, peasants and soldiers.
A creative method, associated with the Soviet Union and adopted in China, that portrays social life realistically while serving socialist aims.

t: The Belt and Road Initiative opens a new era of win-win cooperation
zh: “一带一路”开启合作共赢新时代
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 30 August 2018, five years after the launch of the Belt and Road Initiative, Chai Shangjin argues that the initiative is both a major step in China's opening up and an engine of stable global growth. The article presents it as a practical platform for building a community with a shared future for mankind. Chai also describes it as offering "Chinese wisdom" and a "Chinese approach" for improving global development models and reforming global governance.

The commentary is organised in three sections. The first treats the initiative as a path of peaceful development and win-win cooperation, set against what Chai calls an unstable international environment. The second considers its contribution to the healthy development of economic globalisation. The third presents it as a platform for a community with a shared future for mankind, covering cultural exchange and green development. Chai draws throughout on speeches by Xi Jinping, including his remarks at the symposium marking the initiative's fifth anniversary.

Chai contends that the world faces unresolved problems of peace and development, widening wealth gaps and non-traditional security threats. He says the current US administration clings to the "law of the jungle" and a Cold War mentality. In Chai's account, the initiative is not a quest for Chinese economic hegemony. It promotes policy coordination, infrastructure connectivity, unimpeded trade, financial integration and closer people-to-people ties. Chai contrasts it with Western aid, which he says came with privatisation and marketisation conditions and failed to resolve developing countries' basic problems. He cites alignment with ASEAN, the Eurasian Economic Union and Kazakhstan's "Bright Path" policy, projects such as the Jakarta–Bandung and China–Laos railways and the ports of Gwadar and Piraeus, and praise from Joseph Stiglitz. On globalisation, Chai argues that Western-led globalisation widened inequality. He holds that the initiative shifts the emphasis to equal participation and mutual benefit, and that it helps African countries move out of the low end of global value chains.

Chai concludes that the initiative has moved from concept to practice, and he notes that United Nations resolutions have incorporated its content. He claims that China will share its development experience without interfering in others' internal affairs or exporting its social system or development model. He adds that green guidelines issued by Chinese government departments aim to make it an ecological road. In his view the initiative will help address the world's "deficits" in peace, development and governance. Read the original if you want an example of how official Chinese commentary in 2018 framed the Belt and Road Initiative in relation to globalisation, Western aid and the community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteEn: The Belt and Road is a road of civilisation: civilisations are made colourful by exchange and enriched by mutual learning.
quoteZh: “一带一路”是文明之路，文明因交流而多彩，文明因互鉴而丰富

glossary.explanation: A Chinese initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2013 to promote infrastructure, trade and financial links between China and countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13 as the guiding idea of Chinese foreign policy. It stresses shared interests, mutual respect and cooperation among states.
A standard phrase in Chinese foreign-policy language, used to present international relations as mutually beneficial rather than zero-sum.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Research on historical figures and the critique of historical nihilism
zh: 历史人物研究与历史虚无主义批判
paras: Zhou Jin takes up the way historical nihilism treats Party leaders and heroes, and asks how such figures should be studied and assessed. Writing in 2018, the author argues that historical nihilism uses the labels of "academic research", "restoring history" and "re-evaluation" to distort the history of the Party, the state and the army. In Zhou's account its aim is to undermine Marxism's guiding position, the historical inevitability of China's socialist path and the leadership of the Communist Party. Only a scientific theory and a seeking-truth-from-facts attitude, Zhou holds, allow history to serve as a "textbook" and a "sobering agent".

The article has three parts. The first describes four manifestations of nihilism in the study of historical figures. The second sets out the harms and the causes. The third proposes responses based on Marxist standards of evaluation. Examples include attacks on Mao Zedong, doubts about heroes such as the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain, Liu Hulan, Huang Jiguang and Lei Feng, and praise for Cixi, Yuan Shikai, Chiang Kai-shek and Wang Jingwei. Zhou also cites online games that mix up historical characters and the example of the Soviet Union.

Zhou argues that nihilism works by magnifying leaders' faults, using individual or minority memories, diaries and oral history to replace collective memory, and reversing right and wrong. The author says its effects are to dissolve mainstream ideology, promote Western "universal values" and political systems, question Party leadership and weaken national cohesion, especially among young internet users. Zhou lists causes: Western hostility, fast and uneven online media, and a backlash against idealised, flawless portrayals of heroes. The remedy rests on Xi Jinping's statement that leaders are people, not gods, and on his "six cannots" for judging figures within their historical conditions, avoiding both worship and wholesale negation.

Zhou calls for deeper research guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and a Marxist system for evaluating figures that rests on practice and historical materialism. The author also calls for legal tools, citing the 2014 Martyrs' Day decision and the Law on the Protection of Heroes and Martyrs, adopted in April 2018 and in force from 1 May. Historians, propaganda departments and media should collect and rebut representative nihilist claims and build public "immunity". Read the original if you want a clear example of the official Chinese framing of historical nihilism and of the policy and legal responses proposed in 2018.
quoteEn: The evaluation of historical figures must start from practice and uphold the principle that practice is the sole criterion for testing truth.
quoteZh: 评价历史人物必须从实践入手,坚持实践是检验真理的唯一标准。

glossary.explanation: A term used in Chinese Party discourse for views that are said to negate or distort the Party's history and the revolutionary and socialist record. It is used critically and often applied to revisionist or sceptical historiography.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.zh: 《中华人民共和国英雄烈士保护法》
glossary.pinyin: Zhōnghuá Rénmín Gònghéguó Yīngxióng Lièshì Bǎohù Fǎ
glossary.en: Law on the Protection of Heroes and Martyrs
