glossary.explanation: A law adopted by the NPC Standing Committee on 27 April 2018 and in force from 1 May 2018. It protects the names, reputations and honour of heroes and martyrs.

t: Socialism with Chinese characteristics as the consistent direction of reform and opening up
zh: 中国特色社会主义是改革开放始终坚持的方向
paras: Writing in 2018, on the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up, Zhu Bingyuan and Wang Haixia ask how reform and opening up relate to socialism with Chinese characteristics. They argue that upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics has been the theme of all the Party's theory and practice since reform began, and is the fundamental direction of China's development. In their view the two are unified in the goal of socialist modernization and national rejuvenation, in the Party's social revolution and self-reform, and in the overall strategic layouts of the 18th Party Congress era.

The article is organised in four parts. Each shows what reform and opening up produced: the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, its theoretical system, its institutions and its culture. The authors trace the theory from Deng Xiaoping Theory through the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

On the path, the authors say it is neither a copy of the classical Marxist template, a continuation of China's historical culture, a reprint of other socialist experiences, nor a version of Western modernization. They present it as the result of combining Marxism's universal truths with Chinese practice. On institutions, they quote the 18th Party Congress (2012) definition and divide the system into three levels: fundamental institutions (Party leadership, the people's congress system, socialist public ownership, the people's democratic dictatorship), basic institutions and specific institutions. The first must be upheld unwaveringly, the second improved while being upheld, and the third reformed and innovated as conditions change. On culture, they describe a socialist culture drawing on traditional Chinese civilization and revolutionary culture and driven by reform practice.

The authors conclude that the whole experience of 40 years comes down to joining Marxism's basic principles with China's practice and taking its own road. They also hold that the theoretical system represents another leap in the Sinicization of Marxism. They warn against "subversive errors" on what may and may not be changed, and against people who would negate the fundamental and basic institutions. They also cite the 19th Party Congress (2017) targets for institutional improvement by 2035 and for modernized national governance by the mid-century. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official 2018 narrative linking reform and opening up to the path, theory, institutions and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteEn: Wherever the historical process of reform and opening up began, there too began the intellectual process of theoretical generalization and theoretical innovation.
quoteZh: 改革开放的历史进程从哪里开始，理论概括和理论创新的思想进程也就从哪里开始。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official name for its model of socialism, introduced by Deng Xiaoping around 1982. It combines Marxism with China's conditions and includes market mechanisms under Party leadership.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into its constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept stressing people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.
Jiang Zemin's theory, which holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the majority.

t: How Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era upholds and develops Marxism
zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想对马克思主义的坚持和发展
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, Hou Huiqin asks what it means to uphold and develop Marxism, and argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era can be properly understood only from this standpoint. Hou presents Marxism and modern China as a community of shared destiny. Upholding and developing Marxism is described as the thread that holds that community together and as the true way of inheriting Marx's intellectual legacy.

The article is organised in three parts, each naming one condition for upholding and developing Marxism. The first concerns grasping the problems of the age, articulating its spirit and leading its currents. The second concerns establishing the people, with the modern working class at their core, as the subject of history. The third concerns a scientific attitude of pursuing truth and a theoretical character capable of self-reform. Hou draws on Mehring, Marx, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping's collected speeches.

In the first part, Hou argues that Marx succeeded because he posed the right question for his age: human emancipation had to mean the emancipation of the proletariat. Hou claims that today's world is undergoing a "great change unseen in a century" and that the new era is a scientific judgement on China's new historical position. In the second part, Hou contrasts individual-subject and people-subject views of history, treating historical materialism as a people's view of history. In this reading the people are an organic whole with the advanced class at its core, not a sum of individuals. Hou holds that the proletariat alone can durably represent the universal interests of humanity. Hou then links this to a people-centred approach, targeted poverty alleviation, a path of national strengthening that rejects the logic that a strong state must seek hegemony, and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind.

In the third part, Hou says Marxism renews itself through a critical spirit, citing Marx's revisions of the Communist Manifesto, and that the Chinese Communist Party combines belief with science, and values with truth. Hou describes Xi's image of governing as a continuing "examination" in which the times set the questions, the Party answers and the people grade. In Hou's account, the Party's capacity for the Party's self-reform stems from the objective needs of social revolution, not from abstract morality. Read the original if you want a Party-theorist's account, from 2018, of how Xi Jinping Thought is placed within the Marxist tradition through the themes of the age, the people as subject and self-revolution.
quoteEn: The people are not a collection of individuals but an organic whole, with the advanced class at its core, the labouring masses as its base, and all groups and individuals who accord with historical development as its outer extension.
quoteZh: 人民不是个人的集合体，而是以先进阶级为核心、劳动群众为基础、一切顺应历史发展的集团和个人为外延的有机整体。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi nián wèi yù zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great change unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse for a perceived deep shift in the global order, involving the rise of emerging economies and growing uncertainty.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping. It calls for peaceful development, cooperation and shared benefit in international relations.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself. It is often rendered as self-revolution in Chinese-language usage.
A policy launched under Xi Jinping that identifies poor households individually and directs aid to them, with the stated aim of eliminating poverty by 2020.

t: The US trade war highlights the hegemonic nature of the United States
zh: 美国发动贸易战凸显其霸权主义本质
paras: Writing in 2018, after the Trump administration imposed high tariffs on Chinese goods and restricted Chinese high-tech investment, He Zili asks why Washington chose such means and whether it can win. He argues that the trade deficit is only a pretext. In his account, the real motives are to preserve US hegemony and to contain China's development, and the administration cannot win the trade war.

The article has three parts. The first sets out five causes of the US–China trade deficit, using 2017 figures: 375.23 billion US dollars in goods, by US statistics. The second examines the administration's motives. The third explains why the policy is bound to fail.

On the deficit, He points to differences in development level and position in the industrial chain, contrasting industrial structures, and processing trade that shifts other economies' surpluses to China. He adds that US statistical methods overstate the deficit and that US export controls on high technology distort the division of labour. For He, the deficit is therefore an objective result, not evidence of unfair practices by China. On motives, He holds that Trump rightly admits American decline but wrongly blames the international order and China. He sees the decline as the product of the US political and economic system and of shifts in the global balance, and he treats Trump's policy as a copy of the views of Bannon and Navarro. On the outlook, He argues that the Triffin dilemma, the rigid demand of US consumers and industrial hollowing-out make the deficit impossible to eliminate. Tariffs would raise costs for American households and firms, he says, and push production abroad.

He concludes that the administration's unilateralism and protectionism undermine global governance and run against economic globalization. He grants that the policy of containment will not succeed but may interfere with China's development, which he says calls for serious attention. He states that China opposes this reverse globalization and will work with other countries to steer globalization in the right direction. Read the original if you want a representative 2018 Chinese official-academic account of the trade war, with its statistics and economic arguments.
quoteEn: The US trade deficit with China is determined jointly by multiple factors: the level of economic development, industrial structure, the international division of labour, statistical methods and policy.
quoteZh: 美国对华贸易出现逆差是由经济发展水平、产业结构、国际分工、统计方法以及政策等多重因素共同决定的

glossary.explanation: A paradox formulated by the economist Robert Triffin. A country whose currency serves as the global reserve currency must run external deficits to supply it, which in turn undermines confidence in that currency.
The decline of a country's manufacturing base as firms relocate production abroad or shift towards services and finance.
A trade mode in which imported materials or components are assembled or processed in China and the finished goods are re-exported.

t: Why China is able to lead new trends in world development
zh: 中国为什么能够引领世界发展新潮流
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, Hong Xianghua takes up a claim that China increasingly leads new trends in world development and asks why this is so. The answer given is threefold: the global influence of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the growing international acceptance of Chinese proposals, and the rising weight of China's economic, technological and green-energy contribution.

The commentary is organised in three numbered sections. The first addresses the reach of Xi Jinping's ideas at home and abroad. The second lists how Chinese concepts have been written into United Nations and other international documents. The third turns to China's role as contributor to global development, supported by growth and innovation figures for the five years since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

In the first section, Hong argues that ideas are the most powerful force in human history and that scientific ideas matching objective reality change the world most. As evidence of influence, the author cites the 2017 CPC in Dialogue with World Political Parties High-level Meeting and the circulation of The Governance of China, whose second volume is said to have exceeded 13 million copies. The second section, the core of the case, traces how "a community with a shared future for mankind" first entered UN resolutions in February and March 2017, and how the Belt and Road Initiative was written into a 2016 General Assembly resolution endorsed by 193 members. Hong adds that the principle of "extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits" and the call for "mass entrepreneurship and innovation" were also taken up by UN resolutions. The third section cites average annual growth of 7.1% against 2.7% for the world economy, a contribution to world growth above 30%, and contributions above 40% to technological innovation and to green energy.

Hong concludes that China is moving from supplier of material goods to supplier of public goods, and from participant in global governance to leader. The author presents China's development as benefiting developing countries and pushing the international order beyond zero-sum thinking. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Chinese official commentary in 2018 marshalled UN resolutions and economic statistics to support claims of growing Chinese global influence.
quoteEn: China is not only an engine of global economic growth, but even more an engine driving the global development agenda.
quoteZh: 中国不仅是全球经济增长的引擎，更是推动全球发展议程的引擎。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13, calling for cooperative international relations and shared development.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.pinyin: gòng shāng, gòng jiàn, gòng xiǎng
glossary.en: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
glossary.literal: joint consultation, joint construction, joint sharing
glossary.explanation: A Chinese formula for global governance and Belt and Road cooperation, stressing joint decision-making, joint building and shared results.
A slogan from the 2014–15 period, promoted by Premier Li Keqiang, encouraging start-ups and innovation among the general public.

t: Is China's modern history one of "sinking" or "rising"?
zh: 中国近代历史是“沉沦”还是“上升”？
paras: Zhang Haipeng takes up a long-running question in the historiography of modern China: whether the period is best described as a story of humiliation and decline ("sinking") or one that also contains advance ("rising"). Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, Zhang argues that neither of two established readings is sufficient. The author proposes instead that modern history follows a pattern of sinking to a "valley floor" and then rising.

The article first sets out the older view, which stressed the slide into a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society after the Opium War. It then covers the 1980s revision, which held that sinking and rising coexisted because "semi-capitalism" was a historical advance on feudalism. Zhang then offers a periodisation that extends modern history from about 80 years to 110 years, running to the 1940s.

Zhang grants each view some validity but holds that the first cannot explain later positive development, and that the second cannot explain the whole period. If there is an "abyss", the author says, it must have a bottom. Zhang places that bottom in the first two decades of the twentieth century, from the Boxer Protocol of 1901 to the warlord era, citing foreign aggression, the Twenty-One Demands, Yuan Shikai's imperial bid and warlord wars. After that, the author argues, the 1911 Revolution, the New Culture and May Fourth movements, the spread of Marxism and the founding of the Chinese Communist Party made rising factors the main trend, even as Japanese aggression worsened.

Zhang concludes that modern Chinese history is both a history of humiliation and a history of unyielding struggle for national independence and prosperity. Humiliation is concentrated in the sinking phase and struggle in the rising phase. In the author's account, the rising phase ended in victory in the war of resistance and laid the basis for China's modernization. Read the original if you want a concise statement of an officially published Chinese view on periodising modern history and on the "sinking" and "rising" debate.
quoteEn: This process in modern China of sinking to the "valley floor" and then rising embodies the law of development of modern Chinese history.
quoteZh: 近代中国这个“沉沦”到“谷底”，然后“上升”的过程，就体现了中国近代史的发展规律。

glossary.explanation: The standard Chinese Marxist characterisation of China from the Opium War (1840) to 1949, combining foreign imperialist domination with surviving feudal structures.
The long-term national project of making China a modern, developed country. Here it appears in a general historical sense, as the goal for which the victory of 1945 laid the foundations.

t: History is the best textbook
zh: 历史是最好的教科书
paras: Jin Chongji, in a short commentary published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, takes up Xi Jinping's remark that "history is the best textbook". The author argues that China's modern history, 1840–1949, must be understood if one is to grasp China's present conditions, and that younger Chinese readers now lack a feel for that past.

The piece opens with Xi's statements on the suffering and resistance of the Chinese nation in modern times and on patriotism as the core of the national spirit. It then treats the 109 years from 1840 to 1949 as a period of special significance, reflects on the generational gap in historical experience, and ends with a practical point about reading.

Jin presents modern China as a transitional stage between ancient China and a China striving for socialist modernization. In this account the period saw both decline and ascent, and ascent prevailed; the change from a country on the edge of extinction to one that stood up again is called a miracle in human history, won by generations of struggle. Jin quotes the scholar Ren Jiyu, who said that only those who lived through disaster and foreign bullying feel a deep sense of liberation, which later-born youth cannot share. Reading some modern history can partly make up for this.

Jin notes that the volume of new sources and scholarship on modern Chinese history is overwhelming for general readers. The author therefore calls for concise, high-quality reading matter that meets this need. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a senior Party historian justifies the study of modern history in terms of Xi Jinping's remarks.
quoteEn: Today's China has come from yesterday's China. Without understanding this, one cannot truly grasp China's actual national conditions, and it is hard to understand China's present deeply or how it moves toward tomorrow.
quoteZh: 今天的中国由昨天的中国走过来。不了解这些，谈不上真正懂得中国的实际国情，也很难做到深刻地了解中国的今天和如何走向明天。

t: Opposing historical nihilism is a serious struggle
zh: 反对历史虚无主义是一场严肃的斗争
paras: Writing in 2018, Wang Weiguang argues that opposing historical nihilism is a serious ideological and political struggle rather than a matter of scholarly disagreement. The short commentary contends that distorted accounts of modern Chinese history harm the public, especially young people, and that historians have a duty to counter them.

The piece opens with the 109 years from 1840 to 1949. Wang describes this as a period in which China sank into a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society, then rose up for independence, democracy and modernization and moved towards socialist modernization. It then turns to the way the internet, television, film and popular publishing have widened public access to historical knowledge, and to the problems this has brought.

Wang grants that popularisation has some value, but says much of it is driven by a mistaken view of history. The author points to anecdotal "unofficial history", costume-drama and time-travel storylines, and to social media accounts and forums that use slogans such as "re-evaluation", "restoring history" and "farewell to revolution". In Wang's account, these attack and negate modern Chinese history, the revolution, socialist construction and the histories of the Party, the People's Republic and the army. Wang says the aim is to weaken the historical legitimacy of the Communist Party's rule, the guiding status of Marxism and the socialist system.

Wang concludes that historical nihilism is fundamentally at odds with the Marxist scientific view of history. The author calls on the historical profession to adopt historical materialism, take up its social responsibility and spread scientific historical knowledge and research findings. Opposing nihilism is cast as a struggle between materialist and idealist views of history, and as a political struggle to uphold Marxism and socialism. Read the original if you want a brief, authoritative statement of how a senior Party theorist framed the campaign against historical nihilism in 2018.)
quoteEn: Upholding the Marxist materialist conception of history and opposing historical nihilism is a serious ideological struggle, a struggle between the materialist and idealist views of history, and above all a serious political struggle to uphold Marxism and socialism.
quoteZh: 坚持马克思主义唯物史观、反对历史虚无主义是一场严肃的思想斗争，是一场唯物主义历史观与唯心主义历史观的斗争，更是一场坚持马克思主义、坚持社会主义严肃的政治斗争。

glossary.explanation: In Party usage, a label for views seen as denying or belittling the Communist Party's revolutionary history, socialist construction and the legitimacy of its rule. It is used as a polemical category rather than a neutral scholarly term.
The Marxist theory that material production and class relations shape historical development. The article presents it as the correct standpoint against nihilist accounts.

t: The capitalist nature and inner paradox of Europe's new populism
zh: 欧洲新民粹主义的资本主义属性及其内在悖论
paras: Writing in 2018, Fu Mei and Li Zhen ask whether Europe's new populism, which has surged since the 2008 financial crisis, is really "anti-capitalist", "anti-establishment" and "anti-political", as it presents itself and as much Chinese scholarship assumes. They argue that it is not. In their account it is a product of capitalist modernity and an acute expression of capitalism's own contradictions, with a clearly capitalist character and an inner paradox.

The authors criticise Chinese studies for staying within political science and international relations and describing surface facts. They set out a Marxist critique in three parts. The first examines four features of new populism: its concept of "the people", its popular-sovereignty ideas, its political mobilisation and its value claims. The second traces its origins to the logic of capital and its institutional dilemma. The third tests its claim to deliver "the people's justice".

Fu and Li argue that the populist "people" is vague, elastic and instrumental, unlike the Marxist notion of a historical bloc led by an advanced class and based on working people. Its popular sovereignty descends from Rousseau's bourgeois tradition, which rests on private property, and it mobilises through a binary of "people" against "non-people". They contend that populists attack the shortcomings of representative democracy rather than the system itself. Populist demands to curb immigration, globalisation and the EU are read as reactions to capital's drive to accumulate. Once populist parties win office, the authors say, the logic of representative politics absorbs them into the "capital politics" they denounced. Drawing on Marx's critique of Proudhon and Lassalle, they hold that populist appeals to equality and fairness remain abstract moral ideas that ignore the productive basis of distribution.

The authors conclude that European new populism cannot resolve the social difficulties caused by capital or achieve genuine justice for the people. In their view it renews and reforms capitalism while deepening its crisis. They call for a clear-eyed judgement of the phenomenon. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist critique that treats European populism as an expression of the logic of capital, and that draws heavily on Marx's analysis of capital and justice.)
quoteEn: European new populism is a product of capitalist modernity, not a rejection of modernity.
quoteZh: 欧洲新民粹主义是资本主义现代性的产物，而非反现代性。

glossary.explanation: A political current that claims to speak for "the people" against elites. Chinese scholarship often divides it into three historical waves, the latest being the "new populism" in Europe and North America after 2008.
The principle, associated with Rousseau, that political authority derives from the people. The authors distinguish its bourgeois form from what they call genuine popular sovereignty.
Parliamentary democracy in which elected officials act for the electorate. The authors treat it as a political form shaped by capital's interests.

t: Seeing through the new changes in imperialism in the internet age
zh: 透视帝国主义在互联网时代的新变化
paras: Du asks whether Lenin's theory of imperialism still explains the present, given the long-running claims that 'ultra-imperialism', the 'transnational bourgeoisie' or a borderless 'Empire' have superseded it. Taking the May 2017 ransomware attack as a starting point, the article argues that imperialism has not changed in essence: plunder once carried out by military invasion and colonial conquest has taken new forms in the internet age, behind an appearance of openness and freedom.

The article has three parts. The first treats exploitation under technological monopoly, covering Apple, Intel and Microsoft, patents and technical standards, and US control of internet infrastructure. The second takes up the 'backlash' of financial imperialism, discussing Bitcoin, Hayek's idea of denationalising money, and the dark web. The third looks at how China can 'overtake on the curve' and defend itself.

Du's central move is to read the ransomware attack through Lenin. Because the attackers' tools came from the US National Security Agency, and because the ransom was demanded in Bitcoin, Du treats the attack as more than ordinary extortion. In this reading it is a form of kidnapping-style marketing by an international financial monopoly group, aimed at pushing up virtual currencies as a successor to the dollar's weakening hegemony. Du describes Bitcoin as another Ponzi scheme, citing the 2014 collapse of the MtGox exchange, and says it circulates mainly on the dark web as a channel for money laundering and illicit trade. Under technological monopoly, Du adds, technology is 'separated from labour' and becomes a tool for extracting value from developing countries, as in the Foxconn–Apple profit split. Du also rejects Hart and Negri's thesis of a peaceful Empire, arguing that monopoly in the technology era is dynamic yet still tends towards stagnation and decay.

Du concludes that monopoly contains the seeds of its own undoing. Technology blockades have pushed China to develop its own systems, such as the BeiDou navigation system, and Du expects such efforts to weaken the basis of hegemony. The author points to China's controls on Bitcoin trading and initial coin offerings, research on a state digital currency, the 2017 Cybersecurity Law and Xi Jinping's call to build a 'cyber power'. Du warns that a declining imperialism will become more aggressive, for instance by selling cyber weapons openly. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist applies Lenin's Imperialism to cryptocurrency, cybersecurity and technology rivalry with the United States.
quoteEn: When imperialism's technological advantage is no longer sufficient for intimidation and extortion, the foundations of hegemony will begin to collapse.
quoteZh: 当帝国主义的技术优势不足以进行恐吓勒索的时候，霸权的基础也就趋于瓦解了。

glossary.explanation: A term for imperialism dominated by finance capital, following Lenin's thesis that finance capital rather than industrial capital characterises the imperialist stage. Chinese scholars use it to describe the present-day world order.
The author's term for the dominant form of contemporary monopoly capitalism, in which market power rests on patents, standards and technical barriers rather than on sheer scale.
A goal stated by Xi Jinping in 2014, calling for China to become a strong power in cyberspace through network security and informatization.

t: Will the proletariat become a "useless class"?
zh: 无产阶级会沦为无用阶级吗？
paras: Writing in 2018, 170 years after the Communist Manifesto, Jiang Hongqun takes up the thesis of the Israeli historian Yuval Noah Harari that artificial intelligence will turn the proletariat into a "useless class". Jiang argues that this view, spread by the media as a successor to the "disappearance of the proletariat" thesis, is a new form of historical nihilism. Re-reading the Manifesto through historical materialism, Jiang contends that AI will exclude workers under capitalism but will not make the proletariat useless. The author concludes that the class facing obsolescence is the bourgeoisie.

The article first sets out Harari's argument from Homo Deus and Sapiens: algorithms will push manual and then mental workers out of employment, wealth will concentrate in a small elite, and the surplus masses will be kept occupied with drugs and computer games. Jiang then traces the origins of AI from manufactory and large-scale machine industry through Turing, the 1956 Dartmouth conference and corporate commercialisation. Next comes an analysis of why machines displace workers, followed by a look at working-class resistance, from Luddism to recent strikes against ride-hailing apps and self-driving legislation.

Jiang's central move is to treat AI as a means of production and constant capital that creates no surplus value itself. Under capitalist private ownership it is therefore a tool for extracting surplus value and sustaining the system, and it sharpens the opposition between capital and labour. Machines have displaced workers since the seventeenth century, and Jiang cites Marx's critique of the "compensation theory" and the law of the rising organic composition of capital against Harari's claim that new jobs always appear. The author notes that AI giants such as Apple and Google employ few workers. Jiang then argues that capitalism's basic contradiction cannot be removed by AI, so the "two inevitables" in the Manifesto still hold.

Jiang concedes that AI may cause unprecedented technological unemployment, but holds that this does not make workers incapable or useless. In the long run, drawing on Marx, Jiang reads AI as laying conditions for the liberation of labour and for large amounts of free time for everyone under a future communist society. The proletariat is therefore for Jiang a capable class that holds the future, while the "useless class" will be the bourgeoisie. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar answers Harari's popular AI-and-work thesis with the Manifesto and Capital, and how that argument is built from historical and contemporary examples.
quoteEn: In this sense, a "useless class" will indeed exist in the future society, but this class is not the proletariat but the bourgeoisie.
quoteZh: 在此意义上，未来社会的确存在一个“无用阶级”，但这个阶级不是无产阶级，而是资产阶级。

glossary.explanation: In Chinese Party discourse, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's and socialism's historical record and the revolutionary tradition. Here Jiang applies it to Harari's picture of the proletariat.
A phrase summarising the Manifesto's statement that the fall of the bourgeoisie and the victory of the proletariat are equally inevitable. It is used here as a statement of historical law.
The Marxist theory that history is driven by the development of productive forces and the relations of production, and by class struggle.

t: Valuable historical experience of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
zh: 马克思主义中国化的宝贵历史经验
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in August 2018, Liu Guangming asks what lessons the Communist Party of China has accumulated from nearly a century of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. The commentary argues that the Party has played the original and leading role in theoretical innovation, advancing Marxism's Sinicization alongside a great social revolution. Liu distils the record into five experiences, each phrased as something that "must" be upheld.

The article is a short commentary built as a numbered list of five principles. These are: holding to the basic tenets of Marxism; treating China's fine traditional culture as a root; putting the people at the centre; emphasising emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts and keeping pace with the times; and upholding Party leadership. Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is presented throughout as the latest result of this process.

Liu argues that the basic tenets, such as the basic contradictions of society, the decisive role of the productive forces and the people as makers of history, remain valid and supply the theoretical foundation for new ideas. Alongside them stands a second source, China's own cultural heritage. Liu cites Mao Zedong's 1938 and 1941 remarks to claim that Marxism in China has "two sets of ancestors" and that Marxism has merged with the nation's cultural genes. The people-centred stance is tied to the mass line: the cycle "masses–leadership–masses" is said to match "practice–knowledge–practice", so that popular practice becomes the source and carrier of theoretical innovation. Liu also warns that some Marxist parties in power became complacent and dogmatic and were eventually discarded by history. Citing Engels, the author says Marxism is a method, not a dogma.

On the fifth point, Liu contends that Marxism must be advanced by a party with no private interests of its own. Without Party leadership, the author says, Marxism would degenerate under the banner of innovation and "subversive errors" would follow. Liu concludes that the fundamental reason for the achievements lies in Party leadership and the guiding position of Sinicized Marxism. For the new era, Liu calls for firm support for the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and for strengthening the Four-sphere Confidence. Read the original if you want a compact, official-media statement of how Chinese Party theorists summarised the Sinicization of Marxism in 2018.
quoteEn: In advancing the Sinicization of Marxism, we must always closely combine Chinese realities and the development of the times in upholding and developing Marxism, and break the shackles of dogmatism and bookishness.
quoteZh: 推进马克思主义中国化，我们要始终紧密结合中国实际和时代发展来坚持和发展马克思主义，打破教条主义和本本主义的束缚

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party discourse referring to confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It was set out in its full four-part form under Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology under Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

The Party's term for applying Marxist principles to Chinese conditions and producing new theory, from Mao Zedong's thought onwards. Later official English usage often says adapting Marxism to the Chinese context.
A Maoist method of leadership in which the Party gathers the views of the masses, systematises them, and returns them as policy. It remains a core principle in Party discourse.

glossary.zh: 解放思想、实事求是、与时俱进
glossary.pinyin: jiěfàng sīxiǎng, shíshì qiúshì, yǔ shí jùjìn
glossary.en: emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts and keeping pace with the times
glossary.explanation: A formula describing the Party's ideological approach, combining Deng Xiaoping-era slogans with a later addition. It is presented as the essence of Marxism in China.

t: The theoretical fallacy and practical error of the US trade war
zh: 美国发动贸易摩擦的理论之谬与实践之误
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in August 2018, Chen Yongjun and Zhang Jihuan take up the trade dispute that the United States launched against China from the second half of 2017. They argue that the US action has no support in economic theory, whether classical Western, Marxist or the mainstream work of Paul Samuelson, and that it is a practical mistake. Their remedy for China is to return to negotiation, push opening up further and build dynamic comparative advantage.

The article opens by describing the deep interdependence of the two economies, which it says have been each other's largest trading partner. It then reads the dispute through three bodies of thought in turn: Adam Smith and David Ricardo, Marx and Engels, and Samuelson. A second half sets out three policy responses for China.

The authors' core move is to show that each tradition favours free trade. From Smith and Ricardo they argue that tariffs raise consumer prices and input costs for US firms, and they cite Caterpillar and General Motors and US Labor Department price data. From Engels's essay on protective tariffs and free trade they draw the claim that a country past its early stage should drop protection, and that the US now risks the 'endless spiral' Engels described for others. On Samuelson's 2004 article, they reject the reading that it justifies a trade war. They call it a numerical experiment on specially chosen cases, cite later work extending it, and note that Samuelson himself warned against protectionism.

For China, the authors call for 'fighting' only to bring the US back to the negotiating table, since trade wars are said to be lose-lose. They urge China to defend economic globalization, quoting Xi Jinping's Davos speech, and to form a new pattern of all-round opening. They also urge it to strengthen learning and innovation, following Joseph Stiglitz, while admitting China's gap in core technologies. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese commentary in 2018 used classical economics, Marxist texts and Samuelson to argue against US tariffs.
quoteEn: The trade friction the United States has launched, using China's technological progress as a pretext, has no theoretical basis.
quoteZh: 美国以中国技术进步为借口发动的贸易摩擦，是没有理论依据的。

t: Building a "amicable and clean" new type of government–business relationship
zh: 构建亲清新型政商关系
paras: Taking up the formula in Xi Jinping's report to the 19th Party Congress (2017), Fang Shinan asks how to build a new type of government–business relationship that is "amicable" (qin) and "clean" (qing). Fang argues that this relationship requires optimising the political ecology and the business ecology together, and that doing so matters for rooting out collusion between officials and businesspeople.

This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in 2018, has three parts. It first explains why the two ecologies must be improved jointly, then identifies the problems the new relationship targets, and finally sets out three areas where effort should be concentrated.

Fang defines the government–business relationship as a complex social tie that binds political power and administrative resources to economic interests and market behaviour. In Fang's account it reflects Party conduct, government conduct and wider social mores, and it is a requirement of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. The problems targeted lie in culture, institutions and the rule of law. Some officials act on power-centred and money-centred values and trade power for money, while some unscrupulous businesspeople court them with gifts. Institutions exist but are evaded, and respect for law is weak. Fang therefore calls for a culture built on socialist core values, institutional innovation that closes space for rent-seeking, stricter enforcement by discipline-inspection bodies, and a legal environment in which power operates openly.

Fang concludes that cleaning up government–business relations will deliver a clean political ecology and a transparent, law-based business ecology, supporting socialist modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-state commentary in 2018 framed the "amicable and clean" formula in terms of culture, institutions and law.
quoteEn: The state of government–business relations directly reflects Party conduct, government conduct and social mores, affects intra-Party political life and ecology as well as corporate culture and market order, and determines whether the political and market environments are good or bad and where they are heading.
quoteZh: 政商关系如何，直接反映党风、政风和社会风气，影响党内政治生活和党内政治生态以及企业文化和市场秩序，决定政治环境和市场环境的优劣和发展趋势。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official slogan for the Party's drive for discipline and anti-corruption, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A set of 24 characters in 12 values promoted officially since 2012, covering the national, social and individual levels.

t: China's great practice in improving global governance
zh: 中国完善全球治理的伟大实践
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 30 August 2018, marks five years of the Belt and Road Initiative. Wang Lei argues that the Initiative shows China, as the world's largest developing country, taking up its historical responsibility in major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics. In the author's account, it also offers a new approach to improving global development and global governance and to building a community with a shared future for mankind.

The piece has two parts. The first presents the Initiative as an important component of China's diplomacy in the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second considers how it contributes to reforming the global governance system, against a background of economic globalization meeting setbacks and anti-globalization sentiment rising.

Wang assesses the Initiative from four diplomatic angles. For global governance, its principles of joint consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits are said to go beyond zero-sum thinking, balance of power and power politics. For neighbourhood diplomacy, it reflects a "greater periphery" approach. For developing countries, it is said to promote North–South and South–South cooperation and the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. For major-country diplomacy, it has become a topic of policy communication with Russia, India, the United States, Japan, the EU and ASEAN. Domestically, the author says it opens border regions and supports regional strategies such as Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei coordination, the development of the western region and the revitalisation of the northeast.

Wang concludes that the Initiative, which builds no geopolitical or military alliances and treats large and small participants equally, is a fundamental remedy for global governance and shared prosperity. It is presented as China's proposal for taking part in global opening up, improving global economic governance and building a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Initiative was framed in official-style commentary in 2018.
quoteEn: The Belt and Road construction does not pursue geopolitical or military alliances, and does not play zero-sum games.
quoteZh: “一带一路”建设不搞地缘政治联盟或军事同盟，不搞零和游戏

glossary.explanation: A programme of infrastructure, trade and investment cooperation proposed by Xi Jinping in 2013, covering the Silk Road Economic Belt and the 21st Century Maritime Silk Road.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13, describing an ideal of shared interests and joint responsibility among states.

glossary.pinyin: gòng shāng gòng jiàn gòng xiǎng
glossary.en: joint consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
glossary.literal: jointly discuss, jointly build, jointly share
glossary.explanation: The stated guiding principle of the Belt and Road Initiative and of China's approach to global governance.
Cooperation among developing countries of the Global South, which Chinese official discourse presents as a complement to North–South cooperation.

t: Leading and driving the revolution in social practice through a revolution in ideas and theory
st: Commemorating the great debate on the criterion of truth and celebrating the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up
zh: 以思想理论革命引领和推动社会实践革命
zhSub: 纪念真理标准大讨论和庆祝改革开放40周年
paras: Writing in 2018, the 40th anniversary of both the truth-criterion debate and reform and opening up, Yan Xiaofeng asks how a philosophical discussion came to start a national transformation. The article argues that reform and opening up began as an ideological revolution within the Party, in which settling the line of thought made it possible to settle the political line. Yan concludes that the same pattern, in which theoretical innovation and practical innovation reinforce each other, continues under Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The piece has three parts. The first traces the path from the 1978 debate, which began with the article "Practice Is the Sole Criterion for Testing Truth", to the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) and the launch of reform and opening up. The second follows how practice and theory interacted along the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics: Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and then Xi's thought. The third sets out why Yan regards Xi's thought as both practical and true. It ends by linking these themes to the 2018 anniversaries of Marx's birth and the Communist Manifesto.

In Yan's account, the Party's line of thought is at bottom a philosophical principle. He treats the Yan'an rectification and Mao Zedong's writings as the earlier corrective to dogmatism and empiricism. The "two whatevers" (the Two Whatevers) made the person, not practice, the standard of truth, so political correction after the Cultural Revolution had to begin with philosophical correction. Restoring practice as the criterion let the Party separate Mao's achievements from the Cultural Revolution's errors, avoid freezing the Soviet model, and treat the people's support as the test of policy. The plenum then shifted the Party's focus to economic construction and corrected the political and organisational lines.

For the new era, Yan argues that Xi's thought has been tested in practice. He cites the shift in the principal contradiction to one between people's growing needs for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development. He also cites the changes since the 18th Party Congress (2012) in areas such as Party leadership, rule of law, ecology and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Yan stresses Party leadership, a people-centred approach and comprehensive deepening of reform as lessons of the past 40 years. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese Party theorists in 2018 linked the 1978 truth-criterion debate to Xi Jinping Thought and to a narrative of continuous theoretical innovation.
quoteEn: Discovering that a problem has been transformed itself marks the beginning of theoretical innovation.
quoteZh: 发现问题的转化本身就意味着理论创新的开始。

glossary.literal: great discussion on the criterion of truth
glossary.explanation: A 1978 national debate set off by a Guangming Daily article arguing that practice is the sole criterion of truth. It challenged the "two whatevers" and is officially seen as preparing the ground for reform and opening up.
A 1977 editorial formula holding that whatever decisions Mao Zedong made and whatever instructions he gave must be upheld. Deng Xiaoping and others opposed it.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into its constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017. The Party presents it as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.
A theory associated with Jiang Zemin. It says the Party must represent advanced productive forces, the advance of culture, and the fundamental interests of the majority.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The slogan for the intensified discipline and anti-corruption drive carried out under Xi Jinping since 2012.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978.

t: Western-style democracy in the predicament of economic globalization, and the future diversification of democracy
zh: 经济全球化困境下的西式民主及未来民主多样化走向
paras: Writing in Hongqi Wengao in 2018, amid a global wave of populism in both developing and Western countries, Zhang Jun asks why this wave has arisen and what it means for the future of democracy. The article argues that populism is a negative tendency internal to Western-style democracy. In Zhang's account, its roots lie in the unequal distribution of benefits under economic globalization, and the stalling of globalization is eroding the standing and quality of Western democracy.

The piece has three sections. The first reviews the course of economic globalization since the 1980s, led by Western developed countries, and the criticism it now faces. The second links the globalization impasse to what Zhang calls the "degradation" of Western democracy, in both developing and developed countries. The third looks ahead to a more pluralised globalization and a more diverse pattern of democratic practice.

Zhang first holds that globalization brought gains, citing a fall of about 1.1 billion in the global poor over 30-odd years, but distributed them unevenly. Developed countries set the rules and occupy the high end of global value chains. Some Asian emerging economies have upgraded, while many developing countries remain at the low end. Within countries, the richest 1% gained most, and lower-middle-income workers in the West saw stagnant real incomes in 1988–2008. Zhang then argues that the West tied competitive-election democracy to globalization and exported it, though such elections are, in the author's words, only a regional West European experience and not universal. Left and right populists respond differently, to inequality and to immigration respectively. Both oppose globalization and distrust elites, which pushes elected governments towards short-sighted protectionism.

Zhang predicts that protectionism and "re-industrialization" will not deliver what voters expect, that the anti-globalization tide will recede, and that emerging economies will gain more voice in global economic governance. Globalization will then become more open, inclusive and balanced, and the expansion of Western-style democracy will fall back. Zhang urges Western governments to restrain transnational capital, tax the top 1% more progressively and rebalance taxation and welfare. Diverse democratic practices, including socialist democracy with Chinese characteristics, are expected to become more attractive to developing countries. Read the original if you want to see how a 2018 Chinese Party-journal article links populism, globalization and the case for democratic diversity.
quoteEn: Of course, economic globalization itself is not the problem; the mechanism for distributing benefits within economic globalization is where the real problem lies.
quoteZh: 当然，经济全球化本身不是问题，经济全球化中的利益分配机制才是问题的真正所在。

glossary.explanation: A political tendency that mobilises ordinary people against elites and established institutions. The author treats it as a negative tendency within Western-style democracy.

The term used in Chinese official and academic writing for liberal, competitive-election democracy as practised in Western countries. The author contrasts it with other democratic forms suited to national conditions.

t: The international responsibility and contemporary value of the Belt and Road Initiative
zh: “一带一路”的国际担当和时代价值
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, on the fifth anniversary of the Belt and Road Initiative, Jiang Li and Jin Xin respond to claims by some Western think-tank scholars that China uses the initiative to build a sphere of influence. The authors reject this reading. They argue that, amid rising protectionism, populism and unilateralism, the initiative has multiple forms of world significance and shows China acting as a responsible major power.

The commentary sets out four vantage points: the trend of the world economy, international mechanisms and global governance, the openness of participating actors, and China's relationship with the world. A closing section states what the initiative is and is not, and what should be done next, including the second Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation planned for the following year.

On the economy, the authors say the world is in a period of sluggish growth. They hold that infrastructure and industrial investment can bring benefits to developing countries along the routes that Western governments and multinationals neglected, and can drive a new round of productivity gains across Eurasia and Africa. On governance, they describe a serious deficit, worsened by the United States' withdrawal from institutions and agreements. In their account the initiative is China's most important public good, advancing a new form of globalization and a community with a shared future for mankind. They also stress its inclusiveness: it sets no preconditions and seeks no uniform institutional arrangement. They cite alignment with UN agencies, regional bodies and national plans such as Kazakhstan's Bright Road and Indonesia's Global Maritime Fulcrum.

The authors conclude that the initiative is not a geopolitical strategy, a Chinese Marshall Plan or a means of exporting a "China model". Its core is connectivity in five areas (policies, infrastructure, trade, finance and people-to-people ties), and its key principle is joint consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits. They say its function should not be stretched beyond infrastructure connectivity and international industrial-capacity cooperation. They call for an "upgraded version" and for telling "new Silk Road stories" with real cases. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese official commentary rebutted Western criticism of the Belt and Road Initiative in 2018.
quoteEn: The Belt and Road Initiative is not the \"geopolitical strategy\" that some Western think tanks slanderously claim, not a Chinese version of the \"Marshall Plan\", not a bid for a Chinese \"sphere of influence\", and still less an attempt to export the \"China model\".
quoteZh: “一带一路”倡议不是某些西方智库所诬称的“地缘政治战略”，不是中国版的“马歇尔计划”，不是为了谋求中国的“势力范围”，更不是为了输出“中国模式”。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese international cooperation initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2013, focused on infrastructure and trade links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping, presenting the world's countries as sharing common interests and fate and calling for cooperative global governance.
The management of transnational issues through international institutions and rules. Chinese official discourse presents China as contributing to its reform.

glossary.pinyin: gòng shāng gòng jiàn gòng xiǎng
glossary.en: joint consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
glossary.literal: jointly discuss, jointly build, jointly share
glossary.explanation: The official guiding principle of the Belt and Road Initiative, stressing equal participation and shared gains.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: From the cruiser Aurora to the Red Boat on South Lake
zh: 从“阿芙乐尔”号巡洋舰到南湖红船
paras: Writing in 2018, a century after the October Revolution and 97 years after the founding of the Chinese Communist Party, Zeng Changqiu links two events through two "red boats": the cruiser Aurora on the Neva and the pleasure boat on Jiaxing's South Lake, where the First Party Congress concluded its work. Zeng argues that the two form one continuous line, and that the Party's present historical mission is to advance along the socialist road opened by the October Revolution and the Chinese revolution.

The article has three parts. The first treats the Aurora and the October Revolution: its world-historical significance and its basic lessons. The second traces the spread of Marxism-Leninism in China after 1917, the rise of the workers' movement, the formation of early Party groups and the founding congress in 1921. The third turns to the "Red Boat spirit", Xi Jinping's 2005 and 2017 statements on it, and what it means for Communists today.

In Zeng's account, the October Revolution was the most profound revolution in history. It put Lenin's thesis of socialist victory in one country into practice, opened the Leninist stage of scientific socialism, broke imperialism's monopoly of the world order, and created a new pattern of competition and coexistence between two systems. Zeng draws four lessons: leadership by a Marxist party, seizure of power by force as the primary task, a firm worker–peasant alliance, and international solidarity. These lessons must be applied to national conditions and not copied mechanically. Zeng presents the Chinese Party as born from Marxism combined with the Chinese workers' movement and modelled on the Bolsheviks, with Li Dazhao as the key propagator.

Zeng concludes that the Soviet collapse does not make the October road obsolete, since its experience endures and socialism with Chinese characteristics continues it after forty years of reform and opening up. The October road should be neither simply negated nor rigidly copied. The Red Boat spirit, defined as a pioneering spirit, a spirit of struggle and a spirit of dedication, is presented as the Party's source of strength for the Chinese Dream, the "Two Centenary Goals" and, ultimately, communism. Read the original if you want an example of Party-historiographical writing that links the October Revolution, the Party's founding and current ideology, with Li Dazhao-era sources and Xi Jinping's statements.
quoteEn: Today, we can neither simply negate the road of the October Revolution nor rigidly copy it; we should follow the direction it pointed out and take our own distinctive road.
quoteZh: 今天，我们对十月革命的道路既不能简单否定，也不能僵化照搬，而应当沿着十月革命指引的方向走自己特色的道路。

glossary.explanation: A Party slogan for the values attributed to the founding of the CCP on a boat on South Lake, Jiaxing. Xi Jinping, then Zhejiang Party secretary, first formulated it in 2005 as a spirit of pioneering, struggle and dedication.
A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2012, meaning the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
Official targets: a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021, and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.
The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership with a market economy.
The policy launched in 1978 that introduced market-oriented reforms and opened China to foreign trade and investment.

t: The ideological struggle has no end in sight
zh: 意识形态斗争正未有穷期
paras: Writing in 2018, Zhang Chuanquan argues that although the Party's ideological work has improved markedly since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the struggle in the ideological sphere remains severe. In Zhang's account, hostile foreign forces will not abandon their plans to "Westernize" and "divide" China, so safeguarding socialist ideological security in the new era is an arduous task. The piece is a short commentary in a Party theoretical journal.

The article has two parts. The first sets out four challenges: Western great-power use of ideological contest to advance national interests; postmodernism's assault on Marxist belief; the export of Western political ideas and values through the media; and persistent distortion and belittling of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The second part offers four ways to safeguard ideological security.

In the first part, Zhang points to social-media-driven "colour revolutions" in North Africa and Syria, the "China threat" and "China collapse" narratives, the US trade war (called a revival of McCarthyism) and the Indo-Pacific strategy. Zhang says postmodernism "deconstructs" Marxism's wholeness and class character and that, in China, it feeds historical nihilism and weakened conviction among some Party members. Zhang also describes "universal values" as a vehicle of Western discourse hegemony. For the remedy, Zhang calls for upholding and developing Marxism and studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and for promoting core socialist values against "universal values". Zhang adds that a community with a shared future for mankind, presented as surpassing the "Western version" of global order, should be advanced.

Zhang concludes that theorists should tell China's story well, rebut Western "misreadings", and raise the global influence of Chinese philosophy and social science. Zhang says the Chinese Dream is not narrow nationalism and that comprehensive national strength is the material basis of socialist ideology. Read the original if you want to see how a 2018 Party journal framed Western ideological pressure and the official countermeasures to it.
quoteEn: Western democratic systems have an innate \"Achilles' heel\" and struggle to meet the needs of modern social development.
quoteZh: 西方民主制度存在与生俱来的“阿喀琉斯之踵”，难以适应现代社会发展的需要。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.
The official name for China's model of socialism combining Party leadership with a market economy, associated with reform and opening up.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for international relations, stressing shared interests and cooperative global governance.
Xi Jinping's slogan, from 2012, for national rejuvenation and prosperity.

t: How mainstream British and American media perceive and evaluate the Communist Party of China
zh: 英美主流媒体对中国共产党的认知与评价
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, Xia Jinmei and Yang Liuyingzi examine how The Guardian, The New York Times and The Washington Post reported on the Communist Party of China after its 19th Party Congress (2017). They ask three questions: how these outlets perceive the Party, what characterises that perception, and how China can raise its international discourse power. The authors argue that the coverage has become more objective and positive, but that negative reporting still carries Western ideological assumptions.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the three papers' praise for the Party's governance record and leadership. The second reviews their reading of the 19th Congress report, focusing on the phrase "new era", the blueprint for national rejuvenation, and the direction of China's democracy. The third analyses the features of the coverage and ends with recommendations for China's external communication.

In the authors' account, the three papers credit the Party's open, win-win governing approach with raising China's international influence. They also credit its anti-corruption campaign with raising public trust, and its confidence in its own path with building national cohesion. They cite the papers as noting the community with a shared future for mankind, Xi Jinping's advocacy of globalisation at Davos, and the Congress's repeated references to a "strong country" and "great rejuvenation". The authors explain the improved objectivity by China's achievements, its more active role in global affairs and its stronger external communication. They add that the papers acknowledge democratic progress as a matter of fact but, on values, remain tied to Western-centrism, using "democratic" for Western systems and "authoritarian" for China's.

The authors conclude that Anglo-American coverage shapes how citizens of both countries see China. They hold that Western discourse hegemony will not disappear soon and that China's external discourse environment remains difficult. They call for a discourse system with Chinese characteristics grounded in Marxist political philosophy, more precise and diversified communication aimed at different cultures, and a more proactive setting of international agendas. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party journal summarises and interprets Western media coverage of the Party after the 19th Congress, and what communication strategy it draws from it.
quoteEn: British and American media have begun to approach China with a more rational and positive attitude.
quoteZh: 英美媒体开始以更加理性、正面的态度认识中国。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2013. It calls for common development and joint global governance, and is presented as an alternative to bloc politics.
The capacity to shape international narratives and agendas and to have one's own account of events heard. Chinese writers often use it when discussing perceived Western media dominance.

t: The scientific conception of history in the Communist Manifesto
zh: 《共产党宣言》的科学历史观
paras: Writing in Hongqi Wengao in 2018, Yin Hanning asks what view of history runs through the Communist Manifesto and why it demonstrates the scientific character and truth of Marxism. The article argues that the Manifesto embodies a dialectical-materialist conception of history, which Yin describes as the most basic and important method of thought in Marxism and the foundation of its scientific standing.

Yin opens by citing four statements by Engels, in Socialism: Utopian and Scientific, Anti-Dühring, the speech at Marx's graveside and the 1883 German preface, to show how much Marx and Engels valued their historical outlook. The article then examines five aspects of the Manifesto in turn: the historical role of the bourgeoisie, the laws of social development, proletarian revolutionary practice, the historical character of class struggle, and the Russian village commune.

Yin's central moves are as follows. First, the Manifesto praises the bourgeoisie as having played a highly revolutionary role against feudalism, while also pointing to the limits of bourgeois society in its later development, notably crises of overproduction. Second, Yin reads the Manifesto's analysis as grounded in the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production. Third, Yin stresses Engels's later qualifications: the prefaces say the Manifesto's practical measures depend on historical conditions and had partly become outdated. Engels's insertion, "since the dissolution of primitive communal landownership", and his 1888 note on recorded history, make class struggle a historical phenomenon tied to the level of productive forces, not the whole of human history. Yin treats the theory of class struggle as subordinate to the theory of productive forces and relations of production. Finally, the 1882 Russian preface is read as showing that backward countries may take a different path, a point Yin says the October Revolution confirmed.

Yin concludes that the Manifesto's view of history is the cornerstone of Marxism's scientific character and of its capacity to move with the times, and he regards the view that Marxism is outdated as a disregard for science and truth. He calls for rereading the Manifesto to strengthen ideals and convictions, to hold to the Four-sphere Confidence, and to arm minds with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Read the original if you want a compact, text-based account of how Chinese Party commentary draws on Engels's prefaces and notes to present the Manifesto's historical materialism and its historical limits on class struggle.
quoteEn: Class antagonism and class struggle are historical phenomena of a particular historical stage, determined by the level of development of social productive forces, and are not the whole of human history.
quoteZh: 阶级对立和阶级斗争是社会生产力发展水平决定的一定历史阶段的历史现象，而不是人类历史的全部。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party discourse, promoted under Xi Jinping, of confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A Party-affiliated theoretical periodical, published under Qiushi's parent organisation, which carries commentary on Marxist theory and Party ideology.

t: Why the October Revolution and not a July Revolution?
st: A rebuttal of Kautsky's "premature birth" theory of socialism
zh: 为什么是十月革命而不是七月革命?
zhSub: 驳考茨基的社会主义“早产论”
source: Journal of Zhengzhou University of Light Industry (Social Sciences Edition), 2018 no. 4
paras: Karl Kautsky compared the proletarian dictatorship in Russia to a pregnant woman who leaps about wildly to shorten her pregnancy and brings on a premature birth, so that the child cannot live. Yu Bin takes up this "premature birth" theory of socialism, which he says gained influence after the setback of the world socialist movement at the end of the twentieth century. Writing in 2018, Yu argues that socialism was not premature. In his view, in Western Europe it was "overdue", and the October Revolution was neither adventurist nor premature.

The article has six parts. It begins with Marx and Engels on the inevitability of socialism and the Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy. It then turns to their remarks on Russia and the possibility of revolution in a relatively backward country. The central sections follow Lenin's strategy from the April Theses and "Letters on Tactics" through his halting of the July 1917 demonstrations to his insistence on insurrection in September and October. A short conclusion draws the lessons.

Yu argues that the "two inevitables" and the "two never's" in Marx do not conflict, because Marx added that humanity sets itself only tasks it can solve. He reads Marx and Engels as treating Russia as capable of absorbing capitalism's positive achievements without its catastrophes. Revolution in a backward country is possible, Yu holds, where the bourgeois revolution is unfinished and a workers' party guided by Marxism already exists. Yu then contends that Lenin followed the principle of a "majority revolution" and rejected Blanquism. In July the Bolsheviks were a minority in the soviets, so an uprising could not have won, and the peaceful path ended after the July events. By September they had majorities in Petrograd and Moscow. Lenin then pressed a hesitant Central Committee, and the revolution broke out on 25 October (Russian calendar).

Yu concludes that whether the revolution was premature is a question of practice, and that Lenin's step-by-step leadership proved Marxism's truth. He argues that the lack of socialism in the developed West a century on shows it is "overdue" there, and cites the crises of 1929 and 2008 and wartime destruction. He reads the Soviet collapse as the penalty for departing from Marxist principles, not as proof of Kautsky. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist defence of the October Revolution against the "premature birth" thesis, built on close citation of Marx, Engels and Lenin.
quoteEn: Socialism was not born prematurely; if anything, it has become somewhat "overdue".
quoteZh: 社会主义不但未早产，反而有点“过月”了。

glossary.explanation: The view, associated with Kautsky, that socialism in Russia came before the material conditions were ripe. Critics of the Soviet experience have used it, and Chinese Marxist authors such as Yu Bin rebut it.
A summary of the Communist Manifesto's claim that the fall of the bourgeoisie and the victory of the proletariat are equally inevitable.

A summary of Marx's 1859 Preface: no social formation perishes before its productive forces are exhausted, and new relations never appear before their material conditions mature. Some read it as postponing socialism.
The doctrine, named after Auguste Blanqui, of seizing power through a small conspiratorial minority instead of mass action. Marxists often use it as a term of criticism.

t: On the three rationalities of the October Revolution
zh: 论十月革命的三大合理性
source: Journal of Zhengzhou University of Light Industry (Social Sciences Edition), 2018 no. 4
paras: Debate over the October Revolution has never ceased, and it grows sharper whenever the world socialist movement is in difficulty. Zhang identifies three lines of challenge: whether the Revolution contradicted historical materialism (theoretical rationality), whether it fitted Russia's historical development (historical rationality), and whether it was progressive rather than regressive (political rationality). The article contends that these correspond to whether the Revolution could, had to, and should have happened, and it argues that all three questions can be answered in the Revolution's favour.

The article has three main sections, one for each form of rationality. The first takes on the "premature birth" thesis associated with Plekhanov, Kamenev, Rykov and especially Kautsky's 1918 The Dictatorship of the Proletariat. The second examines the contradictions of early twentieth-century Russia and the rise of the Bolsheviks between the February and October revolutions. The third assesses the Revolution's consequences for institutions, colonial peoples and capitalism itself.

On theory, Zhang recasts Marx's second "never" in the 1859 Preface as a logical proposition and argues that its converse is equivalent. Since new relations of production did appear in Russia after 1917, the material conditions must already have matured, so the "premature birth" claim is a mechanical reading of historical materialism. Zhang adds that, in a world history created by capitalism, backward countries can draw on global productive forces, and that the workers' own activity is a productive force. On history, the author argues that four contradictions in Russia, the failure of the Provisional Government to deliver peace, bread and land, and the Bolsheviks' organisational preparation (membership rising from 100,000 in April 1917 to 350,000 by the eve of the Revolution) made the Revolution inevitable rather than a conspiracy or coup. On politics, Zhang holds that revolutions should be judged by whether they advance human emancipation, and credits October with creating a new social system, spurring national liberation movements, and forcing concessions from capitalism.

Zhang concludes that the Revolution was theoretically possible, historically necessary and politically justified. As evidence for the third point, the article says that the weakening of world socialism after the Soviet collapse let capitalism slide back towards "barbarism", with workers' rights eroded and wealth concentrated. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist defence of the October Revolution that answers the "premature birth" critique through formal logic and world-historical argument.
quoteEn: The theoretical error of the "premature birth" thesis lies in its mechanical understanding of historical materialism.
quoteZh: “早产论”的理论错误在于其机械地理解了历史唯物主义。

t: How Russia's new secondary-school history textbook judges the Soviet system and Soviet Party leaders
zh: 俄新编中学历史教材对苏联体制和苏共领导人的评价
paras: After the Soviet collapse, Russia had no unified history textbook, and, the author says, many textbooks blackened Russian history. Wu examines the 2016 national textbook History of Russia, Grade 10 (Moscow Education Publishing House), produced after Putin's 2014 call for an objective, fair and respectful treatment of the past. The article, published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, argues that the book affirms the October Revolution and Lenin, assesses Stalin and his system in a largely balanced way, and takes a critical view of Gorbachev.

The textbook covers Russian history from 1914 to the early twenty-first century. Wu organises the review in three parts, each built around the textbook's own wording: the October Revolution and Lenin; the Stalin system and Stalin's role in the Great Patriotic War; and Gorbachev's reforms and the collapse of the USSR. The article is largely descriptive, quoting passages and drawing out the judgements they imply.

On the revolution, Wu reads the textbook as presenting it as a historical choice. The tsarist government failed under the strain of the First World War, the Provisional Government failed to meet workers' and soldiers' demands, and the Bolsheviks gained support with simple slogans. Lenin is described as an undisputed leader, and the Brest-Litovsk peace is explained as a realistic step. On Stalin, Wu says the textbook records both the costs and the achievements of industrialisation and collectivisation, giving more space to the achievements, and never uses them to reject the whole Stalin system. It also treats Stalin as part of a people's war. On Gorbachev, the textbook rejects the "new thinking", which it says put universal human values above class, and judges his economic reform and "democratisation" failures. It also blames glasnost for letting in ideological conflict. It concludes that Gorbachev did not understand the system the Bolsheviks built.

Wu concludes that the textbook, resting on historical facts, offers an objective account of the key questions of Russian history from 1914 on and is a useful reference for understanding Soviet history. Wu stresses that the textbook leaves readers room to draw their own value judgements.
