Read the original if you want a Chinese reading of how post-2014 official Russian schooling presents Lenin, Stalin and Gorbachev, with extensive quotation from the textbook.
quoteEn: The textbook gives industrialisation and agricultural collectivisation an objective assessment that includes both positive and negative aspects, but it never uses either to negate the Stalin system as a whole.
quoteZh: 教科书给了工业化和农业集体化以包含正向和负向的客观评价，但从未以工业化或农业集体化来否认整个斯大林体制。

t: Rereading the classics, advancing with the times, and being a loyal guardian of Marxism
st: On the 170th anniversary of the Communist Manifesto
zh: 重温经典，与时俱进，做马克思主义的忠诚卫士
paras: Marking the 170th anniversary of the Communist Manifesto in 2018, this text (apparently delivered at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and published in World Socialism Studies, 2018 no. 4) asks what reading the Manifesto means for Communists today. Wang argues that only a proper grasp of it secures firm belief in Marxism, and that in the present this means upholding Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and pursuing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

The piece has three parts. The first treats understanding the Manifesto as the basis of Party spirit and of correct revolutionary practice. The second concerns studying Xi Jinping's thought and strengthening the Four-sphere Confidence. The third argues that the Party must be willing to carry out self-reform. Wang draws on Lenin, Deng Xiaoping, the Soviet collapse, the Wenchuan earthquake recovery and the author's own observations of Party work.

Wang contends that without grasping the Manifesto one cannot hold to the conviction that communism will prevail, see the main trend of history, or keep to a people-centred stance. The author reads the failure of once-large parties, especially the Soviet party, as the result of betraying Marxist positions, and says the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012) has corrected earlier deviations. Xi Jinping Thought is presented as both the contemporary form and the Chinese form of Marxism, with world significance because it offers developing countries a path to modernization distinct from the Western one. In the author's view, the Wenchuan reconstruction shows the superiority of Party leadership.

Wang concludes that ideological work remains a weak point: some leading cadres are indifferent to ideology, adopt Western discourse or avoid the word itself. The author calls for raising the Party's Marxist theoretical level, improving the quality of Party building, tackling formalism and bureaucratism, and extending rigorous self-governance down to grassroots "flies", the petty corruption that affects ordinary people. Read the original if you want a Party-affiliated academic's account, from 2018, of how the Manifesto anniversary was tied to ideological discipline and anti-corruption work.
quoteEn: Whether a movement "works in the interests of the vast majority" is the touchstone and dividing line for telling genuine from false socialism and genuine from false Marxism.
quoteZh: 是否“为绝大多数人谋利益”，是检验和区别真假社会主义、真假马克思主义的试金石和分水岭。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the campaign since 2012 to tighten Party discipline, combat corruption and strengthen internal supervision.
Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name of China's path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, public ownership and market mechanisms.

t: Learning from the revolutionary spirit of the New People's Study Society's pioneers and continuing the struggle for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
zh: 学习新民学会前辈们的革命精神 为中华民族伟大复兴继续奋斗
paras: Zhu Jiamu's text, published in World Socialism Studies in 2018, reads as an address to a scholarly symposium marking the 100th anniversary of the New People's Study Society (Xinmin xuehui), founded in 1918 by Mao Zedong, Cai Hesen and others. The symposium was co-hosted by the Marxism schools of Nankai, Lanzhou and Sichuan universities and the Hefu Research Centre. Zhu argues that the Society was an important source of the Party's early organisations. He holds that its founding generation had three outstanding qualities that today's young people should learn from.

Zhu situates the event in the Party's call, after the 19th Party Congress (2017), for a campaign of education under the slogan 'remain true to our original aspiration and keep our mission firmly in mind'. The text then takes the three qualities in turn, drawing on the biographies of the Society's members, on Mao's recollections and on his 1925 poem Changsha. A final section collects statements by Xi Jinping on studying Party and national history, opposing historical nihilism, and sustaining ideals and convictions.

The three qualities are concern for country and people with lofty aims; unceasing pursuit of truth; and steadfast loyalty to belief. On the first, Zhu stresses the members' youth and poverty and the Society's aims and rules of conduct. On the second, Zhu traces how members in France and in Hunan moved from patriotism and utopian idealism to Marxism, citing Cai Hesen's 1920 letters and Mao's reply. From this Zhu concludes that the Chinese Communist Party would have been founded sooner or later even without Comintern help. On the third, Zhu cites that 37 of the Society's 78 members joined the Party and describes the deaths of martyrs such as Cai Hesen and Xiang Jingyu.

Zhu then links this history to Xi Jinping's warnings that denying Party and Soviet history, which Xi calls historical nihilism, undermines Marxism's guiding role and Party leadership. Zhu concludes that, with the nation at a critical stage of development, every Communist Party member and young student should follow the Society's pioneers. They should keep to the communist ideal and keep striving for the happiness of the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-affiliated scholars use early revolutionary history for ideological education, or if you want details on the Society's members.
quoteEn: The New People's Study Society was the one that gathered the most talented people, was the most tightly organised and had the greatest influence.
quoteZh: 新民学会是汇聚人才最多、组织最为严密、影响最大的一个。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan for restoring China's strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'. It has been a central theme of Party discourse, especially since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: remain true to our original aspiration and keep our mission firmly in mind
glossary.literal: do not forget the original heart, firmly remember the mission
glossary.explanation: The slogan of a Party-wide education campaign launched after the 19th Party Congress (2017). It urges members to hold to the Party's founding ideals.
In Party usage, a label for views that negate the official account of revolutionary and Party history. Xi Jinping has repeatedly criticised it as a threat to the Party's legitimacy.
A student society founded in Changsha, Hunan, in 1918 by Mao Zedong, Cai Hesen and others. Many of its members later joined the Communist Party.

t: Making the study of Marxism the essential skill of Communists
zh: 把学好马克思主义作为共产党人的看家本领
paras: Written for the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth (2018), the article takes up Xi Jinping's call for Party cadres to treat Marxism as their "essential skill" (看家本领). Wang argues that mastering Marxism is the most meaningful way to commemorate Marx. In Wang's account, it is also a requirement grounded in theoretical logic, historical experience and present realities.

The article has three main sections. The first concerns firm belief in Marxism as the spiritual pillar of every Communist. The second concerns a Marxist style of study, and the third concerns Marxist ways of thinking and working. Wang draws throughout on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping, and the discussion is anchored in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

On belief, Wang gives four reasons why Marxism can serve as such a pillar. These are its scientific character (dialectical and historical materialism), its revolutionary character (the fundamental interests of the labouring majority), its practical character (seeking truth from facts) and its lofty ideal of communism. Wang holds that the present remains Marx's "great historical epoch", marked by a continuing contest between socialism and capitalism. On study, Wang calls for a problem-oriented approach that aims at the principal contradiction identified at the 19th Party Congress (2017). Wang also stresses grasping Marxism's basic tenets and scientific method rather than doctrine, and advancing the adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions. On method, Wang names four elements: a people-centred standpoint, the ideological line of seeking truth from facts, materialist dialectics, and the historical thinking of historical materialism. Wang presents Xi's thought as a model of all four.

Wang concludes that learning Marxism means above all absorbing its method and applying it to concrete problems, and that this will help Party members to grasp historical trends and advance socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. Wang also calls for unifying the lofty communist ideal with the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a representative statement of how Party theorists in 2018 linked Marx's bicentenary to cadre education and to the study of Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: In studying Marxism we must promote a style of study that links theory with practice: learn with problems in mind, take the people as teachers, learn while doing and do while learning, and on no account indulge in bombast or fall into empty talk.
quoteZh: 学习马克思主义，要发扬理论联系实际的学风，带着问题学，拜人民为师，做到干中学、学中干，学以致用、用以促学、学用相长，千万不能夸夸其谈、陷于“假大空”。

glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping used for Marxism, meaning the core competence every Party cadre must master. It appears in his 2018 remarks on Marx's 200th birthday.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest outcome of adapting Marxism to China.
A slogan associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, used to name the Party's ideological line of starting from actual conditions.

In Party theory, the central tension in society at a given stage. The 19th Party Congress (2017) defined it as the contradiction between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.
The official name for China's current path, theory and system, which combines Party leadership with a market-oriented economy.

t: Upholding faith in Marxism and writing a new chapter of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 坚定马克思主义信仰,谱写中国特色社会主义新篇章
paras: Written for the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth, this commentary asks what it means for Party members to remain faithful to Marxism today. Wang argues that strengthening belief in the truth and scientific character of Marxism is the basis of political firmness. In Wang's view, this belief is what allows the Party to be built stronger and to unite its strength for the "two centenary goals" and the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation.

The article has three parts. The first concerns theoretical confidence and the Party's "spiritual core". The second sets out three points for upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics. The third concerns the Party's leadership and its self-building as a Marxist governing party. Wang draws on the Communist Manifesto, Lenin, Xi Jinping's speech at the Marx anniversary meeting, and the author's own experience in Party discipline inspection work.

Wang pictures the Party as concentric circles with Marxist belief at the core, organisation in the middle and individual members outside. Wang says theory must keep innovating with practice, and traces this through Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Wang also notes weaknesses in Marxist research, such as thin explanatory power and a role limited to political exposition. The three points on socialism are these: China remains in the primary stage of socialism, so development must stay central; the principal social contradiction has changed, so unbalanced and inadequate development must be addressed; and external containment must be met with the Four-sphere Confidence and bottom-line thinking. The third part claims, drawing on inspection work since the 18th Party Congress (2012), that Party leadership had been weakened or hollowed out in some localities, state-owned enterprises and universities. Wang argues this was largely reversed and calls for upholding the authority of the Central Committee and its centralised, unified leadership.

Wang concludes that Marxism's truth remains as bright as ever, and that Party members should hold to their faith, draw wisdom from Marxism, and push on the Party's "great new project" of self-building. The text is a Party-oriented exhortation rather than a scholarly study, and it presents the Party's leadership as the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want an example of how a senior Party discipline official linked the Marx bicentenary to Party discipline, leadership and ideological work in 2018.
quoteEn: Theoretical clarity is the foundation of political firmness.
quoteZh: 理论上清醒是政治上坚定的基础。

glossary.explanation: The official Party judgement, dating from the 1980s, that China is in a long initial phase of socialism marked by relatively underdeveloped productive forces.
The Party's official name for its path, theory and system of socialism, associated with reform and opening up since 1978.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official call for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
Xi Jinping's slogan, introduced in 2012, for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
The guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development.

t: Marxism is first of all a theory of revolution
zh: 马克思主义首先是革命的理论
paras: Writing for the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth in 2018, Zhu Jiamu asks what it means to study Marxism today and whether insisting on its revolutionary character is out of touch with a China that has long since passed from revolution to construction and reform. Zhu answers that Marxism is first of all the theory of proletarian revolution, and that it should be studied for the sake of the emancipation of the proletariat and the cause of communism, not as mere knowledge or decoration. Zhu builds the piece around Xi Jinping's speech at the anniversary meeting on 4 May 2018.

The article opens with Engels's graveside description of Marx as "first of all a revolutionary", then moves through several connected themes. These are the criticism of "Western Marxism", the claim that the Communist Party should turn from a "revolutionary party" into a "ruling party", the meaning of "revolution", the status of communism as an ideal, and the character of the present era. Zhu draws throughout on Lenin, Chen Yun, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and above all Xi Jinping's repeated phrase "revolutionary ideals are higher than the heavens".

Zhu argues that "Western Marxism" treats Marxism as scholarship, does not aim at revolution and leaves the basic capitalist system untouched. Citing Lenin, Zhu describes this as the dulling of a revolutionary doctrine. Against the idea of a shift from revolutionary to ruling party, Zhu holds that "revolution" has several senses (in the productive forces, in social relations, in spirit), so it does not mean only one class overthrowing another. Rejecting the Cultural Revolution's "continuing revolution under the dictatorship of the proletariat", Zhu says, does not reject the continuing task of building socialism towards communism. Zhu blames the "farewell to revolution" argument and historical nihilism for weakening Party members' ideals and working style. Citing Xi, Zhu offers four reasons to hold to communist ideals. Socialism with Chinese characteristics derives from communist theory, ideals give Party members spiritual support, communism can be reached only through generations of effort, and abandoning it would cause the Party to disintegrate. Zhu also distinguishes the "character" of the era from its "features". Peace and development are features, while the era remains one of transition from capitalism to socialism.

Zhu concludes that the present era is still the historical era Marxism identified, and that the general trend of social development, socialism replacing capitalism, has not changed. In Zhu's view this is what justifies upholding socialism with Chinese characteristics and communist convictions, and what makes it necessary for Communists, though in power, to remember that they are revolutionaries. Read the original if you want a compact example of how a senior Party historian ties the anniversary speech to arguments about Party identity, communism and the nature of the era.
quoteEn: Therefore, we should study Marxism first of all for the sake of revolution, for the cause of proletarian emancipation and communism, and not treat it merely as a body of knowledge or a discipline, still less as window-dressing.
quoteZh: 因此，我们学习和研究马克思主义，首先应当是为了革命，为了要进行无产阶级解放和共产主义的事业，而不应当把它单纯作为一种知识、一门学问，更不应当是为了装潢门面。

glossary.explanation: The tradition of Marxist thought in Western Europe from Lukács, Korsch and Gramsci to the Frankfurt School. Zhu uses the term critically, as an academic Marxism detached from revolutionary practice.

glossary.en: from a revolutionary party into a ruling party
glossary.explanation: A formula in Chinese debates holding that after taking power the Communist Party should shift from a revolutionary to a governing role. Zhu rejects it as a false opposition.
A line of argument, associated with 1990s intellectual debates, that rejects revolution as a path for modern China. Zhu links it to historical nihilism.
In official Chinese usage, a label for interpretations that negate the Party's revolutionary history or the socialist period. Zhu treats it as a source of ideological harm.

glossary.en: revolutionary ideals are higher than the heavens
glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping has repeated since the 18th Party Congress (2012) to stress that communist ideals take priority for Party members.
The official name for China's current path, system and theory of socialism since the reform era.

t: Exploration, innovation and development in contemporary socialism
zh: 当代社会主义的探索、创新与发展
source: Studies on Marxism (马克思主义研究), 2018 no. 3
paras: Writing in 2018, a century after the October Revolution, Pan Jin'e asks how the five remaining socialist states (China, Vietnam, Laos, Cuba and North Korea) have charted their own paths since the Soviet-led socialist camp collapsed. The article argues that these countries kept their socialist direction while adapting institutions to national conditions. In Pan's account, this independent exploration also produced localised forms of Marxist theory, and countries that changed direction failed.

The article begins with the Soviet model, which Pan says helped establish socialist systems but ended independent exploration of other paths. It then compares the five countries on three points: when reform began and how each names it, the reform of the economic system, and political change. A second part surveys the guiding ideologies each ruling party has built from its own practice. A final part assesses prospects for world socialism and the external pressures it faces.

Pan's core argument is that paths differ because national conditions differ. China's reform dates from 1978, Vietnam's and Laos's from 1986, and Cuba's "updating" of its economic model from 2011. North Korea avoids the labels "reform" and "renovation". China, Vietnam and Laos pursue a socialist market economy or a "socialist-oriented market economy". Pan notes that Vietnam and Laos treat themselves as still in a transition to socialism, which allows more room for private capital. Cuba keeps planning dominant, and North Korea's measures are described as less coherent. On politics, all five constitutions drop "dictatorship of the proletariat", but Vietnam and Laos aim at a "socialist rule-of-law state". Pan also reports that Vietnam's Party now faces "self-evolution" and ideological decay. Each party has also localised Marxism, from Deng Xiaoping Theory to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, Ho Chi Minh Thought, Kaysone Phomvihane Thought, Fidel Castro Thought and Kim Il Sung–Kim Jong Il-ism.

Pan concludes that Marxism sets the direction but each Party must combine its basic principles with national realities. The article credits China, Vietnam and Laos with rapid growth and middle-income status. It credits Cuba and North Korea with achievements in education, health and the environment despite sanctions. Pan warns that the post-Obama shift from blockade to engagement is a more deceptive form of "peaceful evolution", and that the internet carries ideological infiltration. Pan expects the Occupy Wall Street movement and the success of socialism with Chinese characteristics to revive socialism worldwide. Read the original if you want a comparative, Party-institution view of how China's scholars frame the five socialist states' reforms and their guiding ideologies.
quoteEn: Practice shows that Marxism has pointed out the direction for the development of world socialism, but each country's Communist Party should, in concrete practice, combine the basic principles of Marxism with its own concrete realities and explore a path of socialist development suited to national conditions.
quoteZh: 实践表明，马克思主义为世界社会主义的发展指明了方向，但各国共产党应在具体实践中把马克思主义基本原理与本国具体实际相结合，探索适合本国国情的社会主义发展道路。

glossary.explanation: The goal of China's economic reform adopted at the 14th Party Congress in 1992. It combines market allocation of resources with state macro-regulation and public ownership as the main body of the economy.

glossary.zh: 社会主义定向的市场经济
glossary.pinyin: shèhuì zhǔyì dìngxiàng de shìchǎng jīngjì
glossary.literal: market economy with a socialist orientation
glossary.explanation: The economic model proclaimed by Vietnam and Laos. It runs on market rules while the state claims to keep it directed toward socialism.
Vietnam's term (Đổi mới) for the comprehensive reform process launched in 1986. Vietnamese theorists see it as broader and deeper than "reform".
A term in Chinese and other socialist-state discourse for alleged Western strategies of changing socialist systems through non-military means such as economic, cultural and ideological influence.
A goal in the Vietnamese and Lao constitutions and Party documents. It places the Party's leadership within a constitutional and legal framework.

t: A review of the memoir of Fuwa Tetsuzo's wife
zh: 不破哲三夫人回忆录评析
paras: This is a review of The Road Without Regrets: Living with Fuwa Tetsuzo (Japanese edition 2012; Chinese edition, CITIC Press, April 2018), a memoir by Uedo Nanakako (上田七加子), wife of the Japanese Communist Party leader and Marxist theorist Fuwa Tetsuzo. The reviewer, Zheng Ping, is also the book's Chinese translator. Zheng presents the work as both a personal biography and a record of Japan from the Second World War to the present.

The review follows the memoir's chronology. It covers Nanakako's turn from a militarist schoolgirl to Communist Party member in 1948, her work as a full-time Party official, factory organiser, community activist and women's movement cadre, and her role in Fuwa's eleven House of Representatives campaigns. It also reports the memoir's account of Fuwa's parliamentary questions and ends with brief remarks on the book's value as social history and as a woman's reflection on marriage and career.

Zheng argues that the memoir shows how the Party, though legal after 1945 and fast-growing, developed through setbacks: Cold War anti-communism, the 'red purge', a Party split, and later electoral-system changes. The review reads Nanakako's factory work as an example of going among the people, analysing concrete problems and avoiding dogmatism. It cites the Party's 1958 line of 'peaceful revolution' through parliament, seat totals over time, and the 2016 opposition cooperation as evidence of resilience. Zheng also reads the Party's electoral path as showing that social change by parliamentary majority within capitalism is arduous and very slow.

Zheng concludes that the couple, married for over sixty years, kept their ideals and shared commitment to world peace and liberation. The review recommends reading the memoir alongside Fuwa's 2011 autobiography Testimony of the Times for a fuller view of the Party's postwar history, on both theory and practice and on front-stage and backstage politics. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist scholar's account of the Japanese Communist Party's postwar history, as told through one memoir, and of how it is presented to Chinese readers.
quoteEn: The history of Japan's contemporary workers' movement embodies the hard work of Fuwa and his wife.
quoteZh: 日本当代工人运动史，凝聚了不破夫妇的辛勤汗水。

t: Tracing back to the source of truth, preserving theoretical confidence
zh: 回溯真理源头 永葆理论自信
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in May 2018, on the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth, Chen Jin argues that firm theoretical confidence is the soul of upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. The commentary takes Xi Jinping's speech at the anniversary meeting as its starting point and holds that returning to Marxism's origins is how Chinese communists renew that confidence.

The piece is a short reflective essay. It sketches the Party's path from seeking, upholding and developing to innovating an "-ism", lists the theoretical results of that path, and notes the Politburo study sessions since the 18th Party Congress (2012) on Marxist fundamentals, including one on the Communist Manifesto. It then poses three questions: why set out, how to advance, and how to gather strength.

Chen's central claim is that theoretical confidence and confidence in the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics support each other. Without the former there can be no confidence in the path, while the path's forty years of successful practice show that its guiding theory is effective and scientific. Chen answers the three questions by pointing to communist ideals as the "calcium of the spirit", Marxism as a worldview and method, and knowledge of Marxist principles as the basis for grasping the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Theoretical confidence, Chen says, means both consistency and keeping pace with the times, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is presented as raising it further.

Chen concludes that the Party should keep raising the banner of Marxism so that the future Marx and Engels envisaged is shown on Chinese soil. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-aligned commentary in 2018 tied the Marx bicentenary to theoretical confidence and the Party's own theoretical lineage.
quoteEn: Without theoretical confidence, there can be no talk of confidence in the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 如果没有理论自信，就根本谈不上对中国特色社会主义道路的自信。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, associated with reform and opening up from 1978 onwards.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
One of the 'confidences' promoted by the Party: conviction in the correctness of its guiding theory. It is usually listed with confidence in the path, system and culture.

t: Approaching the real Marx
st: On reading Marx, an Intellectual Giant
zh: 走近真实的马克思
zhSub: 读《思想巨人马克思》
paras: This is a book review, published in Guangming Daily in May 2018, shortly after the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth. Jin Nuo and Hao Lixin review Jin Huiming's Marx, an Intellectual Giant (思想巨人马克思). They argue that the book presents a real, thinking Marx and conveys both his personal stature and his lasting theoretical contribution.

The reviewers describe the book as neither an ordinary biography nor a purely theoretical study. They say it combines Marx's theoretical creation, revolutionary practice and life, and treats his social setting, personal hardships and struggles together with the development of his thought. They credit the author, a long-time researcher of Marxist philosophy and the history of Marxism, with writing it in old age. The book has 14 chapters organised around Marx's intellectual turning points and his two great discoveries.

The review identifies three features of method: combining history with theory, with theory predominant; unifying history and logic, and thought with social practice; and tracing how concepts evolve alongside ideas, since, as the book puts it, the content of thought develops before its formal expression. On structure, the reviewers report that early chapters cover Marx's shift from idealism to materialism and from revolutionary democracy to socialism. Later chapters treat the materialist conception of history, the Communist Manifesto and the 1848 revolutions, and the theory of surplus value. The final chapters cover his later years and the contemporary significance of Marxism.

The reviewers conclude that few systems of thought show such enduring appeal as Marx's. In their view this comes from his personal character, his theoretical quality and the scientific force of his thought. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese account of how a leading Party-affiliated reviewer assesses this biography and its chapter structure.
quoteEn: The book has 14 chapters and is organised around Marx's intellectual transformation and his two great discoveries.
quoteZh: 全书共分14个章节，以马克思的思想转变和两个伟大发现为主线展开了论述。

t: Sensing and grasping the truth-power of Marxism in practice
st: Marking the 40th anniversary of "Practice is the sole criterion for testing truth"
zh: 在实践中感悟和把握马克思主义的真理力量
zhSub: 纪念《实践是检验真理的唯一标准》发表40周年
paras: Commissioned by Guangming Daily for the 40th anniversary of its 11 May 1978 editorial "Practice is the sole criterion for testing truth", this commentary by Yang Geng of Beijing Normal University asks what that debate still teaches. Yang argues that the discussion was more than an epistemological exercise. In Yang's account it restored the Party's seeking-truth-from-facts line, prefigured reform and opening up, and reveals the truth-power of Marxism when read from the vantage point of the "new era".

The piece has three parts. The first treats the truth-criterion debate as a political as well as philosophical event and draws lessons on the relation between philosophy and politics. The second traces how contemporary Chinese practice deepened the "practice criterion" into two further criteria. The third turns to how Marxism should be upheld and developed in practice, including a defence of its contemporary relevance. Yang draws on Marx, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

Yang contends that the debate undermined the "two whatevers" and so was a question of the Party's and the country's fate. Philosophy, Yang says, has both a knowledge and an ideological character, so philosophical change precedes political change and Marxist philosophy is in effect political philosophy. Reform practice added a "productivity criterion" (an objective or scientific measure) and a "people's criterion" (a value measure based on popular needs and interests). Yang says the two together complete the practice criterion, because developing productive forces without serving the people, or serving them only in intention, would fail. Yang rejects the claim that Marxism is outdated, citing successive capitalist crises, but denies that it is a system of "ultimate truth". Marx, Yang writes, was a Prometheus rather than a god, and Marxism supplies a method rather than ready-made answers.

Yang calls for Marxism to be developed by studying China's socialist reality, contemporary Western capitalism and foreign Marxist currents. Yang proposes renewing familiar theories (reflection theory, class theory, the labour theory of value, capital accumulation, public ownership) and developing ideas Marx and Engels only sketched, such as world-system ideas and ecological civilization. Yang presents Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the systematic answer to the problems raised by reform. Read the original if you want a representative 2018 statement of how Chinese Marxist philosophers link the 1978 truth-criterion debate to the Party's current theoretical line.
quoteEn: Establishing the "productivity criterion" and the "people's criterion" in effect defines the tasks, character and goals of reform from the standpoint of the relation between social object and subject.
quoteZh: 确立“生产力标准”和确立“人民群众标准”，实际上是从社会客体和主体关系的视角界定了改革的任务、性质和目标。

glossary.zh: 实践是检验真理的唯一标准
glossary.pinyin: shíjiàn shì jiǎnyàn zhēnlǐ de wéiyī biāozhǔn
glossary.en: Practice is the sole criterion for testing truth
glossary.explanation: Title of the Guangming Daily editorial of 11 May 1978, which launched a nationwide debate. It challenged dogmatic adherence to earlier directives and is regarded in China as the ideological preparation for reform and opening up.
A 1977 formula holding that whatever policy Mao Zedong decided and whatever instruction he gave must be upheld. Deng Xiaoping and the truth-criterion debate opposed it.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978.
Deng Xiaoping's idea that whether productive forces develop is the fundamental test of whether the Party's lines and policies are correct.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: The truth of Marxism has strong and lasting vitality
st: In commemoration of the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth
zh: 马克思主义真理具有强大而持久的生命力
zhSub: 纪念马克思诞辰200周年
paras: Written for the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth and published in Qiushi in 2018, this article by Wang Weiguang asks why Marxism has kept its vitality since the 1840s. Wang's answer is that Marxism is a complete system of scientific truth that is also open to development, and that it renews itself by being combined with the practice of the working class and of each nation. The article presents Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the latest stage of this process.

The text has three sections. The first presents Marxism as the greatest revolution in the history of human thought, in its standpoint, its basic views and its method. The second looks for the internal sources of its vitality in three pairs of features. The third surveys Marxism in practice: the First and Second Internationals, the Paris Commune, Lenin's development of Marxism in Russia, and the adaptation of Marxism to China.

Wang argues that the standpoint of Marxism is the proletariat and the liberation of all humanity. Its basic views are the materialist conception of history and the theory of surplus value, which Engels called the "two discoveries", and its method is materialist dialectics. Its vitality, Wang says, comes from tensions it holds together: theoretical completeness and orientation towards practice, scientific truth and openness to development, and universality and national specificity. Wang holds that its basic principles do not become outdated, while it stays abreast of the times by enriching its content as practice develops. Dogmatic application of Marxist phrases that ignores national conditions would, in Wang's view, stifle it.

In the account of China, Wang describes 170 years in which the country moved from humiliation to "standing up, becoming prosperous and becoming strong". Wang sets out two historic leaps in adapting Marxism to China: Mao Zedong Thought and then socialism with Chinese characteristics under Deng Xiaoping. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Wang says, the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has opened a new era and created Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Wang concludes that Marxism shows strong vitality when combined with the practice of different nations. Read the original if you want an example of the official 2018 account of why Marxism endures and how it is placed in the Chinese tradition.
quoteEn: Scientific truth is the essential characteristic of Marxism, and keeping pace with the times is its theoretical quality; uniting the two is an inherent requirement of the development of Marxist theory and the key to its strong vitality.
quoteZh: 科学真理性是马克思主义的本质特征，与时俱进性是马克思主义的理论品质，把二者统一起来是马克思主义理论发展的内在要求，也是马克思主义强大生命力的关键所在。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of the adaptation of Marxism to China.
The official name for China's path of socialist development, associated with Deng Xiaoping and the reform period from the late 1970s.
The Party's official term for the adaptation of Marxism-Leninism to China under Mao Zedong. The article calls it the first major theoretical result of that process.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: Western multiparty democracy in theoretical and practical predicament
zh: 西方多党民主陷入理论与现实困境
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in April 2018, Chai Shangjin argues that Western multiparty competitive democracy has fallen into both theoretical and practical difficulty. The author points to the rise of populist and extreme parties, political polarisation, ineffective governance and social disorder, and says reflection on the system has become an important topic even among Western theorists.

The commentary is organised under four headings: the loss of the "political legitimacy" of multiparty elections; partisan infighting as the "pathogen" of Western disorder; the damage caused by forcing Western-style democracy on other countries; and a short closing section on China.

Chai contends that elections have become contests decided by campaign tricks and money rather than by popular will. The author cites falling turnout, especially among the young, and the claim that governments serve capital whichever party wins. Party rivalry, in this account, produces "veto politics", referendums that deepen social divisions, and an "elite democracy" that hardens into oligarchy and provokes populist backlash. Chai also describes the export of Western democracy, through "colour revolutions", multiparty reforms in Africa, neoliberal reform in Latin America and the Iraq war, as a source of instability, civil war and refugee flows, and as proof of "false democracy, real hegemony".

Chai concludes that the democratic system of socialism with Chinese characteristics has outstanding advantages. The author calls for confidence in presenting those advantages and the world significance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, so as to offer Chinese wisdom and solutions. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese Party-theory commentator in 2018 criticised Western electoral democracy.
quoteEn: Governments produced by democratic voting do not act according to public opinion, and elite politics increasingly becomes oligarchic politics.
quoteZh: 民主投票出来的政府不依民意办事，精英政治越来越成为寡头政治。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official term for China's path since reform and opening up, combining one-party leadership and a socialist system with market mechanisms.
Term for the popular uprisings that changed governments in several post-Soviet states in the 2000s. Chinese official commentary typically presents them as Western-engineered.

t: The wide spread and profound influence of Marxism in the world
zh: 马克思主义在世界上的广泛传播和深刻影响
paras: Published in Guangming Daily in May 2018, shortly after the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth, this commentary by Chai Shangjin takes up Xi Jinping's remark that no body of thought has influenced humanity as widely and deeply as Marxism. Chai argues that, despite 170 years of slander, attack and banning by the bourgeoisie and reactionary forces, Marxism remains an internationally influential system of thought and discourse. The article presents this as a record of repeated confirmation in practice.

The piece is organised in four sections. It begins with how Marxism became the guiding idea of the workers' movement, then turns to the confirmation of its truth in socialist revolution and construction worldwide. A third section deals with the vitality of scientific socialism in China, and a fourth with the continuing need to consult Marxism in solving present-day problems.

Chai first traces how Marx and Engels drew the Communist Manifesto from the workers' movement. In this account, the First International and the struggle against Proudhonism, trade unionism and Bakuninism made Marxism the dominant guiding idea, and the Paris Commune enriched its doctrine of proletarian revolution. Lenin's theory of imperialism and of socialism's victory in one country then turned scientific socialism into a real social system through the October Revolution. After 1945 new socialist states and decolonisation followed, with the founding of the People's Republic of China greatly strengthening world socialism. Chai treats socialism with Chinese characteristics as solving a problem earlier socialist practice left unresolved, namely how to build socialism and show its superiority. He cites 40 years of reform and opening up, China's rise to second place in economic output, and a contribution of over 30 per cent to world growth.

Chai concludes that Marx's two great discoveries still describe the historical epoch. He points to the 2008 financial crisis, widening inequality and political polarisation in the West, a renewed "Marx fever", and a US poll showing millennials turning towards socialism. Socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era, he says, will advance world socialism and contribute "Chinese wisdom and Chinese solutions". Read the original if you want a concise example of how a 2018 Chinese Party-press article narrates Marxism's global history and links it to China's path.
quoteEn: China's taking its own road and building socialism with Chinese characteristics means solving the problems that past socialist practice "did not resolve well", and showing the superiority of the socialist system through new practice and achievements.
quoteZh: 中国走自己的路，搞中国特色社会主义，就是要把过去社会主义实践中“没有解决得很好”的问题解决好，以新的实践和成就，彰显社会主义制度的优越性。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since reform and opening up, which combines Marxist principles with China's national conditions.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
The term for the socialist theory of Marx and Engels, set against earlier "utopian" socialism; it is also the name of a discipline in Chinese Marxist studies.

t: Sensing the truth-power of Marxism
st: On the documentary film Immortal Marx
zh: 感悟马克思主义的真理力量
zhSub: 评文献纪录片《不朽的马克思》
paras: This short commentary, published in Qiushi in 2018, reviews the documentary Immortal Marx, broadcast for the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth. Wei Haisheng presents the film as a union of scientific theory and television art. In Wei's account, it pays tribute to Marx as the greatest thinker of humanity and affirms firm belief in the scientific truth of Marxism.

The film was produced by the Central Party History and Literature Research Institute and China Media Group under the guidance of the Central Propaganda Department. Wei describes how it tells the story of Marx's life, opens with Xi Jinping's statement on the unmatched scientific character and influence of Marxism, and concentrates on the writing and content of the Communist Manifesto and Capital.

Wei argues that the film weaves historical background, documentary sources and theoretical content into a narrative told through people and events. Viewers, Wei says, come to understand Marx's achievements, his character and the contemporary vitality of his theory, which strengthens confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Wei also links the film to Xi Jinping's calls to read the classics and popularise them, and sees it as a first step by the new research institute in that work.

Wei concludes that development is the best way to inherit Marxism: it must keep pace with the times, answer the major questions of practice, and be given new contemporary content. Doing so would let Marxism of the twenty-first century keep developing in China. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Party journal presented a commemorative Marx documentary in 2018 and tied it to the promotion of the classics.
quoteEn: To be true heirs of Marxism, we must treat scientific theory with a scientific attitude and keep giving Marxism new content for the times.
quoteZh: 做马克思主义的真正传人，就要以科学的态度对待科学的理论，不断赋予马克思主义以新的时代内涵。

glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up. It is presented as Marxism applied to Chinese conditions.

glossary.en: confidence in the path, theory, system and culture
glossary.explanation: Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The article uses the four items without the later label.

t: The best way to commemorate Marx
st: Reflections on the original contributions of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to the development of Marxism
zh: 对马克思的最好纪念
zhSub: 关于习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想对发展马克思主义作出的原创性贡献的思考
paras: Written for the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth, this Qiushi article asks what it means to commemorate Marx properly. Ouyang answers that the best commemoration is to keep adapting Marxism to China's conditions and to keep making original contributions to its development. The author presents Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the current outcome of that effort.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the Marxist and Party tradition of keeping pace with the times, from the classic writers through the Party's history from 1921 to the present. The second defines what "originality" means and gives examples of original ideas in Xi Jinping Thought. The third explains why this body of thought emerged and what its status is.

Ouyang argues that originality has three marks: newness, truth and "integration" of Marxist principles with Chinese reality. Original results are either statements the founders never made or developments of what they did say, and the author says the second kind is more common. The examples include the judgement that socialism with Chinese characteristics has entered a new era, the new principal contradiction, the Party's historical mission, the two-stage plan to 2050 with basic modernization by 2035, and a community with a shared future for mankind. Each is described as inheriting and developing a specific Marxist or Party theory. Ouyang attributes the thought's emergence to the questions of the era, Marxism as its theoretical source, practice under Party leadership, and Xi's own character, cultural grounding and career experience.

Ouyang concludes that Marxism's scientific character, popular character and openness have been demonstrated in China. In this account Xi Jinping Thought is "contemporary Chinese Marxism" and "twenty-first-century Marxism", so upholding it in China amounts to genuinely upholding Marxism. The author calls it a new milestone that is still developing. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official line in 2018 framed Xi Jinping Thought as an original contribution to Marxism and as the proper way to mark Marx's bicentenary.
quoteEn: In China today, upholding Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is genuinely upholding Marxism.
quoteZh: 在当今中国，坚持习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想，就是真正坚持马克思主义。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

The Party's formula for the central tension in society at a given stage. The 19th Party Congress (2017) restated it as the contradiction between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations, stressing cooperation, shared security and common development.

t: The "new era" in the eyes of Marx and Engels
zh: 马克思恩格斯眼中的“新时代”
paras: Yang Yingjie asks what Marx and Engels meant when they used the phrase "new era" (xin shidai), a phrase that gained prominence in Chinese political discourse after the 19th Party Congress (2017). Writing in Hongqi Wengao in 2018, Yang argues that in the classic texts the phrase carries three connected meanings: a leap in productive forces driven by science and technology, the emergence of revolutionary new relations of production, and the prospect of the free and all-round development of the human being.

The article is a short exegetical piece organised in three numbered sections, one for each meaning. It gathers passages from Capital, Engels's Dialectics of Nature, his Principles of Communism, the Communist Manifesto and Marx's journalism on the French joint-stock bank Crédit Mobilier. It also draws on Engels's remarks on Dante and on the bourgeoisie and proletariat as children of a new age.

In the first section, Yang reads Marx's comment that the self-acting mule opened a new epoch of automatic machinery, and Engels's praise for Dalton's atomic theory and Mendeleev's periodic table, as marking scientific progress that propels productive forces. Engels's account of agriculture flourishing after the abolition of private property is taken as a new era of liberated productive forces. In the second section, Yang follows Marx's claim that the appearance of capital inaugurates a new epoch. This depends on the free worker who owns nothing but labour-power, so that labour-power becomes a commodity and the bourgeoisie and proletariat arise together. Yang adds Marx's view of joint-stock companies as a powerful lever of capitalist productive forces that also concentrate capital and enlarge the proletariat, the bourgeoisie's grave-diggers.

In the third section, Yang notes that Engels's "new era" develops in meaning and finally points to the future communist society. In Yang's reading, this is the association in which, as the Manifesto puts it, the free development of each is the condition for the free development of all. There, the old division of labour disappears, classes and wealth gaps are abolished, town and country merge, and the fruits of development are shared. Yang concludes that for Marx and Engels the new era rests on a great liberation of productive forces, transforms the relations of production and the principal contradiction in society, and ends in the free development of all humanity. Read the original if you want a compact guide to the passages in Marx and Engels where "new era" appears, as used in the Chinese discourse of 2018.
quoteEn: The "new era" in the eyes of Marx and Engels rests on a great liberation and development of productive forces, drives major changes in the relations of production and shifts in the principal contradiction of society, and ultimately realises a fine society in which every individual, and thereby all humanity, develops freely.
quoteZh: 马克思恩格斯眼中的“新时代”，依托于生产力的大解放大发展，推动生产关系发生重大变革、社会主要矛盾发展变化，最终实现一个每个人都得到自由发展进而全人类得以实现自由发展的美好社会。

glossary.explanation: A term in Chinese Party discourse, prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017), which declared that socialism with Chinese characteristics had entered a new era. The article traces the phrase back to Marx and Engels's uses of the German word for a new epoch.
A concept in Chinese Party theory for the central social contradiction that shapes policy priorities. The 19th Party Congress redefined it in 2017.
A Marxist term for the social relations, above all ownership and class relations, into which people enter in production.

t: A guiding light from victory to victory
st: Commemorating the 170th anniversary of the publication of the Communist Manifesto
zh: 从胜利走向胜利的指路明灯
zhSub: 纪念《共产党宣言》发表170周年
paras: Writing in 2018, the year of the Manifesto's 170th anniversary, Marx's 200th birthday and the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up, Zhang Quanjing argues that rereading the Communist Manifesto helps Party members hold to their original aspiration and mission. In Zhang's view the text remains a practical guide for realising the blueprint set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017). The piece is a commemorative commentary rather than a scholarly study.

The article has four parts. It first traces how the Manifesto shaped the Chinese revolution, from Chen Wangdao's 1920 translation and the founding of the Party to Mao Zedong's repeated reading of it and the example of revolutionary martyrs. It then discusses which of the Manifesto's principles endure, turns to the struggle against historical nihilism, and ends with Party building under Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

Zhang holds that the Manifesto's basic principles have not become outdated, although some of its specific measures have. Citing Engels's prefaces, Zhang says the principles must be applied according to historical conditions: abandoning them is revisionism, and ignoring concrete circumstances is dogmatism. Zhang defends class analysis and the Manifesto's formula of abolishing private property, understood as the private ownership of the means of production, a process of a very long historical period. Zhang also reads the Manifesto's polemics against feudal and other forms of socialism as a model for criticising historical nihilism, which Zhang accuses of denying the history of the Chinese revolution and its leaders.

Zhang concludes that the victory of socialism and communism is certain, as an objective law arising from the contradiction between the productive forces and the relations of production, despite setbacks. Since a revolution needs a revolutionary party, Zhang calls for stronger Party building: upholding the authority of the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, studying Xi's thought, tightening discipline, fighting bureaucratism and corruption, and strengthening democratic centralism and grassroots organisations. Read the original if you want an example of how a senior Party veteran in 2018 linked the Manifesto to Party building, the campaign against historical nihilism and loyalty to Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: In the 170 years since the Communist Manifesto was published, society and history have changed greatly and the international situation has become complex and volatile. Some of the specific measures it proposed are out of date, but the basic principles it sets out are not, and we must still uphold them.
quoteZh: 《共产党宣言》发表170年来，社会历史发生了很大变化，国际形势复杂多变，《宣言》中提出的某些具体措施虽然已经过时，但其所阐述的基本原理并没有过时，仍然是我们必须坚持的。

glossary.explanation: A term used in Party discourse for views said to deny or distort the history of the Chinese revolution, socialist construction and the Party's leaders. The Party has campaigned against it, especially since the early 2010s.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name of Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017. The Party presents it as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.literal: never forget the original aspiration, keep the mission firmly in mind
glossary.explanation: A slogan stressed by Xi Jinping after the 19th Party Congress, calling on Party members to remember why the Party was founded. It was used in a campaign of Party education.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978, which the article marks at its 40th anniversary.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party, combining discussion and election within the Party with binding unity of action once decisions are taken.

t: A true social revolution is necessarily an ideological revolution
st: Commemorating the 170th anniversary of the Communist Manifesto
zh: 真正的社会革命必然是意识形态革命
zhSub: 纪念《共产党宣言》问世一百七十周年
paras: Writing for the 170th anniversary of the Communist Manifesto (2018), Hou argues that every genuine social revolution is an ideological revolution. In the author's reading this has two meanings: a shared future ideal must rally the masses behind a banner, a road and an 'ism', and that ideal must rest on a new worldview. Hou holds that the second point most needs attention today, and calls for rereading the Manifesto as a revolution in worldview.

The article has three sections. The first presents the Manifesto as announcing a new worldview, setting Engels's 1883 summary of its basic idea beside Lenin's reading of it as dialectical materialism applied. The second defends dialectical materialism against three charges: that it is metaphysical, that it is a detached epistemology, and that it is a partisan philosophy. The third takes the identification of the historical subject as the core of the worldview struggle. Along the way Hou cites Mao Zedong, Xi Jinping, Brzezinski and Fukuyama.

Hou contends that the Soviet collapse and the 'end of ideology' thesis led to 'de-ideologizing' Marxist philosophy, which in Hou's view dissolves communism at its root. Dialectical materialism, the author argues, supplies objective truth and laws of history. The proletariat cannot build a moral high ground inside capitalism, so it can only overturn bourgeois morality by taking the 'historical high ground' through scientific theory. Turning socialism into an ethical appeal would lose both heights. Hou then separates two historical subjects: the individual, which belongs to idealist history, and the people, which is the standpoint of materialist history. The author takes Marx's 'real human beings' to be the people, an organic whole with the advanced class at its core, not a sum of individuals.

Hou concludes that dialectical materialism is now the focus of the worldview struggle, and that a people-centred view of history versus an individual-centred one is the test of a true or false historical materialism. The author calls for resisting tendencies to drop materialism, de-ideologize, and reduce the people to individuals, in order to advance socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want to see how a leading Chinese Marxist philosopher links the Manifesto, the Soviet collapse and current debates on practice, humanism and 'the people' to a defence of dialectical materialism.
quoteEn: The Communist Manifesto shows that every genuine social revolution is an ideological revolution.
quoteZh: 《共产党宣言》表明，真正的社会革命都是意识形态革命。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path and system since the reform era. The Party presents it as Marxism applied to Chinese conditions.

glossary.literal: theory of the end of ideology
glossary.explanation: A thesis from Western social science holding that grand ideological conflict has ended. Hou treats it as the context for Fukuyama's 'end of history' and for 'de-ideologizing' Marxism.
In Hou's usage, the claim that the people, understood as an organic whole led by the advanced class, is the subject of history. It is contrasted with an individual-centred view of history.
Hou's term for the tendency to strip Marxist philosophy of its class and worldview character. He describes it as depoliticizing and as a form of 'removing the firewood from under the pot'.

t: The historical necessity of socialist revolution first breaking out in underdeveloped countries, and confidence in the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 不发达国家首先发生社会主义革命的历史必然性与中国特色社会主义道路自信
paras: Liu Shulin takes up a question he regards as foundational for belief in Marxism, for communist ideals and for confidence in the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics: why did socialist revolution first occur in economically underdeveloped countries? He argues that if the question is left unresolved, the legitimacy of existing socialist states, including the Soviet Union, Eastern Europe and China, cannot be defended. His thesis is that such revolutions follow historical necessity and are consistent with Marxism, not departures from it.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs a dispute over Marx's "two inevitables" (the inevitable fall of capitalism and victory of communism) and his "two never wills" in the 1859 Preface. The second reviews how Marx and Engels revised their views on where and when revolution would break out, up to their discussions of Russia. The third turns to Mao Zedong's reading notes on the Soviet political economy textbook and sets out a general law of social development. Liu also cites the 1981 Party resolution on history to defend the socialist transformation of the 1950s.

Liu first rejects the view that the "two never wills" overturn the "two inevitables". He argues that Marx's sentence on tasks arising when material conditions exist "or are at least in the process of formation" shows that capitalism need not be fully developed. He reads Engels's late admission that "we were wrong" as concerning tactics, such as barricade fighting, not the basic conditions for revolution. Liu holds that the opposing view implies that no socialist revolution should have happened since 1917, and that it denies the legitimacy of reform-era China's pre-1978 history. Second, drawing on Mao and on Marx and Engels's global view of capitalism, he proposes a law of "alternating leadership". In each transition between social formations, the more developed regions have a hard social shell and tend to resist change, so the breakthrough comes first where the old order is weaker. In Liu's account this explains feudalism in China, capitalism in western Europe, and socialism in Russia and China.

Liu concludes that settling this question is not merely academic but concerns the future of socialist states. He holds that the opposing position, which he links to historical nihilism, would require every existing socialist country to return to capitalism. Resolving it in theory and practice, he says, is necessary to sustain confidence in socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-affiliated theorist defends the legitimacy of socialist revolution in backward countries against the argument that Marx's own preconditions rule it out.
quoteEn: This law, by which the development of human social formations proceeds through alternating leadership, can be unravelled only by applying the basic principles of historical materialism.
quoteZh: 这种人类社会形态的发展以交替领先的规律进行，只有运用历史唯物主义的基本原理才能解开。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership with a market-oriented economy.
Marx and Engels's conclusion in the Communist Manifesto that capitalism will inevitably perish and communism inevitably triumph.

Marx's 1859 Preface claim that no social formation perishes before its productive forces are fully developed, and that new relations of production never appear before their material conditions mature in the old society.
In Chinese official discourse, a label for interpretations seen as negating the history of the Party and of socialism, such as the pre-1978 period.
The collectivisation of agriculture and the transfer of handicrafts and private industry and commerce to public ownership in China, largely completed by 1956.

keywords: Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy

t: Characteristics, development trends and impact of party politics in Nepal
zh: 尼泊尔政党政治的特点、发展趋势及其影响
paras: Writing in 2018, shortly after the November–December 2017 elections in Nepal, Yuan Qun asks how Nepal's party politics has developed since the 1940s and where it is heading. The article argues that the parties have grown from an illegal movement against feudal autocracy into the dominant political force, and that a left alliance of the two main communist parties is now set to reshape the country's politics and its relations with India and China.

The article first sets out the four stages of party politics: the overthrow of Rana rule and the founding of a constitutional monarchy, the struggle against the partyless panchayat system, the restoration of multiparty parliamentary government, and the move to a republic. It then identifies three features of the party system, three current trends, and three consequences of those trends. Its material is mainly the histories of the Nepali Congress, the communist parties and the Madhesi parties.

On features, Yuan stresses frequent splits and mergers, as parties that entered parliament put pragmatic pursuit of power ahead of ideals and become factional "election parties". A "three-legged" structure has also formed: the Nepali Congress, the CPN (UML) and the Maoists, each with about 300,000 members, favoured by a mixed electoral system, with Madhesi parties in fourth place. On trends, Yuan contends that India, which the author says treats Nepal's communists as close to China, will intensify interference through Congress, Madhesi parties and the 2015–16 blockade. The communists are expected to consolidate, with a merger likely because the dispute over the revolutionary road has ended. Anti-Indian nationalism is also expected to rise, while Congress under Deuba is described as tilting towards India.

As consequences, Yuan predicts that the Nepali communist movement will enter a new, higher stage. The author also expects the left alliance government to bring much greater stability, citing ten prime ministers in nine years and a constitutional two-year bar on no-confidence motions. In foreign policy it is expected to keep Nepal's traditional "equidistance" balance, avoiding a break with India while deepening practical cooperation with China to gain room for manoeuvre. Read the original if you want a China-based scholar's 2018 reading of Nepal's party system, its communist factions and India–China rivalry, with detailed chronologies of party splits and mergers.
quoteEn: As Nepal's communist forces consolidate and an unprecedented unity takes shape, the left alliance government about to take office will be better able to withstand internal and external interference.
quoteZh: 随着尼泊尔共产主义运动力量整合和空前团结局面的形成, 即将执政的左翼联盟政府抵抗内外因素干扰的能力也将随之增强

glossary.explanation: This entry is not used in the paragraphs and is replaced below.

t: Adaptive change and political direction of Europe's radical left parties
zh: 欧洲激进左翼政党的适应性变革与政治走向
paras: How have Europe's radical left parties adapted since the collapse of the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe, and where are they heading? Writing in 2017, Wang Congcong argues that parties which updated their ideology and organisation to national conditions have fared best, while electoral results depend on many factors besides ideological renewal. The article sets this against the background of a prolonged crisis in European social democracy.

The article first defines radical left parties, following Luke March and others, as parties to the left of social democrats and Greens that oppose the basic structure of contemporary capitalism. It reviews typologies by Uwe Backes and Patrick Moreau and by March, and proposes four groups: traditional communist parties, successor parties, new left alliances, and "red-green" parties. It then compares adaptation among traditional parties and "new left" parties, and ends with a survey of electoral trends since the 1990s.

Wang argues that traditional parties such as the Greek and Portuguese communist parties kept the communist name, Marxism-Leninism and, in varying degrees, democratic centralism, with only small organisational changes. The French party abandoned democratic centralism in 1994, and the Italian Refoundation party also democratised. "New left" parties dropped the communist label and democratic centralism, opened their structures, set term limits and gender quotas, and cooperated at EU level through the European United Left–Nordic Green Left group and the Party of the European Left (2004). Ideologically they turned to democratic socialism or eco-socialism, absorbing environmentalist and feminist themes, and revised their electoral strategies and attitude to government participation. The author sees national party systems, the strength of social democrats and Greens, and party leaderships as shaping which path is possible.

Wang concludes that the link between renewal and votes is complex. Nordic parties and several Western European ones, such as the German Left Party and the Greek Syriza (which formed a government in 2015), have gained ground. Some traditionalist communist parties have kept stable support, while the French and Italian parties have declined. Wang judges that most radical left parties are unlikely to overtake social democrats in the short term, citing fragmentation at European level and weak, untested policy programmes at home. Their future depends mainly on credible, forward-looking policies. Read the original if you want a structured comparison of how European communist and post-communist parties changed after 1989, including electoral data.
quoteEn: The future development of Europe's radical left parties still depends mainly on putting forward convincing, forward-looking policies that are accepted by the masses.
quoteZh: 欧洲激进左翼政党的未来发展,依然主要靠提出令人信服的、为大众所接受的、前瞻性的政策。

glossary.explanation: A Leninist organisational principle combining internal discussion with binding discipline once decisions are taken. The article says it often became a top-down hierarchy in communist parties.
Here it denotes radical left parties open to 'new politics' themes such as environmentalism, feminism and pacifism, as opposed to traditional communist parties.
A socialist orientation pursued through democratic and parliamentary means. The article treats it as a common ideological choice of the 'new left' parties, distinct from Keynesian social democracy.
A current that combines socialist anti-capitalism with ecological concerns. The article cites the French Left Party's programme as an example.

t: The Japanese Communist Party's "setback" in the House of Representatives election
zh: 日本共产党众议院选举“退步”
paras: Why did the Japanese Communist Party (JCP) lose ground in the 48th House of Representatives election of 22 October 2017? This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2018, answers that the party's own explanation, "insufficient party strength", is incomplete. Cao argues that a surprise election, a collapsed opposition front, a lack of funds and an unchanging campaign strategy all contributed.

The piece opens with the results: the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) won 284 seats and, with its coalition partner Komeito, 313 of 465, more than two-thirds. The JCP won 12 seats, down from 21 in 2014, and its proportional-representation vote fell from 6.06 million to 4.4 million. Cao then examines four factors in turn and ends with a general assessment of the party.

On timing, Cao describes how Prime Minister Abe Shinzo, weakened by the Moritomo and Kake scandals, reshuffled his cabinet. Cao says he then used North Korea's missile and nuclear tests and Trump's planned visit to recover support before calling a snap election, which left small parties little time to prepare. The opposition front built for the 2016 upper-house election broke up when the Democratic Party split, so the JCP had to renegotiate alliances. Cao adds that the party's refusal of state political funds forces it to contest only winnable districts, and that its strategy of recruiting members and expanding Akahata circulation has barely changed and does not appeal to young voters.

Cao concludes that the LDP coalition's political manoeuvring made the contest very hard for the JCP. In Cao's view, the party's own lack of political sensitivity and weak party-building were what finally caused the defeat. Cao proposes that raising political sensitivity and the ability to respond to changing circumstances should be the practical goal of the party's future building. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language assessment of the JCP's 2017 electoral performance and of its structural weaknesses.
quoteEn: Subjectively, it was the JCP's own lack of political sensitivity and the absence and weakness of its own political party-building that ultimately led to this electoral defeat.
quoteZh: 从主观上看，日共自身的政治敏感度以及党的自身政治建设的缺失和乏力，最终导致此次选举失利。

t: The shift in logic of the Communist Party of the Russian Federation's parliamentary anti-corruption work
zh: 俄罗斯共产党议会反腐的逻辑转换
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2018, asks how the Communist Party of the Russian Federation (CPRF), the largest successor of the CPSU and now the leading opposition party in the State Duma, has changed its approach to fighting corruption. Liao and Xu argue that the party has moved from "subversive" confrontation with the authorities to "constructive" cooperation inside parliament.

The article first traces the cognitive shift: early street struggle and the overthrow of the regime as the main goal gave way, after poor results, to the view that anti-corruption should be pursued jointly by ruling and opposition forces. It then examines four reasons for the change and closes by assessing the effects on Russian party politics and the difficulties that remain.

The authors present the shift as an expedient route to the party's own goals, a requirement of theoretical and practical innovation, a way to consolidate its political position among a divided left, and a path into the political mainstream, where they say Putin wants a "constructive" centre-left opposition. They credit the CPRF with helping shape a more regular party system and with hundreds of anti-corruption bills, including the 2013 proposal to introduce the UN Convention's "illicit enrichment" concept and a 2012 proposal on officials' luxury official cars.

Liao and Xu note unresolved tensions: the party must reconcile being an in-system party with the risk of implicitly legitimising the current regime, and it needs better anti-corruption personnel, more young members and less radical positions. They conclude that the CPRF still has a long road ahead. Read the original if you want a brief, sympathetic Chinese account of how a major post-Soviet communist party has adapted to parliamentary politics.
quoteEn: The change in attitude from \"subversion\" to \"construction\" signifies not only a shift in the logic of the CPRF's parliamentary anti-corruption work, but also a change of course in its strategy of political participation.
quoteZh: 由“颠覆”到“建设”的态度变化，不仅意味着俄共议会反腐的逻辑转换，更代表着政治参与的策略转轨。
keywords: Communist Party of the Russian Federation

t: "Capitalism has always been an unstable system"
st: Foreign left-wing scholars on the current crisis of capitalism
zh: “资本主义一直是个不稳定的系统”
zhSub: 国外左翼学者看当前资本主义危机现象
paras: This short commentary, published in Beijing Daily in 2018, surveys how foreign left-wing scholars have analysed the capitalist crisis that began in the early twenty-first century. Tong reports that these analyses trace the crisis to five dimensions: it is a crisis of the mode of production, of democracy, of values, of ecology and of the system as a whole.

The piece is organised under one heading for each dimension. It draws on David Harvey, Paul Jorion, Mary Warren, Noam Chomsky, Joseph Stiglitz, Andrew W. Jones, Richard Smith, Immanuel Wallerstein, Wolfgang Streeck and Kozo Yamamura, mostly through short quotations.

On production, Tong presents the view that capitalism's room for manoeuvre is narrowing. Harvey is cited as saying that internal contradictions are repeatedly displaced outwards, while Jorion calls capitalism a perpetually unstable system. On democracy and values, the scholars are reported to describe Western democracy as rule by money, with campaign donations, lobbying and the Wall Street–Treasury "revolving door" tying the state to capital. Cited poll figures say 61 per cent of Americans think their economy favours the rich. Their claim is that ideals of freedom and equality are undermined by inequality and by hegemonic practice abroad.
