On ecology, Jones and Smith are said to hold that green capitalism cannot work, because growth as capital accumulation is built into the system. Tong closes with scholars who see a structural crisis. Wallerstein foresees the system reaching its limits within thirty to forty years, Streeck lists five systemic problems, and Yamamura calls for change "outside the box" rather than reform within the existing system. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-press digest of Western left critiques of capitalism after the 2008 crisis, with names to follow up.
quoteEn: Capitalism's room for manoeuvre is narrowing, and the measures it once used to overcome crises will, over time, lose their effect under the fundamental contradiction between the socialisation of production and the private capitalist appropriation of the means of production.
quoteZh: 资本主义的回旋空间在收窄，资本主义曾经用以克服危机的种种举措，随着时间的推移，都将在生产的社会化与生产资料的资本主义私人占有这个根本矛盾的影响下失去效用。

t: Why Marx is receiving ever more attention
zh: 马克思为何越来越受重视
paras: Marking the 170th anniversary of the Communist Manifesto in February 2018, this short commentary, first published in the People's Daily, asks why Marx is increasingly valued in both China and the West. Feng argues that the Manifesto deserves commemoration in socialist and capitalist countries alike, because Marx decisively shaped the course of history and changed how people understand it.

The piece cites the Manifesto's translation into more than 110 languages and over 1,000 editions, and Terry Eagleton's description of it as the most influential work of the nineteenth century. It then turns to the West, where it points to university reading lists, to Eric Hobsbawm's assessment of Marx's twentieth-century legacy, and to the anniversaries of 1998, 2008 and 2018. Finally it turns to China.

Feng contends that recent developments in the United States and Europe confirm Marx's judgement that capitalism cannot remove its own basic contradictions. In Feng's image, the "verdict" Marx passed on capitalism has been postponed but remains valid. The author notes that capitalists and Western politicians and scholars, including George Soros, are rediscovering the Manifesto. For China, Feng claims that the victories of revolution, construction and reform and opening up have repeatedly proved the Manifesto's truth in practice.

Feng concludes that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017), carries Marxism forward and revitalises scientific socialism in twenty-first-century China. In the article's account, it also offers developing countries a new path to modernization and a Chinese approach to human problems. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese official media presented Marx's global relevance on the Manifesto's 170th anniversary.
quoteEn: The influence of the Communist Manifesto in the West is growing with each passing day.
quoteZh: 《共产党宣言》在西方的影响与日俱增。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from 1978.
The term for the socialist theory founded by Marx and Engels, as distinguished from utopian socialism. In Chinese usage it denotes Marxist theory of socialism and communism.

t: The original aspiration revealed in the Communist Manifesto
zh: 《共产党宣言》昭示的初心
paras: Marking the 170th anniversary of the Communist Manifesto in 2018, Zhang Kuiliang argues in this newspaper commentary that the document expresses the original aspiration (chuxin) of all communists: the complete emancipation of humankind. For Zhang, its goal of communism and its call to overthrow capitalism are the ideological foundation that no communist should forget.

The piece sets the Manifesto in its mid-nineteenth-century context, when capitalist contradictions had surfaced and an independent workers' movement lacked party leadership. It then turns to the Chinese Communist Party's relationship to the text and to the present call to remain true to the original aspiration since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Zhang presents the Manifesto as both a party programme and the formal birth of Marxism. Applying historical materialism, it shows capitalism's necessary demise, but Zhang stresses that social laws do not operate automatically: the proletariat and its party must carry out the historical mission. Zhang reads the Manifesto's "two ruptures" with traditional property relations and traditional ideas as the content of communist revolution, while insisting that they cannot happen all at once and require gradual measures.

Zhang concludes that the Party must hold to the communist ideal as a bottom line for policy, while recognising that achieving it is gradual and staged. Building a moderately prosperous society and pursuing socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era are said to match the Manifesto's final aim and lay its foundations. Read the original if you want a brief example of how the Manifesto was invoked in 2018 to support the Party's "original aspiration" discourse.
quoteEn: Communism must never remain mere talk; it must be a bottom line that none of our practical policies may fundamentally violate.
quoteZh: 共产主义绝不能流于口头,而必须是我们一切现实政策不能根本违背的底线。

glossary.explanation: A slogan stressed by Xi Jinping, especially from 2017, that the Party must "not forget its original aspiration" of serving the people and pursuing communism.
The Manifesto's call for the most radical break with traditional property relations and with traditional ideas, which the author treats as the content of communist revolution.
A Chinese development goal of general, moderate prosperity, which the Party aimed to complete by 2020.
The official name for the Chinese Party-state's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.

t: The contemporary value of the Communist Manifesto
zh: 《共产党宣言》的时代价值
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in March 2018, Niu Xianfeng asks what the Communist Manifesto, first published in German in London in February 1848, still offers today. Niu argues that it marks the birth of Marxism and that its influence reaches beyond its own era and Western Europe, supplying a worldview, a scientific method and a guide to action.

The short commentary moves through five claims: the Manifesto answered the basic question of its time; it turned socialism from utopia into science; it changed the global political order; it offers a method for understanding the contemporary world; and it is a source of spiritual strength for Communists.

Niu holds that, with industrial transformation in mid-nineteenth-century Britain, the bourgeoisie and proletariat became the two main classes. The Manifesto, in Niu's reading, used the theory of surplus value and historical materialism to expose exploitation and conclude that the fall of the bourgeoisie and the victory of the proletariat are equally inevitable. Niu traces from it the October Revolution, the founding of the Communist Party of China in 1921 and what the article calls the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Niu rejects doubts about this conclusion, including claims that communism is remote or Marxism outdated, as seeing only surface appearances. Communism, the article says, may take many generations, but the movement toward it has never stopped.

Niu concludes that the Manifesto's spirit of selflessness, struggle and concern for humanity should motivate Party members today. Upholding Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, which Niu calls Marxism of contemporary China and of the twenty-first century, is presented as carrying the Manifesto forward. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Manifesto's legacy was presented in the Party press in 2018.
quoteEn: The Manifesto not only found the causes of the bourgeoisie's demise but also found its gravediggers, achieving socialism's leap from utopia to science.
quoteZh: 《宣言》不仅找到了资产阶级灭亡的原因,而且找到了埋葬它的掘墓人,实现了社会主义从空想到科学的飞跃。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official name for China's path, system and theory of socialism since reform and opening up.

t: Opportunities and challenges for the American socialist movement in the early twenty-first century
zh: 21世纪初美国社会主义运动面临的机遇与挑战
paras: Lei Hongyan asks what prospects the socialist movement in the United States has in the early twenty-first century. The article argues that the movement faces both real opportunities and serious difficulties. Writing in 2018, Lei concludes that, while success in the short term is unlikely, the general direction of social development means that exploration of the socialist road will not disappear as long as capitalism exists in the United States.

The article begins with the global setting, claiming that world socialism has entered a stage of revival after the upheavals in Eastern Europe and the Soviet Union. It then takes up three sources of opportunity: the spread and study of socialist ideas in the US, the shift in public opinion after the 2007–08 financial crisis, and the weakening of capitalism's legitimacy. A final section turns to challenges in the Trump period, namely reformism, the split between the workers' movement and the socialist movement, the weakness of the Communist Party USA (CPUSA), and entrenched prejudice against socialism.

Lei grounds the opportunities in the claim that the crisis exposed the basic contradiction of capitalism between socialised production and private ownership of the means of production. The article cites the annual Socialist Scholars Conference, the CPUSA debate on what socialism means, rising university interest in Marxism, and Piketty's figures on inequality. It also cites polls showing that many young Americans view socialism favourably and notes the Sanders campaign and Occupy Wall Street. Using Sombart's argument about why the US lacked socialism, Lei reasons that stagnation and widening inequality now favour the movement.

On the challenges, Lei argues that mass protest is fragmented, aims mostly at reforming capitalism and lacks organisational leadership. Many workers, including a stratum of "labour aristocracy", were drawn to Trump rather than to socialist organisations. The CPUSA, with fewer than 10,000 mostly elderly members, is described as marginal and theoretically immature. Lei says it blames the crisis on neoliberal policy errors and proposes Keynesian, New Deal-style remedies. Lei calls on the Party to reform itself and to link socialism with the workers' movement. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly assessment of American socialism after 2008, including its use of polls, party-building and Sanders-era debates.
quoteEn: As long as the capitalist system continues to exist in the United States, the American exploration of the socialist road will not die out.
quoteZh: 只要资本主义制度仍然在美国存在，美国对社会主义道路的探索就不会消亡。

t: Foreign left-wing scholars on opportunities, problems, challenges and proposals for publicity work of the world socialist movement
zh: 国外左翼学者谈世界社会主义运动宣传工作的 机遇、问题、挑战与建议
paras: This is a report on views voiced at the 8th World Socialism Forum, held in Beijing on 14–15 October 2017 on the eve of the 19th Party Congress. The forum was hosted by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences under the theme of the era's great development, great change and great adjustment and socialism with Chinese characteristics. Li Qiang and Li Shuqing summarise what visiting left-wing scholars said about publicity work for socialism. In the authors' account, the visitors saw favourable conditions for the world socialist movement but weak propaganda capacity, and offered concrete proposals.

The report speaks of participants from several countries and organisations. They include Allan Freeman (University of Manitoba), Roger van Zwanenberg of Pluto Press, Radhika Desai, Cem Kizilcec from Turkey, Andrea Catone of the Italian journal Marx XXI, Wadih Halabi of the US Communist Party's economic commission, Egon Krenz and the Brazilian student Gaio Doria. It is organised in three parts: new opportunities, problems and challenges, and strategies for improvement.

On opportunities, the speakers are reported as saying that mass movements are rising worldwide and that China's development contributes to the world economy and demonstrates the superiority of the socialist system. Several are quoted as saying that the Belt and Road Initiative and a strong socialist state help to restrain imperialism. On problems, the scholars say socialist publicity is weak and that Western media distort socialism and China. Freeman is quoted as saying many people consider socialism attractive but unrealistic. Zwanenberg admits he does not clearly understand socialism with Chinese characteristics, and others say it is wrongly seen as applicable only to China.

The proposals reported are: keep up forums and journals and invite more Western left-wing scholars and politicians; focus on the Third World, the former Soviet and East European states and Latin America, and on ordinary people rather than elites; build internet, television, radio and training networks, including summer schools and a Marxist international university; translate key documents such as the 19th Party Congress report; and choose suitable forms of ideological struggle. The authors close by presenting the Forum as a platform for Marxists and a window for publicising socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want to see how invited foreign leftists, as reported by Chinese organisers, assessed China's external publicity work in 2017.
quoteEn: World socialism needs media outlets so that it can carry out socialist publicity on a global scale.
quoteZh: 世界社会主义需要有媒体出口，在全球范围内进行社会主义宣传。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path of building socialism since reform and opening up. It is presented as combining Marxism with China's conditions.
An annual forum held since 2009 by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, bringing together Chinese and foreign Marxists and left-wing figures.
A Chinese infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

t: The world significance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的世界意义
paras: Writing in early 2018, after the 19th Party Congress (2017) made Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era the Party's guiding ideology, Li Shenming asks what historical position and world significance this body of thought has. The article argues that its significance is global as well as national. Li presents it as supplying "Chinese confidence", "Chinese ideas" and a "Chinese solution" to a world in flux, and as advancing the development of twenty-first-century Marxism.

The article is organised in four parts. The first views the thought from the angle of China's own development, tracing the path from the semi-colonial period after 1840 through the 1949 revolution and reform and opening up to the "stood up, grown rich, becoming strong" sequence. The second looks at the broad currents of human development and the values, development outlook and foreign relations that China offers. The third considers the changing world order and China's proposals for global governance. The fourth places the thought within a periodisation of capitalist epochs and within the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

Li's central claims run as follows. China's rise, in his account, is itself a contribution to world peace, and socialism with Chinese characteristics is a "brand-new reference" for developing countries seeking modernisation while keeping their independence. Building a community with a shared future for mankind is described as resting on humanity's common values, on a broad international united front, on developing countries and peoples as the main force, and ultimately on Marx and Engels's "association" of free development. Li insists that these common values are relative and must not be confused with "universal values", which he calls a Western tool for Westernising and dividing China. Drawing on Lenin, he argues that the present is the era of financial imperialism, marked by extreme global polarisation and now at a turning point of decline, with neoliberalism giving way to socialism's growing appeal. He holds that new technology, including artificial intelligence, cannot resolve capitalism's basic contradiction.

Li concludes that the world needs new theory and can produce it, and that Xi Jinping Thought, which contains a Chinese solution for global governance, arises at the right moment. He calls for firm adherence to Marxism together with innovation based on new practice, so as to advance the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. He notes that China neither imports foreign models nor exports its own. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how a senior Chinese Marxist scholar links Xi Jinping Thought, Lenin's theory of imperialism and the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteEn: Today's China and today's world are a China and a world that need theory and are able to produce new theory.
quoteZh: 当今中国和当今世界是一个需要理论而且能够产生新理论的中国与世界。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations built on shared interests and common challenges, promoted since the early 2010s and presented in his January 2017 Geneva speech.
The official name for China's system and path since the reform era, combining Marxist principles with China's conditions.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era opens a new horizon for the international communist movement
zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想开辟国际共产主义运动新境界
paras: Writing in Contemporary World (Dangdai shijie) in 2018, shortly after the 19th Party Congress (2017), Lü Weizhou asks what the Party's new guiding ideology means for scientific socialism and the international communist movement. The article argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era enriches scientific socialism, shows the advantages of the socialist system, and will lead the international communist movement into a new stage.

The article has three main sections. The first treats the Thought as a development of scientific socialism, drawing on lessons from the movement's history since the Communist Manifesto, including the upheavals in Eastern Europe and the Soviet collapse. The second turns to socialist construction in China since reform and opening up, citing growth, high-speed rail and foreign-exchange figures. The third considers what China's experience means abroad.

Lü draws two lessons from the movement's history: the basic principles of scientific socialism and the ultimate communist goal must not be abandoned, and scientific socialism is a method, not a dogma, to be applied creatively to each country's conditions. On this basis Lü presents the Thought as continuing Marxism-Leninism, Mao Zedong Thought and later Party theory, and as advancing understanding of the stage of socialist development and the principal contradiction in Chinese society. The system's advantages are said to lie in keeping people at the centre, upholding Party leadership, and holding firm to ideals and convictions. Lü holds that China's path has encouraged foreign communist parties and left forces, offered developing countries a reference model for modernization with independence, and, through a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative, offered a global vision. Evidence includes a Uruguayan editor's remarks and a Thomas Friedman comment.

Lü concludes that the new two-step plan to build a modern socialist country by the mid-century will further show the strengths of scientific socialism and socialism with Chinese characteristics. The author predicts that this will drive a full revival of the international communist movement. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese Party scholarship in 2018 framed the Thought's significance for world socialism and the international communist movement.
quoteEn: Contemporary China, guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, has opened a new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics and at the same time a new horizon for the international communist movement.
quoteZh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想引领下的当代中国，在开启中国特色社会主义新时代的同时，也开启了国际共产主义运动新境界。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017. It is presented officially as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism, associated with Deng Xiaoping and the reform era. It combines Party leadership and public ownership with market mechanisms.

The term Marxists use for socialism grounded in Marx and Engels's analysis of history and capitalism, as opposed to utopian socialism. In Chinese usage it is also a name for the theory guiding the international communist movement.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2013. It calls for joint development and cooperation among states.
A Chinese infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, linking China with countries in Asia, Europe and Africa.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world that began in China in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: A century of ups and downs of the Swedish Communist Party
zh: 瑞典共产党的百年沧桑
paras: Writing in 2017, a century after the Swedish Communist Party was founded in May 1917, Yuan Qun uses the party as a case study of the Swedish communist movement and, more broadly, of European communism. The article argues that the party's history falls into three stages: a period as a communist party, a period of de-Sovietization, and a period as a socialist party. In Yuan's account, this path explains the party's present achievements and its continuing difficulties.

The article is a chronological narrative. It begins with the split of the Social Democratic Left Party from the Swedish Social Democratic Party in 1917 and the party's entry into the Comintern. It then follows the repeated expulsions and splits of the 1920s and 1930s, the party's positions in the Second World War and its postwar rise. For the later decades it covers the break with Moscow after 1956, the changes of name to Left Communist Party (1967) and Left Party (1990), and the party's role in Swedish parliamentary politics up to 2014.

Yuan's central point is that the party was repeatedly weakened by disputes over its line, above all its relation to the Soviet Union and to the Social Democrats. In this reading, Comintern interference, the pro-Soviet stance during the Soviet–Finnish war, and later the shocks of 1956, 1968 and 1989–91 cost it support. Carl-Henric Hermansson's reforms from 1964 dropped democratic centralism and Marxism-Leninism and pursued a parliamentary road. After 1990 the party redefined itself as a socialist and feminist party, which Yuan says brought parliamentary gains and a 'red-green' alliance with the Social Democrats and Greens. Yuan judges that the party has played down Marxism and relied on environmental, feminist and internationalist themes. According to the article, these themes overlap with those of rival parties and have alienated traditional working-class voters.

Yuan concludes that the party remains much weaker than the Social Democrats, who built the 'Swedish model' and long dominated politics. It was also left out of government in 2014. Yuan nonetheless sees a emerging image as the 'left of the left', a more united party and a growing membership. Its future is said to depend on three things: balancing transformation with its socialist character, strengthening cooperation with the left and with extra-parliamentary movements, and widening its international influence. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese-language account of the party's internal factions, name changes and electoral record, or a Chinese scholarly view of the European communist movement.
quoteEn: The hundred-year history of the Swedish Communist Party is a history of twists and turns, and also a history of continuous exploration of a socialist road with Swedish characteristics.
quoteZh: 瑞典共产党的百年历史是一个曲折发展的历史, 也是一个不断探索具有瑞典特色的社会主义道路的历史。

t: The Communist Party of the Russian Federation's understanding and assessment of the October Revolution
zh: 俄罗斯联邦共产党对十月革命的认识与评价
source: Journal of China University of Mining and Technology (Social Sciences), 2017 no. 5
paras: Writing on the eve of the centenary of the October Revolution in 2017, Li Yazhou asks how the Communist Party of the Russian Federation (CPRF), successor to the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, understands and evaluates that revolution. Li argues that the CPRF has defended the Revolution consistently since its founding. The article presents the party's stance as holding to the Revolution's historical achievements while offering a sober account of why Soviet socialism failed.

The article has three parts. The first traces the CPRF's defence of the Revolution from its founding in 1990 through its ban after the August 1991 events and its restoration in 1993. It follows the party's conflicts with the Yeltsin and Putin governments over the 7 November holiday and its preparations for the 2017 centenary, including plenums, a preparatory committee and a proposal to hold the 19th international meeting of communist and workers' parties in Russia. The second part sets out six basic CPRF positions, drawing on Zyuganov's reports and his 2016 Xinhua interview. The third part draws lessons.

In Li's account, the CPRF holds that the Revolution was neither accidental nor a coup. It was the outcome of Lenin's analysis of imperialism, in which tsarist Russia was the weakest link in the capitalist chain, and of Bolshevik slogans that won mass support. The party credits the Revolution with defeating foreign intervention, rapid industrialisation, the victory in the Great Patriotic War and the ending of national oppression. It also credits the Revolution with a global impact on national liberation movements and on the founding of the Chinese Communist Party. The CPRF is also reported as attributing the Soviet collapse partly to betrayal by Gorbachev and his circle and to Western hostility. It names deeper causes too: over-centralisation, excessive statisation, a simplified view of socialism, and a ruling party cut off from ordinary workers.

Li concludes that the CPRF adopts a historical-materialist approach, affirming the Stalin model's historical rationality under the conditions of its time while analysing its failures candidly. From this Li draws four principles for assessing the history of socialist revolution and construction: seeking truth from facts, historical analysis, comprehensiveness and objectivity, and a forward-looking orientation. Li says these would strengthen confidence in the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic overview of the CPRF's official line on 1917, its commemorative politics and its explanation of the Soviet collapse.
quoteEn: The CPRF's historical-materialist way of understanding and assessing the October Revolution shows us that any assessment of the historical role of socialist revolution and construction must follow four basic principles: seeking truth from facts, historical analysis, comprehensiveness and objectivity, and a forward-looking orientation.
quoteZh: 俄共这种以历史唯物主义态度认识与评价十月革命的做法启示我们, 对社会主义革命和建设历史作用的认识和评价, 必须遵循实事求是、历史分析、全面客观、面向未来四个基本原则

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's current path of socialist development, associated with reform and opening up since 1978. Official texts present it as Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions.
A principle associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping that stresses judging matters by actual conditions rather than doctrine. It is a standard formula in Party discourse on method.

t: The contingency and necessity of the October Revolution
zh: 十月革命的偶然性与必然性
paras: This is a Chinese translation of an article by the Russian author S. N. Malyeyev, written shortly before the centenary of 1917. It takes up the claim, which the author attributes to liberal media and politicians, that the October Revolution was an accident or the work of a malign Bolshevik conspiracy. Malyeyev argues instead that October followed with objective logic from the war, the unresolved questions of land and peace, and the failure of the Provisional Government.

The article follows events chronologically. It begins with the February Revolution and the bread queues, then covers the dual power of the Provisional Government and the Petrograd Soviet, the crises of spring and summer 1917, the July Days, the Kornilov affair, the storming of the Winter Palace and the Second Congress of Soviets. It then turns to the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly in January 1918 and the record of the White regimes in the civil war. Malyeyev draws heavily on Kerensky's memoirs, Lenin's writings, Sukhanov and the Soviet military historian N. E. Kakurin.

The central claim is that the war was the decisive factor and that the revolution must be understood as a process with two stages, following Lenin's April Theses. The Provisional Government could neither end the war nor distribute land, so the Soviets' strength grew. Malyeyev cites Kerensky's own admissions that the army had lost its will to fight and that without Kornilov's attempted coup there would have been no October. In this reading the seizure of power was close to a formality: the Petrograd garrison had gone over to the Soviet, and the defenders of the Winter Palace numbered about 2,000.

Malyeyev also presents the choice in late 1917 as one between a military dictatorship of reactionary generals and "all power to the Soviets". He cites accounts of Kolchak, Denikin, Yudenich and Wrangel to argue that the White regimes' brutality drove the peasantry to the revolution. He says the Mensheviks and Socialist Revolutionaries ended up objectively on the counter-revolutionary side. The article closes by announcing a separate treatment of the post-Brest-Litovsk measures and state capitalism. Read the original if you want a Russian author's polemical defence of the revolution's historical necessity against liberal revisionism, built largely on contemporary memoir sources.
quoteEn: The coexistence of dual power in Russia thus created the preconditions for the outbreak of the October Revolution.
quoteZh: 俄国的双重政权并存就这样为十月革命的爆发创造了前提条件。

t: The October Revolution and the new era in human history: a further discussion
zh: 再论十月革命开辟的人类历史新纪元
source: Marxist Theory Discipline Studies (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2017 no. 3
paras: Marking the centenary of the 1917 October Revolution, Wu Enyuan asks what the Revolution opened for world history and whether the collapse of the Soviet Union discredits it. Wu argues that the Revolution inaugurated a new era: it broke capitalism's monopoly on the world order, made Marxism a practical reality, and still shapes the course of world socialism through socialism with Chinese characteristics. The collapse of the USSR, in Wu's view, was not a failure of the socialist system.

The article has four parts. The first treats the Revolution as the realisation of Marxist revolutionary theory, its effects on Soviet development, and its influence on a capitalist world in crisis. The second covers the contribution of the Communist International, the Soviet Union and the Chinese Communist Party to defeating German and Japanese fascism. The third rebuts the claim that Soviet dissolution proves socialism failed. The fourth links the Revolution to China's revolutionary and reform record.

Wu holds that the Bolsheviks won through firm Party leadership, Soviet policies on land, peace and national self-determination, and Lenin's creative application of Marxism to Russia, which rejected both a purely bourgeois and an immediately socialist course. Citing Soviet and Russian sources, Wu points to rapid industrialisation, full employment, expanded education and social insurance in the 1930s, and argues that capitalist states absorbed socialist-style planning and social policy to escape the post-1920 crises. On the USSR's end, Wu concedes serious institutional flaws but cites Russian economists, Security Council secretary Nikolai Patrushev and Gorbachev himself to argue that the collapse resulted from reform errors, not inevitability.

Wu concludes that socialism with Chinese characteristics is both a product of the October Revolution and an extension of its significance. Wu credits successive Chinese leaders with drawing on Soviet experience and lessons, and cites economic data from 1949 to 2016, including growth since the 18th Party Congress (2012), to contrast China's stability with Western stagnation. The movement of world socialism, Wu says, is still thriving. Read the original if you want a Chinese-academy defence of the Revolution's legacy and an account of how Chinese scholars rebut the "inevitable collapse" view of the Soviet Union.
quoteEn: But this does not accord with the facts.
quoteZh: 但这并不符合事实。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's current path and system, introduced by Deng Xiaoping in the early 1980s. It combines Party leadership and public ownership with market reform.
The Comintern, an international organisation of communist parties founded in Moscow in 1919 and dissolved in 1943.

t: The development of the Latin American communist movement after the October Revolution
zh: 十月革命后拉美共产主义运动发展
paras: Writing in 2017, the centenary of the October Revolution, Xu Shicheng asks how that event shaped communism in Latin America and how the movement has fared since. The article argues that the revolution acted as a catalyst for the founding of communist parties across the region, which then went through a winding history of repression, split, collapse and recovery. Xu holds that the Latin American left has not died despite recent setbacks.

The article follows the movement in four stages. It begins with the early spread of knowledge of the revolution and the founding of parties from the 1910s to the 1950s, then turns to the effects of the Soviet collapse in the early 1990s. It next covers the rise of the left and of what some Chinese scholars call "Latin American national socialism" from the late 1990s, and ends with the position of the movement around 2015–2017. Xu draws on Latin American thinkers such as Mariátegui, on party histories and on election results.

Xu argues that the Cold War, the Sino-Soviet split and military coups in the 1960s and 1970s repeatedly pushed the parties underground and divided them. The 1973 coup in Chile ended the "Chilean road" to socialism. The Soviet collapse hit Cuba hardest, with the author citing a 34 per cent fall in GDP between 1990 and 1993. It also split parties, and some, such as the Brazilian PCB, changed their identity, while others that held to Marxism-Leninism, such as the Communist Party of Brazil, grew. From about 1999, left governments came to power in Venezuela, Brazil, Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador and elsewhere, and the São Paulo Forum grew to 110 organisations. Xu names the problems of this left as an unchanged primary-export economy, corruption, conservative offensives, internal divisions and US interference, and these were followed by the "left down, right up" shift from 2015.

Xu concludes that the pendulum has swung right but that the left retains strength. In support, Xu cites Ortega's re-election in Nicaragua in 2016, left governments still in office elsewhere, and the region's deep inequality. The article adds that more than twenty communist parties remain, that most are legal and uphold Marxism-Leninism, and that Cuba will keep to socialism. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly overview of Latin American communist and left politics, with dates, party names and election data, from 1917 to 2017.
quoteEn: However, the Latin American left has not "died", the cycle of progressive governments in Latin America has not ended, and the Latin American right cannot make a full comeback.
quoteZh: 但是, 拉美左派并没有“死亡”, 拉美进步政府的周期也没有终结, 拉美右翼不可能全面回潮

glossary.explanation: A label used by some Chinese scholars for the varieties of socialism proclaimed by left-wing governments in Latin America since the late 1990s, such as Venezuela's "21st-century socialism". It is not the European fascist usage.
A grouping of Latin American left-wing parties and organisations. It first met in São Paulo in July 1990, and the article says it has grown to 110 members.
The attempt of Salvador Allende's government (1970–1973) to reach socialism by constitutional and peaceful means. The 1973 military coup ended it.

t: On the Soviet Republic and the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly
st: With a critique of the "nihilist view of the October Revolution"
zh: 论苏维埃共和国与立宪会议的解散
zhSub: 兼评“十月革命虚无论”
paras: Writing on the eve of the revolution's centenary, Nie Yunlin takes up the question of why the Soviet government dissolved the Russian Constituent Assembly in January 1918. Nie argues that, since the collapse of the Soviet Union, some commentators have used the dissolution to cast the October Revolution as a conspiracy or coup, or even to deny it happened. In Nie's account the dissolution was justified and fully consistent with Marxist principles, and attacks on it amount to a bourgeois-democratic standpoint.

The article has three parts. The first traces the separate origins of the soviets, from the 1905 revolution through February and October 1917, and of the idea of a constituent assembly, from the American and French precedents through the Decembrists to 1905 and 1917. The second explains why the Bolsheviks still convened the Assembly after October, narrating the elections, the measures taken against opponents and the single day of the Assembly's sitting. The third gives three reasons for dissolution.

Nie holds that the soviets were organs of workers' and peasants' power and a form of proletarian dictatorship, whereas the Assembly was a product of the bourgeois-democratic revolution and a "negative political asset" left by February. The Bolsheviks, Nie says, convened it so that the masses could see its bourgeois character through experience. Nie reports that the Socialist Revolutionaries won a majority of delegates, that the Assembly refused to approve the Declaration of Rights of the Working and Exploited People and the decrees on peace and land, and that its slogan "all power to the Constituent Assembly" served counter-revolution. Nie then follows Lenin: the Soviet republic is a higher form of democracy, the Assembly belonged to the old state machine and refused transformation, and the interests of the proletariat and people stand above formal democracy. Nie supports the last point with three claims: democracy is always class democracy, it cannot abolish class struggle, and content determines form.

Nie concludes that the dissolution consolidated the October victory, defeated an attempted restoration and cleared the way for resisting foreign intervention and for socialist construction. Nie describes the Assembly as a short-lived political farce against the tide of history. Nie also presents contemporary world socialism, with China as its mainstay, as the continuation of the cause the October Revolution began. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar defends the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly and rebuts the "nihilist" reading of October, drawing mainly on Lenin's own texts.
quoteEn: The interests of the proletariat and of the people stand above formal democracy.
quoteZh: 无产阶级的利益、人民的利益高于形式上的民主制

t: The dictatorship of monopoly finance capital has destroyed the participation in and meaning of elections
zh: 垄断金融资本的独裁统治已经毁掉了选举的参与度和意义
paras: This is a Chinese translation of a short commentary by the Egyptian economist Samir Amin on the 2017 French elections. Amin argues that multi-party elections, the signature device of modern democracy in Europe and the United States, are decaying because the dictatorship of monopoly finance capital has emptied them of participation and meaning.

The piece takes France as its case. It covers the April 2017 presidential election and the two rounds of parliamentary voting in June, and recalls the earlier referendum on the European constitution. It then widens to the political situation of Europe and North America over the previous thirty years, and ends with the prospects for the left.

Amin reports that 60 per cent of French voters abstained, which he calls unprecedented in Western democratic history. He says Macron won with no more than 16 per cent of French citizens behind him, mainly the middle class and business owners, so that the media's talk of an overwhelming victory is false. In his account, French voters learned from the ignored referendum result that voting no longer decides anything. He describes a "single party" serving the very rich, in which socialist and conservative governments no longer differ, and he says Western media would condemn such a farce in Russia, Iran or any country of the South.

Amin cautions that the loss of legitimacy of elections will not by itself bring a more advanced, genuinely democratic form. He sees openings in the "Unbowed France" movement and in intensified social struggle, but holds that thirty years of experience show that struggle alone cannot stop the rightward drift. He calls on the radical left in France, Europe and elsewhere to move beyond defence and to build a positive, social and democratic alternative that challenges the world system underpinning imperialism and its Atlantic European subsystem. Read the original if you want a brief example of a Marxist critique of Western electoral democracy from a leading dependency-school thinker.
quoteEn: The loss of legitimacy of \"democratic elections\" will not lead to the formation of another new, more advanced and creative form of genuine democracy.
quoteZh: “民主选举”丧失合法性，并不会导致另一种新的更先进的、有创造力的真正民主形式的形成。

t: Why Trump came onto the stage of history
st: Reflections on Trump, American conservatism and fascism
zh: 特朗普为何会登上历史舞台
zhSub: 关于特朗普、美国保守主义与法西斯主义的思考
paras: Writing in 2017, Ma Zhongcheng asks why Donald Trump won the 2016 US presidential election. The article argues that Trump's rise did not begin with his campaign but with the 2008 financial crisis, which released the economic, political and social contradictions accumulated by neoliberal policy since the 1980s. In Ma's reading, sharpening polarisation and class struggle produced Brexit, the Sanders phenomenon and the Trump phenomenon. American racism, the author holds, is the key instrument for drawing white working-class voters behind monopoly capital, so Trump was backed by both big business and many low-income voters.

The article has five sections. It begins with the Tea Party and Occupy Wall Street movements of 2011, then turns to the billionaire and far-right networks behind the Tea Party, including the Koch brothers, the John Birch Society and Mike Pence. It then compares the 2016 primaries of Sanders and Clinton and Trump's campaign strategy. The last section traces the history of American racism, from the destruction of Native Americans and slavery to the Declaration of Independence, social Darwinism, eugenics and sterilisation laws.

Ma contends that the Democrats' defeat was settled in 2011, when the state suppressed the peaceful Occupy movement while the Tea Party, funded by Trump and the Kochs, was absorbed into the Republican Party. In the author's account, Democratic leaders, citing leaked emails, sabotaged Sanders, who might otherwise have led a New Deal-style reform of capitalism, and monopoly capital instead chose Trump. Ma argues that Trump's strategy resembles historical fascism: it diverts class struggle into conflict between 'middle' and 'bottom' groups, and blames immigrants and 'cronyism' rather than capital. Ma cites Lyndon Johnson's remark about poor whites to illustrate the old tactic, and claims that Nazi racial policy drew on American precedents.

Ma concludes that a working class not yet organised by a Marxist-Leninist party remains a class 'in itself', open to attraction by right-wing racial, nationalist and religious ideologies. Racism, rooted in American founding history, is described as a lasting means of splitting the working people and keeping class consciousness from reviving. The article treats Trump's government of conservative politicians and billionaires as serving finance and business interests despite its anti-elite rhetoric. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist class-analysis reading of Trump, the Tea Party and American racism in the aftermath of the 2016 election.
quoteEn: In fact, racism has always been a powerful weapon in American history for dividing the proletariat and working people.
quoteZh: 实际上，种族主义一直是美国历史上用来分化无产阶级和劳动人民的有力武器。

glossary.explanation: A US right-wing populist movement that emerged around 2009–2011, opposing government spending, taxation and welfare. The article treats it as funded by billionaires and as a base of Trump's support.
A protest movement begun in New York in September 2011 against financial power and economic inequality. The author contrasts it with the Tea Party.

A Marxist distinction between a class defined by its objective position and a class 'for itself' that is conscious and organised. The author says the American working class has not yet been organised into the latter.

t: Class politics in the United States under Trump and the international situation
zh: 特朗普执政条件下美国国内阶级政治与国际局势
paras: Writing in 2017, Zhou Miao asks how Donald Trump's candidacy, election and early executive orders should be understood, and what they mean for US domestic politics, Sino-US relations and the wider international order. The article argues that a Marxist class analysis is needed. It reads the 2008 financial crisis as a crisis of the American neoliberal accumulation regime and a sign that US hegemony is declining further.

The article has three parts. The first surveys the American class structure: a hollowed-out middle class, a fragmented and insecure working class, and a bourgeoisie dominated by financial monopoly groups, with a new financial 'ruling class' and a revolving door between business, government and the intellectual elite. The second part examines the financialised accumulation model and how it shapes party politics and the 2016 election. The third part assesses Trump's domestic and foreign measures and draws conclusions for China.

Zhou's central claim is that the US is ruled by financial monopoly capital, whose core interest is the dollar-centred system and the cycle of debt, financial turbulence and capital return that sustains it. In Zhou's account the Democratic and Republican parties are both bourgeois parties without essential difference, and Trump and Hillary Clinton both belong to the bourgeois right. Trump won because monopoly capital could use him in a time of crisis and because a weakened, race-conscious working class, with little class consciousness, looked to him for deliverance. His anti-immigrant politics, Zhou argues, diverts anger away from capital. His promises of reindustrialisation conflict with the accumulation regime, so recovery rests on 'refinancialisation', and his early rhetoric of retrenchment has reverted to established policy, including the military presence in Asia and a larger defence budget.

Zhou concludes that Trump's task is to serve and repair this regime, and that the regime cannot be repaired indefinitely. Zhou expects the US to keep up strategic pressure on China over the Korean peninsula, the South China Sea, the Diaoyu Islands and Taiwan, and to target China's accumulated national wealth. The article calls for vigilance on financial and economic security, capital-account liberalisation, the dominant position of public ownership in mixed-ownership reform, and the securitisation of state assets. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist class-analytic reading of Trump's election and of US policy towards China as seen in 2017.
quoteEn: Trump's emergence and election are not only the choice of monopoly capital in a time of crisis, but also a product of the present state of the strength and class consciousness of the American working class.
quoteZh: 特朗普的出现和当选，不仅是危机时代垄断资本的选择，也是美国工人阶级力量和阶级意识现状的产物。

glossary.explanation: A Marxist-Leninist category for the fusion of bank and industrial capital in large financial groups. The author treats it as the real ruling force in the United States.
A term from political economy for the institutional arrangement that sustains profit-making over a period. Here it refers to neoliberal, financialised, dollar-led accumulation.
A Chinese policy of bringing private and other non-state capital into state-owned enterprises. The author warns that it must not undermine the dominant position of public ownership.

t: Fidel Castro's outstanding contributions to Cuba and to the development of world socialism
zh: 卡斯特罗对古巴和世界社会主义发展的卓越贡献
paras: Written after Fidel Castro's death on 25 November 2016, this article assesses his legacy in three dimensions. Mao Xianglin argues that Castro made lasting contributions to the Cuban people, to Latin America through the example of the Cuban Revolution, and to world socialism through his theoretical thinking. The article concludes that his achievements will go down in history.

The article has three main parts. The first lists what Castro did for Cuba: a thorough social revolution, a transformed national character, the reorganisation of the Communist Party and the founding of the socialist system, and his example as a revolutionary. The second sets out the international significance of the Cuban Revolution in Latin America. The third presents eleven areas of Castro's thought, from national independence and social justice to Party building, universal education and healthcare, and resistance to "peaceful evolution".

Mao's central claim is that Castro both held to the basic principles of scientific socialism and adapted socialism to Cuban conditions, which the author calls its "localisation". As evidence, Mao points to the 1976 and 1992 constitutions, which kept the leading role of the Communist Party and the goal of communism even after the Soviet collapse, and to four Party-wide theoretical debates on markets and the role of the law of value. Mao also describes Castro's personal conduct as a model: he went into a 1994 riot unarmed, opposed statues and namings in his honour, practised self-criticism, disciplined relatives and friends, and gave up office voluntarily. On the international side, Mao reports that Castro called neoliberal globalisation "re-colonisation" and rejected multi-party politics as a tool of division. Mao presents the Cuban Revolution as the most thorough anti-dictatorship and anti-imperialist revolution in Latin America, the first to move from a national-democratic stage to socialism, and as refuting the claim that socialism suits only Eastern cultures.

Mao concludes that Cuba, one of five existing socialist countries, came through the ebb of world socialism at the end of the twentieth century, and that its experience of localising socialism offers lessons for other socialist states. Mao credits this largely to Castro. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's commemorative account of Castro's ideas and personal example, and of the lessons Cuba's experience holds for socialist countries.
quoteEn: Over decades of leadership, Castro localised the theory of scientific socialism, kept exploring and summing up lessons from revolutionary practice, put forward a series of brilliant ideas, and made outstanding contributions to enriching and developing Marxist scientific socialism.
quoteZh: 卡斯特罗在数十年的领导工作中,将科学社会主义理论本土化,从革命的实践中不断探索和总结,提出了一系列光辉的思想,为丰富和发展马克思主义的科学社会主义理论做出了卓越的贡献。

glossary.explanation: The idea that a general theory such as socialism must be adapted to a country's own conditions. It is related to Chinese discussions of adapting Marxism to the national context.
A term used in Chinese and Cuban communist discourse for the alleged Western strategy of undermining socialist systems through ideological, cultural and political infiltration rather than force.
The term for the socialist theory of Marx and Engels, set against utopian socialism. In Chinese academia it is also the name of a discipline.

t: New developments in European Green Party politics
zh: 欧洲绿党政治的新进展
paras: Huan Qingzhi asks how European Green parties have responded to the two events that, in the author's view, most tested them after the May 2014 European Parliament elections: the Paris Agreement of December 2015 and the British referendum on leaving the EU in June 2016. The commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in March 2017, argues that the Greens kept a fairly positive stance on climate and other ecological issues and took a still clearer position in support of maintaining and deepening European integration.

The piece is organised around the two issues. It first reports how the European Green Party co-chairs, Reinhard Bütikofer and Monica Frassoni, reacted to the European Parliament's ratification of the Paris Agreement (October 2016), its entry into force, and the Marrakech climate conference. It then gathers reactions to the Brexit vote from Green politicians in England, Scotland, Northern Ireland, Ireland and Germany. It ends with the German Greens' September 2016 joint resolution, the Party Council in Glasgow and the Münster party congress.

Huan reports that the Green leaders urged the EU to move faster on emissions targets for 2020, 2030 and 2050, and on energy, transport and financial transition. They also called for a "zero-carbon Europe" before 2050 and described the Commission's energy package as lacking force. On Brexit, the Greens condemned what they called deceptive and xenophobic campaigning. The German Greens' resolution presented the EU as a historic achievement that turned former enemies into partners, and said transnational problems cannot be solved by nation states. It called for a "better Europe" that is more democratic, social and sustainable. Huan treats this combination of support for integration and demand for reform as the party family's defining stance.

Looking ahead, Huan expects the Greens to back global climate politics and EU-led integration more firmly. The author sees the climate stance as increasingly shaped by European interests and the integration stance as moving further from the "European regionalism" of the early 1980s. In the short term, Huan expects them to turn the damage from Brexit, including the Scottish question and falling public trust in the EU, into a chance to rebuild confidence and push EU reform. The Münster congress is described as a bellwether, taking up social justice, opposition to populism and green reform of transport. Huan concludes that the Greens did not waver from supporting integration despite Brexit and the rise of populism. Read the original if you want a brief, source-based account of how Green leaders framed the Paris Agreement and Brexit, as seen from a Chinese scholarly perspective.
quoteEn: European Green parties still hold a fairly positive stance on ecological and environmental issues, including the response to global climate change, and take a still clearer, supportive attitude towards maintaining and deepening European integration.
quoteZh: 欧洲绿党对于包括全球气候变化应对在内的生态环境议题依然持一种较为积极的立场,而对于维系和进一步的欧洲一体化,则是一种更为明确的支持性态度。

t: Why socialist reform in Eastern Europe failed
zh: 东欧社会主义改革为何失败
paras: Li Jiayi and Jun Hongfei ask why the socialist reform movements of Eastern Europe failed, and what that failure means for China. They argue that two main causes were at work: the rigid Stalinist model imposed from outside, and a failure within the region to join socialism to a market economy. The authors treat the lessons as a confirmation of the course of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The short piece, published in People's Forum in 2017, begins with the long process of de-Stalinisation in Eastern Europe. It names the Soviet–Yugoslav conflict, the Poznań events, the Hungarian events and the Prague Spring as its main expressions. It then covers the causes of failure, the roles of politicians and theorists, and the implications for China.

The authors hold that the Stalinist model was deeply entrenched and was defended by conservative forces inside the region. Most politicians and theorists, with the Czech economist Ota Šik a minority exception, did not see the need to combine socialism with a market economy. Some even rejected markets out of a critique of reification, and focused on enterprise autonomy and workers' self-management. The authors add that the reformers were not ordinary dissidents but founders or leaders of communist parties, such as Tito, Gomułka, Dubček and Nagy. They locate the real conflict between reformers and anti-reform forces in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe. A secondary cause was the clash between politicians' pragmatism and theorists' idealism, which the authors illustrate with Yugoslav self-management.

For China, the authors draw the conclusion that socialism must break with the traditional Soviet model and solve China's own problems. They call for adherence to the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship, Party leadership, the Four Cardinal Principles and reform and opening up. They describe socialism with Chinese characteristics as the product of integrating Marxism with China's conditions, which absorbs foreign achievements creatively without copying other countries' models. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese commentary in 2017 drew lessons from Eastern Europe's reform failures.
quoteEn: The primary question for the healthy development of contemporary socialism is how to achieve an organic combination of socialism and the market economy, joining market economy, democratic politics and the socialist system, and this combination must be superior to capitalism.
quoteZh: 当代社会主义健康发展的首要问题就是,如何实现社会主义同市场经济之间的有机结合,将市场经济、民主政治以及社会主义体制有机结合在一起,并且这种结合必须是高于资本主义的结合。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path since reform and opening up, associated with Deng Xiaoping. It describes socialism adapted to China's national conditions.
Principles set out by Deng Xiaoping in 1979: the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship, Communist Party leadership, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought.
The policy launched in 1978 of domestic economic reform and opening to the outside world.
The official description of China's state system, which combines democracy for the people with coercion against those designated as enemies.

t: The theory and practice of the Workers' Party of Belgium
zh: 比利时工人党的理论与实践
source: World Socialism Movement (Shijie shehuizhuyi yundong), 2017 no. 2
paras: Shen Yang introduces the Workers' Party of Belgium (PTB/PVDA), a Marxist party that the author describes as Belgium's largest undisputed radical left party, with two seats in the national parliament. Writing in 2017, Shen notes that Chinese scholarship has paid little attention to the party. The article argues that its theoretical positions and practical activity since its 2008 congress, known as the "renewal congress", offer lessons for China.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the party's main theoretical positions, the second its practical activities, and the third the lessons Shen draws for China. The material is descriptive and relies on the party's own statements and activities rather than on outside sources or comparative analysis.

On theory, Shen reports four positions. The party treats Marxism and the founders' basic works as the foundation of the party. It defines itself in its statutes as a working-class party and focuses on large industry and key economic sectors. It holds that socialism comes from long conflict between bourgeoisie and working class and needs both a prepared working class and ripe conditions, which it considers still distant. It also regards socialism with chinese characteristics as an application and development of Marxism, a view Shen links to the party's Maoist origins. In practice, the party runs a Marxist research institute and quarterly journal, takes part in anti-austerity strikes in 2014, 2015 and 2016, and holds an international communist seminar. It also runs a youth movement, eleven medical centres and two legal offices offering free services, and has promoted Chinese socialism abroad and exchanged visits with China.

Shen concludes that the party's persistence in a capitalist Europe supports three conclusions for China. China should keep to Marxism and the working-class character of the Party, strengthening the Four-sphere Confidence. It should make socialism with Chinese characteristics the main theme of its external publicity. And it should deepen exchanges with friendly parties and countries to raise China's international standing. Read the original if you want a short, China-oriented account of how a small Western European Marxist party presents itself and is viewed in Chinese Party-theory circles.
quoteEn: In a Europe where capitalism is strong, the Workers' Party of Belgium still stresses and upholds Marxism and the working-class character of the party.
quoteZh: 比利时工人党在资本主义强势的欧洲,仍然强调并坚持马克思主义及工人阶级政党性质。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's current path, associated with Deng Xiaoping and reform and opening up. It describes socialism adapted to China's conditions, including a market economy under Party leadership.
A formula that calls for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It was popularised under Xi Jinping.

t: The current state and future choices of foreign socialism and the left
zh: 国外社会主义及左翼现状与未来选择
paras: Writing in early 2017, Zou Guoyu and Sun Yuning ask why socialist and left forces outside China have not benefited from the crisis of capitalism. Their answer is that, despite widespread criticism of capitalism since the 2008 financial crisis, most of these forces remain in a trough and have failed to turn critical "momentum" into political strength. The authors see the main bright spot in the vitality of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The article surveys three groups: communist parties in capitalist countries, national-democratic parties with a socialist-leaning orientation (in Africa and Latin America), and the left wing of socialist and social-democratic parties. It then reviews multilateral platforms: the International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties, the Socialist International, the São Paulo Forum, the Party of the European Left, and regional forums in the former Soviet area and Africa. It closes with the causes of decline and the available choices.

The authors argue that Western anti-capitalist sentiment, lacking effective political leadership, is turning into populism, which squeezes the left between traditional right-wing parties and populist ones. They describe communist parties as suffering from theoretical disputes, slogans without workable programmes, and sectarianism, and the Socialist International from bureaucratic rigidity and the 2013 split that produced the "Progressive Alliance". Subjectively, they say, parties lack programmes suited to the times, and social democrats have converged with the right through the "Third Way". Objectively, they cite the unchanged "strong capital, weak socialism" balance, the fragmentation of identities among workers, and electoral systems that set high thresholds.

Zou and Sun conclude that recovery will take time and that the immediate tasks are to build strength, rethink ideology, and improve organisation. They report that many communist parties agree on rejecting a single guiding centre or single model, and they call this the "greatest common divisor". They propose that the experience of the Communist Party of China in governing the country and the Party be summarised and turned into a "Chinese approach" of worldwide significance, as a possible reference for foreign left forces. Read the original if you want a compact 2017 Chinese official-academic overview of the world's communist, socialist and left parties and their international platforms.
quoteEn: The development of socialist and left forces has never been smooth sailing; it always advances through twists and turns, and every major upswing has been preceded by a period of dormancy.
quoteZh: 社会主义及左翼力量的发展从来都不是一帆风顺的，总是迂回曲折、砥砺前行，在每次大发展之前都伴有一段蛰伏期。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the path, theory and system of the Communist Party of China since reform and opening up. The article presents its success as an inspiration to foreign left forces.
The worldwide organisation of social-democratic and socialist parties, whose roots the article traces to the First International and the 1923 Hamburg body.
A forum of Latin American left parties founded in the 1990s on the initiative of Brazil's Workers' Party and others.
A centre-left political approach of the 1990s associated with European social-democratic parties. The authors argue it made them converge with the right.
An official phrase for China's experience and proposals offered as a contribution to global problems and to other countries' development paths.

t: Analysis of the 18th International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties
zh: 第18次共产党和工人党国际会议论析
paras: This is a report and commentary on the 18th International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties, hosted by the Communist Party of Vietnam in Hanoi on 28–29 October 2016. Liu Xudong notes that it was the first such meeting held in a socialist country. More than 100 delegates from 57 parties attended, and the four other ruling communist parties sent representatives. The Workers' Party of Austria took part for the first time. The theme was the crisis of capitalism and imperialist attacks, and the strategy and tactics of communist parties. The meeting adopted a joint document, the Appeal, and four resolutions, and chose Russia to host the 19th meeting.

The article summarises delegates' positions in four thematic sections, drawing mainly on party statements and the Vietnamese opening address: the deepening capitalist crisis; imperialist aggression and its consequences; socialism as the only alternative; and the parties' plans for joint action. A short assessment follows. Liu quotes many parties by name, including the communist parties of Greece, Portugal, Ireland, Pakistan and India, the Cyprus AKEL and the Workers' Party of Hungary.

According to Liu's account, delegates agreed that the post-2008 crisis is a crisis of the capitalist system, rooted in private ownership of the means of production. They held that bourgeois governments have shifted its burdens onto working people, and that measures such as quantitative easing only delay collapse. Delegates also argued that the United States, NATO and their allies pursue imperialist aggression to escape the crisis and secure resources. They blamed military intervention and support for terrorist groups for regional turmoil, wars in the Middle East and the refugee crisis. Many favoured negotiated settlements under the UN Charter, for example in Syria. The article reports delegates' view that revolutionary transition to socialism is historically inevitable, and that socialist states' record shows its superiority, although the task will be long.

On joint action, the Appeal calls for theoretical exchange on twenty-first-century socialism, joint commemoration of the centenary of the October Revolution and the 150th anniversary of Capital, and an expanded anti-imperialist front. It also calls for solidarity with the Communist Party of Ukraine, Cuba and Palestine. In his assessment Liu credits Vietnam's coordinating role for the shared document, after three earlier meetings (the 15th to 17th) produced none. He lists weaknesses: a shortened schedule, loose organisation between sessions, and little exchange on party-building. Liu remains optimistic about the meeting as a platform. Read the original if you want a detailed, sympathetic digest of how communist parties worldwide framed crisis, imperialism and socialism in 2016.
quoteEn: Over 18 years, the International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties has become an influential platform for exchange among the world's progressive forces, pushing forward the world communist movement since the upheavals in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe.
quoteZh: 18年来，共产党和工人党国际会议已经成为世界上进步力量进行交流的有重要影响力的一个平台，推动着自苏联东欧剧变以来的世界共产主义运动的向前发展。

glossary.zh: 共产党和工人党国际会议
glossary.en: International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties
glossary.literal: International Conference of Communist and Workers' Parties
glossary.explanation: An annual gathering of communist and workers' parties from around the world, held since 1998. It serves as a forum for exchange and joint statements, and is not a formal international organisation.

keywords: International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties

t: The 21st century is the century of the revival of world socialism
zh: 21世纪是世界社会主义复兴的世纪
source: China Social Sciences Today, 14 March 2017, p. 1
paras: Writing in March 2017 in the China Social Sciences Today, Lü Weizhou argues that world socialism, after its deep trough at the end of the 20th century, is gradually recovering. The commentary holds that the view that "the 21st century is the century of the revival of world socialism" is becoming a growing consensus worldwide.

The piece opens with a brief arc from the appearance of socialism as a current of thought in 1516, through its 20th-century rise as theory and system, to the setback of the upheavals in Eastern Europe and the Soviet collapse. It then surveys five signs of revival: reforms in socialist countries, communist parties in capitalist countries, varied socialist currents, growing exchange among socialist forces, and finally the remaining challenges.

Lü presents socialism with Chinese characteristics as a central factor: its success is said to show the need for diverse models and to have shifted a badly unbalanced power relation between socialism and capitalism. The author also cites party congresses in Vietnam, Cuba and Laos in 2016, and reports more than 120 communist parties with over 8 million members in capitalist countries, with electoral results in Greece, Cyprus and Japan. Lü further names market socialism, democratic socialism, eco-socialism and Latin American "21st-century socialism" as currents, along with left alliances such as the European Left Party and forums such as the World Socialism Forum in China.

Lü cautions that the road is not smooth. The author points to the continuing dominance of capital over labour, ideological attacks by the United States-led capitalist states, weak class consciousness among workers, disunity within the socialist camp and the rise of populism. Lü calls on left forces, including communist parties, to build strength, improve organisation and innovate in their methods. Read the original if you want a short, official-leaning overview of how Chinese scholars in 2017 assessed the state of the international left.
quoteEn: \"The 21st century is the century of the revival of world socialism\" is becoming the consensus of more and more people worldwide.
quoteZh: “２１世纪是世界社会主义复兴的世纪”，正成为世界范围内越来越多人的共识。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's current path, theory and system, associated with reform and opening up since the late 1970s.
An international academic conference on socialism held in China, cited in the article as one platform for exchange among socialist forces.

t: Why we should commemorate the October Revolution
zh: 为什么要纪念十月革命
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2017 no. 4
paras: Writing in the centenary year of 1917, Zhou Xincheng asks why the October Revolution still deserves commemoration, given that some in China doubt its path and that the Soviet Union itself abandoned it. Zhou argues that the October Revolution road is the practical embodiment of the basic principles of scientific socialism, that it has universal significance, and that giving it up leads to the ruin of socialism.

The article first sets out the Chinese Communist Party's historical attitude to the revolution and the rise since reform and opening up of a view that reform means "de-Sovietization". It then reduces the question of the road's validity to three issues: how to assess the Soviet socialist model, why the Soviet Union turned to capitalism, and how socialism with Chinese characteristics relates to the October road. Each issue gets its own section, drawing on statements by Mao Zedong, Jiang Zemin and Xi Jinping.

On the first issue, Zhou defends Mao's "seventy-thirty" verdict: achievements are primary and errors secondary. Zhou disputes the figure of fifty million victims of the purges, citing archival totals of sentences and calling for a method that separates mainstream from tributary and basic from specific institutions. Soviet errors, in this reading, lay in specific institutions, not the basic system. On the second issue, Zhou holds that the Soviet collapse followed from Gorbachev's "humane, democratic socialist" reforms, which attacked the Party's leadership, public ownership and Marxist guidance as "three monopolies". On the third, Zhou argues that socialism with Chinese characteristics is scientific socialism and the "continuation and development" of the October Revolution, with Chinese features only in how the principles are applied. Zhou also warns that some domestic critics use criticism of the USSR to argue against Party leadership in China.

Zhou concludes that China must unswervingly follow the October road and the basic principles of scientific socialism, and should keep the Eighth Party Congress formulation that its cause continues the October Revolution. Zhou reads Mao's "follow the Russians" and "take our own road" as answers at different levels, not as contradictory. Read the original if you want a detailed statement of the orthodox Chinese Marxist case for continuity between the Soviet model, Mao-era socialism and the reform era, and for how the Soviet collapse is explained within it.
quoteEn: Socialism with Chinese characteristics is the theoretical crystallisation of combining the basic principles of scientific socialism with China's current concrete realities.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义是科学社会主义基本原则同当前中国具体实际相结合的理论结晶。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path and theory since reform and opening up. Zhou treats it as scientific socialism applied under Chinese conditions.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched in China in 1978.

glossary.literal: the road of the October Revolution
glossary.explanation: In Zhou's usage, the path of establishing socialism on the basic principles of scientific socialism, first taken in Russia in 1917. He presents it as universally valid.

glossary.zh: 科学社会主义基本原则
glossary.explanation: In Zhou's account these include Communist Party leadership, the dictatorship of the proletariat, public ownership, distribution according to work, and Marxism as guiding ideology.
Mao Zedong's rough verdict on Stalin: seventy per cent achievements and thirty per cent errors. Later Party leaders repeated it as "merits outweigh faults".

t: The Seventh Congress of the Cuban Communist Party and the significance of updating the Cuban model
st: An interview with Xu Shicheng, Honorary Academic Member of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences
zh: 古共七大召开及古巴模式更新的意义
zhSub: 访中国社会科学院荣誉学部委员徐世澄研究员
paras: This is an interview with Xu Shicheng, researcher at the Institute of Latin American Studies and Honorary Academic Member of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, conducted by an unnamed interviewer and published in Studies on Marxism in 2017. Against the background of a low ebb in the international communist movement, it asks what the Seventh Congress of the Cuban Communist Party (April 2016) decided and what the 'updating' of the Cuban socialist model means. Xu presents the congress as a bridge between past and future that gives the Cuban cause lasting momentum.

The interview has three parts: the congress itself, the Cuban model, and Fidel Castro. It covers Raúl Castro's central report, the assessment of the five years since the Sixth Congress (2011), three key documents, the make-up of the new Central Committee, and Fidel's closing speech and death in October 2016.

On the report, Xu stresses that Raúl Castro ties the updating to socialism: neither a closed, rigid old path nor a change of banner, no privatisation, and continued Party leadership. Xu also reports figures given at the congress: 2.8% average annual growth for 2011–2015, and 75% of the workforce in the state sector. Xu summarises the 'Conceptualisation' document, which keeps public ownership as the pillar and accepts private property only as a supplement, with the market taken into account but not allowed to dominate. Xu notes that Cuba, unlike China and Vietnam, does not call its economy a socialist market economy. Xu then outlines the 2030 development plan and the updated 274-point Guidelines (50 of them new, in 13 sections). Xu reads the younger, more diverse Central Committee as an organisational guarantee of continuity.

Xu concludes that Fidel Castro's death is a heavy loss, but that Raúl Castro had led in practice since 2006, and Fidel endorsed the congress's programme and attended its close. Xu therefore expects no major turmoil and expects the updating to continue. The interview also reproduces Xi Jinping's condolences, which stress Sino-Cuban friendship. Read the original if you want a Chinese specialist's summary of the 2016 Cuban congress documents, including point-by-point details of the Guidelines, and its view of how Cuban reform compares with China's.
